For just as the darkness of night is especially suited to every kind of trickery, and those who delight in deceiving the ignorant generally abuse it for their schemes, so it seemed hardly credible that a matter of such great moment should be first announced to poor shepherds, whom no public or private authority commended. There was also reason to fear that they would expose themselves to the ridicule of all if they blurted out anything of this kind, which could be proved by no other witnesses. Indeed, it might seem dangerous to speak about the Messiah, since Herod had long been persecuting the family of David, having heard that he would be born from it. And those who spoke more freely about him were generally regarded as seditious. But men whose minds were stirred by a certain assent of faith were not moved by arguments of this kind. This is especially necessary: for unless we believe that what is preached is the Word of God, we shall be able neither to perceive it in its true sense nor to be kindled with a serious zeal for salvation. Therefore Paul commends his Galatians and Thessalonians especially on this ground, that they received him as an angel of God, and recognised the message he preached not as the word of men but as the word of God (which indeed it was). What Christ says of the apostles must extend to all lawful heralds of the Gospel: "He who hears you hears me; and he who receives him whom I send receives me." Luke 10; John 13.

units.la: At quale nam fuit istorum colloquium? Num in nuda apparitionis narratione acquiescunt, aut etiam ea confidentiores facti superbiunt? Vel num stupore belluino perculsi incertis consilijs tumultuantur? Nequaquam. Imo, Eamus (inquiunt) usque Bethlehem, ut videamus factum istud, quod Dominus notum fecit nobis. Intelligunt ergo hoc sibi faciendum esse, etsi nullum expressum Angeli praeceptum de eo accepissent. Nec mora, relictis gregibus suis ad quaerendum verum illum animarum pastorem festinant, ut eius oues ipsi efficiantur. Et hi verae & germanae fidei fructus sunt, ex quibus illa agnoscitur. Nam ut Paulus ait, regnum Dei non est in sermone, sed in virtute. Recte igitur pastores isti non contenti verbis, re ipsa fidem declarant, per quam nobis ad regni Dei possessionem aditus patet. Fidei enim opus est, quod mutuis adhortationibus alij alios ad quaerendum mundi Seruatorem excitant. Nam eo charitatem suam produnt, in qua fidem in primis efficacem esse Paulus testatur. Fidei item opus est festinatio illa, qua omnes rationes abrumpunt, quibus retineri poterant. Ergo iam Christi quoq; amore ardent, & ideo omnem moram longam putant, quae quod ex eius conspectu sperabat, gaudium differre videbatur. Accedit quod ista omnia superat, quod relicto grege suo Bethlehemum festinant. Id enim non absq; periculo factum fuisse patet ex vigilijs siue excubijs, quas prius tam diligentes egerunt. Constat ergo tales omnino fuisse pastores illos, quales Christus vult esse verbi sui auditores, ut ex eo fructum dignum percipiant. Et ideo nō frustratur illos hac sua industria, sed mox (ut Angelus promiserat) cum Maria & Iosepho eum inueniunt, quem tanto tamq; longo desiderio patres sanctissimi & omnes prophetae expectarant.
units.tr: But what kind of conversation was this of theirs? Did they rest in a bare narrative of the appearance, or were they puffed up, becoming more confident because of it? Or were they thrown into bestial stupor and bustle with uncertain plans? By no means. On the contrary, they say, "Let us go even unto Bethlehem, and see this thing which the Lord has made known to us." They understand, therefore, that this must be done by them, even though they had received no express command from the angel about it. Without delay, leaving their flocks, they hasten to seek that true shepherd of souls, so that they might become his sheep. And these are the fruits of true and genuine faith, by which it is recognised. For, as Paul says, "the kingdom of God is not in word but in power." Rightly, then, these shepherds, not content with words, declare their faith by deed, through which a way lies open to us to possess the kingdom of God. For it is the work of faith that, by mutual exhortations, they stir one another up to seek the Saviour of the world. For in this they show forth their charity, in which Paul testifies that faith is above all effective. It is also the work of faith that haste by which they break through all the considerations that could have held them back. Therefore they now burn with the love of Christ, and so they think every delay long, since the joy they hoped for from the sight of him seemed to be postponed. Moreover, what surpasses all these things is that they leave their flock and hasten to Bethlehem. For that this was not done without danger is evident from the vigils or watches which they had kept so diligently before. It is clear, then, that those shepherds were altogether such as Christ wills the hearers of his Word to be, so that they may receive fruit worthy of it from it. And therefore he does not disappoint them in their diligence, but soon (as the angel had promised) they find with Mary and Joseph him whom the most holy fathers and all the prophets had awaited with such long and great desire.

units.la: Prodest ergo, ut singuli sibi ipsis exemplum istud applicent, & quid ipsis faciendum sit discant. Est hoc commune omnium nostrum officium, ut Dominum quaeramus. Ut enim hic nos amat, & olim Adamum ipse quaesuit, & ex perditione retraxit; ita ut nos ipsum quaeramus iubet, & quam ipse nobis offert salutem serio inuestigemus. Ideo olim prophetae clamabant: Quaerite Dominum, dum inueniri potest, innocate eum, dum prope est. Item: Dominus vobiscum est, si vos fueritis cum eo: & si quaesieritis eum, inuenietur vobis. Scribitur denique eodem loco, quasi fuisse Iudaeos Dominum tota voluntate sua, & hunc ab illis inuentum esse, & pacem eis dedisse circumquaque. Caeterum in eo iam rei totius cardo versatur, ut rationem vaaram teneamus, qua Dominus quaeri & inueniri potest. Quia enim Deum nemo vidit vnquam, & idem lucem (vt Paulus ait) inhabitat inaccessam, filius autem Dei carnem, quam ex nobis assumpsit, in coelos subuexit, nulla visibili ratione a nobis ille vel quaeri vel inueniri poterit, sed eum modum nos sequi oportet, quo ille nobis adesse solet. Adest autem nobis spiritu suo, quem nobis paracletum & aduocatum promisit: & proinde spiritualiter quoque a nobis quaeri vult. Itaque hic fide opus est, quae cum sola omnem carnis rationem atque intellectum transcendat, sola etiam Deum inuenit, & ea in illo apprehendit, quae omnem humanae sapientiae captum superant. Fide enim intelligimus Deum nobis patrem esse. Fide cernimus aeterno huius consilio Christum nobis datum esse Seruatorem. Fides item sola nouit, hunc in mundum venisse, peccata nostra mortis suae merito expiauisse, & redemptionem nobis meruisse sempiternam. Denique sola fides omnia Iesu Christi mysteria penetrare potest. Et licet hic multa occurrant, quae carni & mundo absurda videntur, tamen haec quoq; fides superat, dum in Dei verbo acquiescit, quem ab omni dolo & impostura alienissimum esse nouit. Et hinc fit, quod soli credentes seruantur, cum qui salutis vnicus author atque mediator est, non aliter quam fide apprehendi potest.
units.tr: It is useful, therefore, that each of us apply this example to himself and learn what he must do. It is the common duty of us all to seek the Lord. For just as he loves us, and once himself sought Adam and drew him back from perdition, so he bids us seek him, and to search earnestly for the salvation that he himself offers us. For this reason the prophets of old cried out: "Seek the Lord while he may be found; call upon him while he is near." Likewise: "The Lord is with you if you are with him; and if you seek him, he will be found by you." Finally, it is written in the same place, as if the Jews had sought the Lord with their whole will, that he was found by them and gave them peace on every side. But the whole matter turns on this point: that we hold the right way by which the Lord can be sought and found. For since no one has ever seen God, and he (as Paul says) dwells in unapproachable light, and the Son of God has carried the flesh he assumed from us up into heaven, he can be sought or found by us in no visible way; rather we must follow the manner in which he is wont to be present to us. He is present to us, however, by his Spirit, whom he promised us as Paraclete and Advocate; and therefore he wills to be sought by us spiritually too. Thus here we need faith, which, since it alone transcends all reason and understanding of the flesh, alone also finds God, and in him apprehends those things which surpass all the grasp of human wisdom. For by faith we understand that God is our Father. By faith we discern that Christ has been given to us as Saviour by the eternal counsel of God. Faith alone also knows that he came into the world, expiated our sins by the merit of his death, and obtained for us eternal redemption. Finally, faith alone can penetrate all the mysteries of Jesus Christ. And although many things occur here which seem absurd to the flesh and the world, yet faith overcomes these too, while it rests in the Word of God, whom it knows to be most free from all deceit and imposture. And hence it comes about that only believers are saved, since he who is the sole author and mediator of salvation cannot be laid hold of otherwise than by faith.

units.la: At ne nobis ipsis inani fidei fuco imponamus, verae fidei ingenium & propria nouisse oportet. Primum inter haec est, quod solo Dei verbo nititur, & ideo inconcussa perstitit, etiamsi humana omnia fallant. Habuerunt hoc fidei suae fundamentum isti etiam pastores, & proinde non vagantur temerarijs affectibus abrepti, sed in Christo quaerendo vera via & per Angelos monstrata ratione insistunt. Deinde in meditando & examinando Dei verbo sedula est fides: non quod non illius iudices faciat, sed vt cautos & attentos reddat, ne falso verbi Dei praetextu seducantur. Est hoc etiam in pastoribus hisce videre, cum de eo tam serios sermones conferant, quod illis Angelus annuntiarat. Sequitur ex his tertium, quod cognita Dei voluntate homo totus abripitur, vt quiescere non possit, donec optatam diu salutem consequatur. Quae omnia cum in pastoribus nostris Lucas nobis monstret, dubium non est, illos vera fide praeditos fuisse, & ideo quod quaerebant inuenisse.
units.tr: But so that we do not deceive ourselves with an empty show of faith, we must know the nature of true faith and its marks. The first of these is that it rests on the Word of God alone, and so it stands firm even when all human things deceive. The shepherds had this foundation for their faith too, and so they did not wander, carried away by rash feelings, but kept to the true way of seeking Christ, the way shown them by the angels. Second, true faith eagerly meditates on and examines the Word of God. This does not mean it sits in judgement on it, but it makes believers cautious and attentive, so that they are not led astray under the pretext of the Word of God. This can be seen in these shepherds too, when they hold such serious talk about what the angel had announced to them. From this follows the third mark: once a person knows God's will, he is wholly swept along and cannot rest until he has won the salvation he has long desired. Since Luke shows us all these things in our shepherds, there is no doubt that they were endowed with true faith, and so they found what they were seeking.

units.la: Quod si cum his nostri seculi mores conferamus, non mirabimur, Christum hodie a paucissimis inueniri. Nam praedicatur quidem verbum Dei, & qui hoc audiant, multi sunt. At inter hos maximus illorum numerus est, qui ad illud audiendum non nisi commodi priuati studio accedunt, Iudaeorum nimirum similes, quos hoc nomine Christus reprehendit, quod ipsum non alia quam gratuiti conuiuij causa quaerorent. Qui vero tales sunt, ij verbum neq; cordibus suis recondunt, neq; de officio faciendo cogitant. Idem vero si quid audiunt, quod ipsos male vrit, id quidem alta mente repositum seruant: non quod mores suos corrigere cupiant, sed vt obtrectandi & calumniandi occasionem habeant, & apud rudes atq; imperitos omnem fidem Dei verbo derogent. Ex hoc igitur fonte impij illi & scandalorum pleni sermones manant: Fatemur equidem in scripturis contineri, quae clamosi illi Stentores in templis aduersus nos proferunt. An vero propterea sermonibus illorum necessario credendum est? Authores fortasse istorum librorum hi ipsi sunt, qui ita in nos fulminant, aut certe qui olim hoc publicum docendi munus vsurparunt. Annon mendacium perinde vt quod verum est, scribi potest & typis vulgari? Sunt voces istae Christianis auribus indignae, & tanta est earum impietas, vt cum detestatione potius reiici quam argumentis confutari mereantur. Veruntamen propter rudes & infirmos quaedam dicenda sunt, quibus illusorum istorum vanitas arguatur.
units.tr: If we compare these things with the manners of our own age, we will not be surprised that Christ is found today by very few. For the Word of God is indeed preached, and there are many who hear it. But among these the greatest number are those who come to hear it only from a desire for private advantage, like the Jews whom Christ rebuked on this very count, because they sought him for nothing but a free meal. Those who are of this sort neither store the Word in their hearts nor think about doing their duty. And if they hear anything that stings them, they keep it deep in their minds, not because they wish to correct their lives, but so that they may have an occasion to carp and slander, and so that they may take away all trust in the Word of God among the simple and unlearned. From this source flow those wicked and scandal-filled speeches: "We admit indeed that the Scriptures contain what those loud Stentors cry out against us in the churches. But must we necessarily believe their words? Perhaps the authors of those books are these very men who thunder against us like this, or at least those who once seized this public office of teaching. Can a lie not be written and published in print just as well as the truth?" These voices are unworthy of Christian ears, and their impiety is so great that they deserve to be rejected with abhorrence rather than refuted by argument. Nevertheless, for the sake of the simple and weak, some things must be said by which the vanity of these mockers may be exposed.

units.la: Hic vero primum firmiter teneamus, scripturam a Paulo θεόπνευστον dici, nimirum quod verus eius author sit Deus, cuius spiritu olim gubernati prophetae & apostoli scriptis mandarunt, quae ex diuina reuelatione didicerant. Id autem verissime a Paulo dictum esse ex eo apparet, quod nihil libris istis omnibus continetur, quod non perfecte consentiat cum legibus naturae, quas Deus omnium gentium cordibus inscripsit, vt iam nihil dicamus de mirifica historiarum & temporum ab orbe condito serie, quae non aliunde, quam ex sacris literis, certa & vera colligi potest: nihil etiam de promissionum promissionum & vaticiniorum veritate, quam ipsi rerum eventus olim confirmarunt, & hodie adhuc confirmant. Deinde si scriptores ex ordine inspicias, quibus in libris hisce conscribendis Spiritus sanctus, quasi amanuensibus, usus est, minimam illorum partem ex sacerdotum aut Ecclesiasticorum praeconum numero fuisse patebit. Primum enim inter hos locum tenet Moses, qui ut scriptorum omnium, quorum libri extant, longe vetustissimus est: ita princeps populi Israelitici fuit, cum quo nemo Imperatorum, quotquot unquam rei militaris peritia & felicitate illustres fuerunt, conferri meretur. Quem enim ex his omnibus dabis, qui nonaginta armatorum millia una cum ipsorum uxoribus atque liberis, armentis item et gregibus omnibus alia substantia, totis annis quadraginta sub signis habuerit? Hunc proximo gradu sequitur eius successor Iosue, dux populi optimus & fortissimus, mihi de quo verissime Homericum illud dixeris: ἀμφότερον βασιλεὺς τ' ἀγαθὸς, κρατερὸς τε ἀιχμὴ τῆς: ut qui paucorum mensium spatio terram natura & arte munitissimam occupavit, & reges circiter triginta & unum deiecit. Accedit his tertius Samuel, propheta quidem, sed simul iudex praestantissimus, qui populum infelicem ex Philistaeorum tyrannide asseruit. Adnumerari istis debent David & Solomon reges, quorum ille victoriosissimus regum, hic vero mortalium omnium sapientissimus fuit. Et ut ipsos etiam prophetas videamus, nec hi quidem eiusdem loci & ordinis fuerunt. Isaiam enim & Danielem ex regio sanguine, Ieremiam ex sacerdotali familia, Helisaeum & Amos ex rusticis parentibus progenitos fuisse constat. Quod ipsum de Apostolis quoque novi testamenti scriptoribus dici potest. Quibus adde, quod neque eodem tempore, neque eodem in loco simul illi omnes vixerunt, cum multi alios plurimis saeculis vel praecesserint vel secuti sint. Ita vero ista Deus instituit certo suae providentiae consilio, ne quis inter scriptores illos collusionem aliquam fuisse putaret, & ideo illorum scripta merito suspecta haberet. At mendacia quoque scribi posse ais. Sed hoc dicendo de scripturis sacris, animum prodis ingratum Deo, impium & sceleratum. Finge enim villicum hoc de rationum libellis heroi suo respondere, cuius beneficentiam prius multo tempore expertus esset, quis non illum hominum ingratissimum & impudentissimum iudicaret, adhuc indignum cui porro quis beneficeret? Et tu vermis unus horae, cuius origo ex terra est, in quam brevi rediturus es, tam scurrili responso Dei scripta eludis, quibus ille nobis sui regni mysteria patefecit, neque aliud a nobis requirit, quam quod lex naturae praecipit, & ex quo maior ad nos quam ad illum, utilitas redit? Possent haec prolixe tractari, & argumentis gravissimis amplificari posset tanti sceleris atrocitas: sed sufficiat de his cogitandi occasionem dedisse hominibus non omnino malis, ne scurrili illusorum istorum dicacitate offendantur: hos autem Dei iudicio permittamus, quando incurabilem constat esse eorum malitiam. Ut vero eos quoque videamus, qui scripturae sacrae authoritatem divinam esse agnoscunt, & suum verbo Dei honorem deferunt, tamen ex his quoque pauciores sunt, qui hoc cum fructu aliquo audiant. Nam etsi intra animos suos conviciati, quid facto opus sit, norint, non tamen sequuntur vocantem Dominum, sed moras nectunt & tempus extrahunt, novasque quotidie fingunt rationes, quibus sese excusent. Nunc enim divitiis suis metuunt, deque his seruandis diligentius cogitandum esse arbitrantur, priusquam sese periculo manifesto exponant. Nunc coniuges, liberos, parentes & nescio quos alios praetexunt, quos deferre nefas sit. Nunc bellorum pericula, nunc civiles motus, nunc finitimorum principum offensiones vitandas aiunt, & tantum non ne caelum ruat metuunt: & dum tempus magis idoneum expectant, omnem salutis obtinendae occasionem praeterlabi, aut sibi e manibus excuti patiuntur. Multi vero etsi manum aratro admoveant, mox tamen a tergo respiciunt, & ita se regno Dei indignos esse testantur. Istis vitiis nos longum valere dicere convenit, & pastorum istorum pietatem atque zelum imitari, ne quod salutis aeternae nuntium est, nobis in testimonium iustae damnationis cedat. Sed pergamus ad reliqua.
units.tr: Here, first, let us hold firmly that Paul calls Scripture [θεόπνευστον], God-breathed, that is, because its true author is God, by whose Spirit the prophets and apostles, once guided, committed to writing what they had learned from divine revelation. That Paul spoke most truly in this is clear from the fact that nothing in all these books is contained that does not perfectly agree with the laws of nature, which God has written on the hearts of all nations; to say nothing yet of the wonderful sequence of histories and times from the creation of the world, which can be gathered with certainty and truth from no other source than the holy letters; nor of the truth of the promises and prophecies, which the events themselves once confirmed and still confirm today. Next, if you look through the writers in order, whom the Holy Spirit used as his amanuenses in writing these books, it will be plain that only a very small part of them came from the number of priests or ecclesiastical heralds. For first among these is Moses, who, as he is by far the most ancient of all the writers whose books survive, so he was the leader of the people of Israel, with whom no commander, however famous for military skill and success, deserves to be compared. For which of all these will you name who kept ninety thousand armed men under his standards for forty whole years, together with their wives and children, and likewise their herds and flocks and all their other possessions? In the next rank follows his successor Joshua, the best and bravest leader of the people, of whom you may most truly speak in Homer's words: [ἀμφότερον βασιλεὺς τ' ἀγαθὸς, κρατερὸς τε αἰχμητής], both a good king and a mighty spearman; for in the space of a few months he took possession of a land most strongly fortified by nature and art, and overthrew about thirty-one kings. To these is added a third, Samuel, a prophet indeed, but at the same time a most outstanding judge, who delivered the unhappy people from the tyranny of the Philistines. David and Solomon, the kings, ought to be counted among them, of whom the former was the most victorious of kings, and the latter the wisest of all mortals. And if we look at the prophets themselves, they too did not come from the same place and rank. For it is known that Isaiah and Daniel were of royal blood, Jeremiah of a priestly family, and Elisha and Amos were born of rustic parents. The same can be said of the apostles, the writers of the New Testament. Add to these that they did not all live at the same time or in the same place, since many others came before or after them over many centuries. God so arranged these things by a certain plan of his providence, lest anyone should think there was some collusion among those writers, and so hold their writings rightly suspect. But you say that lies can be written too. Yet in saying this about the holy Scriptures you betray a mind ungrateful to God, impious and wicked. Imagine a steward giving this answer about his account books to his lord, whose kindness he had long experienced; who would not judge him the most ungrateful and shameless of men, and unworthy that anyone should do him further kindness? And you, a worm of an hour, whose origin is from the earth, to which you will soon return, do you mock with such a buffoon's reply the writings of God, by which he has revealed to us the mysteries of his kingdom, and asks nothing of us but what the law of nature prescribes, and from which the profit returns to us rather than to him? These matters could be treated at length, and the atrocity of so great a crime could be enlarged with the weightiest arguments. But let it suffice to have given occasion for thought to men who are not altogether evil, lest they be offended by the buffoonish wit of these mockers; and let us leave those men to the judgement of God, since it is plain that their malice is incurable. But if we consider also those who acknowledge the divine authority of the holy Scripture and render honour to the Word of God, yet even among these there are fewer who hear it with any fruit. For although, while they inwardly reproach themselves, they know what must be done, they do not follow the Lord who calls them, but they delay and drag out the time, and invent new excuses every day to make their case. Now they fear for their riches, and think that these must be guarded with more care before they expose themselves to manifest danger. Now they plead their wives, children, parents, and I know not what others, whom it would be wrong to abandon. Now they say the dangers of war, now civil disturbances, now the enmity of neighbouring princes must be avoided, and they fear almost as if the sky were about to fall; and while they wait for a more suitable time, they allow the chance of obtaining salvation to slip past or to be snatched out of their hands. Many, though they put their hand to the plough, soon look back over their shoulder, and in this way testify that they are unworthy of the kingdom of God. It is fitting that we bid a long farewell to these vices, and imitate the piety and zeal of those shepherds, lest the message of eternal salvation turn, for us, into a witness of just damnation. But let us go on to the rest.

units.la: Quid enim inuento puero pastores fecerint, Lucas sic narrat: Cum vidissent autem, divulgaverunt id quod dictum fuerat ipsis de puerulo illo, &c. Quo loco primum observatu dignissimum est, quod vilissima pauperis tugurij & pueruli in praesepi iacentis specie non offenduntur. Unde apparet, ipsos non in hanc, sed potius in Angeli verba intentos fuisse, quae cum fide vera apprehendissent (ut dictum est) animos suos altius attollere potuerunt, & sub vilibus pannis latentem humani generis Seruatorem agnoscere. Simile quid de Magis Orientalibus Matthaeus scribit. Id vero cum primis necessarium est ijs, qui Christum sibi salutarem esse cupiunt, cum ipse dicat: Beatus, qui in
units.tr: For what the shepherds did after they had found the child, Luke narrates it thus: "When they had seen it, they made known the saying which had been told them about this little child," and so on. Here the first thing most worthy of notice is that they were not offended by the very humble appearance of the poor hut and of the little child lying in the manger. From this it is clear that they were not fixed on this appearance but on the words of the angel. Having grasped those words with true faith, as has been said, they were able to lift their minds higher and to recognise under mean rags the Saviour of the human race. Matthew writes something similar about the Eastern Magi. This is especially necessary for those who desire Christ to be their Saviour, since he himself says: "Blessed is he who is not offended in me."

units.la: Cunctatores in studio pietatis. me non offendetur. Nam si carnis & mundi iudicium audiamus, nihil in illo apparebit, quod magni ficum & admiratione dignum videri queat. Alios ergo Christi & in hunc credentium paupertas, alios doctrinae Euangelij simplicitas, alios ministrorum contemptibilis species, plerosque autem crux, indiuulsa fidei comes, offendit. Ad ista ergo nos praeparari conuenit, ut discamus, regni coelorum mysteria non ex splendore externo aut mundi iudicio aestimanda esse: sed ita solere Deum quae inter homines contempta & stulta sunt eligere, ut ea confundat, quae in mundo praeclara & magnifica putantur. Neque eos cruce & persecutionibus offendi par est, qui in his ferendis ducem praire vident Dei filium, & per has nobis ad regni Dei possessionem ingrediendum esse norunt.
units.tr: Those who hesitate in the pursuit of godliness. For if we listen to the judgement of the flesh and of the world, nothing will appear in him that could seem great or worthy of admiration. Thus the poverty of Christ and of those who believe in him offends some, the simplicity of the teaching of the Gospel offends others, the contemptible appearance of the ministers offends others, and for many the cross, the inseparable companion of faith, offends. We must therefore prepare ourselves for these things, that we may learn that the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven are not to be measured by external splendour or by the judgement of the world, but that God is accustomed to choose what is despised and foolish among men, so that he may confound what is thought illustrious and magnificent in the world. Nor should those be offended by the cross and persecutions who see that the Son of God went before them as leader in bearing them, and who know that through these we must enter into the possession of the kingdom of God.

units.la: At non eo contenti sunt pastores, quod intra animos suos de Christo magnificè sentiunt, sed insu per publicè ea denuntiant astantibus, quaecunque de illo ex Angeli relatione didicerant. Inter quae praecipuum erat, hunc esse unctum illum Dei, promissum humani generis Seruatorem & Dominum, cui omnes homines fidere atque obedire debeant. Ergo non pudet illos Christi pauperis & contempti, neque vulgi ludibria metuunt, si de illo tam magnifica loquantur. At quod isti fecerunt, hoc omnes eos facere conuenit, qui Christi beneficio seruari volunt. Nam ut Paulus ait, corde creditur ad iustitiam, ore autem fit confessio ad salutem. Et Christi vox est: Si quis me confitebitur coram hominibus, confitebor & ego illum coram patre meo coelesti. Quemcunque vero mei puduerit coram mundo hoc prauo & adultero, eius pudebit etiam filium hominis, cum venerit in gloria patris sui cum Angelis illis sanctis. Debebant hoc diligentius obseruare nonnulli, qui dum Euangelij successus felicior appa-ret, & ex illo commodi alicuius spes affulget, fidem in Christum plenis buccis iactant: eandem vero vel turpiter dissimulant, vel etiam impie negant, quam primum ex eius confessione periculum sibi imminere vident. Qui dum vitae & fortunis suis consulunt, seipsos Christi simul & aeternis regni coelorum thesauris spoliant. Nos ergo pastores ipsos imitati, Christum tunc quoque libere confiteamur, quando in praesepi iacet, id est, quando a plerisque ridetur & contemnitur: imo ne in cruce quidem pudeat, quando constat hanc nobile per ipsum partae salutis trophaeum esse, & hoc illum nobis meruisse, ut huius seculi afflictionibus gloriari liceat. Rom. 5.
units.tr: But the shepherds were not content merely to think magnificently of Christ within their own hearts; they also proclaimed publicly to those standing by whatever they had learned about him from the angel's message. Among these things the chief was that this man is the anointed one of God, the promised Saviour and Lord of the human race, whom all men ought to trust and obey. Therefore they were not ashamed of Christ, poor and despised, nor did they fear the mockery of the crowd when they spoke so magnificently of him. But what they did, all those who wish to be saved by the benefit of Christ ought to do. For, as Paul says, "with the heart one believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation." And the voice of Christ is: "Whoever shall confess me before men, I will confess him also before my heavenly Father. But whoever is ashamed of me before this perverse and adulterous world, the Son of man will also be ashamed of him, when he comes in the glory of his Father with those holy angels." Some ought to observe this more carefully: when the success of the Gospel appears more favourable and some hope of advantage from it shines forth, they boast of their faith in Christ with full cheeks; yet as soon as they see danger threatening them from its confession, they either shamefully conceal that same faith or even impiously deny it. While they look after their life and fortunes, they rob themselves both of Christ and of the eternal treasures of the kingdom of heaven. Therefore, imitating the shepherds, let us freely confess Christ even when he lies in the manger, that is, when he is laughed at and despised by many; indeed, let us not be ashamed even of the cross, since it is clear that this is the noble trophy of the salvation obtained through him, and that he has merited for us that we may glory in the afflictions of this age. Rom. 5.

units.la: Caeterum non sui capitis figmenta, aut quod ipsis visum fuit, de Christo pastores praedicant, sed quod ex Angelo intellexerunt, id bona fide referunt. Quo loco officij sui admonentur verbi administri, quos Ecclesiae suae pastores constituit Deus. Est haec necessaria in primis Christi cognitio, quam simul suae curae creditus diligenter tradere debent. Talem vero praedicari oportet Christum, qualem libri sacri describunt: neque aliquis sibi licere putet, ut in horum doctrina aliquid mutet, addat siue auferat pro suo arbitrio. Scimus enim Apostolos ipsos certo mandato astrictos fuisse, ut ea docerent, quae a Christo acceperant. Et Paulus anathema eum pronuntiat, qui Euangelium aliud docet, etiamsi Apostolus, vel etiam Angelus de coelo fuerit. Est ergo sacrilega & intolerabilis omnino illorum audacia, qui in ipsum Dei filium tantum iuris sibi sumunt, ut & ipsum alium fingant, quam revera sit, & ab ipso traditam doctrinam proprijs figmentis corrumpant. Afferunt hi vocem alienam, & proinde indigni sunt, qui a Christi ovibus audiantur.
units.tr: Moreover, the shepherds do not preach about Christ according to the inventions of their own head, or according to what seemed good to them, but they faithfully report what they understood from the angel. Here the ministers of the Word, whom God has appointed as the shepherds of his Church, are reminded of their duty. The knowledge of Christ is above all necessary, and those entrusted with the care of others ought to hand it on diligently. Christ must be preached in such a way as the holy books describe him, and no one should think it permitted to change anything in their teaching, to add or take away at his own pleasure. For we know that the Apostles themselves were bound by a definite command to teach those things which they had received from Christ. And Paul pronounces anathema on anyone who teaches another gospel, even if he be an apostle or even an angel from heaven. Therefore the boldness of those is sacrilegious and utterly intolerable, who assume to themselves such right over the Son of God himself that they both invent for him a different person from what he truly is, and corrupt the doctrine delivered by him with their own inventions. Such men bring forward a foreign voice, and therefore they are unworthy to be heard by the sheep of Christ.

units.la: Porrò transeamus tandem ad eos quoque, qui huius rei spectatores & auditores fuerunt. Inter quos primi censentur, qui vel in eandem domum cum Maria tunc diuerterant, vel etiam singulari diuinae prouidentiae consilio ad spectaculum illud euocati conuenerunt. De his sic scribit Lucas: Et omnes qui audierunt, mirati sunt ea, quae ipsis dicta fuerant a pastoribus. Mysterium quidem tantae rei non intellexerunt, & proinde fide quoque vera nondum fuerunt illuminati. Veruntamen laudem merentur, quòd non improbè respondant, neque pastorum verba cum ludibrio reijciunt. Sunt horum multùm dissimiles impij illusores, de quibus paulò ante etiam dictum est, qui non contenti Christum & salutem in hoc nobis exhibitam neglexisse, insuper alios de his differentes non ferunt, & scurriliter nimis reijciunt, quicquid ipsorum desiderijs repugnat, aut quod captum ipsorum superat: quasi nimirum Dei sapientia ad humanae rationis modulum astricta sit. Sunt hi maximorum scandalorum auctores: sed idem dum Deum ludibrio habent, sibipsis ignominiam summam conflant. Firma enim & semper rata manet Dei sententia: Qui me contemnunt, ignominia afficientur. Itaque discamus nos attentis animis audire quaecunque de Deo praedicantur, & si quid a nobis intelligi nequit, id pia admiratione dignemur, & sensus atque intellectu omnem per fidei obedientiam Dei verbo subiiciamus.
units.tr: Let us now at last pass on to those also who were spectators and hearers of this event. Among them are counted first those who had at that time lodged in the same house as Mary, or who were gathered to that sight by the singular counsel of divine providence. Of these Luke writes thus: "And all who heard it wondered at those things which were told them by the shepherds." Indeed they did not understand the mystery of so great a thing, and therefore they had not yet been enlightened by true faith. Nevertheless they deserve praise because they do not respond wickedly, nor do they reject the shepherds' words with mockery. Very unlike them are the impious scoffers, of whom it was said a little earlier, who, not content with having neglected Christ and the salvation offered to us in him, moreover do not tolerate others who speak differently about these things, and too buffoonishly reject whatever resists their desires or exceeds their comprehension, as if forsooth the wisdom of God were bound to the measure of human reason. Such men are authors of the greatest scandals; but while they make God an object of mockery, they bring upon themselves the greatest disgrace. For the sentence of God remains firm and always valid: "Those who despise me shall be dishonoured." Therefore let us learn to hear with attentive minds whatever is preached about God, and if anything cannot be understood by us, let us honour it with pious admiration, and subject our feelings and our understanding to the Word of God by the obedience of faith.

units.la: Porrò omnes astantes longè superat Diua Virgo, quæ verba ista omnia conseruasse & in corde suo contulisse dicitur. Ergo & memori mente recondidit ista, & diligenti meditatione examinauit, vt in eius cognitione, quem modò pepererat, magis proficeret. Vbi rursus fidei veræ ingenium cernitur. Nam ante omnia ista ex Angelo Gabriele audiuerat, vt novis magistris non haberet opus. At tamen pastores quoq; eadem dicentes attentè audit, & horum verba cum ijs, quæ Angelus ipse dixerat, diligenter confert. Et quod modestiæ singularis exemplum est, non superba suæ dignitatis ostentatione effertur, neq; gloriosula iactat quæ sibi hucusq; contigerant. Est hæc virtus hodie rara inter homines. Pleriq; enim, vbi se in salutis cognitione aliquò vsq; progressos putant, omnem doctrinam, ceu inutilem sibi & superuacaneam reijciunt, & ne eos quidem audire dignantur, qui in Ecclesiæ ministerio constituti sunt, cuius authorem esse Deum ex vtriusq; testamenti scripturis constat. At dum suæ scientiæ opes illi ostentant, turpiter nimis suam inopiam atq; stultitiam produnt: quòd nimirum ne se ipsos quidem norint, quod sapientiæ veræ principium esse olim philosophi dixerunt. In primis autem Mariæ exemplum parentes obseruent, ne exse prognatis liberis confidentius superbiant. Sciebat illa Dei Filium & olim promissum Seruatorem esse, quem ipsa pepererat, neq; dubium est, quin in illo omnem salutis fiduciam habuerit collocatam. Non tamen illo ambitiosè gloriatur, sed tacitè gaudio suo fruitur cum modestia. Quæ ergo dementia est illorum fiducia efferri, qui ex nobis nati, & quanti quanti sunt, peccatores sunt, neque nobis alicuius commodi authores esse possunt, nisi ex æterno verbi Dei semine in Christo regenerentur?
units.tr: Moreover, the blessed Virgin far surpasses all who were present, for she is said to have kept all these words and pondered them in her heart. Therefore she stored them in a retentive mind and examined them by diligent meditation, so that she might make progress in the knowledge of him whom she had just borne. Here again the nature of true faith is seen. For she had heard all these things beforehand from the angel Gabriel, so that she had no need of new teachers. Yet she listens attentively also to the shepherds who speak the same things, and carefully compares their words with those which the angel himself had spoken. And this is a singular example of modesty: she is not puffed up by a proud display of her dignity, nor does she boast with vainglory of what had happened to her so far. This virtue is rare among men today. For most people, when they think they have progressed somewhat in the knowledge of salvation, reject all teaching as useless and superfluous for themselves, and do not deign to hear even those who are appointed to the ministry of the Church, whose author God is evident from the Scriptures of both Testaments. But while they display the riches of their knowledge, they shamefully betray their poverty and folly, since they do not even know themselves, which the philosophers of old said was the beginning of true wisdom. Above all, parents should observe the example of Mary, lest they become too confidently proud of their offspring. She knew that the Son of God, the Saviour long promised, was the one whom she had borne, and there is no doubt that she had placed all her trust of salvation in him. Yet she does not glory in him ambitiously, but quietly enjoys her joy with modesty. What madness, then, is it to be puffed up by the confidence of those who, born of us and however many they are, are sinners, and cannot be the authors of any benefit to us unless they are regenerated in Christ from the eternal seed of the Word of God?

units.la: Sed tempus est, vt ad postremam huius loci partem accedamus, quam his verbis Lucas absoluit: Et reuersi sunt pastores, glorificantes et laudantes Deum super omnibus, quæ audierant & viderant, pro vt ipsis dictum fuerat. Occurrunt hic quoq; multa obseruatu dignißima. Primum, fidem & Christianæ pietatis studium non obstare, quò minus a Deo impositâ functionem obeamus, & honestis laboribus vacemus, quibus necessaria vitæ huius subsidia parantur. Imò iubet Euangelium, vt singVli proprijs manibus sibi victum parent, & docet, vt in quauis vocatione salua conscientia versari & Deo seruire possimus. Ioānes certè Baptista, neq; publicanos à suo officio, neq; milites ab armis disce dere iubet, sed quid facere debeant, docet. Paulus vero nò mundo vti prohibet, sed ne illo abutamur monet, & vnusquisq; (ait) in vocatione sua maneat, in qua vocatus est. Rectè igitur pastores isti ad gregem suum redeunt, neq; opus erat, vt quoad corporalem præsentiam Christo induulsi comites ad essent, cùm illù iam cordibus suis gestarent fide vera apprehensum. Damnantur horū exemplo otiosi ventres, qui sub religionis prætextu familias alienas subeunt, & ex aliorū laboribus viuunt. Monachi itē, qui vt mundo mortui videantur, vel in loca deserta secedunt, vel diuersorū ordinum septa ingrediuntur, & illic vitā viuunt segnem, nemini mortalium vtiles. Quos magna ex parte imitantur Anabaptistæ, fanatici & seditiosum hominum genus, qui tunc demum se Christianos esse arbitrantur, si relicta re domestica & omni honesto artificio, priuatim omnibus molesti sint, publice verò omne ordinem tam in repub. quàm in Ecclesia turbare satagant. Vult quidē Christus, vt propter ipsum, si ita opus sit, omnia nostra relinquamus: at qui id faciunt nulla vrgente necessitate, neq; suis honestè pro spiciūt, cū id salua fide et pietate posset, ij se à fide alienos & ethnicis deteriores esse testatur. 1. Ti. 5.
units.tr: But it is time to come to the final part of this passage, which Luke concludes with these words: "And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things they had heard and seen, just as it had been told to them." Here too many things worth noting present themselves. First, faith and the zeal of Christian piety do not stand in the way of our carrying out the function imposed on us by God and devoting ourselves to honest labours by which the necessities of this life are provided. Indeed, the Gospel commands that each one provide for himself by his own hands, and it teaches that in any calling we can live with a clear conscience and serve God. John the Baptist certainly does not bid the tax collectors leave their office or the soldiers leave their arms, but teaches them what they ought to do. Paul, moreover, does not forbid the use of the world but warns against abusing it, and says: "Let each one remain in the calling in which he was called." Rightly, therefore, these shepherds return to their flock, nor was there any need that, as regards bodily presence, they should remain as companions to Christ, since they already bore him in their hearts, grasped by true faith. By their example are condemned the idle bellies who, under the pretext of religion, creep into other people's households and live off the labours of others. Likewise the monks, who withdraw either into deserted places or enter the enclosures of various orders, so that they may seem dead to the world, and there live a sluggish life, useful to none of mortals. Largely imitating them are the Anabaptists, a fanatical and seditious kind of men, who think they are Christians only when, having abandoned their household affairs and every honest craft, they are a nuisance to everyone in private, while in public they strive to upset all order both in the commonwealth and in the Church. Christ indeed wills that, for his sake, if need be, we leave behind all that is ours; but those who do so without any pressing necessity, and without providing honestly for their own, when this could be done with faith and piety intact, show that they are alien to the faith and worse than the heathen. 1 Tim. 5.

units.la: Deinde apparet ex pastorū gaudio, quod Dei & bonitatis eius prædicatione declarant, illos ni hil interea damni accepisse, dū relicto grege suo Christū quæsiuerunt. Est hoc exemplum plenū con solationis, quo docemur, nullam rerū necessariarū iacturā nos factuos esse, si Christū quæramus, & propter hunc res nostra ad tempus periculo exponamus. Quia enim Dei prouidentia ad aues & corvorum pullos, imò ad flores vsq; temere in agris nascentes extenditur, minimè putandum est, eos à Deo negligi, qui in ipso quærendo occupātur. Quærite ante omnia (inquit Christus) regnum Dei & iustitiā eius, & reliqua omnia vobis adijcientur. Quæ promissio cùm exemplis infinitis confirmata sit, & quotidie magis confirmetur, etiam atq; etiam cauendum est, ne anxia solicitudine & nimio re rum terrenarum studio nos ipsos illius fructu spoliemus. Requiritur quidem à nobis industria & cura rei domesticæ, sed hanc cum fide coniunctam esse decet, vt meminerimus frustraneṡ laboribus nos fatigari, nisi Dominus ipse domū ædificet. Huius ergo curæ nosipsos et nostra omnia committamus, si quid cum periculo tentandum est, & procul dubio illum in nobis seruandis fidelem experientur.
units.tr: Next, it appears from the shepherds' joy, which they declare by proclaiming God and his goodness, that they suffered no loss in the meantime while, having left their flock, they sought Christ. This is an example full of consolation, by which we are taught that we shall suffer no loss of necessary things if we seek Christ and for his sake expose our possessions to danger for a time. For since God's providence extends even to the birds and the young ravens, indeed even to the flowers that spring up carelessly in the fields, we must by no means think that those are neglected by God who are occupied in seeking him. "Seek first," says Christ, "the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these other things will be added to you." Since this promise has been confirmed by countless examples, and is confirmed more and more every day, we must take all the more care lest, through anxious solicitude and excessive devotion to earthly things, we deprive ourselves of its fruit. Indeed, diligence and care for household affairs are required of us, but this ought to be joined with faith, so that we remember we labour in vain unless the Lord himself builds the house. Let us therefore commit ourselves and all that is ours to this care, if anything must be attempted at risk, and without doubt they will find him faithful in preserving us.

units.la: Postremò pastores isti Deum glorificauisse et laudauisse dicuntur super omnibus, quæ audierant
units.tr: Finally, these shepherds are said to have glorified and praised God for all the things they had heard

units.la: Mariæ mente reponit om. et cōferт, &c. & viderant, prout ipsis dictum fuerat. Repetit subinde Lucas ea, quæ ab Angelis, fidis Dei internuntijs, dicta fuerunt, vt ostendat, pastorum fidem Dei verbo gubernatam fuisse. Etenim frustra in considerandis illius operibus versantur, qui verbum negligunt, quo illorum author & vsus indicantur. Simul autem officij nos admonet Spiritus sanctus, vt ipsi quoq; Deum glorificemus atq; laudemus pro omnibus beneficijs, quæ in nos secundum promissiones suas per Iesum Christum contulit. Promi serat autem, quòd is serpentis caput conculcare & diaboli regnū destruere, peccata nostra expiare, mortem vincere, nosq; in libertatem filiorū Dei asserere deberet. Atqui hæc ille omnia præstitit, idq; iam moriturus testatus est, cùm iam omnia consummata esse diceret. Docemur item per Euangelium, nos Deo per illum reconciliatos esse, & reconciliationis istius arrhabonem habemus Spiritum sanctum, qui eandem Sacramentis quoq; visibilibus nobis obsignat. Deniq; quem pastores isti in præsepi vilem & contemptibilem viderunt, eum nos Regem & Sacerdote, adhæc mortis atq; inferorum vi stiorem, cœli item terræq; dominum in Euangelio conspicimus. Excitet ergo nos pastorū exemplum, vt ipsi quoq; Deum glorificemus & laudemus pro exhibito nobis salutis æternæ beneficio, neq; nos pudeat eum confiteri coram mundo hoc prauo & adultero, qui pro nobis omnia huius miserę & mortalis vitæ discrimina subire dignatus fuit. Illi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum, Amen.
units.tr: ...and seen, just as it had been told them. Luke repeats again what was spoken by the angels, the faithful messengers of God, so as to show that the shepherds' faith was governed by the Word of God. For those who neglect the Word, by which the author and use of God's works are made known, labour in vain in contemplating his works. At the same time the Holy Spirit admonishes us of our duty, that we too should glorify and praise God for all the benefits which he has bestowed upon us through Jesus Christ, according to his promises. He had promised that he would crush the head of the serpent, destroy the kingdom of the devil, expiate our sins, conquer death, and assert us into the liberty of the sons of God. Yet he accomplished all these things, and testified this when about to die, saying that all things were now finished. We are also taught through the Gospel that we are reconciled to God through him, and we have the Holy Spirit as the pledge of this reconciliation, who seals the same to us also by the visible sacraments. Lastly, him whom those shepherds saw in the manger, lowly and contemptible, we in the Gospel behold as King and Priest, moreover stronger than the power of death and hell, and likewise Lord of heaven and earth. Let the example of the shepherds therefore stir us up to glorify and praise God too, for the eternal salvation bestowed upon us, and let us not be ashamed to confess him before this wicked and adulterous world, who deigned to undergo for us all the perils of this miserable and mortal life. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever, Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA XIX.
units.tr: HOMILY XIX.

units.la: Et cum impleti essent dies octo, vt circumciderent puerulum, tunc vocatum est nomen eius Iesus, quod vocatū fuerat ab Angelo, priusquam ipse in vtero conciperetur.
units.tr: And when eight days were fulfilled, that they should circumcise the child, his name was then called Jesus, which had been given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.

units.la: VEmadmodum veteres prophetæ duce Spiritu sancto promissum humanigeneris Seruatorem magno studio inuestigarunt, & de eius afflictionibus simul atq; has secuta gloria vaticinati sunt: Ita Euangelistæ ex eiusdem spiritus suggestione illius in carne manifestationem, et quæcunq; ab illo in terris hisce facta sunt, diligenter narrant, neq; illos piget in ijs etiam immorari, quæ carnis iudicio leuia & ridicula videntur. Quia enim pater in illo reconditos nobis esse voluit omnes sapientiæ & scientiæ thesauros, et idé nobis ab illo sapientia, iustitia, sanctificatio et redemptio factus est, nihil in illo tam minutum aut vile inuenitur, quod non certa nostræ salutis mysteria contineat, nosq; in Dei & salutis nostræ cognitionem pleniorem inducat. Argumentum huius euidens est Circumcisio, quam etsi Lucas paucis attingat, & eadem primo intuitu nihil magni aut eximij præse ferat, tamen de ijs nos admonet, sine quorum cognitione salus nostra consistere non potest. Nam fœderis, quod nobis cum Deo intercedit, rationem tradit, & simul verum Baptismi vsum indicat, qui in illius locum successit. Adhæc veram doctrinam de Christo illustrat, vt rectius intelligamus, quid nobis in illo sit traditum. Quæ omnia vt magis perspicua sint, primò de Circumcisione ipsa dicemus, et quæ eius ratio & vsus olim apud veteres fuerit. Inde Christi circumcisionem & huius causas inuestigabimus. His quædam subijciemus de nomine Iesu, quod tunc pro more illi fuit impositum.
units.tr: Just as the ancient prophets, led by the Holy Spirit, searched with great diligence for the promised Saviour of mankind, and prophesied of his sufferings and of the glory that followed them, so the Evangelists, moved by the same Spirit, carefully relate his manifestation in the flesh and all that he did on earth. Nor are they ashamed to linger over things that seem trivial and ridiculous by the judgement of the flesh. For since the Father willed that all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge should be hidden in him for us, and since he has been made for us wisdom, righteousness, sanctification and redemption, nothing in him is so small or lowly that it does not contain the sure mysteries of our salvation and lead us into a fuller knowledge of God and of our salvation. Circumcision is clear evidence of this. Although Luke touches on it briefly, and at first sight it seems to carry nothing great or remarkable, it nonetheless teaches us things without knowing which our salvation cannot stand. For it sets out the nature of the covenant that stands between us and God, and at the same time shows the true use of Baptism, which took its place. Besides this, it illumines the true doctrine concerning Christ, so that we may better understand what has been handed down to us in him. To make all this clearer, we shall first speak of circumcision itself, and of its reason and use among the ancients. Then we shall examine the circumcision of Christ and its causes. To these we shall add a few remarks on the name Jesus, which was given to him at that time according to custom.

units.la: Circumcisio olim actio sacra erat, qua ex Dei instituto præputium resecabatur ijs, qui adsocietatem populi Dei seu Ecclesiæ pertinebant, in quam adoptabantur, vt fœderis diuini & promissionum consortes fierent, & simul officij sui admonerentur. Ideo verè signum populi Dei dicebatur, et infantibus quoq; adhibebatur, cùm etiā hos Deus fœdere suo esset complexus. Institutio eius tota ex fœdere Dei dependet. Quia enim promissio salutis Adamo olim data, posteris temporibus propter vniuersalem totius humani generis corruptionem & horribile iudicij Dei exemplum in diluuio editum, prorsus abolita videbatur, solenni illius instauratione opus fuit. Ad eam verò rem ex gratia peculiari Deus Abrahamum elegit, quem inter idololatras agentem ex Chaldæa in terram Chanaan euocat, vt salutis fœdus cum illo instauret. Capita huius præcipua sunt hæc: Primum, Ego sum El Schadai id est, Deus omnipotens, qui ad omnia omnibus sufficio, & cui nihil deest eorum, quæ ad perfectionem salutis desiderari possunt. Secundum, Ambula coram me, & esto integer. Tertiū, In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes terræ. Et primo quidem Cap. seipsum nobis obstringit Deus, secundo autem nostri nos officij admonet, tertio veterem salutis per semen mulieris, id est, Christum reparandæ promissione repetit. Itaq; paucis istis vniuersa salutis ratio continetur, quam postea Spiritus sanctus in scripturis vtriusq; testamenti fusius exposuit atq; illustrauit. Quid enim aliud docent Moses, prophetæ & apostoli, quàm quid nobis ex Deo sperandum sit, vt hic se totum nobis fruendum offerat, quod item nostrum sit officium, vt seruorum instar fidelium coram ipso ambulare & omnia nostra secundùm illius voluntatem instituere debeamus, in quo integritas tota hominis cõsistit: vt denique filium suum ille in mundum miserit, qui propter nos homo factus peccatum mundi omne expiauit, & cum iustitia sempiterna benedictionem quoq; & salutem veram nobis reddidit? Est autè hoc ingens bonitatis Dei & amoris, quo nos complectitur, incomparabilis argumentum. Qui enim ipsissima est iustitia, veritas, sapientia, omnipotentia, fons item vitæ & bonorum omnium inexhaustus et nullius egens, nobis obstringi voluit, qui natura iniusti, mendaces, stulti et cœlestium rerum ignari, miseri & infirmi, mortales deniq; & omnium indigi sumus, adeò vt ne nosipsos quidè iuuare possimus, nedum illi gratiam aliquâ referre. Laudantur mirificè principes, qui vel subditis sese affabiles præbent, vel cum vicinis amicitiâ studiosè colunt, quibus cum naturæ communione habent, & quorum obedientia atq; amicitia ipsis quoq; necessaria est. At hic, quoad nos & Dei nihil huius inuenire licet: quando neq; nostris officijs hic opus habet, neq; vllis cõditionibus alijs nos obstringit, quâ quæ nobis vtiles sunt, & sine quarũ obseruatione vita hæc neq; cõmodè transigi, neq; iucunda esse potest. O si in horũ consideratione diligentiores essemus, plurimũ ad veræ pietatis studiũ procul dubio accederet.
units.tr: Circumcision was once a sacred act, by which, according to God's institution, the foreskin was cut away from those who belonged to the fellowship of the people of God, or the Church, into which they were adopted, so that they might become sharers in the divine covenant and its promises, and at the same time be reminded of their duty. For this reason it was rightly called the sign of the people of God, and it was applied even to infants, since God had included them too in his covenant. The whole institution of it depends on God's covenant. For since the promise of salvation once given to Adam seemed utterly abolished in later times, because of the universal corruption of the whole human race and the terrible example of God's judgement displayed in the Flood, a solemn renewal of it was needed. For this purpose God, by a peculiar grace, chose Abraham, whom he called out of Chaldea into the land of Canaan while he was living among idolaters, so that he might renew the covenant of salvation with him. The main heads of this are these. First: "I am El Shaddai," that is, God Almighty, who suffices for all things for all men, and who lacks nothing of those things that can be desired for the perfection of salvation. Second: "Walk before me, and be perfect." Third: "In your seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed." In the first, God binds himself to us; in the second, he reminds us of our duty; in the third, he repeats the old promise of salvation through the seed of the woman, that is, Christ, to be restored. Thus the whole plan of salvation is contained in these few words, which the Holy Spirit afterwards set out and illustrated more fully in the Scriptures of both Testaments. For what else do Moses, the prophets and the apostles teach, than what we are to hope for from God, namely that he offers himself to us wholly to enjoy; and likewise what our duty is, namely that, like faithful servants, we should walk before him and order all our affairs according to his will, in which the whole integrity of man consists; and finally that he sent his Son into the world, who, being made man for our sake, expiated all the sin of the world and restored to us, with everlasting righteousness, both blessing and true salvation? This is an immense and incomparable proof of the goodness and love of God, by which he embraces us. For he who is very righteousness, truth, wisdom and omnipotence, the fountain of life and of all good things, inexhaustible and needing nothing, has willed to bind himself to us, who by nature are unrighteous, lying, foolish and ignorant of heavenly things, wretched and weak, mortal in the end and in want of everything, so that we cannot even help ourselves, much less return any favour to him. Princes are greatly praised when they show themselves affable to their subjects, or cultivate friendship eagerly with their neighbours, with whom they share a common nature, and whose obedience and friendship are also necessary to them. But here, as far as we and God are concerned, nothing of this can be found; for he has no need of our services, nor does he bind himself to us by any conditions other than those that are useful to us, and without the observance of which this life can be neither well spent nor happy. Oh, if we were more diligent in considering these things, no doubt much would be added to our zeal for true piety.

units.la: Cæterum vt in fœderibus non solum conditiones vtrinq; proponi & conscribi solent, verumetiã sigilla addi, quibus illæ confirmentur: Ita suum fœdus circuncisione obsignari in hominibus voluit Deus, quò minus de eius fide dubitaremus. Quo rursus suam erga nos bonitatem declarat, quando qui fidem & obedientiam pro suo iure à nobis exigere poterat, ad nostros mores sese demittit, vt nostræ infirmitati succurrat. Signum verò adhibet in speciem vile & contemptibile, ne qui in illo hærentes ipsum fœdus negligerent, sed potius signi vilitate ad mysteriorũ sub illo latentium consideratio-nem excitarentur. Quod ipsum in nostris etiam Sacramentis ab illo obseruatum esse, nuper dixi-mus. Signum verò eiusmodi instituit, quod ab hominibus solis vsurparetur. Vt enim ipse sibi semper constat, ita nulla quoq; in ipsum cadit dubitatio. At quia fides nostra varijs tentationum arietibus impulsa fluctuat, nobis sigillis opus est, quibus illa confirmetur, & de ipsius veritate certior fiat. Et ne quis Circuncisionem ob speciem contemptibilem negligeret ceu superuacaneam, graui præcepto et non sine comminatione ad eius obseruationem. Abrahami posteros obstrinxit. Sic enim loquitur: Omnis mas, qui fuerit in generationibus vestris dierũ octo, circuncidetur vobis, siue verna fuerit, siue ære emptus à quocunq; extraneo, qui non est de semine tuo. Omnino verna & ære tuo emptus circun-cidi debent, vt sit fœdus meum in carne vestra fœdere sempiterno. Porrò mas præputiatus, cuius præputium carnis circuncisum non fuerit, huius anima excindatur è populo suo: quia fœdus meum irri-tum fecit. Nec vanas fuisse minas istas, Moses exemplo docemur, quem ex Madianitica terra in Ægyptum redeuntem Angelus Domini occidere voluit, quòd Gersonem filium non curasset circun-cidi. Et qui in deserto sub Mose nati erant, non prius ad terræ promissæ possessionem admissi sunt, quàm circuncisionis sigillum accepissent. Non autem temere illam à Deo tam seueriter mandatum fuisse patebit, si illius usum diligentius consideremus.
units.tr: Moreover, just as in covenants the conditions are not only proposed and written down on both sides, but seals are also added by which they are confirmed, so God willed that his covenant be sealed among men by circumcision, so that we should have less doubt of his faithfulness. In this again he declares his goodness towards us, since he who could demand faith and obedience from us as his due, stoops to our manner, so as to help our weakness. He appointed a sign that is outwardly lowly and contemptible, so that those who clung to it would not neglect the covenant itself, but rather be stirred, by the humbleness of the sign, to consider the mysteries hidden beneath it. We have said recently that he observed this same practice in our sacraments too. He instituted a sign of such a kind that it could be used by men alone. For just as he is always consistent with himself, so no doubt can fall upon him. But because our faith, struck by the various battering rams of temptations, wavers, we need seals by which it may be strengthened and made more certain of the truth of God. And lest anyone should neglect circumcision as superfluous because of its contemptible appearance, he bound the posterity of Abraham to its observance by a grave command, and not without threat. For he speaks thus: "Every male among you in your generations, when he is eight days old, shall be circumcised, whether he be born in the house or bought with money from any stranger who is not of your seed. Certainly those born in your house and those bought with your money must be circumcised, so that my covenant may be in your flesh an everlasting covenant. But the uncircumcised male, whose flesh of the foreskin has not been circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people, because he has broken my covenant." That these threats were not empty we are taught by the example of Moses, whom the angel of the Lord wished to kill when he was returning from the land of Midian into Egypt, because he had not had his son Gershom circumcised. And those who were born in the wilderness under Moses were not admitted to the possession of the promised land until they had received the seal of circumcision. Nor will it be evident that God commanded it so strictly without reason, if we consider its use more carefully.

units.la: Primò testera erat externa, quæ Abrahami posteros, populum Iudaicum, à reliquis gentibus se-cernebat. Id verò facto opus erat, partim vt eius vsu fidem suam publicè profiterentur, partim ne aliis gentibus miscerentur, & ne genus illud amitteretur, ex quo promissus ille humani generis re-demptor nasci debebat. Noverat enim Deus, populum illũ modò inter Ægyptios, modò inter Assy-rios & infinitas alias gentes dispergendum fore, & ideo cauere voluit, ne illis commixtus à sua so-cietate in vniuersum excideret. Secundò cùm in membro genitali fieret, & recens quoq; natus infan-tibus adhiberetur, innatæ vitiositatis admonebat, quæ omnibus hominib9 ex primo parente inhæret, & proinde illos putatione opus habere docebat, qua illa auferatur, ne in homine regnum obtineat. Tertiò, quia fœderis diuini signum erat, cuius complementum in semine illo benedicto, Iesu Christo, habetur, hunc quoq; figurabat, qui vera Circuncisionis vnicus author est, vt Paulus ad Col.2.cap. testatur. Itaq; ad illum remittebat, ne putationem illam, qua ab Originali prauitate & ex hac ma-nantibus frustibus liberamur, alibi quàm in illo vno quærerent. Quartò promissiones Dei omnes ob signabat, & in primis quidem eam, quæ de Christo habetur: quo nomine Paulus illam vocat sigil- lum iustitiæ fidei, id est, eius iustitiæ, quæ nobis per fidem in Iesum Christum obtingit. Itaq; certò do- cebat, Deum pro iustis habere et suo fauore gratuito omnes eos prosequi, qui Christum fide vera ap- prehendunt. Quæ causa est, quòd pij olim ex Circumcisione consolationis argumenta petebant, si quid grauioris periculi ex hostibus exteris immineret. Tunc enim (vt in Ionathani et Dauidis cum Goliatho congressuri historia patet) illos incircumcisos dicebant, nō tam opprobrij causa, quàm quòd se in Dei peculium cooptatos esse & fœderis diuini sigillum certum in corpore suo gestare significa- bant. Postremò ad Legis obseruationem astringebat Circumcisio, quando constat fœdera & pacta omnia irrita & inutilia fieri, nisi conditiones obseruentur, quibus illa constat. Ideò Paulus Gala- tis scribebat: Testor omni homini qui circumciditur, quòd debitor est totius Legis seruandæ. Et ad Romanos: Circumcisio quidem prodest, si Legem seruaris. Quòd si transgressor Legis fueris, circum- cisio tua præputium facta est, &c. Multiplex ergo Circumcisionis vsus fuit apud veteres, & ideo illam minimè negligere licuit.
units.tr: First, it was an external mark that separated the posterity of Abraham, the Jewish people, from the other nations. This was necessary partly so that they might publicly profess their faith by its use, and partly so that they would not mix with other nations, and so that that race, from which the promised Redeemer of mankind was to be born, would not be lost. For God knew that this people would be scattered now among the Egyptians, now among the Assyrians and countless other nations, and therefore he wished to guard against their being mingled with these and falling altogether from his fellowship. Second, since it was performed on the member of generation, and was applied even to newborn infants, it reminded them of the innate sinfulness that clings to all men from the first parent, and so taught that they needed a pruning by which it might be taken away, lest it should hold sway in the man. Third, because it was a sign of the divine covenant, whose fulfilment is found in that blessed seed, Jesus Christ, it also foreshadowed him, who is the sole author of true circumcision, as Paul testifies to the Colossians, chapter 2. Therefore it sent them to him, so that they would not seek that cutting away, by which we are freed from original depravity and from the fruits that flow from it, anywhere but in him alone. Fourth, it sealed all the promises of God, and especially that which concerns Christ. For this reason Paul calls it "the seal of the righteousness of faith," that is, of that righteousness which comes to us through faith in Jesus Christ. Thus it certainly taught that God regards as righteous, and embraces with his free favour, all those who lay hold of Christ by true faith. This is why the godly of old drew arguments of comfort from circumcision whenever some more serious danger threatened from foreign enemies. For then (as appears from the history of Jonathan and David when they went out against Goliath) they called the enemies uncircumcised, not so much as a reproach, but because they signified that they themselves had been chosen as God's peculiar people and bore in their body the sure seal of the divine covenant. Lastly, circumcision bound men to the observance of the Law, since it is plain that all covenants and pacts become void and useless unless the conditions on which they rest are kept. Therefore Paul wrote to the Galatians: "I testify to every man who is circumcised that he is a debtor to keep the whole Law." And to the Romans: "Circumcision indeed profits, if you keep the Law. But if you are a transgressor of the Law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision," and so on. Circumcision therefore had many uses among the ancients, and so it was by no means permissible to neglect it.

units.la: Quia autem eadem est Sacramentorum omnium ratio, proderit ista ad Baptismum transferre, qui in illius locum successit, vt de eo etiam rectè iudicare discamus. Constat enim Iudæorum gentem non stetisse conditionibus à Deo præscriptis, & proinde à fœdere illius excidisse, & exstat ea de re pas- sim ipsius Dei testimonia, qui de illorum perfidia per prophetas acerbè conqueritur. Opus ergo erat instauratione, & ideo nouum fœdus siue testamentum Deus per Ieremiam pollicetur. Nouum verò hoc dicit, non quòd nouas conditiones præscribat, sed quòd populus nouus ex gentibus assumptus, & abolitis veteribus Sacramentis, quæ cruenta & operosiora erant, noua et obseruatu facilíora institu- ta sunt. Oportebat enim in Christi sanguine omne veteris testamenti sanguine sisti, & ideo circum- cisionem quoq; aboleri oportuit, cui Christus Baptismum substituit, cuius idē omnino vsus est. Nam per hunc ceu tessera quadam militarii in ecclesiæ & militiæ Iesu Christi consortium ascribimur, & à Iudæis & Turcis atq; reliquis aliarū superstitionum sectatoribus secernimur: quod vt ad ordinem ecclesiæ seruandum facit, ita fidei quoq; professionem continet, quam liberam & ingenuam esse de- cet. Deinde idē nos pollutos & peccati sordibus inquinatos esse innuit, qui ablutione opus habeamus.
units.tr: Since all the sacraments rest on the same reasoning, it will help to apply this to Baptism, which has taken the place of circumcision, so that we may also learn to judge it rightly. It is established that the Jewish nation did not abide by the conditions prescribed by God, and so fell away from his covenant. God's own testimonies on this point are found throughout the prophets, where he complains bitterly of their faithlessness. Restoration was therefore needed, and so God promised through Jeremiah a new covenant or testament. He calls it new not because he prescribes new conditions, but because a new people taken from the Gentiles was being admitted, and because the old sacraments, which were bloody and more burdensome, were abolished and replaced by new ones that were easier to observe. For it was fitting that in the blood of Christ all the blood of the Old Testament should come to an end, and so circumcision also had to be abolished, and Christ put Baptism in its place, which has exactly the same use. For through it, as through a kind of military token, we are enrolled in the fellowship of the Church and the army of Jesus Christ, and we are distinguished from Jews, Turks and the adherents of the other superstitions. This serves to maintain the order of the Church, and it also contains a profession of faith, which ought to be free and sincere. Further, it signals that we are polluted and stained with the filth of sin, and so have need of washing.

units.la: Et quia in Christi mortem baptizamur (vt Paulus inquit) ablutionem illam in hoc vno nos habe- re docet. Adhæc obsignantur nobis in Baptismo omnes Dei promissiones, & idem infallibile est in stitiæ fidei sigillum, ex quo in grauissimis conscientiæ tentationibus argumenta solida consolationis peti possunt, quòd nimirum nunquam eos abiecturus sit Deus, qui per fidem Christo insiti & illi iam pridem reconciliati sunt. Simul autem officij nostri admonemur, vt tanto tamq; pretioso sanguinis Christi lauacro abluti, in posterum sanctimoniæ studeamus, & vt Christus pro nobis mortuus ad vitam verè diuinam & cœlestem resurrexit: ita ipsi quoq; peccato prorsus moriamur, resurgamus autem ad vitam nouam & Christiana professione dignam. Et hæc quidem de circumcisione & de Baptismo, qui illi successit, dicta sint.
units.tr: And because we are baptized into the death of Christ (as Paul says), it teaches us that we have that washing in this one thing alone. Moreover, all God's promises are sealed to us in Baptism, and it is the unfailing seal of the faith of our justification, from which solid grounds of comfort can be sought in the gravest temptations of conscience: namely, that God will never cast off those who have been grafted into Christ through faith and have long since been reconciled to him. At the same time we are reminded of our duty, that, having been washed in the so precious bath of Christ's blood, we should strive for holiness from now on; and that just as Christ died for us and rose again to a life truly divine and heavenly, so we too should die entirely to sin and rise to a new life worthy of the Christian profession. And let this suffice on circumcision and on Baptism, which succeeded it.

units.la: Transeamus nunc ad Iesu Christi circumcisionem, cuius causas in primis inuestigare oportet, vt ex his discamus, quis ex illa fructus ad nos redeat. Si enim quæ hucusq; dicta sunt cum illo confera- mus, mox patebit, illum minimè opus habuisse vt circumcideretur. Quia enim filius Dei vnigeni- tus, adhæc absq; peccato conceptus & natus est, nequaquam opus erat vt vel signo aliquo externo à reliquis dignosceretur, vel emundationis alicuius & officij admoneretur, vel sigillum aliquod iusti- tiæ aliunde acciperet, quod illum in fide erga Deum patrem confirmaret. Ergo ne (inquis) superua canea censeri debet eius circumcisio? Vel num illam inscius aut etiam inuitus accepit, qualia mul- ta infantibus accidere solent? Nequaquam. Quamuis enim quoad carnem infirmus infans factus fuit, idem tamen filius Dei erat æternus, æterna item patris sapientia, & Verbum illud omnipo- tens, cuius virtute omnia condita sunt & gubernantur. Quare huius circumcisionis causas non tam in illo quàm in nobis quærere oportet. Vt enim nostræ salutis ergò in mundum venit, & homo factus est: ita propter nos etiam circumcidi voluit, eò quòd istud nostræ salutis mtio postularet, & pluri- mum faceret ad fidei nostræ confirmationem.
units.tr: Let us now pass to the circumcision of Jesus Christ, whose causes we must first investigate, so that we may learn from them what fruit comes back to us from it. For if we compare what has been said so far with him, it will soon be clear that he had no need to be circumcised. For since the only-begotten Son of God was conceived and born without sin, there was no necessity for him to be distinguished from others by some external sign, or to be reminded of some cleansing and duty, or to receive from elsewhere some seal of righteousness that would confirm him in faith towards God the Father. Are we then to think (you will say) that his circumcision was superfluous? Or did he receive it unknowingly or even unwillingly, as many things happen to infants? By no means. For although as to the flesh he became a weak infant, he was nonetheless the same eternal Son of God, the eternal wisdom of the Father, and that almighty Word by whose power all things were created and are governed. Therefore we ought to seek the causes of this circumcision not so much in him as in us. For just as he came into the world and became man for our salvation, so he also willed to be circumcised for our sake, because the reason of our salvation required it and it would greatly serve to confirm our faith.

units.la: Primò enim habemus hic verae humanitatis, quam ex Maria assumpsit testimonium, quod publicè editum voluit, vt ipsum & fratrem nostrum esse, & eodem nobiscum fœdere continerì constaret. Scimus enim pro confæderatis recte censeri, qui in signo fœderis legitimè recepto participant. Quia ergo Dei filius fœderis, quod nobiscum inierat pater, signum in se recepit, ipsum quoq; fœderis illius socium, & proinde hominem verum factum esse, non possumus dubitare. Hanc ipsam ob causam idem postea baptizari voluit, & novi etiam fœderis signo obstringi, ut se utriusq; testamenti Seruatorem esse doceret, cuius merito & veteres olim seruati sint, & nos hodie seruari oportet. Ideo illum scripturæ lapidem angularem dicunt, eò quòd utrunq; populum Dei, veterem nimirum & novum, quasi duos muros, in idem ecclesiæ ædificium connectit: ut qui prius per ceremonias legales, ut maceriam aliquam diuidebantur, nunc eiusdem ecclesiæ membra et salutis eiusdem hæredes sint. Par-rit hoc dulcissimam consolationem, qua nosipsos in tentationibus quibuscunq; sustentemus. Quia enim fœderis eiusdem socius nobiscum est Christus, imò frater noster est, ad nos utiq; pertinet vniuersus meriti ipsius fructus, nosque illius in regno patris cohæredes erimus.
units.tr: For first, here we have a testimony to the true humanity that he took from Mary, which he willed to be made public, so that it might be plain that he is both our brother and bound by the same covenant as we are. For we know that those are rightly regarded as fellow-covenanters who take part in the lawfully received sign of the covenant. Since, then, the Son of God received in himself the sign of the covenant that the Father had entered into with us, we cannot doubt that he too became a partner in that covenant and therefore a true man. For this same reason he afterwards wished to be baptized and bound with the sign of the new covenant as well, so that he might show himself to be the Saviour of both testaments, by whose merit the men of old were saved and we today ought to be saved. Hence they call him the cornerstone of Scripture, because he joins the two peoples of God, the old and the new, as two walls, into the same building of the Church, so that those who were formerly divided by the legal ceremonies, as by some dividing wall, are now members of the same Church and heirs of the same salvation. This brings the sweetest consolation, by which we may sustain ourselves in whatever temptations. For since Christ is a fellow-partner of this covenant with us, and indeed our brother, the whole fruit of his merit certainly belongs to us, and we shall be co-heirs with him in the Father's kingdom.

units.la: Deinde quia qui circuncidantur, debitores sunt totius Legis seruandæ, Christum etiam circuncidi oportuit, ut Legi obnoxius fieret, & nos per illum in Legis maledictione liberaremur. Ita mysterium hoc Paulus exponit ad Galatas scribens: Vbi venit plenitudo temporis, emisit Deus filium suum factum ex muliere, factu Legi obnoxium, ut eos qui erant Legi obnoxij, redimeret, ut adoptionem filiorum reciperemus.
