Nam nos quidem omnes ad Legis obseruationem ex fœdere astringebamur: & quia illam præstare impossibile erat, omnes etiam sententiæ illi horribili obnoxij fuimus, quæ maledictos pronunciat quoscunq; qui Legi non in omnibus obtemperant. At quoniam ideo in mundum venerat Dei filius, ut maledictionem istam aboleret, ipsum prius Legi subiici oportuit, ut causam nostram posset suscipere, nosque suæ obedientiæ merito tueretur. Quo respiciens dicebat, uos iam non esse amplius sub Lege, sed sub gratia. Nam etsi adhuc teneamur obedientiæ debito, maledictionem tamen Christus sustulit, & nos cum patre in gratiam reduxit. Quoties ergo Satan conscientijs nostris obijcit: Maledictus omnis, qui non fecerit quæcunq; scripta sunt in libro Legis istius: mox tu arrepto fidei clypeo Christum oppone, qui quod nobis præstitu impossibile erat, confecit, & sententiæ istius rigorem a nostris ceruicibus depulit. Quòd si ogganniat quadruplator ille: Quid verò ad te Christus? Est hic æternus Dei filius, iustitia est, veritas & vita est: tu autem homo es mortalis, peccator, mendax & exitio obnoxius. Tunc rursus ad Circuncisionem illius recurrito, & ideo hanc illum recepisse cogita, ut se & hominem atq; fratrem tuum esse testaretur, & pro nobis Legi obnoxius fieret, nosq; suæ satisfactionis merito seruaret. Hæc qui non ofcitanter expendunt, facile vident, quam profundus & inexhaustus gratiæ thesaurus nobis in Christo recoditus sit, cum eius Circuncisio consolationem tantam exhibeat, quæ sola nobis aduersus omne genus tentationum poterit sufficere.
units.tr: Next, since those who are circumcised are debtors to keep the whole Law, it was also necessary for Christ to be circumcised, so that he might become subject to the Law and through him we might be freed from the curse of the Law. Paul sets out this mystery thus, writing to the Galatians: "When the fullness of time came, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made subject to the Law, that he might redeem those who were under the Law, that we might receive the adoption of sons" (Gal. 4). For all of us were bound by the covenant to keep the Law; and since it was impossible for us to perform it, we were all also liable to that dreadful sentence which pronounces accursed all who do not obey the Law in every point. But since the Son of God had come into the world for the purpose of abolishing that curse, it was necessary that he himself first be made subject to the Law, so that he could take up our cause and protect us by the merit of his obedience. Looking to this, he said that you are no longer under the Law but under grace. For although we are still held to the debt of obedience, Christ has nevertheless removed the curse and brought us back into favour with the Father. Therefore whenever Satan throws in our consciences the words, "Cursed is everyone who does not do all that is written in the book of this Law," then straightaway, taking up the shield of faith, set Christ against him, who accomplished what was impossible for us and drove the rigour of that sentence from our necks. But if that informer should sneer, "What has Christ to do with you? He is the eternal Son of God, he is righteousness, truth and life; but you are a mortal man, a sinner, a liar, and liable to destruction," then turn back to his circumcision, and reflect that he received it so that he might witness that he is both man and your brother, and so that he might become subject to the Law on our behalf and keep us by the merit of his satisfaction. Those who weigh these things carefully easily see how deep and inexhaustible is the treasure of grace laid up for us in Christ, since his circumcision offers so great a consolation, which alone can suffice for us against every kind of temptation.

units.la: Tertio Legis disciplinam suo exemplo nobis Christus commendat, ne illi colla nostra subducamus insolenter, quia ipse tam obedienter subijt. Quod ut in omnibus Dei institutis obseruandum est: ita maxime ad Sacramenta referri debet, ne illorum vsum ceu inutilem aut superuacaneum negligamus. Nam ut ante diximus, Circuncisione Christus nequaquam opus habebat, neq; iludignorabant Iosephus & Maria, cum uterq; ex Angeli relatione, ipsum æternum Dei filium & olim promissum humani generis redemptorem esse didicissent. Verumtamen nihil hi de eo disputat, quod a Deo institutum et veteri more in ecclesia receptum esse sciebant: ipse etiam nihil huius subire detrectat, ut æterno patris decreto sese per omnia accommodet. Quod ipsum postea in Baptismo factum esse audiemus. Cum enim Ioannes diuina spiritus reuelatione edoctus illum Dei filium et Messiam esse intellexisset, et proinde baptismum ab ipso peteti diceret: Mihi opus est ut abs te baptizer, et tu venis ad me? Respondit ille: Omitte nunc, sic enim decet nos implere omnem iustitiam. Seruit ergo Christi exemplum confutandis omnibus, qui Sacramentorum vsum, ut superuacaneum, negligunt, vel etiam impie aspernantur. Qua in re multum & varie nostro seculo peccatur. Quàm multos enim est videre, qui Baptismum, quo infantes ipsorum tingi & in ecclesiæ societatem ascribi debebant, diutius differunt, ut vel maiori cum fastu & ostentatione rem administrare, vel aliunde testes (quos Compatres & Commatres vulgò vocat) accersere possint, quasi nemo in tota loci illius ecclesia sit, qui hoc officium ipsis præstare queat. Produnt hi animos parum religiosos et iniquos nimium Christianæ societatis æstimatores. Maior tamen est Anabaptistarum audacia, qui sub plausibili religionis et pietatis prætextu Baptismum infantium omnino damnat, et hos (quantum in ipsis est) ab ecclesiæ et salutis cofortio excludut. Baptizandos enim esse negant, eò quòd mysterium salutis nondum intelligat, et fide nondum sint præditi. At nō quid illi
units.tr: Third, Christ commends to us by his own example the discipline of the Law, so that we do not shake off its yoke insolently, since he himself submitted so obediently. This must be observed in all of God's institutions, and it applies especially to the sacraments, so that we do not neglect their use as useless or superfluous. For, as we said before, Christ had no need of circumcision, nor did Joseph and Mary fail to know this, since both had learned from the angel's report that he was the eternal Son of God and the redeemer of the human race promised of old. Yet they raised no dispute about it, because they knew it had been instituted by God and was received in the Church by ancient custom; and he too does not shrink from undergoing it, so that he might accommodate himself in all things to the eternal decree of the Father. We shall hear later that he did the same in Baptism. For when John, taught by a divine revelation, had understood that he was the Son of God and the Messiah, and therefore said that he should ask baptism from him, saying, "I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?", he answered: "Let it be so now, for thus it becomes us to fulfil all righteousness." Christ's example therefore serves to refute all who neglect the use of the sacraments as superfluous, or even impiously despise them. In this matter there is much sin in our age, and in many different ways. For how many may be seen who put off the Baptism by which their infants ought to be washed and enrolled in the fellowship of the Church for so long, either so that they may conduct the rite with greater pomp and display, or so that they may send for witnesses from elsewhere (whom they commonly call godfathers and godmothers), as if there were no one in the whole congregation of that place who could perform this office for them. These show minds that are little religious and that value the Christian fellowship far too little. Yet the boldness of the Anabaptists is greater, who under the plausible pretext of religion and piety utterly condemn the Baptism of infants, and exclude them (as far as in them lies) from the fellowship of the Church and of salvation. For they deny that infants are to be baptized, because they do not yet understand the mystery of salvation and are not yet endowed with faith. But it is not what they understand that should be regarded, but what God wishes to be done

units.la: 2. Christus Legis obnoxius factus. intelligant, sed quid Deus fieri velit, spectare oportebat. Nesciebant olim, quid in Circumcisione agere retur, infantes iidem tamen circumcidebantur, eo quod eos in foedere suo comprehendisset Deus. Quid ergo prohibet, quo minus nostri baptizentur, quos eodem foedere continerinemo negabit, nisi qui Christum mendacij arguere velit? Clamant illi, nusquam mandatum hoc esse, ut paruulis baptismus detur. Fateor: at simul id ne prohibitum quidem esse dico, & Christi praeceptum urgemus, qui iuber, ut puerulos ad se adducamus, quia ad illos regnum coelorum pertineat. Quae autem illos ad Christum deducendi ratio esse potest? alia, quam ut per Baptismum cooptentur in ecclesiam, quae Christi corpus est? Hanc ergo nobis saluam esse sinant phanatici illi turbatores, aut aliam monstret, qua infantes Christo coniungi possint. Id vero tum facient, quando mula pepererit. Quod vero illos a fide alienos dicunt, eo suam produnt confidentiam et impudentem quiduis dicendi temeritatem, qua Christo contradicunt, qui paruulos in se credere testatur. Nam in Euangelio dicit: Quisquis offenderit unum ex paruulis istis, qui in me credunt, &c. Quod si fidei illorum ratio nostrum sensum & intellectum superat, num id illis fraudi esse debet & ecclesiae, quam homines isti maxima & nobilissima membrorum suorum parte spoliare tentant? Neminem ergo moueant illorum sophismata, quin potius sanctorum utriusque testamenti exemplum omnes imitentur, quibus hoc potissimum cordi fuit, ut ex se natos in ecclesiae album adscriptos viderent. Simul autem hic eorum error confutatur, qui a communione Coenae Dominicae in universum abstinent, vel saltem ad illam rarius accedunt, quod Dei gratiam et Christi meritum huic minime alligari, & proinde eius usum superuacaneum esse putent. Fatemur equidem & nos gratiam Dei nullis externis rebus debere astringi: at simul necessariam esse dicimus obedientiam fidei, quam nos in iis quoque Deo praestare decet, quae carnis iudicio nullius omnino momenti esse videntur. Quia ergo Christus coenam suam, iam moriturus, magna cum authoritate in mortis suae commemorationem instituit, & Corinthios olim lue punitos esse Paulus scribit, quod in eius usu aliquid ex suo arbitrio mutauissent, nimium temerarij parumq; religiosi sunt, qui illa in universum negligunt. Scimus equidem nonnullos ideo abstinere, quod se indignos esse vident, aut saltem conscientia peccatorum grauati ad illam accedere verentur. De his in praesenti non est sermo, sed illis, qui minus recte Christi instituta aestimant, quos nullae rationes excusare possunt. Alteros autem illos monemus, ne infirmitati suae nimium indulgeat, sed meminerint, Coena pro hominibus instituta esse, quorum infirmitates Deus non ignorat. Itaq; eius gratia innocent, et eius spe freti se esse ecclesiae coniungant, neq; carebit fructu suo fides: sed ex contemptis principiis in immensum crescet, sicuti in sinapis parabola Christus docet.
units.tr: 2. Christ made subject to the Law. They should not look at what they understand, but at what God wishes to be done. The Israelites of old did not know what was being done in circumcision, yet infants were circumcised all the same, because God had included them in his covenant. What, then, prevents our children from being baptized, when no one will deny that they are included in the same covenant, unless he wishes to charge Christ with lying? Those men cry out that nowhere is it commanded that baptism be given to little children. I grant it; but at the same time I say that it is not forbidden either, and we press the precept of Christ, who bids us bring the little ones to him, because the kingdom of heaven belongs to them. And what way of bringing them to Christ can there be other than their being admitted through baptism into the Church, which is the body of Christ? Let those fanatical troublemakers therefore allow us to keep this way, or let them show another by which infants can be joined to Christ. They will do that only when the mule bears young. As for their claim that infants are strangers to faith, that shows their boldness and their shameless rashness in saying anything at all, by which they contradict Christ, who testifies that little children believe in him. For in the Gospel he says: "Whoever shall offend one of these little ones who believe in me," etc. But if the reason for their faith surpasses our sense and understanding, ought that to harm them, or the Church, which these men try to strip of its most noble and greatest part, its members? Let no one, then, be moved by their sophistries; rather let all imitate the example of the saints of both Testaments, for whom it was above all a matter of heart that their children, born of themselves, should be enrolled in the register of the Church. At the same time this error is refuted of those who abstain altogether from the communion of the Lord's Supper, or at least approach it rarely, because they think that God's grace and Christ's merit are in no way bound to it, and that its use is therefore superfluous. Indeed we too confess that the grace of God must be bound to no external things; but at the same time we say that obedience of faith is necessary, which it is fitting for us to render to God even in those things which seem to be of no importance at all by the judgement of the flesh. Therefore, since Christ, about to die, instituted his supper with great authority in memory of his death, and since Paul writes that the Corinthians were once punished with plague because they had altered something in its use according to their own judgement, those are excessively rash and not sufficiently religious who neglect it altogether. I know indeed that some abstain because they see themselves to be unworthy, or at least, weighed down by the consciousness of their sins, they fear to approach it. Our present discussion is not about these, but about those who value Christ's institutions too lightly, whom no reasons can excuse. The former, however, we warn not to indulge their weakness too much, but to remember that the Supper was instituted for men, whose weaknesses God does not overlook. Therefore, let them rely on his grace and his promise, and join themselves to the Church, and their faith will not lack its fruit; but from despised beginnings it will grow beyond measure, just as Christ teaches in the parable of the mustard seed.

units.la: Restat postrema huius loci pars, qua inter circumcidendum puerulo nome Iesu impositum fuisse narratur, quia ab Angelo vocatum fuisse supra audiuimus, priusq; in utero virginis conciperetur. Huc enim veteres fuisse more, ut cum Circumcisione nomina quoq; propria infantes acciperet, dictum est, qui historia nati Ioannis expositum. Nouum aut obedientia fidei exemplum Iosephi et Mariae nobis exhibet, quia do Angeli praecepto simpliciter obtemperat, et ne in illo quoq; Dei voluntate transgrediuntur, & carnis in dicio indifferens videbatur. Quod ergo supra de Zachariae et Elizabetae obedientia diximus hic etiam repeti et in mente reuocari debet, ne ad nobis indulgeamus in iis, de quib. certum Dei mandatum extat.
units.tr: There remains the last part of this passage, in which it is told that during the circumcision the name Jesus was given to the little boy, because, as we heard above, he had been called so by the angel before he was conceived in the virgin's womb. For it was said, when the birth of John was explained in the history, that it was the custom of the ancients for infants to receive their proper names along with circumcision. Joseph and Mary present us with a new example of obedience of faith, because they simply obey the angel's command, and in this too they do not transgress God's will, though it seemed indifferent to human judgement. Therefore what we said above about the obedience of Zacharias and Elizabeth must be repeated here as well and kept in mind, so that we do not indulge ourselves in those matters about which there is a certain command of God.

units.la: Erfi vero de nomine Iesu quaedam in primo Cap. dicta sint, nemini tamen graue videri debet, eadem hic diligentius repetere, cum & Angelus de eodem Iosephum quoq; admonuerit, & huius praeceptum in praesenti Lucas rursum attingat. Et Iesu quidem nomine Seruatorem significari, satis iam notum est: at in eo nobis duo potissimum obseruanda sunt. Primum, qualis Seruator sit Christus. Ut enim variae hominum afflictiones et varia sunt pericula: ita varios quoq; Seruatores esse constat, quorum alij ex morbis eripiunt, alij inopia laborantibus succurrunt, alij ex ignominia liberant, alij in bellis aut quocunq; alio discrimine opem ferunt. Et in his quidem omnibus Christus suos seruare potest, et non raro illis manum porrigit. Non tamen hoc proprium eius efficium est, neq; semper ad hunc modum seruat, cum interdum utilius sit, nos diutius periclitari, vel etiam quoad corpus periculis eiusmodi succumbere. Quare Angelum interpretem audiamus, qui nominis istius rationem hanc reddit, quod populum suum liberet a peccatis ipsorum. Et haec vera hominis salus est, quia illis sublatis, iram Dei & maledictionem simul auferri necesse est. Itaq; peccatorum remissionem in illo quaerant, qui spe sua frustrari nolunt: alioqui dum sibi in illo opes, honores & huius seculi commoda pollicentur, fere cum Iudaeis impingunt, qui quod Messiam regni terreni instauratorem ipsis fore putarent, qui euersa Romanorum tyrannide auitam libertatem & gloriam ipsis restitueret, Iesum hunc pro illo agnoscere non potuerunt, cum eum nihil huius praeferre viderent. At nō suffi
units.tr: Although some things about the name of Jesus were said in the first chapter, no one should find it tiresome if we here repeat the same more carefully, since the angel also admonished Joseph about the same name, and Luke now touches again on this command. That the name Jesus signifies Saviour is already well enough known; but in it two things above all are to be observed. First, what sort of Saviour Christ is. For just as human afflictions and dangers are various, so it is clear that saviours are various too: some rescue from diseases, others help those labouring in poverty, others free from disgrace, others bring aid in wars or in any other peril. And in all these matters Christ can save his people, and often he stretches out his hand to them. Yet this is not his proper office, nor does he always save in this way, since sometimes it is more profitable for us to remain longer in danger, or even to succumb to such perils in body. Let us therefore hear the angel as interpreter, who gives this reason for the name, that he will free his people from their sins. And this is man's true salvation, because once sins are removed, the wrath and curse of God must necessarily be removed too. Therefore let those who do not want to be disappointed in their hope seek forgiveness of sins in him. Otherwise, while they promise themselves in him riches, honours and the advantages of this age, they nearly stumble with the Jews, who, thinking that the Messiah would be the restorer of an earthly kingdom, who would overthrow the tyranny of the Romans and restore to them their ancestral liberty and glory, could not recognise this Jesus as that one, since they saw that he promised nothing of this kind. But it is not enough

units.la: cit Seruatorem agnoscere, nisi hunc solum Seruatorē esse agnoscamus, quod alterum huius cognitio nis caput est. Et hoc illud est, de quo hodie passim contenditur. Nam fatentur plerique, Dei filium, qui ex Maria virgine homo natus est, Seruatorem esse, sed ijdē fere illo vno nō contenti sunt, quin con iungunt ei Diuos & Diuas caelites, quibus in periculis vota nuncupant, & praecipua salutis fiduciam in illis collocata habet. Semper ergo meminisse oportet eius, quod per Isaiam ille proclamat: Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum, & gloriam meam alteri non dabo. Item quod Samaritidi ait: Qui biberit ex aqua hac (elementali nimirum, sub cuius typo omnia alia salutis praesidia intelligit) sitiet iterum: qui vero biberit ex aqua, quam ego dabo, non sitiet in aeternum. Obseruarunt ista diligenter Apostoli, qui Christum sic praedicarunt, vt ipsi vni omnem humanae salutis gloriam transcripserint. Haec enim omnium communis vox est, quam in Senatu Hierosolymitano protestati sunt: Non est in alio quoquam salus: nec enim aliud nomen est sub caelo, quod datū sit inter homines, per quod oportet nos seruari. Paulus equidem, etsi raptus in tertium caelum ineffabilia multa audiuisset, non ve- retur tamen publicè testari, se nihil nouisse aliud, quàm Iesum Christum, pro nobis crucifixum. Tuntur piter ergo & pernitiose errant, qui gloriam, quae vni Christo debetur, in Diuos partiuntur, & non solum seipsos salute, quae in hoc nobis offertur, spoliant, verum etiam sibi ipsis impensarum & laborum inutilium authores sunt. Quia vero Christus hic sola fide apprehenditur, hinc dogma illud suū duce Spiritu sancto Apostoli deriuarunt, hominem sola fide iustificari et seruari; in quo vniuersa vtriusq; testamenti scriptura consentit. Indignantur propter hoc nobis hodie aduersarij: at qui nos sumus, qui vel Christo suum in regno patris sui ius eripiamus, vel nouam salutis in ipso consequendae rationem ex nobis fingamus? Discant potius omnes Dei bonitatem agnoscere, qui Filium suum vnigenitum propter nos hominem & legi obnoxium fieri voluit, & hunc fide constanti amplectamur, vt salutis per illius meritum acquisitae participes efficiamur. Illi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum, Amen.
units.tr: to acknowledge him as Saviour, unless we acknowledge that he alone is Saviour; and this is the other main head of this knowledge. And this is that point about which there is everywhere dispute today. For most men confess that the Son of God, who was born a man of the virgin Mary, is Saviour; yet nearly the same people are not content with him alone, but join to him the divine men and women of heaven, to whom they make vows in dangers, and in whom they place their chief confidence of salvation. We must therefore always remember what he proclaims through Isaiah: "I am the Lord, this is my name, and I will not give my glory to another." Likewise what he says to the Samaritan woman: "Whoever drinks of this water" (of the elemental water, namely, under whose type he understands all other means of salvation) "will thirst again; but whoever drinks of the water which I shall give will not thirst for ever." The apostles observed these things carefully, who preached Christ in such a way that they ascribed to him alone all the glory of human salvation. For this is the common voice of them all, which they declared in the Council at Jerusalem: "There is no salvation in any other; for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved." Paul indeed, although he had been caught up to the third heaven and had heard many unspeakable things, nevertheless did not hesitate to testify publicly that he knew nothing other than Jesus Christ, crucified for us. Therefore those who divide among the saints the glory that is owed to Christ alone are shamefully and ruinously mistaken, and not only despoil themselves of the salvation offered to us in him, but also become the authors of useless expenses and labours for themselves. And because Christ is here apprehended by faith alone, the apostles, led by the Holy Spirit, derived from this the doctrine that man is justified and saved by faith alone; in this all the scripture of both Testaments agrees. Our adversaries are indignant at this today; but who are we, that we should either snatch from Christ his right in his Father's kingdom, or invent for ourselves a new way of obtaining salvation in him? Rather let all learn to acknowledge the goodness of God, who willed that his only-begotten Son should become man and subject to the law for our sake, and let us embrace him with a steadfast faith, that we may be made partakers of the salvation acquired through his merit. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever, Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA XX.
units.tr: Homily 20.

units.la: Et cum impleti fuissent dies purgationis eorum secundum Legem Mosis, adduxerunt eū Hierosolymam, vt sisterent eum Domino (prout scriptum est in Lege Domini. Omnis masculus, qui aperit vterum, sanctus Domino vocabitur) & vt darent oblationem, secundum id quod dictum est in Lege Domini, par turturum, aut duos pullos columbarum.
units.tr: And when the days of their purification according to the Law of Moses were fulfilled, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord (as it is written in the Law of the Lord: Every male that opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord), and to offer a sacrifice, according to what is said in the Law of the Lord, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.

units.la: Quoniam Deus Filium suum aeternum & vnigenitum aeterno suo consilio praedestinauit, vt humani generis vindex esset, eundem nobis similem fieri, & nostram conditionem in sereci-pere necesse fuit, vt ita nostram causam suscipiendi & nos vindicandi ius obtineret. Ideo Legi obnoxium fieri oportebat, vt nos qui huius maledictioni obnoxij eramus, liberaret. Et ad hoc illi Circumcisionem in primis seruiuisse, nuper diximus. Quia tamen hoc ad probandum salutis nostrae certitudinem in primis faciebat, non solum circuncidi voluit, verumetiā alia in se recepit, quae in Lege praescribuntur, ne quid obedientiae, quàm nostrum omnium nomine praestare debebat, deesset. Itaq; in praesenti de duobus agit Lucas, quibus sese ex legis praescripto subiecit, quorum vtrunq; multa continet cognitu & obseruatu necessaria, & ideo locum istum propius inspexisse, non inutile fuerit. Et quia vtrunq; Lucas ita connectit, vt ad primum postea demum redeat, cum secundum absoluit, nos perspicuitatis ergo de singulis seorsim dicemus.
units.tr: Since God, by his eternal counsel, predestined his eternal and only-begotten Son to be the avenger of the human race, it was necessary that he should become like us and take on our condition, so that he might thereby obtain the right to take up our cause and vindicate us. For this reason he had to be made subject to the Law, so that he might free us, who were bound over to its curse. We have lately said that his circumcision served this purpose in the first place. But since this chiefly served to confirm the certainty of our salvation, he willed not only to be circumcised but also to undertake the other things prescribed in the Law, so that nothing of the obedience he owed in the name of us all should be lacking. Accordingly, in the present passage Luke speaks of two things by which he submitted himself to the prescription of the Law. Each of them contains much that is necessary to know and to observe, so it will not be unprofitable to look more closely at this passage. And because Luke connects the two in such a way that he returns to the first only after completing the second, we will, for the sake of clarity, speak of each separately.

units.la: Ad primum pertinent haec verba: Et cum impleti fuissent dies purgationis eorum secundum le gem Mosis, adduxerunt eum Hierosolymam, vt darent oblationem secundum id quod dictum est in lege Domini, par turturum, aut duos pullos collumbarum. Agitur ergo hic de purificatione aut pur gatione, qua puerperae secundum Legem expiabantur, priusquam ad hominū consuetudinem & Ec clesiae atq; sacrorum societatem admitterentur. Extat Lex ista in libro Leuitici ad hunc modū: Mu lier, si suscepto semine conceperit, & pepererit masculū, immunda erit septem diebus, secundum dies separationis morbi sui immunda erit. Porro die octauo circuncidetur caro praeputij eius, masculi sci licet. Ipsa autem triginta tribus diebus sedebit in sanguine purificationis: nullam rem sacra tanger, & ad sanctuarium non veniet, donec completi fuerint dies purificationis suæ. Quòd si fœmina peperit, immunda erit duabus hebdomadibus secundum separationem suam, & sexaginta sex diebus sedebit in sanguine purificationis suæ. Postquam autem impleti fuerint dies purificationis suæ, pro filio aut pro filia, afferet agnum anniculum in holocaustum, et pullum columbæ aut turturem in oblationem pro peccato ad ostium tabernaculi ecclesiæ, ad sacerdotem. Et offeret ipsum coram Domino, & mundabitur à vena sanguinis sui. Hæc est Lex parientis masculum vel fœminam. Quòd si non invenerit manus eius, ut possit offerre agnum, tunc accipiet duos turtures, aut duos pullos columbarum, unum in holocaustum, et alterum in oblationem pro peccato, expiabitq; eam sacerdos, & mundabitur. Istis si Lucæ narrationem conferamus, Mariam diligenter præstitisse patebit, quod Lex Domini requirebat. Est autem nobis diligenter versandum in huius facti consideratione, eò quòd illo Satan insidiose nimis abusus est ad invehendum errores turpissimos et omnis generis superstitiones, quibus vera Christi & salutis nostræ ratio obscuratur. Nam primò coniugij dignitatem hoc argumento oppugnavit, ut multi huius vsum per se immundum & illicitum putarent, quum mulierem à partu pro immunda censeri, et proinde singulari purgatione opus habere audirent. Quam sententiam olim secuti sunt Manichæi, Adamiani, Hierarchitæ, & qui veteribus Apostolici dicti sunt. Et hodie non multùm ab illis differunt Papistæ, qui coniugij vsu interdicunt Ecclesiæ ministris quòd in carne eos viuere sentiant, qui illo vtuntur. At vehementer illos errare ex eo apparet, quòd scriptura coniugij authore facit Deum, & eadem thorum coniugale sanctum & impollutum esse docet, nimirum quòd libidinis affectus, plerunq; vitiosus, propter Dei institutum non imputetur. Quæ igitur ratio fuerit, aliquem eo pollui & inquinari, quod per se sanctum & impollutum est? Impuri potius et prophani, imò dæmoniorum ministri (vt Paulus monet) censeri debent, qui coniugij vsum non minus necessarium quàm sanctum inter res prophanas numerare audent. At non hunc solum errorem Satan inuexit, sed vt simul Dei quoq; cultum corrumperet, festum diem indixit, quo facti huius memoriam aliqui conseruare voluerunt, reuera autem superstitionibus ineptissimis omne, quod hic consideradum venit, mysterium obscurarunt. Nam nulla prorsus eius mentione facta, ad templum omnes concursant, & eò candelas cereas deferunt, quas vbi sacrificulus consecrauit accendunt, & ex earum fulgore sibi omnia fausta pollicentur. Imò ijsdem in posterum quoq; vim quandam diuinam inesse credunt ad sedandum tempestates & arcendum dæmones & cuiuscunq; generis spectra. Ea de nig tunt in templis rerum facies cernitur, vt Cereris potius sacra quàm Iesu Christi memoriam celebrari merito putes. Et quasi non satis esset simul omnes publicè insanire, priuatim ad puerperas superstitio peruasit. Has enim à dæmonibus & impuris spiritibus infestari, & tantumnon in diaboli potestate esse dixerunt. Itaq; varias commenti sunt expiationes, quibus primò quidem domi veteretur, postea verò in publicis etiā sacris priuinæ libertati restituerentur. Sunt hæc omnia à religionis Christianæ puritate alienissima, & miseris mulierculis consolatione illam dulcissimam abstulerunt, qua Paulus illas confirmat, quando eas per liberorum generationem seruari ait, si in fide & charitate, in sanctificatione item cum modestia perseuerent. Quia ergo superstitiones istæ & errores ex κακοζηλεία emerserunt, quando huius exempli ratio minus obseruata est, necesse omnino fuerit diligentius inspicere, quid sibi ista Lege de purgandis puerperis Deus voluerit, & cur Maria quoque eidem sese cum suo filio, Christo Iesu, subiecerit.
units.tr: To the first belong these words: "And when the days of their purification according to the law of Moses were fulfilled, they brought him to Jerusalem to offer a sacrifice according to what is said in the law of the Lord, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons." This passage therefore deals with the purification, or cleansing, by which women after childbirth were atoned for according to the Law, before they were admitted again to the company of men, to the Church and to the sacred things. That Law stands in the book of Leviticus in this form: "If a woman conceive seed and bear a male child, she shall be unclean seven days; according to the days of her separation for her infirmity she shall be unclean. And on the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised. But she shall continue in the blood of her purifying thirty-three days; she shall touch no hallowed thing, nor come into the sanctuary, until the days of her purification are fulfilled. But if she bear a female child, she shall be unclean two weeks, according to her separation, and she shall continue in the blood of her purifying sixty-six days. And when the days of her purification are fulfilled, for a son or for a daughter she shall bring a lamb of the first year for a burnt offering, and a young pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering, to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, to the priest. And he shall offer it before the Lord, and she shall be cleansed from the issue of her blood. This is the Law for her who bears a male or a female. But if she cannot afford a lamb, then she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering; and the priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean." If we compare Luke's narrative with this, it will be evident that Mary carefully performed what the Law of the Lord required. We must, however, dwell carefully on the consideration of this fact, because Satan has craftily abused it to introduce most shameful errors and superstitions of every kind, by which the true doctrine of Christ and of our salvation is obscured. For first he attacked the dignity of marriage with this argument, so that many thought its use in itself unclean and unlawful, since they heard that a woman after childbirth is counted unclean and therefore needs a special purification. The Manichaeans, the Adamites, the Hierarchites and those called Apostolici of old followed this opinion. And today the Papists do not differ much from them, who forbid the ministers of the Church the use of marriage, because they judge that those who use it live in the flesh. But that they err greatly is clear from this: Scripture makes God the author of marriage, and the same Scripture teaches that the marriage bed is holy and undefiled, since the affection of lust, which is commonly sinful, is not imputed on account of God's institution. What reason, then, is there for anyone to be polluted and defiled by that which is holy and undefiled in itself? Rather, those who dare to count the use of marriage, no less necessary than holy, among profane things ought to be judged impure and profane, indeed ministers of demons (as Paul warns). But Satan did not introduce this error alone; in order also to corrupt the worship of God at the same time, he appointed a festival day, on which some wished to keep the memory of this event, but in fact by most absurd superstitions they obscured every mystery that is to be considered here. For, with no mention made of it at all, everyone runs together to the temple and carries thither wax candles, which they light once the little sacrificer has consecrated them, and from their brightness they promise themselves every blessing. Indeed, they believe that a certain divine power resides in them even afterwards, to calm storms and to ward off demons and spectres of every kind. In the temples a face of things is seen on these days such that you might rightly think the rites of Ceres are being celebrated rather than the memory of Jesus Christ. And as if it were not enough for all to go mad together in public, superstition also crept into private life with regard to women in childbed. For they said that these women are harassed by demons and unclean spirits and are almost in the power of the devil. Therefore they devised various expiations, which were at first practised at home, and afterwards were restored to the women even in public sacred rites, so that they might be admitted again to the privileges of the Church. All these things are most alien to the purity of the Christian religion, and they have taken from the wretched women that most sweet consolation by which Paul comforts them, when he says that they are saved through the bearing of children, if they persevere in faith and charity, and in sanctification with modesty. Since, therefore, these superstitions and errors have arisen from misdirected zeal [κακοζηλεία], when the reason for this example was little observed, it is altogether necessary to examine more carefully what God meant by this Law concerning the purification of women in childbed, and why Mary also submitted herself to the same, together with her son Jesus Christ.

units.la: Quoad Legem & ritum illum sub Mosaico cultu obseruatum, primò miserabilis & omnibus mortalis corrupta hominum conditio adumbratur, quòd nimirum omnes, qui ex Adamo descendunt, in peccatis concipi & nasci soleant, & proinde natura peccatores atq; propter peccatum morti obnoxij sint, quibus expiatione et purgatione opus sit. Sufficit ergo hæc vnica ceremonia omnib.ijs confutandis, qui originale peccatum vel omnino negant, vel extenuat. Si enim mulierem, quæ concepto viri semine prolem peperit, peculiari purgatione oportuit expiari, negari non potest, et ipsam ex concepto illo atq; partu nouam immunditiem sibi contraxisse, & infantem ex ipso matris vtero pollutum & infectu prodire. Vnde verò ista immundities? Num ex coniugio & eius legitimo vsu? Nequaquam. Quia enim illud (vt supra diximus) sanctum, & thorus coniugū ex Dei institutione impollutus est, nemo illis potest inquinari. Ergo immunditiei causa est, quòd ex eius semine fœtus ille concipiatur, qui natura peccator et proprius prauitatis illius hæres est, quam ex Adamo in omnem posteritatem deriuari deriuari constat. Vnde apparet originale pecccatum non solùm alienæ trasgressionis imputationem esse, qua nos immerentes grauemur; sed naturæ vitiositatem, quæ nobis ipsi ex utero matris insita est, & cuius vis sit tanta, ut ipsum quoque coniugij vsum, per se sanctum & concessum, inficiat. At quid de coniugio dico, quando ipsam Dei Legem, qua nihil sanctius, iustius & melius excogitari potest, nobis noxiam reddit? Nam peccatum (inquit Paulus, de originali illo loquens) per præceptum occasione sumpta, genuit in me omnem concupiscentiam, imò decepit me & per præceptum illud occidit. Quia enim in vetitum nitimur natura, præceptis diuinæ Legis cupiditates prauæ irritantur, ut ardentiores fiant, nosq; ad illicita fortius abripiant. Quod cum pauci in semetipsis obseruent, non verbis solùm nos de hac nostræ naturæ depravatione admoneri, sed eandem aliqua ceremonia visibili ob oculos poni oportuit, ut conditionis nostræ memores humiliemur in Dei conspectu, omnes autem carnis nostræ cogitationes & consilia suspecta habeamus, et illi coercendæ sedulò incumbamus. Et hic primus purgationis istius, qua puerperas expiari olim oportebat, usus fuit.
units.tr: As to the Law and that rite observed under the Mosaic worship, first there is shadowed forth the wretched condition of man, corrupted and common to all mortals: namely, that all who are descended from Adam are wont to be conceived and born in sins, and therefore are by nature sinners and, because of sin, subject to death, and so need atonement and purification. This single ceremony is therefore enough to refute all those who either altogether deny original sin or diminish it. For if a woman who, after the seed of a man has been conceived, has brought forth offspring had to be atoned for by a special purification, it cannot be denied that she herself has contracted a new uncleanness from that conception and childbirth, and that the infant comes forth from the very womb of the mother polluted and infected. But whence comes this uncleanness? From marriage and its lawful use? By no means. For since that (as we said above) is holy, and the marriage bed is undefiled by God's institution, no one can be defiled by it. Therefore the cause of the uncleanness is that from her seed that offspring is conceived which is by nature a sinner and the heir of that depravity which is derived from Adam into all posterity is established. Hence it appears that original sin is not only the imputation of another's transgression, by which we, though undeserving, are burdened; but also the vitiousness of nature, which is implanted in us from our mother's womb, and whose force is so great that it taints even the use of marriage itself, which is in itself holy and permitted. But why do I speak of marriage, when the very Law of God, than which nothing holier, more just and better can be devised, makes it harmful to us? For sin (says Paul, speaking of that original sin) "taking occasion by the commandment, produced in me all concupiscence; indeed it deceived me and through that commandment slew me." For since we by nature strive after what is forbidden, the depraved desires are provoked by the precepts of the divine Law, so that they become more ardent and drag us more strongly into unlawful things. Since few observe this in themselves, it was necessary not only that we be admonished of this depravity of our nature in words, but that the same be set before our eyes by some visible ceremony, so that, mindful of our condition, we might humble ourselves in the sight of God, and hold all the thoughts and counsels of our flesh under suspicion, and apply ourselves diligently to restraining them. And this was the first use of that purification by which women in childbed were formerly bound to be cleansed.

units.la: Deinde ut in aliis fere sacrificijs fieri consueuerat, ita hic quoque una cum morbo remedium simul monstrabatur. Quia enim puerpera agnum annieulum in holocaustum, & pullum columbæ in oblationem pro peccato adducere iubetur, non obscurè eam Spiritus sanctus ad Christum remittebat, quem agnus illis & omnibus fere sacrificijs legalibus olim figuratū fuisse satis constat, & vel Ioannis testimonio abundè probatur, qui digito in Christum extenso dixit: Ecce agnus ille Dei, qui tollit peccatum mundi. Mundi peccatum dicit, ut omnia comprehendat, quæ sub peccati censum veniunt, inter quæ innatam & hereditariam naturæ nostræ prauitatem primo quasi loco numerare oportet, cum ex ea reliquæ iniquitates omnes protuberent. At hanc quoq; per Christum emundari, ne nobis porrò imputetur aut noceat, Zacharias diserte docet, quando de eius morte & piorum ad hunc conuersione vaticinatus mox subijcit: In die illo aperietur fons, sive scaturigo perennis, domui Dauid & habitatoribus Hierosolymæ ad peccatum & ad menstruam immunditiem. Vocat autem immunditiem menstruam, hereditariam illam vitiositatem, quæ per illam proprissimè adumbratur, cùm nobis cognata & naturalis sit, & in nobis perdendis effectus habeat vehementissimos. Ad hunc ergo fontem remittebantur puerperæ, ut consolationem acciperent, quæ dolorem ex diutina separatione conceptum leniret, & se cum sua prole apud Deum in gratiam receptas esse certò sperare possent. Et huc Dauid etiam respexisse videtur, qui cum se in iniquitate conceptum & in peccato formatum esse conquestus esset, mox ad Deum clamat: Expia me hyssopo, & mundus ero: lava me, & nive ero candidior. Item: Libera me de sanguinibus Deus, Deus salutis meæ.
units.tr: Then, as was usual in most other sacrifices, the remedy was shown together with the disease. For since the woman who had given birth was commanded to bring a yearling lamb for a burnt offering, and a young pigeon or dove for a sin offering, the Holy Spirit not obscurely referred her to Christ, whom the lamb was surely a figure of in those sacrifices and in almost all the legal sacrifices. This is abundantly proved even by the testimony of John, who, pointing his finger at Christ, said: "Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world." He says "the sin of the world" so as to comprehend everything that comes under the category of sin, among which the innate and hereditary corruption of our nature must be counted first, as it were, since all the other iniquities sprout from it. But that this too is cleansed through Christ, so that it is no longer imputed to us or harms us, Zechariah plainly teaches, when, prophesying of his death and of the conversion of the godly to him, he immediately adds: "On that day a fountain shall be opened, or a perennial spring, to the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for sin and for menstrual uncleanness." He calls it menstrual uncleanness, that hereditary vice which is most fittingly foreshadowed by it, since it is kin to us and natural, and has most powerful effects in destroying us. So to this fountain the women who had given birth were directed, that they might receive a comfort which would ease the sorrow conceived from the long separation, and could confidently hope that they and their offspring were received into favour with God. David too seems to have had this in view, who, having complained that he was conceived in iniquity and formed in sin, straightaway cries out to God: "Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean; wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow." Likewise: "Deliver me from bloods, O God, God of my salvation."

units.la: Præterea cùm in ista purgatione columbæ aut turtures adhiberi iubarentur, simul officij sui ad monebantur mulieres. Scimus enim istas aues coniugio certo delectari & eius fidelissimas esse custodes, cùm neque cum alieno compare misceantur, & simul excludendis atq; educandis pullis mutuam operam sibi inuicem præbeant. Quæ causa est, quòd apud gentes quoque prophanas fidei coniugalis symbolum & typus semper fuerint. Voluit ergo hoc sacrificio Spiritus sanctus innuere, mulieres non omni ergo viros suos officio defunctas neque vinculo coniugij solutas esse, si semel aut iterum, imò quàm sæpissimè fieri potest, peperint: sed debere illas ad officium redire, fidem coniugibus inuiolatam seruare, liberos educare, domus suæ curam gerere, neque vllam subterfugere molestiam, quæ in istis rebus est subeunda. Turpe enim fuerit homines à brutis animantibus superari in ijs officijs, ad quæ per Legem naturæ astringimur. Hæc (inquam) sunt, quæ Deus veterem populum purgatione ista puerperarum docere voluit. Ea autem hodie minimè opus est, imò eam reducere nefas est, quando in Christi sanguine omnis veteris Testamenti sanguis sisti debuit, quod in illius morte facta veli sacri scissio aperte declarauit. Multò minus ergo audiantur, qui nouas expiationes fingunt, quibus (ut diximus) & coniugij dignitas euertitur, et fides mulierum tunc labefactatur, quando consolatione & confirmatione in primis opus est. Interim in eorum obseruatione diligentes sint Christianæ fœminæ, quæ ritu illo veteri fuerunt adumbrata. Agnoscant naturæ communis depravatione, & proinde nulla propriæ sanctitatis aut iustitiæ fiducia efferantur. Non desperent autem de gratia Dei, sed in Christo spem salutis firmam certamq; habeant, & eius merito se purgatas & ab omni immunditie expiatas tutum ad thronum gratiæ aditum habere credant. Ea autem spe plenæ ad officium redeant, & in seruanda fide coniugali diligentes, in domus administratione sedulae, in liberorum educatione patientes, & quoad totius vitae consuetudine modestiae, probae & sanctae sint. His studijs & Deo probabuntur, & ecclesiae eius membra se esse probabunt non poenitenda.
units.tr: Moreover, since in this purification doves or turtledoves were ordered to be used, the women were at the same time reminded of their duty. For we know that these birds delight in a fixed mate and are most faithful guardians of it, since they do not mix with another's partner, and in hatching and rearing their young they give each other mutual help. This is why, even among the profane nations, they have always been a symbol and type of faithfulness in marriage. The Holy Spirit therefore wished by this sacrifice to suggest that women who have given birth, once or twice (indeed as often as it can happen), have not thereby been discharged from all duty to their husbands nor released from the bond of marriage, but ought to return to their duty: keep faith inviolate with their spouses, bring up their children, take care of their household, and shun no trouble that must be undertaken in these matters. For it would be shameful for men to be surpassed by brute animals in those duties to which we are bound by the law of nature. These, I say, are the things which God wished to teach the old people by this purification of women. But today there is by no means any need of it; indeed it is wrong to revive it, since in the blood of Christ all the blood of the Old Testament ought to have been stopped, which the tearing of the sacred veil at his death clearly declared. Far less, therefore, should those be heard who invent new expiations, by which (as we have said) both the dignity of marriage is overturned and the faith of women is shaken at the very time when consolation and confirmation are above all needed. Meanwhile let Christian women, who were foreshadowed by that old rite, be diligent in observing these duties. Let them acknowledge the corruption common to our nature, and therefore not be puffed up with any confidence in their own holiness or righteousness. Yet let them not despair of the grace of God, but have a firm and certain hope of salvation in Christ, and believe that through his merit, having been purged and expiated from all uncleanness, they have a safe access to the throne of grace. Full of this hope, let them return to their duties: diligent in keeping conjugal faith, careful in managing the household, patient in bringing up children, and in the whole course of their lives modest, upright and holy. By these pursuits they will also be approved before God, and they will show themselves to be members of his Church, not to be ashamed of.

units.la: Accedamus nunc ad Mariae factum, quae & seipsam & filium suum ceremoniae isti subijcere voluit, neq; quo minus id faceret a spiritu prohibetur. Nam sive Mariam spectes, sive Christum ex ea natum, purificatione nequaquam opus fuisse videbis. Lex enim diserte de muliere loquitur, quae suscepto semine ex viri congressu concepit. Atqui illam ex Spiritu sancto concepisse audivimus, qui sua virtute eam obumbravit, ut illaesa virginitate sua mater fieret. Similiter Christus homo quidem natus erat, sed non in corrupta Adami imagine natus erat, neq; in eo locum habuit, quae nobiscum nascitur, naturae vitiositas, ideoq; Sanctus ille sanctorum verissime dicitur, in quo dolus nullus unquam inventus est. Poterat etiam facile obstare, ne quid huius Virgo mater faceret. Voluit autem id fieri, ut in hac quidem obedientiae exemplum nobis proponeret, cuius tantum apud nos studium esse debet, ut ne in licitis quidem nostrum ius cum aliorum scandalo pertinacius & rigidius persequamur: in seipso autem argumentum novum praebet, quo salutis nostrae fiducia magis confirmetur. Nam etsi ab omni peccati labe alienissimus sit; nobis tamen accenseri vult, neq; illum pudet nostrae corruptionis personam in totius mundi conspectu suscipere, & iam recens natum cum iniquis reputari, ut nos suo merito purget & nostram immunditiem expiet. Ideo Lucas diserte scripsit, Cum impleti fuissent dies purgationis eorum, Mariae scilicet & Christi. Nam etsi illa ceremonia ad solam matrem pertinere videretur, non obscure tamen de infantis quoq; immunditie testabatur, cuius indicium prius in Circumcisione extabat. Continet ergo haec Mariae purificatio eximiam consolationem, quando Christum ad nos pertinere docet, & eius merito nobis applicando, in eo finem illum nobis quasi digito monstrat, quem Deus aperuit, ut nos ab omni peccato & menstrua immunditie abluat, sicuti ex Zacharia nuper annotavimus. Hunc ergo opponamus satanae suggestionibus, quibus innatam immunditiem objicit ut nos ex regno Dei exclusos esse euincat. Quia enim illam in se transtulit Christus & eandem sui sanguinis merito expiavit, illa nobis porro imputari non potest. Interim in hoc uno nos acquiescere decet, neq; eos audire, qui nobis novas purificationes extra Christum fingunt. Fatigant illi hominum conscientias, et ipsis quoq; corporibus novos quotidie labores atq; molestias exhibent, nihil autem conferunt miseris, quando inutile, imo noxium & pernitiosum est, quic quid sine Christo instituitur.
units.tr: Let us now come to Mary's act, for she wished both herself and her son to submit to that ceremony, and the Spirit did not prohibit her from doing so. For whether you look at Mary or at Christ born of her, you will see that there was by no means any need of purification. The Law speaks plainly of a woman who, having received seed from union with a man, conceives. But we have heard that Mary conceived by the Holy Spirit, who overshadowed her by his power, so that she might become a mother with her virginity unharmed. Likewise Christ was indeed born a man, but he was not born in the corrupted image of Adam, and the vice of nature which is born with us had no place in him; therefore that Holy One of holies is most truly called one in whom no guile was ever found. The Virgin mother could also easily have prevented anything of this from happening. But he wished it to be done, so that in this he might set before us an example of obedience, of which we ought to have such zeal that we do not pursue our rights, even lawful ones, too stubbornly and rigidly to the scandal of others. In himself, however, he provides a new argument by which confidence in our salvation may be more firmly confirmed. For although he is most remote from every stain of sin, yet he wishes to be reckoned among us, and he is not ashamed to take upon himself, in the sight of the whole world, the person of our corruption, and to be counted among the unclean though newly born, so that by his merit he might cleanse us and expiate our uncleanness. Therefore Luke wrote plainly: "When the days of their purification were fulfilled," namely of Mary and of Christ. For although that ceremony seemed to pertain to the mother alone, nevertheless it bore witness not obscurely to the uncleanness of the infant too, the sign of which had earlier stood in circumcision. This purification of Mary therefore contains exceptional consolation, since it teaches that Christ belongs to us, and by applying his merit to us, it shows us, as it were with a finger, that end which God has opened so that he might wash us from all sin and menstrual uncleanness, as we lately noted from Zechariah. Let us therefore oppose this to the suggestions of Satan, by which he objects our innate uncleanness in order to prove that we are excluded from the kingdom of God. For since Christ has taken it upon himself and expiated it by the merit of his blood, it can no longer be imputed to us. Meanwhile it becomes us to rest in this one thing alone, and not to listen to those who invent new purifications apart from Christ. Such men wear out people's consciences and inflict on their very bodies new labours and troubles every day, yet they bring nothing to the wretched, since whatever is instituted without Christ is not only useless but harmful and pernicious.

units.la: Sed pergamus in historia, qua narratur quid in purificatione ista Virgo mater obtulerit. Nulla autem sit agni mentio, quem ditiores offerre iubebantur, sed pullorum columbae & turturum modo Lucas meminit, quos debebant ex Lege, quorum fortunae erant tenuiores, offerre. Erat aut hoc praeclarum bonitatis Dei argumentum, qui pauperum tam diligentem rationem habuit, ne propter egestatem a sacris communibus exclusi, ab Ecclesiae etiam & salutis communione se exclusos & reiectos putarent. Pertinent eodem praecepta, quibus graviter monet, ut in festis solennibus, quando publice epulabantur, pauperum & peregrinorum meminerint, & suas illis partes decidant, ut etiam hi communis illius & sanctae laetitiae consortes efficiantur. Quid, quod Christus tenuiora pauperum donaria maximis divitum muneribus praefert, ut in viduae exemplo apud Marcum docemur? Soletur hoc egenos omnes, et quoties propter tenuitatem suam se se tentari sentiunt, cogitent se in Baptismo & Coena mystica nihil minus, quam ditissimos Croesos accipere, et regni coelorum thesauros, quos per Evangelium nobis Deus offert, ad ipsos etiam pertinere, si quidem eos cum fide apprehendant. Rursus autem Christi paupertas nobis ob oculos statuitur. Qui enim Bethlehemi in misero tugurio natus & primas cunas in praesepi habuit, eius mater nunc in publico etiam sacro suam egestatem profitetur. Idem postea non habuit, quo caput suum reclinaret. Ubi nos meminisse oportet, id quoq; ad redemptionis nostrae causam pertinere. Debuit enim inter alias peccati poenas inopiam quoq; subire Dei filius, ut nobis ad opum coelestium possessionem aditum faceret. Simul autem egestatem (ut alibi diximus) suo exemplo consecrat, ne credentibus in ipsum porro peccati poena, sed salutare fidei & patientiae exercitium sit, in quo veras divitias inveniant. Nondum ergo Christu recte agnoverunt, quos adhuc inopiae pudet, & hanc extremum omnium malorum esse iudicant. Est haec maximorum scelerum causa: nam ut illam effugiant, ad dolos, impostauras, mendacia, furta, rapinas, caedes, periuria & quaevis alia flagitia se conferunt, & quos pudet cum Christo paupertatis onus suscipere, eos non pudet diabolo militare, vt iniquo Mammone abundent. Nemo tamen hoc exemplo mendicitatem doceri, aut monachorum hypocrisim stabiliri putet, qui dum voluntariam paupertatē profitentur, reuera ditissimi sunt, & rerum securi ex alieno viuunt. Pauper quidem Christus fuit sed mendicus oftiatim victum quaeritans non fuit, neque impudenter quosuis obuios compellauit. Sciebat enim istud diuina Lege prohiberi, neq; id immerito: quando constat mendicitatem bonis moribus inimicam esse, et eadem omnem disciplinam cum Ecclesiasticam tum politicam turbari. Paupertatem quoq; non ipse sibi accersiuit voto temerario aut hypocritico, sed patris vocationi paruit. Nihil ergo faciunt hypocritae illi, quam quod ex Christi exemplo sibi ludos fingunt, & huius gloriam in se transferunt, dum sibi vendicant quod illus merito debetur. Christianorum hominum est suam vocationem sequi, & in quouis vitae genere Deo seruire, fortunam quoq; omnē patienter ferre, vt cum Paulo quisq; dicere possit. Didici in quibus sum, ijs ipsis contentus esse: noui deprimi, noui abundare, vbique & in omnibus initiatus sum, & ad saturitatem & ad esuritionem, cum ad abundantiam tum ad inopiam. Itaque si diuitiae affluant, ne apponant illis cor, sed bonis operibus similiter abundent & beneficentiae studeant: si inopia premantur, patienter ferant & hanc & quae ei coniuncta sunt vitae incommoda.
units.tr: But let us go on with the narrative, which tells what the Virgin mother offered in this purification. No mention is made of a lamb, which the richer were ordered to offer; Luke mentions only young pigeons and turtledoves, which the Law required of those whose means were more slender. This was a remarkable proof of God's goodness, who took such careful account of the poor, lest, excluded from the common sacred rites by their poverty, they should think they were also excluded and rejected from the communion of the Church and of salvation. To the same end pertain the precepts by which he earnestly admonishes that at solemn feasts, when they feasted publicly, they should remember the poor and strangers and set aside portions for them, so that these too might become sharers in that common and holy joy. And what of the fact that Christ prefers the smaller gifts of the poor to the greatest gifts of the rich, as we are taught in the example of the widow in Mark? Let all the needy take comfort from this, and whenever they feel tempted because of their meagreness, let them consider that in Baptism and the mystical Supper they receive nothing less than the richest Croesuses, and that the treasures of the kingdom of heaven, which God offers us through the Gospel, belong to them too, provided they lay hold of them with faith. Again, the poverty of Christ is set before our eyes. He who was born at Bethlehem in a wretched hut and had his first cradle in a manger, his mother now professes her poverty even in public sacred rite. Afterwards he had nowhere to lay his head. Here we ought to remember that this too pertains to the cause of our redemption. For the Son of God was bound to undergo poverty, among the other penalties of sin, so that he might make for us an entrance to the possession of heavenly riches. At the same time he consecrates poverty by his example (as we have said elsewhere), so that for those who believe in him it may no longer be the penalty of sin, but a salutary exercise of faith and patience, in which they may find true riches. Those, then, have not rightly recognised Christ who are still ashamed of want and judge it the worst of all evils. This is the cause of very great crimes: to escape it, they betake themselves to trickery, deceit, lies, thefts, robberies, murders, perjuries and any other shameful deeds. Those who are ashamed to bear the burden of poverty with Christ are not ashamed to serve the devil, so that they may abound with unrighteous Mammon. Yet let no one think that this example teaches begging, or that it confirms the hypocrisy of monks, who, while they profess voluntary poverty, are in truth very rich and live free of care at another's expense. Christ indeed was poor, but he was not a beggar seeking his food from door to door, nor did he shamelessly accost whoever came in his way. For he knew that this was forbidden by the divine Law, and not without reason: since begging is known to be hostile to good morals, and by it both ecclesiastical and civil order are thrown into confusion. Nor did he bring poverty on himself by a rash or hypocritical vow, but obeyed his Father's calling. Those hypocrites, therefore, do nothing but, following Christ's example, invent games for themselves and transfer to themselves his glory, while they claim for themselves what is due to his merit alone. It is the duty of Christians to follow their calling, to serve God in whatever kind of life they have, and to bear patiently every lot, so that each may say with Paul: "I have learned, in whatever state I am, to be content. I know how to be brought low, and I know how to abound; everywhere and in all things I am initiated, both to being full and to being hungry, both to abundance and to want. So if riches flow in, let them not set their heart on them, but likewise let them abound in good works and be zealous in beneficence; if they are pressed by want, let them bear patiently both this and the discomforts of life joined to it."

units.la: Videamus nunc alterum, quod Maria & Iosephi in praesenti fecere. Adduxerunt Iesum Hierosolymam, vt sisterent eum Domino. Et vt hoc quoq; ex Legis praescripto factu esse constaret, addit Lucas: Prout scriptum est in Lege Domini, Omnis masculus, qui aperit vterum, sanctus Domino vocabitur. Obseruandum est autem in ista commemoratione tertio Legu diuinae mentionem fieri, qua diligentia, superflua quodammodo Spiritus sanctus Lucae vti voluit, vt satis exprimeret, Mariam, etsi tunc humanae traditiones regnarent, omnia tamen secundum Lege Dei fecisse. Est igitur hoc praeclarum argumentum pietatis & sanctae obedientiae, quam praestare debent quam diligentissime qui cultum suum Deo probari volunt. Neq; enim nobis licet vel Deum vel cultum eius ex nostro arbitrio fingere. Et notū est illud dictum: Frustra me colunt docentes doctrinas hominum. Porro Lex, quā in praesenti Euangelista adducit, apud Mosem habetur. Na Exod.13. Cap. ait Dominus: Consecra mihi omne primogenitū, apertionem scilicet omnis vteri (id est omne quod primū nascitur, & nascendo vterū aperit) in filijs Israel, tam in homine quā in iumento. Et in li. Num. praecepti huius causam exprimit, dicens: Meū est omne primogenitū filiorū Israel, tam in hominibus quā in iumentis, à die quo percussi omne primogenitū in terra Aegypti, consecraui eos mihi. Iure ergo sibi vendicabat Deus illos, quos peculiari beneficio vnā cū tota gente seruauerat. Quia vero loco primogenitorum omnium, qui in duodecim tribubus Israelis nascebantur inter homines, Leuitas omnes sibi selegerat, alteri illi sistebantur quidē Domino, sed redimebantur simul certo numerato pretio, quinq; nimirum siclis sanctuarij, qui sacerdotibus cedebant. Erat ergo huius quoq; ceremoniae vsus non contemnendus. Nam in mentem reuocabat beneficium, olim patribus in Aegypto exhibitum, quod simul vniuersum nostrae redemptionis mysterium adumbrabat. Constat enim omnes nos sub Angelo vastatore periclitatos fuisse, imo periturus fuisse quoad corpus & animam, nisi Christus pascha nostrum (vt Paulus ait) pro nobis immolatus esset, & sui sanguinis pretio diabolum à nobis profligasset. Itaque quoties primogenitos suos Domino sistebant, toties & veteris beneficij admonebantur, & in fidere demptionis futurae confirmabantur. Adhaec officij sui illos Deus admonebat, vt nimirum pretiosissima quaeque sibi consecrarent, & quidem liberos in primis. Etsi enim non omnes ad sacerdotium admitterentur, omnes tamen in veri Dei cognitione instituti debebant, vt huic seruire possent in ea vocatione, ad quam postea destinabantur. Debent huc referri, quaecunq; de liberorum educatione & institutione tradit Dominus, qualia sunt quae Exod.13. Deut. 6. Psalm.78. leguntur. Vt ergo Maria huic Legi de sistendis Deo primogenitis pie & recte obtemperat: ita quamuis illius ceremonia externa cum reliquis in Christo abolita sit, manet tamen praeceptum, quo hodie etiam astringimur, vt ex nobis natos Deo consecremus, qui illos dedit. Etenim frustra Dei amore & veri cultus studium profitentur, qui non curant qua possunt diligentia, vt illius cognitio atq; cultus apud posteros quoq; conseruetur. Fuerunt in hoc feruentes admodum, quotquot verae pietatis nomine in scripturis commendantur, & hoc ipsum in Abrahamo Deus potissimum praedicat. Num celabo Abrahamum (inquit) quae ego facturus sum? Scio quod mandaturus sit filijs suis & domui suae post se, vt cuflodiant viam Domini, & c. Sed o infelicem parentum nostri seculi incuriam, quam cum deplorare facilius fit quam emendare, nihil quam Cyclopicum omnis religionis contemptum breui oriturum spe rare possumus, quem infelix omnium rerum euersio tandem sequetur.
units.tr: Let us now consider the second thing that Mary and Joseph did at this time. They brought Jesus to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord. And so that it might be established that this too was done according to the prescription of the Law, Luke adds: "As it is written in the Law of the Lord, Every male that opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord." In this account it must be observed that mention is made of the divine Law three times. The Holy Spirit wished to use this care, which might seem superfluous in a way, so that Luke might clearly express that Mary, although human traditions then held sway, nevertheless did everything according to the Law of God. This is therefore an excellent proof of piety and holy obedience, which those must render most diligently who wish their worship to be approved by God. For it is not permitted to us to devise God, or his worship, by our own judgment. And that saying is well known: "In vain do they worship me, teaching the doctrines of men." Moreover, the Law which the Evangelist here cites is found in Moses. For in Exodus 13 the Lord says: "Consecrate to me every firstborn, that is, every opening of the womb (that is, everything which is born first and by being born opens the womb) among the sons of Israel, both in man and in beast." And in the book of Numbers he states the reason for this command, saying: "The firstborn of the sons of Israel, both among men and among beasts, is mine, from the day on which I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt; I have consecrated them to myself." God therefore rightly claimed for himself those whom he had preserved with the whole nation by a special benefit. But because, in place of all the firstborn who were born among men in the twelve tribes of Israel, he had chosen for himself all the Levites, those others were indeed presented to the Lord, but were at the same time redeemed by a fixed sum of money paid, namely five shekels of the sanctuary, which went to the priests. Therefore the practice of this ceremony was also not to be despised. For it recalled to mind the benefit once shown to the fathers in Egypt, and at the same time it foreshadowed the whole mystery of our redemption. For it is certain that we all were in danger under the destroying Angel, and indeed would have perished in body and soul, unless Christ, our Passover (as Paul says), had been sacrificed for us and had by the price of his blood driven the devil away from us. Thus, as often as they presented their firstborn to the Lord, so often were they reminded of the ancient benefit and confirmed in faith in the future deliverance. Moreover, God was reminding them of their duty, namely that they should consecrate to him the most precious things they had, and indeed their children above all. For although not all were admitted to the priesthood, yet all ought to be instructed in the knowledge of the true God, so that they might be able to serve him in that calling to which they were afterwards destined. To this belong whatever the Lord teaches about the upbringing and instruction of children, such as what is read in Exodus 13, Deuteronomy 6, and Psalm 78. Therefore, just as Mary piously and rightly obeyed this Law concerning presenting the firstborn to God, so, although its external ceremony has been abolished in Christ along with the rest, the command still remains, by which we too are bound today to consecrate to God those born of us, since he has given them. For those profess in vain the love of God and zeal for true worship who do not take care, with what diligence they can, that the knowledge and worship of him are preserved among their posterity also. All who are commended in the Scriptures for true piety were very fervent in this, and God especially praises this very thing in Abraham: "Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do? I know that he will command his sons and his house after him to keep the way of the Lord," and so on. But alas for the carelessness of our age's parents, which is easier to deplore than to correct; we can hope for nothing but a Cyclopean contempt of all religion soon to arise, which an unhappy overthrow of all things will at last follow.

units.la: Porro facit hæc quoque Ceremonia ad commendandam Iesu Christi dignitatem. Sic enim rur sus indicatur, hunc esse verum illum primogenitum inter multos fratres (vt Paulus loquitur) cui soli regnum & sacerdotium inter Dei filios debeatur. Istum ergo omnes audire & obseruare debent, quotquot in numero filiorum Dei & horum Ecclesia censeri volunt. Excitet nos hic, quòd ita primogenitus Mariæ virginis factus est, vt simul omnium in se credentium natales sanctificarit, & nobis omnibus primogenituræ dignitatem meruerit. Ideo enim hic Patri sistitur, & postea eidem in ara crucis offertur, vt in seipso nos omnes sanctificet: vt nimirum Reges & sacerdotes simus Dei altissimi, qui & nostipsos huic viuentem hostiam sistimus, & mundo atque principe eius superiores factı in illo triumphamus. Et hæc quidem huius loci historia nobis consideranda proponit, quæ primo intuitu nihil præter Iudaicos & iampridem abolitos ritus continere videbatur. Agnoscamus igitur profunditatem diuinæ sapientiæ & scientiæ, quæ nobis in Christo Iesu proponitur, & huic vni si damus atq; seruiamus fide constanti & charitate non fucata. Illi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: Moreover, this ceremony also serves to commend the dignity of Jesus Christ. For it is again shown that he is the true firstborn among many brothers (as Paul speaks), to whom alone the kingdom and priesthood among the sons of God is due. Therefore all who wish to be counted among the number of God's sons and of his Church ought to hear and obey him. Let it stir us that he was made the firstborn of the virgin Mary in such a way that at the same time he sanctified the birth of all who believe in him, and has merited for us all the dignity of the firstborn. For this reason he is presented here to the Father, and afterwards is offered to the same on the altar of the cross, so that he may sanctify us all in himself: namely that we may be kings and priests of the most high God, who both present ourselves to him as a living sacrifice, and, made superior to the world and its prince, triumph in him. And these things indeed the history of this place sets before us for consideration, which at first sight seemed to contain nothing but Jewish rites, long since abolished. Let us therefore acknowledge the depth of the divine wisdom and knowledge, which is set before us in Jesus Christ, and let us give ourselves to this one alone and serve him with constant faith and unfeigned love. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA XXI.
units.tr: HOMILY XXI.

units.la: Et ecce quidam erat in Hierusalem, cui nomen Simeon: eratq; homo ille iustus & religiosus, expectans consolationem Israelis: & spiritus sanctus erat super eum: fueratq; ipsi diuinitus nuntiatum à spiritu sancto, ipsum non visurum mortem, priusquam vidisset Christum il lum Domini. Is venit duce spiritu in templum: & cum introducerent puerulum Iesum parentes, vt secundum Legis consuetudinem de illo facerent, tunc ipse accepit eum in vlnas suas, & benedixit Deo, ac dixit: Nunc dimittis seruum tuum Domine, secundum verbum tuum, in pace. Quia viderunt oculi mei salutem tuam, quam parasti in conspectu omnium populorum; lumen ad revelationem gentium, & gloriam populi tui Israelis.
units.tr: And behold, there was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon. He was a just and devout man, waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him. It had been divinely revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord's Christ. Guided by the Spirit, he came into the temple. When the parents brought in the little child Jesus, to do for him according to the custom of the Law, Simeon took him up in his arms, blessed God, and said: "Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word. For mine eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all peoples: a light to lighten the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel."

units.la: VT Lucas euangelista incarnationem & natiuitatem filij Dei, cum omnibus quæ in hac accideruntDiligenter descripsit: ita non minori studio narrat, vt idem ille mundo manifestatus sit, & quod nō defuerint, qui illum recens ex Virgine natum agnouerint pro Messia & promisso humani generis redemptore. Fuerunt hic primi pastores, quibus Angeli rem omnem denuntiarunt. His proximi successerunt Magi Orientales, quos stella duce in Iudæam ad quærendū Christum ve nisse Matthæus scribit. Sequuntur nunc ex Hierosolymitanis ciuibus senex Simeon & Anna vi dua, qui illū in templo, cum secundum Legem Domino sisteretur, ex peculiari spiritus afflatu agno uere, & eidem testimonium dederunt publicum. Vbi ante omnia obseruari debet, non defuisse in Iu daeorum gente corruptissima reliquias piorum, quos Deus ex peculiari gratia illo tempore seruauit, vt Ecclesiæ suæ seminarium essent. Extant de his non pauca prophetarū veterū vaticinia, quibus hic sua fides astruitur. Simul autē obseruabis, illos vere fuisse homines obscuros & nullius apud mundū authoritatis. Seruiunt ista non parum consolationi nostræ, ne de ecclesiæ instauratione desperemus, si quando res ad extremum deuenisse videtur. Nouit enim suos Dominus, & eos in medio luporum, quantumuis pauculos seruare potest. Docent item exempla ista, fidem & religionem nequaquam ex hominum splendore æstimari debere. Solet enim humiles & qui mundi iudicio pro stultis habentur, deligere Deus, vt mundi fastum atq; sapientiam confundat, et constet regnum Christi non terre num esse, & proinde in illo cœlestı solum & æterna bona quæri debere. Cæterum in præsenti Simeo nis historia narratur, quæ multa cōtinet obseruatu dignissima. Docet enim, quales esse coueniat, qui salutis in Christo exhibitæ participes fieri cupiunt; quis item ille sit, quidq; ex illo nos sperare liceat.
units.tr: Luke the evangelist described with great care the incarnation and birth of the Son of God, with everything that happened in these matters. With no less diligence he relates that this same Son was made manifest to the world, and that there were not lacking those who recognised him, newly born of the Virgin, as the Messiah and the promised Redeemer of mankind. First came the shepherds, to whom the angels announced the whole matter. Close after them came the Eastern Magi, who, as Matthew writes, came into Judea led by a star to seek Christ. Now follow, from among the citizens of Jerusalem, the old man Simeon and the widow Anna. When the child was presented to the Lord in the temple according to the Law, they recognised him by a special inspiration of the Spirit and gave public testimony to him. Here it must be observed above all that in the Jewish nation, though it was very corrupt, there were not lacking remnants of the godly, whom God in that age preserved by special grace, so that they might be a seed-bed for his Church. Many ancient prophecies concerning these people exist, by which their faith is confirmed here. At the same time you will observe that they were truly obscure men, of no authority in the world. These things serve not a little to console us, so that we do not despair of the restoration of the Church whenever affairs seem to have come to an extremity. For the Lord knows his own, and can preserve even a very few of them in the midst of wolves. These examples also teach that faith and religion must by no means be judged by the splendour of men. God is wont to choose the humble, and those whom the judgement of the world holds to be fools, so that he may confound the pride and wisdom of the world, and so that it may be plain that the kingdom of Christ is not earthly, and that therefore in it alone heavenly and eternal goods are to be sought. But in the present case the history of Simeon is related, which contains many things most worthy of notice. For it teaches what kind of people those ought to be who desire to share in the salvation exhibited in Christ. It also shows who he is, and what we may hope for from him.

units.la: Commodùm verù à personæ descriptione narrationem istam Euangelista orditur, præmissa demonstrandi particula, qua omnes ad diligentiore rei totius considerationem excitat. Ecce (inquit) erat quidem Hierosolymæ, cui nomen Simeon, eratq; homo ille iustus & religiosus, expectans consolationē Israelis, & Spiritus sanctus erat super eum. Hierosolymæ eum habit auisse ait, quæ etsi ob vererem religionis & diuini cultus sedem celeberrima esset, illo tamen tempore sentina quædam scelerum & schola hæresum censeri poterat, eò quòd illic Herodes regnaret, sacris autem dominarentur Pharisæi, qui hominũ traditionibus ad hypocrisim & quæstum compositis doctrinam simul atq; cultum Dei iampridē corruperant. Nihil ergo obstare poterat, quò minus spiret Spiritus sanctus vbicũq; vult, & illic quoq; vim suam exerat, vbi inuictis repagulis conclusus esse videtur. Sed qualis nam Simeon ille fuerit, videamus. Primò iustum & religiosum, id est, Dei timentem cultusq; diuini stu diosum fuisse dicit. Comprehendit duobus hisce epithetis, quæcunq; ad vitam recte instituendam necessaria sunt. Nam duabus Decalogi tabulis illa respondent & religio quidem veri Dei cognitionem, timorem, cultum & obedientiam continet; iustitiæ autem vocabulo denotantur quæcunq; proximo debemus officia.
