Similis zelus in Iosua & Caleb o cernitur, qui etiam ipsi cum aperto vitæ suæ discrimine, gloriâ Dei aduersus perfidos speculatores defenderunt. His adnumerari meretur Phinees, qui nefarium Zamri vnà cum Madianitico scorto confodit, cùm occasione scortationis populū à Deo abduci & ad cultus nefarios solicitari videret. Eodem zelo Dauidem arripisse legimus, qui ipsum iuuenem licet & pugnandi imperitum coegit, vt immanem Goliam aggredi auderet, qui Deo Israelis palàm conuitiabatur. Et huius generis multa de Elia Propheta & sanctissimis regibus, Ezechia & Iosia, commemorari possent, qui simili ardore & studio aduersus falsam doctrinam & idololatriam vsi sunt. Neq; illo Apostoli caruerunt, quibus intolerabile scelus visum fuit, si vel cultibus nefarijs aliquos deditos esse viderunt, vel ipsis homines imperiti aliquid sublimius cum diuini nominis contumelia coniunctum tribuere voluerunt. Exempla in Ioanne & Petro, Paulo & Barnaba habentur. Ex quibus facile colligitur, admodum frigidos esse in zelo gloriæ & nominis Dei omnes eos, qui apertam multorum incredulitatem, idololatriam, blasphemias, scandala item omnis generis absq; omni contradictione ferre possunt. At quia talium precatio, quoad primam hanc petitionem, futata & proinde inutilis est, nos priores illos, quorum exempla commemorauimus imitari conuenit, vt nec in aliis quidem feramus quæ gloriam Dei obscurant.
units.tr: Secondly, it is required that we not only be such ourselves, but also promote the glory of the divine name among others with whom we have any dealings. Just as it is not enough for a well-natured son to honour his parent himself, but he wants his father to be honoured and esteemed by others too, so those who are true and genuine children of God are not satisfied if they alone worship and revere their heavenly Father. In addition, they direct all their zeal to this, that as many others as possible acknowledge this God and revere and observe his name. Hence it happens that those who are endowed with true faith cannot see or bear anything that they know to be detrimental to God's glory and holy name. As soon as they perceive such a thing, not all of them, forgetful of modesty, patience and gentleness, display their zeal, and if need be, they vindicate the glory of the divine name even at the risk of life. For just as they love God above all things, so nothing is as dear to them as his glory. To this belong those famous examples of God's servants who showed this zeal at the peril of their present life. Among them, no small place is owed to Moses. When the people of Israel, against God's explicit command, had defiled themselves with the sin of idolatry, and had exchanged the immortal majesty of God (as David says) for the image of a calf eating hay, he burned with such anger and zeal that he cast away the tablets of God's covenant, written with God's finger, than which this world has never seen anything more precious. He broke the idol and reduced it to powder, and having thrown the powder into water, he compelled those unhappy people to drink their so splendid God, so that it might be more plainly shown how shamefully and wickedly they had gone astray. Besides, he ordered the authors of this idolatry to be put to death, which could not be done without danger to life. A similar zeal is seen in Joshua and Caleb, who also, at the open risk of their own lives, defended the glory of God against the faithless spies. Phinehas deserves to be counted among these, who ran through the wicked Zimri together with the Midianite harlot, when he saw the people being led away from God by occasion of fornication and enticed to wicked worship. We read that David was seized by the same zeal, who, though a young man and inexperienced in fighting, compelled himself to dare to attack the monstrous Goliath, who openly reviled the God of Israel. Many things of this kind could be recalled about the prophet Elijah and the most holy kings Hezekiah and Josiah, who used like ardour and zeal against false doctrine and idolatry. Nor were the apostles lacking in this: it seemed to them an intolerable crime if they saw anyone given over to wicked cults, or if ignorant men wished to attribute to them something more exalted, joined with dishonour to the divine name. Examples are found in John and Peter, Paul and Barnabas. From these it is easily gathered that all those are very cold in zeal for the glory and name of God who can bear, without any contradiction, the open unbelief of many, idolatry, blasphemies, and likewise scandals of every kind. But since the prayer of such people, as regards this first petition, is vain and therefore useless, it is fitting that we imitate those former men whose examples we have recalled, so that we may not even bear with those things in others which obscure God's glory.

units.la: Sed ne hîc quidem pedem sistunt germani filij Dei, quin simul omne id plantare & prouehere studeant, quo Dei nomen & eius gloria illustratur. Inter quæ primum locum tenet pura & sana Euangelij doctrina, per quam vera Dei cognitio traditur, fides in hominum animis plantatur, & purus atq; syncerus Dei cultus docetur. Deinde in repub. hoc agunt, vt leges bonæ ferantur & defendantur, vt disciplina & publica honestas conseruetur, vt denique scandala omnia tollantur è medio. Et hæc fere olim fuerunt sanctorum principum & regum studia, sicut in Dauide, Iosaphato, Ezechia, Iosia, & postea hos in Constantino Magno, Theodosio & aliis similibus cernitur: qui omnes hunc suæ gubernationis scopum sibi proposuerunt, vt locum haberent leges bonæ, & in primis vt doctrina Verbi diuini pure prædicaretur, & cultus secundum eius præscriptum esset institutus. Et in hunc scopum hodie etiam respicere debent, quicunq; rempub. administrant, nisi per primam hanc petitionem apud Deum falsi & hypocrisis argui & convinci velint. Quod vero illis dicitur, id omnibus Christianis commune est, qui singuli in suæ vitæ conditione hoc ipsum obseruare debent: vtpote parentes erga suos liberos, & singuli erga proximum suum: vt nimirum hos ad verum Dei cultum instituant & ab erroribus impijs abducant. Quod nisi fecerint, prima hac petitione nunquam vere apud Deum vti poterunt. Quo ore enim princeps aut Senator aliquis dicet, Sanctificetur nomen tuum, si illud à quouis impune violari patiatur, neq; ea cura habet, per quæ honorari aut sanctificari potest? Quo ore item paterfamilias eandem precatione faciet, si inter suos omne id fieri patitur, quod ad nominis diuini contumeliam facit? Singuli deniq; respondeant velim, quo argumento hypocrisim excusabunt, si labijs quidem hæc verba proferant, proximum vero quenq; absq; omni admonitione aut correptione pergere sinant in ijs, propter quæ Dei nomen male audit?
units.tr: But the true children of God do not stop even here; at the same time they strive to plant and advance everything by which God's name and glory are made illustrious. Among these, the first place belongs to the pure and sound doctrine of the Gospel, through which the true knowledge of God is handed down, faith is planted in men's minds, and pure and sincere worship of God is taught. Next, in the commonwealth they work to ensure that good laws are enacted and defended, that discipline and public decency are preserved, and finally that all scandals are removed from the midst. These were formerly the chief concerns of holy princes and kings, as is seen in David, Jehoshaphat, Hezekiah and Josiah, and afterwards in Constantine the Great, Theodosius and other like men. All of them set before themselves this aim of their government: that good laws should prevail, and above all that the doctrine of the divine Word should be preached purely and worship instituted according to its prescription. Those who administer the commonwealth ought to keep this aim in view even today, unless they wish to be shown up and convicted before God of falsehood and hypocrisy in this first petition. What is said to them is common to all Christians, who each in their own station ought to observe this very thing: namely, parents towards their children, and each person towards his neighbour, that is, to instruct them in the true worship of God and lead them away from impious errors. Unless they do so, they will never be able to use this first petition truly before God. For with what mouth will a prince or some senator say, "Hallowed be your name," if he allows it to be violated with impunity by anyone, and takes no care for those things by which it can be honoured and sanctified? With what mouth likewise will the head of a household make the same prayer, if he allows among his own people everything to be done that tends to the dishonour of the divine name? Lastly, let each one answer me: by what argument will they excuse their hypocrisy, if with their lips they indeed utter these words, but allow each neighbour to go on without any admonition or correction in those things on account of which God's name is ill spoken of?

units.la: In hu ergo apparet, qualis sit nostri seculi, & quàm corrupta omnium ordinum conditio, quando pauci sunt, qui rem tanti momenti digne considerent. Ore quidem omnes precamur, Sanctificetur nomen tuum: at quotus quisq; curat, vt huic petitioni mores & studia sua respondeant? Principes & qui in magistratu sunt, fere sui honoris & gloriæ priuatæ maiorem quàm diuinæ rationem habent. Multi etiam ex horum numero sibi ipsis persuadent, religionis causam nihil ad se pertinere, sed sui muneris esse res huius seculi tractare, quæ vero ad fidem & religionem spectant, Episcopi & sacer
units.tr: In this, then, it appears what our age is like, and how corrupt the condition of all orders is, when there are so few who duly consider a matter of such importance. We all pray with our mouths, "Hallowed be your name," but how few take care that their morals and pursuits correspond to this petition? Princes and those who hold office for the most part have more regard for their own honour and private glory than for the divine. Many of them also persuade themselves that the cause of religion does not concern them, but that it is their business to handle the affairs of this world, while matters pertaining to faith and religion should be left to bishops and priests

units.la: Psal. 106. dotibus vel monachis relinquere. Quae causa est, quod ab his Dei Verbum opprimitur, & fideles Iesu Christi serui crudeliter affliguntur. Sed & inter Ecclesiarum ministros multos est videre, qui sui officij immemores, huius seculi res pluris quam divinas faciunt. Apud parentes nihil vulgarius est, quam quod liberos suos mundo potius quam Deo consecrant, seque officio suo egregie defunctos arbitrantur, si filios ad opes & honores amplissimos euehat, quamvis & Dei & nominis eius cognitione destituantur. Inter plebeios singulorum fere ea est sententia, quod divina minus ad ipsos pertineant, & stulte nimis eos facere, qui propter ea aliquem sibi inimicum faciunt, cum interim opum & lucri causa omnium odia facile contemnant. Hinc sequitur, quod nulli fere hominum ordini suus honor tribuitur. Cur enim eorum honore Deus tueatur, qui ipsius tam facile negligunt? Impleri potius oportet quod per Prophetam dixit: Qui me honorant, eos honorabo: contumelia autem efficientur, qui me contemnunt. Cur item in aliquo pretio eos esse putaretur, quos non pudet inter precandum quoque simulare & mentiri? Est ergo res non leuis momenti haec prima petitio. Probe igitur eam expendere, & ea animo minime fucato uti debemus, simul omnibus ijs studere, quibus Dei nomen glorificatur, ut & nos Deus pro filijs suis agnoscat, Spiritu suo donet, & tandem cohaeredes faciat Filij sui unigeniti Iesu Christi, Domini nostri, cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: Psal. 106. or to monks. This is the reason why the Word of God is oppressed by them, and the faithful servants of Jesus Christ are cruelly afflicted. Among the ministers of the churches, too, many are to be seen who, forgetful of their office, make more of worldly affairs than of divine ones. Among parents nothing is more common than to consecrate their children to the world rather than to God, and to think they have discharged their duty admirably if they raise their sons to great wealth and the highest honours, even though those sons are destitute of the knowledge of God and his name. Among the common people, the opinion of almost everyone is that divine matters concern them less, and that those are foolish who make an enemy of someone on their account, whereas for the sake of wealth and gain they easily disregard the hatred of all. Hence it follows that almost no honour is given to any class of men. For why should God protect the honour of those who so easily neglect his own? Rather, what he said through the Prophet ought to be fulfilled: "Those who honour me I will honour, but those who despise me shall be brought to contempt." Likewise, why should they be thought to be in any esteem who are not ashamed to pretend and lie even while praying? This first petition, therefore, is no matter of slight importance. We ought to weigh it carefully, use it with a mind not feigned at all, and at the same time strive for all those things by which God's name is glorified, so that God may also acknowledge us as his sons, give us his Spirit, and at last make us co-heirs of his only-begotten Son, Jesus Christ our Lord, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CVIII. PETITIO II. Adueniat Regnum tuum.
units.tr: HOMILY CVIII. PETITION II. Thy kingdom come.

units.la: Dominus & redemptor noster Iesus Christus certam precandi formulam nobis praescripsit, non quidem eo proposito, quod nefas sit alijs quoque inter precandum verbis uti (quod plures Dei serui in utroque Testamento fecerunt), sed partim docere vult, quibus rebus in hoc seculo nobis potissimum opus sit, & quid prae alijs a Deo peti debeat: partim, quis nostrarum precum finis aut scopus debeat constitui, ne carnis nostrae caeca prudentia decepti, in eo ipso erremus, in quo opera atque fidem quaerimus. Videmus hoc satis evidenter in prima petitione, quae filiorum Dei propria est, a quibus hoc iure exigitur, ut Patris sui caelestis gloriam prae omnibus alijs rebus commendatam habeant, & proinde eam quantum possunt studeant promovere.
units.tr: Our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ prescribed to us a fixed form of prayer. He did not intend thereby to forbid the use of other words in prayer, which many servants of God did in both Testaments. Rather, he wished partly to teach us what we most need in this world and what above all else we ought to ask of God, and partly to show what goal or aim our prayers should have, so that we do not, deceived by the blind wisdom of our flesh, go wrong in the very thing we seek through our works and faith. We see this quite clearly in the first petition, which belongs peculiarly to the children of God. By right, they are bound to hold the glory of their heavenly Father above all other things and therefore to strive as far as they can to advance it.

units.la: Sequitur secunda petitio, qua precamur, ut Dei regnum ad nos veniat. Subijcitur haec priori admodum opportuno & ordine commodissimo, ut quae ei cohaereat, & ex ea deriuetur. Qui enim fieri potest, ut Dei nomen per nos, qui natura corrupti & peccatores sumus sanctificetur, nisi Deus ipse per Spiritum suum in nobis regnet? Quoad hoc non fit, nihil in nobis est praeter peccatum, neque ex nobis ipsis aliud poterimus, quam quod ad diuini nominis contumeliam facit. Quia ergo ante omnia precari debemus, ut Dei nomen in nobis sanctificetur, id vero nobis praestitu impossibile est, necesse est ut mox subijciamus: Adueniat regnum. Id est: O Pater, nostri quidem officij erat sanctificare nomen tuum: ad id vero praestandum non inepti modo & imbecilles, verumetiam indigni sumus, ut qui nostris deliciis iampridem meruimus, ne unquam gloriae tuae vasa censeamur. Quia vero ita nos precari iubes, nimirum pro tua bonitate & clementia nos pro talibus denuo agnosci. Quaesumus ergo, ut tu cum tuo regno ad nos venias, & nos regas, ut tuae voluntati satisfiat, & nomen tuum per nos vere sanctificetur, & c. Ut vero huius petitionis sensum probe intelligamus, ante omnia tenendum erit, quid sit Regnum Dei, & quae eius conditio. Ex eo enim patebit, quis huius petitionis in omni tentatione propius usus sit.
units.tr: The second petition follows, in which we pray that God's kingdom may come to us. It is placed after the first very fittingly and in the most suitable order, since it clings to the first and arises from it. For how can God's name be sanctified through us, who are by nature corrupt and sinners, unless God himself reigns in us by his Spirit? As long as this does not happen, there is nothing in us but sin, and from ourselves we can produce nothing but what brings dishonour to the name of God. Since, then, we must above all pray that God's name be sanctified in us, and since this is impossible for us to accomplish, we must immediately add: "Thy kingdom come." That is to say: O Father, it was indeed our duty to sanctify your name, but we are not only unfit and feeble for this task, we are also unworthy, since by our wickedness we have long deserved never to be counted vessels of your glory. Yet because you bid us pray in this way, we ask that by your goodness and mercy you acknowledge us again as such people. We beg you, then, to come to us with your kingdom and to rule us, so that your will may be done, your name truly sanctified through us, and so on. In order to understand the sense of this petition properly, we must first hold firmly to what the kingdom of God is and what its condition is. For from this it will be clear how this petition is most helpful in every temptation.

units.la: Regna inter homines in terris hisce duo sunt, quod ipsum petitio haec non obscure docet. Quia enim Dei Regnum venire precamur, fatemur utiq; regnum quoddam aliud in nobis esse, cuius potentia sentiamus. Id vero diaboli regnum est, quod in ipsa mundi origine per primorum parentum transgressionem obtinuit, & quod omni studio retinere atq; augere conatur. Quo nomine princeps huius mundi dicitur: non quidem eo sensu, quod Deu a mundi gubernaculis deiecerit, & ipse pro sua libidine illum gubernet: sed quod Deus iusto iudicio aliqua ex parte tale quid illi permisit, ut mundi malitia & ingratitudo dignus poenis multetur. Quia enim Deus hominem secundum suam imaginem conditum insum-
units.tr: There are two kinds of kingdoms among men on earth, and this petition itself teaches it plainly. For when we pray that the kingdom of God come, we certainly confess that there is another kingdom in us, whose power we feel. This is the kingdom of the devil, which he obtained at the very origin of the world through the transgression of our first parents, and which he strives with all his effort to keep and enlarge. By this name he is called the prince of this world. Not, indeed, in the sense that God has cast him down from the government of the world and that he governs it at his own pleasure, but in the sense that God, by his just judgement, has in some measure allowed him this, so that the wickedness and ingratitude of the world may be punished as it deserves. For since God had created man in his own image and had exalted him

units.la: Ordo huius petitionis.
units.tr: The order of this petition.

units.la: Regnum diaboli in mundo. in summam dignitatem extulerat, vt omnium creatorū dominus haberetur, ipse vero tantum Dei beneficium non agnouit, sed ex diaboli instinctu rebellione facta diuinitatem ipsam affectauit, iusto & aequo Dei iudicio factum est, vt in diaboli potestatem traderetur, vt ita homines magno suo malo experirentur, quem nam Regem, seu tyrannum potius, loco Dei optimi & beneficentissimi, sibi delegissent. Ab eo itaq; tempore diaboli regnum coepit, quod in duobus potissimum consistit, mendacijs & apertis sceleribus. Vt enim ipse mendax est, & in veritate non perstitit: ita men-dacijs quoq; regnū suū prouehit, & homines ab ea, quā Deo debent, obedientia abducit. Cuius rei initium in primis parentibus factum est, quos diuinitatis mendaci promissione Deo inobedientes fecit. Postea inter gentes philosophos excitauit, qui falsa sapientiae professione seipsos & alios quoq; dementarunt, falsis de Deo opinionibus & infinitis in religionem erroribus inuolu. Accesserunt hi vates omnis generis & Deorum Oracula, quorum tanta fuit apud infelices homines authoritas, vt potentissimi quoq; reges in regnorum administratione, nihil nisi illis consultu tentandum putarent. In Dei populo autem humanas traditiones induxit, quibus Verbi diuini doctrina obscurata fuit, vera Dei cognitio paulatim euanuit, fides extincta, cultus externus corruptus, & hominum mentes a Deo abstractae fuerunt, vt salutem extra illum quaesiuerint. Factum hoc olim apud Iudaeos, postea vero temporibus inter Christianos quoq;, quorum plerique hac ratione decepti sunt, vt Mahumeticis fabulis & Antichristiana tyrannidi locum dederint. Tanta fuit diaboli astutia in regno suo per mendacia & dolos propagando: quod ideo regnum tenebrarum dicitur, quod omnia in eo obscura & incerta, adhaec terrorum plena & periculosa sunt.
units.tr: The kingdom of the devil in the world. to the highest dignity, so that he would be regarded as lord of all creatures, yet man did not acknowledge this great benefit of God. Instead, at the prompting of the devil, he rebelled and aspired to divinity itself. By the just and equitable judgement of God it came about that he was handed over into the power of the devil, so that men might learn by their great harm whom they had chosen as king, or rather tyrant, in place of the best and most beneficent God. From that time on the kingdom of the devil began, and it consists chiefly of two things: lies and open crimes. For just as he is himself a liar and did not stand in the truth, so he also extends his kingdom by lies and draws men away from the obedience they owe to God. The beginning of this was made in our first parents, whom he made disobedient to God by the lying promise of divinity. Afterwards he stirred up among the Gentiles philosophers who, by a false profession of wisdom, drove both themselves and others mad, and entangled them in false opinions about God and in endless errors of religion. Then came soothsayers of every kind and oracles of the gods, whose authority among wretched men was so great that even the most powerful kings thought that nothing should be undertaken in governing their realms without consulting them. Among the people of God, however, he introduced human traditions, by which the teaching of the divine Word was obscured, the true knowledge of God gradually faded away, faith was extinguished, outward worship was corrupted, and men's minds were turned away from God so that they sought salvation outside him. This happened long ago among the Jews, and later in the times of the Christians as well, where many were deceived in this way and gave place to Mahometan fables and to Antichristian tyranny. So great was the devil's cunning in spreading his kingdom by lies and tricks. For this reason it is called the kingdom of darkness: everything in it is obscure and uncertain, and moreover it is full of terrors and dangerous.

units.la: Deinde per aperta quoq; scelera regnat, quibus quam maxime delectatur, eò quòd per illa a Deo abstracti, ipsi diabolo conformes efficimur. Est ipse spiritus immundus & impurus: impuros ergo et immundos quoq; reddit homines, in quorum cordibus foeda cogitationes nascuntur, impurae cupiditates accenduntur, quae postea per verba scandali plena, per stupra, fornicationem, adulteria, incestus & nefarios masculorum concubitus ita erumpunt, vt impurus ille in omnibus membris nostris dominetur. Quibus addi debent quaecunq; ab ebriosis & intemperantibus foedissima scelera designantur. Adhaec (vt ante diximus) mendax est: ideò homines quoq; mendaces reddit & impostores, quae omnis iniustitiae in contractibus & commerciis causa est. Idem insatiabili cupiditate nocendi ardet, & subinde rugienti leoni similis oberrat. Itaq; in hominibus quoq; accendit insatiabiles cupiditates opum, voluptatum, honorum, quibus ita immerguntur, vt nec Deum nec Regnum eius deiceps magni faciant. Adhaec ab initio homicida fuit, & in Adamo (quantum in ipso fuit) totum genus humanum perdidit. Ergo vt infelices quoq; homines sibi similes reddat, in illu priuati commodi studium accendit, ex quo deinde aemulatio, inuidia, odium, simultates, iniuriae, contumelia, contentiones, rixae, pugnae, verbera, vulnera, & tandem caedes atq; parricidia nascuntur: cuius rei exemplum memorabile in illius primogenito, Caino, extat. Taceo nunc bella & praelia, quibus saepe vnius horae spatio multa millia crudeliter trucidantur, qui ira & vindicta cupiditate flagrantes absque paeniteritia & diuini nominis invocatione decedunt. Taceo agrorum vastationes, praedationes, incendia, stupra matronarum & virginum, & quae alia in bello fieri consueuerunt. Deniq; superbus ille spiritus est Satan, qui Altissimo aequalis fieri voluit, & adhuc hodie aduersus eum immani arrogantia seipsum extollit. Ergo eos quoque qui ipsum audiunt superbiae spiritu inflat, quo decepti omnes alios prae se contemnunt, Dei donis insolentissime abutuntur, & simul aduersus Deum & Verbum eius indomita confidentia insurgunt, neque se eius legibus teneri sibi ipsis persuadent: quae omnis inobedientiae praecipua causa est. Et haec quidem omnia ex diaboli suggestione fiunt, cui seruit, & qui hac ratione regni sui fines protendit. At regni huius non aliud stipendiu est, quàm dam natio & mors aeterna. Nam ex Dei Verbo constat, peccati stipendium esse mortem. Et ideò regni huius conditio per tyrannidem Aegyptiacam proprissime adumbratur. Vt enim Israelitae sub Pharaone in sordido luto opus facere cogebantur, laborum verò & seruitutis durissimae non aliud stipendium recipiebant, quàm indignas suorum infantium caedes, & quòd tandem primogenitus ipsorum ab Angelo vastatore periculum praesens paratum fuit, è quo non alia ratione, quàm ex gratia Dei per agni sanguinem erepti sunt: Ita quotquot diaboli regno subsunt, ij in luto & sordibus incredulitatis idololatriae & scelerum illi seruiunt, neq; ex eo seruitio aliam mercedem possunt speDocument end rare, quàm æternos inferorum cruciatus. Et hæc de infelici hoc regno dicta sint, cuius sensu cogimur precari, vt Dei regnum adueniat.
units.tr: Then he also reigns through open crimes, in which he takes the greatest delight, because by them we are drawn away from God and made like the devil himself. He is an unclean and impure spirit, so he also makes men unclean and impure. In their hearts foul thoughts arise and impure desires are kindled, which afterwards break out in words full of scandal, in debauchery, fornication, adultery, incest and the abominable intercourse of men with men, so that this impure spirit rules over all our members. To these must be added all the most foul crimes that are attributed to drunkards and the intemperate. Moreover, as we said before, he is a liar, and so he makes men liars and impostors as well, which is the cause of all injustice in contracts and dealings. He burns with an insatiable desire to harm, and wanders about like a roaring lion. Thus he also kindles in men insatiable desires for wealth, pleasures and honours, by which they are so immersed that they no longer care for God or his kingdom. Furthermore, from the beginning he was a murderer, and in Adam he destroyed, as far as lay in him, the whole human race. So, in order to make wretched men like himself, he kindles in them the pursuit of private advantage, from which then arise rivalry, envy, hatred, quarrels, injuries, insults, contentions, brawls, fights, beatings, wounds, and at last slaughter and parricide. A memorable example of this is found in his firstborn, Cain. I say nothing now of wars and battles, in which often many thousands are cruelly slaughtered within the space of a single hour, men who, burning with anger and the lust for revenge, die without repentance and without calling upon the name of God. I say nothing of the devastation of fields, plunder, fires, the rape of matrons and virgins, and whatever else is customarily done in war. Finally, Satan is that proud spirit who wished to be equal to the Most High and even today exalts himself against him with monstrous arrogance. Therefore he also inflates with the spirit of pride those who listen to him, by which deceived men all despise others in comparison with themselves, most insolently abuse the gifts of God, and at the same time rise up against God and his Word with unbridled confidence, persuading themselves that they are not bound by his laws. This is the chief cause of all disobedience. All these things happen at the suggestion of the devil, whom they serve, and who in this way extends the bounds of his kingdom. But the wages of this kingdom are nothing other than death and eternal damnation. For it is established by the Word of God that the wages of sin is death. Therefore the condition of this kingdom is most aptly foreshadowed by the Egyptian tyranny. Just as the Israelites under Pharaoh were compelled to do work in filthy mud, and received no other wage for their labours and most harsh servitude than the unworthy slaughter of their infants, and finally the danger that their firstborn was prepared for destruction by the destroying angel, from which they were rescued by no other means than by the grace of God through the blood of the lamb, so all who are subject to the kingdom of the devil serve him in the mud and filth of unbelief, idolatry and wickedness, and from that service they can hope for no other reward than the eternal torments of hell. Let these things be said of this wretched kingdom, by whose meaning we are compelled to pray that the kingdom of God may come.

units.la: Porrò vt Deus ab æterno prævidit, humanum genus diaboli regno & huius infelici tyrannidi subijciendum fore, & vt id fieret, iusto suo iudicio permisit: ita æterno suo decreto Regnū aliud constituere statuit, cuius instauratione diaboli regnū destrueretur, nos autem ex eius seruitio liberati, denuo ipsi reconciliaremur. Et hoc Dei Regnum dicitur, eò quòd huius princeps & vnicum caput est Filius Dei, quem is nobis antequam mundus hic conderetur (vt Petrus ait) liberatorem constituit, qui diaboli caput conculcaret, nosq; ad salutarem Dei obedientiam & beatam regni cœlestis hæreditatem siue communionem reduceret. De hoc regno intelligi debent præclara illa prophetarum vaticinia, quæ in Psal. 2. 45. 72. &c. Item Isa. 9. Ierem. 23. & in primis apud Danielem leguntur. De eodem quoq; Paulus ait, quando nos Deo Patri gratias agere iubet, qui nos liberauerit à potestate tenebrarum, ac transtulerit in Regnum Filij sui dilecti. Et hoc proprie Regnum illud est, quod vt veniat hic precamur.
units.tr: Moreover, just as God foreknew from eternity that the human race would be made subject to the kingdom of the devil and to his unhappy tyranny, and in his just judgment permitted this, so by his eternal decree he determined to establish another kingdom. By its restoration the kingdom of the devil would be destroyed, and we, freed from his service, would be reconciled to him again. This is called the Kingdom of God, because its prince and sole head is the Son of God, whom he appointed before the world was made (as Peter says) to be our deliverer, to crush the head of the devil and to bring us back to the saving obedience of God and to the blessed inheritance, or fellowship, of the heavenly kingdom. The notable prophecies of the prophets, which are read in Psalms 2, 45, 72, and so on, also Isaiah 9, Jeremiah 23, and above all in Daniel, must be understood of this kingdom. Paul too speaks of it when he bids us give thanks to God the Father, who has delivered us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son. This is properly that Kingdom which we pray may come.

units.la: Vt verò diaboli regnum suis progressionibus augetur & propagatur, dum à mendacijs, dolis & imposturis initio facto, deinceps per incredulitatem, superstitiones, idolomaniam & manifesta scelera subinde altius assurgit, donec vna cum membris suis ad æternum exitium præcipitabitur: Ita Dei quoq; regnum ordine certo constat, & sua habet incrementa, quibus inter homines instauratum atq; subinde latius propagatum fuit.
units.tr: But just as the kingdom of the devil grows and spreads by its advances, since, having begun with lies, deceits and impostures, it then rises higher through unbelief, superstitions, idolatry and open crimes, until at last it is cast down to eternal destruction together with its members, so the Kingdom of God also has a fixed order and its own increases, by which it was established among men and from time to time spread more widely.

units.la: Principio enim Deus illud hominibus per Verbum suum manifestauit, & ea ratione propter electos suos diabolo se fortissime oppositum, quo minus se apud incautos & rerum ignaros intrude re posset. Quia enim semen quoddam peculiare mulieris promisit, quod diaboli caput contriturum & regnum eius destructurum esset, non obscure docuit, suos cultores nequaquam animum despondere, neq; se diabolo subijcere debere, sed constanti fide Regnum illud gratia expectare. Rursus quando humani generis redemptionem in promissio illo semine monstrauit, satis admonuit, non aliam doctrinam audiendam, neque alios admittendos esse, qui aliam ab hac salutis rationem aut alia redemptionis nostra media fingere ausint. Adhæc cum promissionibus istis eos de redemptione tam certos fecerit, simul exhortari voluit, ne diaboli seruitio se submittant, sed illi resistant, vt promissi & tandem venturi Regni melioris cives fieri possint. Et hic præcipuus promissionum omnium, quibus Patriarchas olim Deus consolatus est, finis atq; scopus fuit: quæ postea per Legis typos & Prophetarum vaticinia clarius illustrata sunt. Quò enim propius accessit prafinitum illud promissi redemptoris tempus, eò clarius lucere cæpit salutaris ille Regni Dei splendor, quo electos recreari & exhilarari oportebat. Estq; hoc plenum consolationis, quod Deus tam Regni sui quàm electorum suorum tantam curam tunc habuit, quando humanum genus prorsus abiecisse & in diaboli potestatem tradidisse videbatur.
units.tr: For at the beginning God made it known to men through his Word, and in this way opposed himself most strongly to the devil on behalf of his elect, so that the devil could not thrust himself in among the unwary and the ignorant. For when he promised a certain peculiar seed of the woman, who would crush the head of the devil and destroy his kingdom, he taught plainly that his worshippers should by no means lose heart, nor submit themselves to the devil, but should with steadfast faith await that kingdom by grace. Again, when he showed the redemption of the human race in that promised seed, he gave sufficient warning that no other doctrine was to be heard, nor were any to be admitted who dared to devise any other way of salvation or other means of our redemption. Besides, since by those promises he made them so certain of redemption, he wished at the same time to exhort them not to submit to the service of the devil, but to resist him, so that they might become citizens of the promised and at last coming better kingdom. This was the chief aim and goal of all the promises by which God formerly comforted the patriarchs, and which were afterwards more clearly illustrated through the types of the Law and the prophecies of the prophets. For as the appointed time of the promised Redeemer drew nearer, that saving splendour of the Kingdom of God began to shine more clearly, by which the elect had to be refreshed and cheered. And this is full of comfort: that God then took such care both of his kingdom and of his elect, when the human race seemed utterly cast off and delivered into the power of the devil.

units.la: Vbi verò præfinitum tempus aduenit, absq; mora Deus promissum illud semen, nempe Filium suum, Iesum Christum, in mundum misit, qui ex intemerata Virgine Maria homo factus, in assumpta carne omne id executus est, quod ad Regni Dei instaurationem fieri necesse erat. Primo enim peccata nostra in se transtulit, & illa mortis suæ merito in ara crucis expiauit: qua ratione nos etiam à peccati pæna liberatos in libertatem filiorum Dei asseruit. Nec enim peccata solum nostra è medio abstulit, verumetiam vult vt ipsi per fidem insiti eius membra efficiamur, quibus suum meritum & iustitiam suam ita communicet, vt quàmus peccatores simus, quantum in nobis est, peccata tamen nobis non imputentur, adeò, vt propter ipsius meritum ad Dei tribunal pro iustis comparere possimus. Et tanta est huius expiationis peccatorum atq; satisfactionis certitudo, vt nullæ diaboli calumniæ nobis posthac timendæ sint, quò minus cum Paulo dicamus: Quis intentabit crimina aduersus electos Dei? Deus est qui iustificat: quis est qui condemnet? Christus est, qui mortuus est, imo verò qui etiam excitatus est, qui etiam est ad dexteram Dei, qui etiam intercedit & postulat pro nobis. Quia ergo Dei Filius pro peccatis satisfecit, & peccatorum pænam mortem videlicet & damnationem, suæ resurrectionis virtute vicit atq; aboleuit, hinc sequitur oportet, quòd diaboli regnum (cuius potentia & vires solo peccato & morte nitebantur) vicerit atque destruxerit. Quod ipsum infinitis miraculis, & in primis damoniorum eiectione testatus est. Quia enim hæc eius timore perculsa ad eius imperium ex hominibus discessere, non obscurè perspi-ci potuit, venisse iam regnum Dei, per quod diaboli regno finem imponi oporteat. Vide Luc.11. Matth.12.
units.tr: But when the appointed time arrived, without delay God sent into the world that promised seed, namely his Son, Jesus Christ, who, made man from the immaculate Virgin Mary, in the flesh he had assumed carried out all that was necessary for the establishment of the Kingdom of God. For first he transferred our sins to himself and expiated them on the altar of the cross by the merit of his death. By this means he also freed us from the punishment of sin and brought us into the liberty of the sons of God. For he did not only take away our sins, but he wills that we, engrafted into him through faith, should become his members, to whom he communicates his merit and his righteousness, so that, however much we are sinners, as far as in us lies, our sins are nevertheless not imputed to us, so that on account of his merit we may appear before the judgment seat of God as righteous. And so great is the certainty of this expiation of sins and of this satisfaction, that no calumnies of the devil are henceforth to be feared by us, so that with Paul we may say: "Who shall bring any charge against God's elect? It is God who justifies; who is he who condemns? It is Christ who died, yes rather who also rose again, who is also at the right hand of God, who also intercedes and makes request for us" (Rom. 8). Therefore, since the Son of God has made satisfaction for sins, and by the power of his resurrection has conquered and abolished the punishment of sins, namely death and damnation, it follows that he has conquered and destroyed the kingdom of the devil, whose power and strength rested only on sin and death. He himself bore witness to this by countless miracles, and above all by the casting out of demons. For since these, struck with fear of him, departed from men at his command, it could be plainly seen that the Kingdom of God had now come, by which the reign of the devil must be brought to an end. See Luke 11 and Matthew 12.

units.la: Cæterum vt redemptionis nostræ fructus perpetuus & Dei regnum inter nos stabile & firmum fit, non solum nos ex peccati seruitio liberauit, sed Spiritum quoque suum sanctum cordibus nostris inserit, per quem vt certissimum salutis nostræ arrhabonem (quo nomine eum Paulus appellat) ad uersus omnes dubias carnis tentationes confirmamur, adhæc ex semine æterni atq; immortalis ver-bi regeneramur innouamurque, & in omnem veritatem inducimur. Quo fit, vt qui ex nobis ipsis nō aliud quam peccare possumus, in posterum duce & cooperante nobis spiritu Christi ad omne bonum idonei simus, peccato resistamus, Deo debitum præstemus obsequium, & in bono indies proficiamus. Exempla huius innouationis passim in veris Christi cultoribus cernuntur, qui non solum illicitas peccati cupiditates fortiter repellunt & subigunt, verumetiam contemptis omnibus mundi huius minis atque furiosis conatibus, in Christo Iesu constanter perseuerant, & in media etiam morte dia-boli tyrannidem vincunt. Quod factu impossibile esset, nisi illos Deus ex illius potestate eripuisset, & suum regnum in ipsis instauraret.
units.tr: Furthermore, so that the fruit of our redemption may be perpetual, and the Kingdom of God may be stable and firm among us, he not only freed us from the service of sin, but also implants his Holy Spirit in our hearts, through whom we are strengthened against all doubtful temptations of the flesh, as the most certain pledge of our salvation (which name Paul gives him), and besides, we are regenerated and renewed from the seed of the eternal and immortal Word, and are led into all truth. Hence it comes about that we, who of ourselves can do nothing but sin, are henceforth, with the Spirit of Christ leading and co-operating with us, fit for every good work, resist sin, render due obedience to God, and make progress in goodness day by day. Examples of this renewal are seen everywhere among the true worshippers of Christ, who not only bravely repel and subdue unlawful desires of sin, but also, despising all the threats and raging attempts of this world, persevere constantly in Christ Jesus, and even in the midst of death overcome the tyranny of the devil. This would be impossible to do, unless God had snatched them from his power and established his kingdom in them.

units.la: Præterea, vt Regnum Dei per totum orbem dinulgaretur, & vbique gentium locum haberet, Christus Iesus Euangelij prædicationem instituit, per quam omnia ea, quæ nostræ redemptionis & salutis causa fecit atque sustinuit, toti mundo annuntiata, & ad ipsum ex omnibus populis discipu-li adducti sunt. Et hoc legitimum atque ordinarium medium est, per quod Deus regni sui limites per totum orbem extendit, & omnium nationum homines ad suam obedientiam adduxit. Ideo Euan-gelium aliquando Sermo aut verbum Regni Dei dicitur. Huius enim prædicatione docemur, pro-missum illud & benedictum semen à Deo exhibitum esse, cuius merito redempti simus, Regnum ve-rò Dei instauratum sit, cuius cives & consortes proculdubio futuri sint, quotquot doctrinam hanc fide vera & constanti amplexantur, & in ea perseuerant. Christi enim promissio est: Qui credide-rit & baptizatus fuerit, saluus erit. Mar.16.
units.tr: Moreover, so that the Kingdom of God might be spread through the whole world and find a place everywhere among the nations, Christ Jesus instituted the preaching of the Gospel, through which all those things that he did and endured for the cause of our redemption and salvation are announced to the whole world, and disciples are brought to him from all peoples. This is the lawful and ordinary means by which God extends the bounds of his kingdom throughout the whole world and brings men of all nations to his obedience. Therefore the Gospel is sometimes called the preaching or word of the Kingdom of God. For by its preaching we are taught that the promised and blessed seed has been given by God, by whose merit we have been redeemed, and that the Kingdom of God has been established, of which all who embrace this doctrine with true and steadfast faith, and persevere in it, will undoubtedly become citizens and partners. For this is the promise of Christ: "He who believes and is baptized shall be saved" (Mark 16).

units.la: Neq; hic multum moramur diaboli improbitatem, qui regnum istud perpetuo oppugnat, mul-tos etiam ab eo diuellit, qui eius membra & cives esse putabantur. Nam etsi ille à Christo deuictus fit, ingenij tamen suum perpetuo retinet, vt nimirum homines perdere cupiat. Quapropter filios suos exitio deuotos, & quos Deus iusto iudicio in reprobum sensum tradidit, perpetuò aduersus Dei fi-lios instruit, & his pugnas mouet assiduas: veruntamen vt exarmatus & iam pridè deuictus hostis, nihil efficere potest, sed tũ ignominia repulsus cedere cogitur, Christo interim suũ regnũ inter medios hostes semper seruante, & interdũ ferreum suũ sceptrum exerete, quo hostium suorum phalanges ceu vasa figuli dissipat atq; comminuit. Idem, cum pastor ille bonus & fidus sit, nullam ex ouium suarum numero sibi eripi patitur. Nam etiamsi interdũ ingens à regno Dei defectio facta esse videa-tur, minime tamen id de electis intelligi debet, sed de perfidis hypocritis, quos Satan ipse prius dolo-sè credentium gregi permiscuit, vt aliquam publici scandali materiam haberet. Hi cruce & perse-quutione exorta, palearum instar dissipantur, & ad suum priorem principem redeunt. Interea au-tem veri & germani cives regni Dei, quorum nomina in cælis adscripta, constantes perseuerant: & licet interdum ex carnis infirmitate vacillent, Dei tamen Spiritu mox iterum confirmantur, & mirifice retinentur ne suam stationem deserant. Testimonia & exempla, quibus hoc demonstre-tur, iam inde à condito orbe infinita habemus. Hac enim ratione Deus Regnum suum (quamuis nondum perfectè reuelatum aut manifestum esset) ante diluuium aduersus impios Caini posteros & immanem nephilim progeniem defendit: & idem mox inter Diluuij aquas arcæ beneficio mi-rabiliter conseruauit. Sic Patriarchas quoque aduersus Cananæorum ferociam tutatus est, in quo-rum animis vocem hanc minacem subinde intonuit, Nolite tangere Christos vel vnctos meos, id est, homines mihi consecratos. Idem postea in Ægypto, Babylone & alibi non semel factum est. Eius-dem tiora tamè habemus in ijs, quæ Christi aduentũ secuta sunt. Nam etsi Imperatores Romani, pe-nes quos tunc erat orbis totius imperium, Christi doctrinam hostiliter oppugnarint, & homines Christianos crudelissimè sint persecuti, Deus tamè per obscuros et nullius in mundo pretij seruos suos regnũ suũ nõ sine totius orbis admiratione per omnes gentes propugnauit, & in hunc vsq; diē aduersus diabolum & omnes eius sectatores, Iudaos, Turcas, haereticos & pseudochristianos defendit. Quo argumento docemur, totum illud negotium Christi, per quod Euangelium annuntiatur, revera Regnum Dei esse, quod in terris exoriturum esse, olim Prophetae praedixerunt. Nisi enim ita se res haberet, nullo modo potuisset subsistere adversus mundi & principis eius machinationes. Ideo ille Pilato dicebat, Regnum meum non est de hoc mundo, &c.
units.tr: Nor do we here dwell long on the wickedness of the devil, who constantly assails this kingdom and tears away many from it who were thought to be its members and citizens. For although he has been conquered by Christ, he nevertheless retains his nature, namely that he desires to destroy men. Therefore he constantly trains his sons, devoted to destruction and whom God, by his just judgment, has given over to a reprobate mind, against the sons of God, and stirs up unceasing battles against them. Yet, like a disarmed and long since vanquished enemy, he can accomplish nothing, but is forced to withdraw, repulsed with shame, while Christ meanwhile always preserves his kingdom in the midst of his enemies, and at times stretches forth his iron sceptre, with which he scatters and grinds to pieces the battalions of his enemies like the vessels of a potter. Likewise, since that good and faithful shepherd is, he allows none from the number of his sheep to be snatched from him. For even if at times a great defection from the Kingdom of God seems to have occurred, this must by no means be understood of the elect, but of faithless hypocrites, whom Satan himself had previously cunningly mingled with the flock of believers, so that he might have some matter of public scandal. When persecution and the cross arise, these are scattered like chaff and return to their former prince. Meanwhile the true and genuine citizens of the Kingdom of God, whose names are written in heaven, persevere steadfastly; and although at times they waver through the weakness of the flesh, they are soon confirmed again by the Spirit of God and are wonderfully kept from abandoning their post. We have from the beginning of the world countless testimonies and examples by which this is shown. For in this way God, before the flood, defended his kingdom (although it was not yet fully revealed or manifest) against the impious posterity of Cain and the monstrous race of the Nephilim, and presently afterwards, amid the waters of the flood, he wonderfully preserved it through the ark. So too he protected the patriarchs against the fierceness of the Canaanites, in whose minds he repeatedly thundered this threatening voice: "Touch not my Christs, or my anointed ones," that is, men consecrated to me (Ps. 105). The same thing happened afterwards in Egypt, Babylon and elsewhere more than once. We have even clearer testimonies of the same in those events which followed the coming of Christ. For although the Roman emperors, in whose hands at that time lay the rule of the whole world, assailed the doctrine of Christ with hostility, and most cruelly persecuted Christian men, nevertheless God, through his servants who were obscure and of no account in the world, defended his kingdom through all nations, to the admiration of the whole world, and to this day defends it against the devil and all his followers: Jews, Turks, heretics and pseudo-Christians. By this argument we are taught that the whole business of Christ, through which the Gospel is announced, is in truth the Kingdom of God, which the prophets foretold of old would arise on earth. For unless this were so, it could in no way have stood against the machinations of the world and its prince. Therefore he said to Pilate, "My kingdom is not of this world," etc.

units.la: Porro ut regni diaboli finm lamentabilis & exitialis est: ita Regnum Dei plenum est gaudij & consolationis, & qui eius cives sunt, salutis spem certam sibi propositam habent. Quia enim il los Christus redemit, & Spiritu suo donauit, qui per Dei verbum in illis agit ac operatur, finis totius vitae ipsorum in hoc seculo is est, ut Deo toti consecrati & dediti sint, & huic soli seruiant, in vera fide, innocentia & charitate non fucata. Ex his deinde pax vera cum Deo & hominibus, gaudium ite in Spiritu sancto enascitur. Ideo Paulus dicebat, Regnum Dei esse iustitiam, pacem & gaudium in Spiritu sancto. Quoniam enim fideles iustificati sunt, iustitia in posterum studebunt. Rursus quia per Christum Deo reconciliati sunt, pace & tranquillitate conscientiarum fruuntur, quae dilectionem Christianam accendit, & quoad mores & vitae commercia pacificos reddit. Haec deinde gaudium verum, sanctum & perpetuum pariunt, quod nullis huius seculi afflictionibus turbari potest. Magna sunt haec & modis omnibus expetenda, exigua tamen censeri possunt, si cum futurae vitae praemio conferantur. Ut primum enim credentium animae corporis vinculo soluta hinc migrant, in beatae immortalitatis sedes colliguntur, ubi omnia ea possident, quae in hac vita sperarunt, & propter quae aduersa quaeque sustinuerunt. Corpora vero in ipsa lata resurrectionis quiescunt, quae in aduentu Iesu Christi fruentur, qui illa non excitabit modo, verumetiam corpori suo gloriosa conformia reddet, ut ad possessionem caelestis Regni sui idonea fiant. Tunc mors quoque absorbetur, inferorum potestas destruetur, nec quicquam reliquum erit, quod electos Dei turbare possit, sed eximijs illis & ineffabilibus bonis fruentur, quae oculus non vidit, neque auris audiuit, neque in cor hominis ascenderunt.
units.tr: Just as the end of the devil's kingdom is wretched and deadly, so the Kingdom of God is full of joy and comfort, and those who are its citizens have a sure hope of salvation set before them. For Christ has redeemed them and given them his Spirit, who works and operates in them through the Word of God. The goal of their whole life in this world is therefore to be wholly consecrated and devoted to God and to serve him alone, in true faith, innocence and unfeigned love. From this comes true peace with God and with men, and joy in the Holy Spirit. So Paul said that the Kingdom of God is "righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Spirit" [Rom. 14.17]. Since believers have been justified, they will strive after righteousness from now on. Again, because they have been reconciled to God through Christ, they enjoy peace and tranquillity of conscience, which kindles Christian love and makes them peaceable in their conduct and in their dealings with one another. This in turn brings forth a true, holy and perpetual joy, which no afflictions of this age can disturb. These blessings are great and to be desired in every way, yet they may seem small if they are compared with the reward of the life to come. For as soon as the souls of believers are loosed from the bond of the body and depart hence, they are gathered into the seats of blessed immortality, where they possess all the things they hoped for in this life and for which they endured every adversity. Their bodies rest in the hope of the coming resurrection, and they will enjoy it at the coming of Jesus Christ, who will not only raise them up but will also make them like his own glorious body, so that they may be fit to possess his heavenly Kingdom. Then death too will be swallowed up, the power of the underworld will be destroyed, and nothing will remain that can trouble God's elect; instead they will enjoy those excellent and unspeakable goods "which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor have entered into the heart of man" [1 Cor. 2.9].

units.la: Ex his iam facile intelligi potest, quid haec secunda petitione nos Christus a Patre suo caelesti rogare doceat, & ut ea in tentationibus nostris uti debeamus. Quia enim Regnum Dei absque diaboli regno recte considerari non potest, ante omnia petimus, ut Deus hoc destruere & eius vires frangere velit, ne nobis dominari & pro arbitrio miseros perdere possit. Et quia audiuimus, diaboli regnum suum propagare per mendacia, dolos, impostauras, idololatriam & incredulitatem, aduersus haec omnia petitio ista dirigitur. Precamur ergo, ut nos Deus a falsa doctrina custodire, hanc destruere & veritatis luce dissipare velit, ne quis per eam seducatur. Item ut incredulitatem superstitiones & idololatriam ex omnium animis excindat; adhaec ut ex peccati seruitio liberet, cogitationes foedas & impuras auferat, prauas cupiditates restinguat, peccati laqueos disrumpat, & totum diaboli regnum in nobis destruat. Quoniam vero ista ad salutem non sufficerent, postulamus praeterea, ut suum Regnum in nobis instauret. Fit hoc, quum corda nostra eius cognitione illuminantur, fide vera in Christum donantur, nosque per eius Spiritum & verbum renati innouamur & in nobis peccati membra mortificantur, adeo, ut toti Deo addicti per fidei obedientiam ei soli seruiamus. Ex his enim certo colligitur, illum in nobis vere regnare, nosque in illo viuere, & tandem regni ipsius caelestis atque aeterni participes fore. Continet ergo petitio haec, quaecunque salutem nostram promouere possunt.
units.tr: From these things it can now easily be understood what Christ teaches us to ask of his heavenly Father in this second petition, and why we ought to use it in our temptations. For since the Kingdom of God cannot rightly be considered apart from the kingdom of the devil, first of all we pray that God will be willing to destroy this kingdom and break its strength, so that it may not rule over us and destroy wretched men at its pleasure. And since we have heard that the devil propagates his kingdom through lies, deceits, impostures, idolatry and unbelief, this petition is directed against all of these. We therefore pray that God will guard us from false doctrine, will be willing to destroy it and scatter it by the light of truth, so that no one may be seduced by it. Likewise, that he will root out unbelief, superstition and idolatry from the minds of all; further, that he will free us from the bondage of sin, take away foul and impure thoughts, quench depraved desires, break the snares of sin, and destroy the whole kingdom of the devil within us. But since these things would not be enough for salvation, we further ask that he would restore his own Kingdom in us. This happens when our hearts are illuminated by the knowledge of him, are given true faith in Christ, and, being reborn, are renewed by his Spirit and Word, and the members of sin in us are mortified, so that, wholly devoted to God, we serve him alone through the obedience of faith. For from these things it is surely gathered that he truly reigns in us, that we live in him, and that at last we shall be partakers of his heavenly and eternal Kingdom. This petition therefore contains whatever can advance our salvation.

units.la: At quoniam petitionem hanc (ut & reliquas omnes) non nostro solum, sed omnium quoque aliorum hominum nomine Deo proponimus, comprehenduntur eadem omnes hominum ordines, quorum ministerio & opera Deus in regno suo prouehendo uti dignatur. Primi hic sunt verbi eius ministri, quos in ista precatione Deo quam maxime commendare debemus, ut (quod Paulus quoque rogabat) os eorum aperiat, & spiritum alacrem fortemque largiatur, ut verbum suum intrepide annuntient: ut deniq; eosdem contra hostium insidias tueatur, & ex inimicorum manibus eripiat. Exempla precum eiusmodi primitiua Ecclesia olim Apostolorum temporibus edidit. Deinde pro iis, qui in magistratu sunt, hic preces facimus (quod fieri Paulus iubet) ut hos Deus verbi sui cognitione illuminet, fide vera instruat, zelo Christi accendat, & Spiritu fortitudinis armet, ut regnum illud suum salutiferum magno serio prouehant, authoritate & potentia sua defendant, quod olim sanctissimos Reges, Davidem, Ezechiam, Iosiam, Constantinum M. Theodosium & horum similes magna cum laude fecisse scimus. Et huc pertinet Psalmus LXXXII. qui pulcherrimam pro principibus precandi formulam subditis omnibus praescribit. Similiter pro parentibus omnibus hic oramus, ut & ipsi syncero pietatis studio accensi ex se natos liberos Deo adducant, eosdem in huius cognitione & vero cultu diligenter instituant. Et hoc inter externa media, quibus Dei Regnum in terris hisce instauratur, nequaquam postremum censeri debet. Praeterea Scholas quoque Deo commendamus, ut has conservare, & suo Spiritu tam doctores quam discipulos regere dignetur, ne vnquam desint viri docti & sapientes, qui rempub. bene administrent. Ecclesijs fideliter praesint, Dei verbum clare praedicent, errores & falsa dogmata fortiter confutent, fidem veram atque Dei cultum fideliter plantent, & ea ratione Regnum Dei in dies promovebant. Quantum enim ad huius conservationem Scholae faciant, impius quoque & astutus apostata Iulianus intellexit, qui illas Christianos claudit, ita fore sperans, ut idoneos doctoribus tandem destituti non possent fidem suam aduersus Sophistarum fallacias tueri. Denique ut summatim omnia dicamus, nihil est quod ad Regni Dei instaurationem sive propagationem facit, quod non hac petitione Christus comprehenda t. Nam praeter haec, quae hucusque commemoravimus, precamur quoque, ut sub cruce & afflictionum pondere laborantes Deus suo spiritu confirmet, ne vel impatientia vel aliis affectibus superati ab eo defectionem faciamus, sed omnia aduersa, persecutiones & tentationes omnes fidei constantia & fortitudine vincamus.
units.tr: But since we offer this petition to God (as indeed all the others) not only in our own name but also in the name of all other men, all the orders of men are included in it, and by their ministry and work God deigns to use them in advancing his Kingdom. The first here are the ministers of his Word, whom in this prayer we ought above all to commend to God, that (as Paul also asked) he may open their mouths and grant them a ready and bold spirit, so that they may proclaim his Word fearlessly; and finally that he may protect them against the snares of their enemies and snatch them from the hands of their foes. The primitive Church set examples of such prayers in the times of the Apostles. Next, for those who hold magistracy we make prayers here (as Paul bids us do), that God would enlighten them with the knowledge of his Word, instruct them in true faith, kindle them with zeal for Christ, and arm them with the Spirit of strength, so that they may advance that salutary Kingdom of his with great earnestness and defend it by their authority and power. We know that the most holy kings did this with great praise: David, Hezekiah, Josiah, Constantine the Great, Theodosius and others like them. To this belongs Psalm 82, which prescribes to all subjects a most beautiful form of prayer for princes. Similarly, here we pray for all parents, that they too, kindled with sincere zeal for godliness, may bring the children born of them to God and diligently instruct them in his knowledge and true worship. Nor should this be considered the least among the external means by which the Kingdom of God is restored in these lands. Furthermore, we also commend the schools to God, that he may deign to preserve them and, by his Spirit, to rule both teachers and pupils, so that there may never be lacking learned and wise men who govern the commonwealth well, preside faithfully over the churches, preach God's Word clearly, vigorously refute errors and false dogmas, faithfully plant the true faith and the worship of God, and by this means advance the Kingdom of God day by day. For the impious and crafty apostate Julian understood how much the schools contribute to its preservation, when he closed them to Christians, hoping that they would in the end be left without learned teachers and so be unable to defend their faith against the fallacies of the sophists. In short, to say everything in summary: there is nothing that pertains to the restoration or propagation of the Kingdom of God which Christ does not include in this petition. For besides those things we have so far mentioned, we also pray that God would strengthen by his Spirit those who labour under the cross and the weight of afflictions, so that we, overcome by impatience or other passions, may not fall away from him, but may conquer all adversities, persecutions and temptations by constancy and fortitude of faith.

units.la: Sed priusquam Sermonem hunc concludamus, adhuc quaedam consideranda veniunt, quae nostrae salutis negotium & simul nostrum in hoc officium concernunt. Primo enim hac petitione nostram miseriam, adeoque exilium nostrum bifariam confitemur. Dum enim oramus, ut Regnum Dei ad nos veniat, satis aperte testamur, nos eo adhuc carere, imo quod extra Regnum Dei in exilio agamus. Est haec ingens miseria, quam omnes electi probe expenderunt, & ideo huius seculi vitam peregrinationem, seipsos autem peregrinos dixerunt, ut qui ad patriam nondum pervenissent. Fatemur praeterea nos proprijs viribus aut meritis Regnum Dei assequi non posse, sed necesse esse, ut illud ad nos veniat. Ut enim primum in caelum non potuimus ascendere, sed Filium Dei ad nos descendere oportuit, ut nos salvos faceret: Ita porro requiritur, ut Deus Spiritum suum nobis caelitus mittat, per quem regeneremur & quasi manu ducamur, ut in nobis ille regnare queat. Quae causa est, quod Christus hunc toties pollicetur, & promissione hanc tunc quoque repetit, quando discipuli de Regno suo ipsum interrogabant, ut doceret, Regnum hoc coeleste esse, quod ad nos e supernis venire oporteat. Confutantur hic validissime peregrinationes sacrae & omnium illorum errores, qui Regnum Dei, id est, salutem suam hinc inde quaerunt, quasi ea certus locus alligata sit: cum Christus Iesus unicum illud gratiae divinae pignus sit, in quo solo salus inveniatur, & qui nulli certo loco in terris alligatus est, sed in caelis ad dextram Patris residet, unde Spiritum suum nobis mittit, meritum suum largitur, & ubique locorum in nobis agit ea, quae nobis ad consequendum Regnum Dei necessaria sunt. Idem nunquam docet, ut hinc inde discurrendo illud assequi conemur, sed ut precemur, ut ad nos veniat. Monet praeterea nos, ne illis fidem habeamus, qui ipsum & salutem nostram certus in locis monstrant, simulque testantur Regnum Dei non venturum ita ut observari possit, etc. Luc. 17. Matth. 24.
units.tr: But before we conclude this sermon, there are still some matters to consider, which concern the business of our salvation and at the same time our duty in it. First, by this petition we confess our misery, and therefore our exile, in two ways. For when we pray that the Kingdom of God may come to us, we testify quite plainly that we are still without it, indeed that we live in exile outside the Kingdom of God. This is a great misery, which all the elect have weighed well; therefore they called the life of this age a pilgrimage, and themselves pilgrims, as those who had not yet arrived at their homeland. We further confess that we cannot attain the Kingdom of God by our own strength or merits, but that it is necessary for it to come to us. For just as we could not at first ascend into heaven, but it was necessary for the Son of God to descend to us in order to save us, so likewise it is required that God send his Spirit to us from heaven, through whom we may be regenerated and, as it were, led by the hand, so that he may be able to reign in us. This is why Christ promises it so often, and repeats the promise then too, when the disciples asked him about his Kingdom, so that he might teach that this Kingdom is heavenly and must come to us from above. Here the sacred pilgrimages and all the errors of those are most powerfully refuted who seek the Kingdom of God, that is, their salvation, here and there, as if it were bound to a certain place; whereas Christ Jesus is the only pledge of divine grace, in whom alone salvation is found. He is bound to no fixed place on earth, but sits in heaven at the right hand of the Father, whence he sends his Spirit to us, bestows his merit, and everywhere works in us those things which are necessary for us to obtain the Kingdom of God. He does not teach us to try to obtain it by running hither and thither, but to pray that it may come to us. He also warns us not to give credence to those who point out Christ and our salvation in certain places, and at the same time testify that the Kingdom of God will not come in such a way that it can be observed, etc. [Luke 17; Matt. 24].

units.la: Rursus officij nostri haec petitio nos admonet. Quia enim oramus, ut Regnum Dei adveniat, & in terris hisce propagetur, docet vtiq;, ut singuli quoad seipsos huic sese subiciant, et diaboli castris relictis Deo obedire ac viuere satagant: denique ut illud apud alios quoque pro virili instaurent atque propagent. Nam si in eo negligentiores simus coram Deo, nos hypocrisis precatio ista arguit. Excitet nos ergo ut quo possumus studio omnibus ijs obstemus, quibus regnum Dei impeditur, studeamus autem ijs quibus promovetur. Ad se igitur hoc singuli transferant pro sua vocationis ratione. Nam si verbi administri precatione hac digne vti velint, necesse fuerit, ut Christi exemplum imitati zelo gloriae & regni Dei ardeant, adeo ut nihil eorum ferre possint quae huic adversantur, & e contra absque omni personarum respectu omnes id agat, quo illud promoveri posse videt. Exemplum huius zeli in Paulo habemus, qui quocunque locorum venit, annunciandi regni Dei occasione captavit. Athenis intolerabile videtur urbem celeberrimam prae aliis idololatriae deditam esse, & insuper Deo ignoto sacra facere; & ideo hinc occasionem arripit de vero Deo apud illos concionandi, quem hucusque ignorauerant. Simili studio Corinthi quoq; Ephesi & vbique alibi vsu est, & ideo vas electum à Domino dicitur. Qui hunc imitantur doctores, ij demum vere precabuntur, & eos Deus exaudiet, vt & ipsi organa gloriæ sint. At qui negligentes & securi rerum, superstitiones, idololatriam & aperta scelera ferre possunt, atque vt muti canes (quo nomine eos Isaias appellat) omnia fieri patiuntur, quæ ad Regni Dei destructionem faciunt, ij hac precatione seipsos damnant, cum proprio ore testentur, se maiori studio in munere suo versari debere. Eadem est eorum ratio, qui rempub administrant, qui & ipsi Regnum Dei pro virili promovere, & diaboli regnum destruere debent, nisi preces suas inutiles esse velint. Idem de parentibus & omnibus iuuentutis gubernatoribus, denique de Christianis omnibus debet intelligi. Nam vt alibi diximus, hypocritas Deus ferre non potest, & dum preces facimus, hoc præcipue nobis cauendum est, ne ore solum Deo appropinquemus, corde autem ab eo alieni simus.
units.tr: Again, this petition reminds us of our duty. Because we pray that the kingdom of God may come and be spread in these lands, it teaches, of course, that each of us should first submit himself to it, leave the camp of the devil, and strive to live in obedience to God; and finally, that we should also set it up and spread it among others, as far as each of us is able. For if we are more careless in this before God, this prayer convicts us of hypocrisy. Let it therefore stir us up to oppose with all the zeal we can all those things by which the kingdom of God is hindered, and to labour for those things by which it is advanced. Let each one apply this to himself according to the nature of his calling. For if the ministers of the Word are to use this prayer worthily, they must imitate the example of Christ and burn with zeal for the glory and kingdom of God, so that they cannot bear anything that opposes it, and on the other hand, without any regard for persons, they must do whatever they see can advance it. We have an example of this zeal in Paul, who, wherever he came, seized the occasion of proclaiming the kingdom of God. At Athens it seemed intolerable that a city so famous, above others given over to idolatry, should even offer sacrifice to the unknown God; and so he seizes on this occasion to preach among them about the true God, whom they had until then not known. He used the same zeal at Corinth, at Ephesus and everywhere else, and therefore he is called by the Lord a chosen vessel. Those teachers who imitate him will at last pray truly, and God will hear them, so that they too may be instruments of his glory. But those who are careless and unconcerned about these things, and can bear superstitions, idolatry and open crimes, and who, like dumb dogs (the name Isaiah gives them), allow everything to be done that tends to the destruction of the kingdom of God, these condemn themselves by this prayer, since by their own mouth they testify that they ought to labour in their office with greater zeal. The same is the case with those who administer the commonwealth, who too ought to advance the kingdom of God as far as they can and destroy the kingdom of the devil, unless they wish their prayers to be useless. The same must be understood of parents and of all those who govern the young, and finally of all Christians. For, as we have said elsewhere, God cannot bear hypocrites, and while we pray we must above all take care that we do not draw near to God with the mouth only while our heart is far from him.

units.la: Docet præterea petitio ista, Regnum Dei ante omnia quærendum esse, neque nos rebus terrenis & temporarijs nimium addictos esse debere. Nam vt supra audiuimus, hic quidem in nobis Regnum Dei inchoatur, in cœlis autem demum perficietur, vt plenum complementum habeat. Siergo huius ex animo cupidi sumus, necesse est, vt eius perfectum complementum quæramus, adiuentu Christi diligamus, & hunc nobis constituamus actionum & studiorum nostrorum finem, vt in cœlesti patria Regnum Dei possidere, & cum Christo æternum regnare possimus. Quotquot ergo huius seculi rebus addicti, nihil præter opes, honores & voluptates animo volutant, ij zelo Regni Dei flagrare non possunt, & proinde nullum huius petitionis fructum sentient, sed per eam potius damnabuntur. Impossibile enim est, vt Regnum Dei in cœlis possideant, & cum Christo regnent, qui dum hic viuunt, illi subesse nolunt.
units.tr: This petition further teaches that the kingdom of God must be sought above all things, and that we must not be too much devoted to earthly and temporal things. For, as we heard above, the kingdom of God is begun in us here, but it will be finally perfected in heaven, so that it may have its full completion. If therefore we eagerly desire this, we must seek its perfect completion, long for the coming of Christ, and set this before us as the end of our actions and endeavours: that we may possess the kingdom of God in the heavenly fatherland and reign eternally with Christ. Therefore, as many as are devoted to the affairs of this age, and turn over in their minds nothing but wealth, honours and pleasures, cannot burn with zeal for the kingdom of God, and consequently they will feel no fruit from this petition, but will rather be condemned by it. For it is impossible that they should possess the kingdom of God in heaven and reign with Christ, who while they live here are unwilling to be subject to him.

units.la: Et hac quidem in secundam Orationis Dominicæ petitionem dicta sint, quæ vniuersum nostra salutis negotium comprehendit, vna cum ijs quæ Deo debemus. Debet illa nobis eo magis cordi esse, quod multis argumentis deprehendimus, quam varie & graviter Regnum Dei oppugnetur. Faciunt hoc falsi doctores ac impostores plurimi, qui doctrinam salutis traditionibus hominum & propriis figmentis impudentissime obscurarunt, & simplices à Regno Dei abducunt. Et hi quidem patronos habent potentissimos, qui armis quoque eos tuentur. Inde sequitur, quod fideles Christi cultores omnium fere odijs subiacent, sedibus suis eiecti exulant, fortunis spoliantur, & demum crudeliter occiduntur. Eò deniq; res deuenit, prob dolor, vt nullum scelus gravius esse æstimetur, quam si quis fidelem Regni Dei subditum esse præbere studeat. Taceo nunc horribiles clades à Turcis intra paucos annos acceptas, per quas infinita millia animarum à Christo abstulsa, & Mahumeticis abominationibus subiecta sunt. Taceo exemplum mundi huius sceleratissimum, effrenem multorum petulantiam, scelera aperta, quæ passim magno cum scandalo patiuntur, & Dei regno plurimum officiunt. Quæ omnia eiusmodi sunt, vt non temere suspicemur, esse iam tempora illa, quibus fidem cessaturam, charitatem interituram esse Christus prædixit. Est ergo huius petitionis consideratio valde necessaria: videndum vero nobis est, vt eam non ore solum recitemus, sed quod docet reipsa præstemus: vt Regnum Dei hic in nobis feliciter inchoatum, per nos etiam longè lateque propagetur, tandem vero in cœlis æterni illius regni consortes simus per Christum Iesum Dominum nostrum: cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: And let these things be said concerning the second petition of the Lord's Prayer, which embraces the whole business of our salvation, together with those things which we owe to God. It ought to be all the more dear to our hearts because we perceive by many arguments how variously and grievously the kingdom of God is assailed. Many false teachers and impostors do this, who most shamelessly obscure the doctrine of salvation with the traditions of men and their own inventions, and draw the simple away from the kingdom of God. And these indeed have most powerful patrons, who even defend them with arms. Hence it follows that the faithful worshippers of Christ are almost everywhere subject to hatred, are driven from their homes into exile, are stripped of their property, and at last are cruelly slain. Things have come to such a point, alas, that no crime is judged more grievous than for someone to strive to be a faithful subject of the kingdom of God. I say nothing now of the horrible disasters received within a few years from the Turks, by which infinite thousands of souls have been taken away from Christ and subjected to Mohammedan abominations. I say nothing of the most wicked example of this world, the unbridled wantonness of many, the open crimes which everywhere they suffer with great scandal, and which greatly harm the kingdom of God. All these things are such that we do not rashly suspect that those times are now at hand, in which Christ foretold that faith would fail and love would perish. Therefore the consideration of this petition is very necessary: and we must take care not only to recite it with the mouth, but to put into practice what it teaches, so that the kingdom of God, happily begun here in us, may also be spread far and wide through us, and at last we may be partners of that eternal kingdom in heaven through Christ Jesus our Lord: to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA. CIX.
units.tr: HOMILY CIX.

units.la: PETITIO III. Fiat voluntas tua, sicut in coelo, etiam in terra.
units.tr: PETITION III. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth.

units.la: Dominus noster Iesus Christus in precandi formula, quâ discipulis & nobis omnibus tradidit petitiones ita connectit, vt alia ex alia quasi deriuetur. Primo enim germanos Dei filios precari docet, vt Patris nostri cœlestis nomen sanctificetur, et vt suum tam in nobis quam alijs hominibus honorem obtineat. Est hoc precum nostrarum fundamentum verum, & hic omnium studiorum nostrorum finis esse debet. At quia illud fieri nequit, quoad Satan in nobis regnat & agit, qui nomi-nis & gloriæ Dei hostis acerrimus est, secundo loco petimus, ut Deus suum Regnum in nobis in-stauret, & per hoc diaboli regnum destruat. Atqui in nobis Deus regnare non potest, nisi nos il-li totos dedamus, & ad obediendum voluntati eius parati ac proni simus. Commodissimo igitur or-dine tertia petitio subtexitur, quæ est: Fiat voluntas tua, sicut in cœlo & in terra. Quibus verbis nos tam animo quam corpore Deo addicimus, simulque ostendimus, æquum esse, ut suo Regno ad nos ille veniat, & in suam protectione nos suscipiat, cum ipsius voluntati parere, & omne obsequiū ei præstare cupiamus.
units.tr: Our Lord Jesus Christ, in the form of prayer by which he taught his disciples and all of us, links the petitions so that one arises from another. First he teaches the true children of God to pray that the name of our heavenly Father may be hallowed and that he may obtain his honour both in us and in other men. This is the true foundation of our prayers, and it ought to be the goal of all our efforts. But since this cannot happen while Satan, the most bitter enemy of God's name and glory, rules and works in us, in the second place we ask that God would establish his kingdom in us and by this destroy the kingdom of the devil. Yet God cannot reign in us unless we surrender ourselves wholly to him and are ready and inclined to obey his will. Therefore the third petition follows in the most fitting order: "Thy will be done, as in heaven and on earth." By these words we devote ourselves to God both in soul and in body, and at the same time we show that it is right for him to come to us with his kingdom and take us under his protection, since we desire to obey his will and render him every service.

units.la: Priusquā vero huius petitionis sensum excutiamur, diligentius hoc expendi debet, cur ut Dei Patris voluntas fiat, precari iubeamur: & nō potius ut nostræ voluntati ille indulgeat, & hanc ra-tam esse velit? Etenim cum communi sensu pugnare videtur, ut quis propria voluntate posthabita alienæ sese subijciat. At in promptu causa est. Quia enim Christus ea petere docet, quæ nobis vtilia & salutaria sunt: non potuit iubere ut nostram voluntatem fieri velimus, quæ mala, iniusta et no-xia est. Quod facile apparebit, si naturā nostrā & carnis ingenii diligenter consideremus.
