These words contain the following argument: Whoever invades the house of a powerful and sturdy man and plunders it must be stronger than him, so that he can overcome even the one who resists. But I invade the house of the prince of demons, I bind and restrain him, and even against his will I snatch from him the people whom he has hitherto used as his vessels. Therefore I am stronger than he is, and I have so little in common with him that I am rather the one who must destroy his kingdom and disarm him completely. The major premise is proved by the common sense of all, since all creatures want their possessions kept safe, and no one is so lazy that he would allow them to be plundered if he could defend them. The minor premise is proved by Christ's miracles, which he now brings back to their minds, especially those by which people possessed by demons were daily delivered through him. At the same time, he also makes a second point here, namely that this business is not accomplished without force and labour, because Satan yields the ground with difficulty and is well armed and equipped for the defence of his kingdom. Luke expresses this, and we have quoted his words a little earlier. Both accounts, however, come to the same sense, and in a few words the Lord sums up the nature of our common enemy together with the whole business of our redemption.

units.la: Validus enim ille & fortis diabolus est, quae alibi sub Leuiathan, immanis & indomita bellua marinae typo Scriptura depingit, ut illius vires atque indomitum ingenium exprimat. Domus siue aula eius est mundus hic, cuius princeps dicitur, eo quod in ijs regnet & triumphet, qui toti rebus huius mundi addicti caelestia & aeterna bona negligunt. Vasa eius sunt homines, qui in primo parente Adamo illius mancipia facti sunt, & quibus ille ad superstitiones, idololatriam, scelera omnis generis, deniq; ad horrendos etiam furores abutitur. Et haec quidem possessio illi multis seculis tuta & tranquilla fuit. Nam etsi apud Patriarchas promissiones de futura redemptione extarent, & inter Iudaeos vera Dei cognitio vna cum promissionibus illis traderetur, reliquas tamen gentes sub potestate tenebrarum detinebat, ut ia nihil dicamus de Israelitis & magna Iudaeorum parte, qui & ipsi religio Deo & cultu eius illi seruierunt. Neq; opus fuit, ut ob regnum defendendum tumultuaretur, cum illud pauci oppugnarent, & ipse armis validis atque idoneis esset instructus. Inter gentes enim falsa sapientia regnabat, quam philosophi profitebantur, qui suis disputationibus veri Dei cognitionem indies obscurabant. Maxima item erat oraculorum authoritas, quae neglecto Dei verbo in rebus ardus consulebantur, & per quae responsis partim obscuris, partim ambiguis Satan infelices homines mirifice ludificabat. Accedebat Regum & principum potentia, qui superstitiones & falsos cultus summo studio tuebantur, adeo ut Deos illos fictitios negare capitale esset, sicut in Socratis & multorum aliorum exemplis est videre. Inter haec omnia autem effrenis erat morum licentia, & scelerum impunitate pleriq; trahebantur, ut mutationem nullam vellent admittere. Neq; multo melior fuit rerum conditio apud Iudaeos, ut in Prophetarum Sermonibus est videre, nisi quod Deus ex singulari gratia seminarium quoddam suorum electorum subinde seruabat, ex quo Ecclesia suo tempore instaurare tur. Quia ergo his artibus eo rem Satan adduxerat, ut sponte ipsi omnes parerent, imo eius seruitio quantumus turpi & infelici delectarentur, vtiq; in pace erant eius omnia, & tranquilla regni male acquisiti possessione fruebatur. Neq; hic aliqua liberationis aut melioris sortis spes erat in hominibus, cum eadem esset omnium conditio, ut nemo sibijpsi opem ferre, nedum alios seruare posset. Nam propter innatam omnibus naturae prauitatem & vitia, quae ex illa nascuntur, in eos etiam ius aliquod erat diabolo, qui atrocibus sceleribus no erat polluti. Itaq; aliquo validiore & fortiore vindice opus fuit, qui tantis praesidijs munitus & tam probe armatum vinceret. Is vero est Iesus Christus aeternus Dei Filius, qui praefinito tempore homo factus est, ut nos ex infelici tyrannide afferret. Fortior is & potentior dicitur diabolo, non solum quoad diuinam naturam, & quod omnem potestatem illi Pater tradidit: verumetiam quoad assumptam carnem. Quia enim absq; omni peccato ex Spiritu sancto conceptus, & ex Virgine casta atq; impolluta natus est, ab omni etiam originalis vitij labe immunis fuit, & ideo nihil in eum iuris habuit improbus ille tyrannus, qui in reliquos homines imperium per peccatum obtinuerat. Venit ergo in mundum, id est, in diaboli domum & aulam Christus, & mox cum illo pugnare cœpit. Initium certaminis enim statim à baptismo in deserto factum est, vbi gloriosa victoria eum repulit, & nobis quoq; eius vincendi rationem monstrauit. Inde apertius cum illo congressus est, quando totam Iudæam & Galilæam Regni Dei prædicatione compleuit, & omnes tantum non excitauit, vt reliĉto infelici Satanæ seruitio illud ampleĉterentur. Doctrinæ miracula accesserunt, inter quæ in primis memorabilia sunt, quòd dæmonia ex obsessis hominibus eie cit, vt ostenderet, iam adesse tempus illud optatum, quo Satanæ ex possessione sua deturbari, & Regnum Dei instaurari oporteret. Iam tum ergo in multorum animis labefactatu est diaboli regnum. Tandem vero illius iugulum petijt Christus, quando in ara crucis mundi peccata expiauit, resurre ĉtione autem sua mortem deuicit, vt credentibus peccati pœna esse desierit. Itaq; omnem armaturā, qua maxime considebat Satan, ei abstulit, peccatum nimirum & mortem: & quod in primis memo rabile est, oraculis quoq; quibus gentes deceptas & dementatas fuisse diximus, silentium imposuit, vt exteri quoq; scriptores testantur. Iam ergo constrictus erat improbus ille, & eius vasa Christus diripuit atq; spolia distribuit. Homines enim, quibus hucusq; turpissimè abusus fuerat, ex eius potestate assertos Patri Deo adduxit, & variis destinauit functionibus, in quibus illi seruientes Regnum ipsius propagarent. Secutus est victoriam gloriosus triumphus, Ascensio Christi nimirum, in qua (vt Paulus ait) supra omnes cælos vectus captiuam duxit captiuitatē, & cœlitus dona Spiritus sui Apostolis atq; viris Apostolicis distribuit, quibus hi ceu armis validissimis instructi, in totum orbem egressi sunt, & salutifera Euangelij prædicatione mundum, cuius princeps iam deuictus & vinctus iacebat, ad Christum adduxerunt. Et hoc illud est, de quo ipse in præsenti loquitur.
units.tr: For that strong and mighty devil is the one whom Scripture elsewhere depicts under the type of Leviathan, a huge and untamed sea monster, in order to express his power and his untameable nature. His house or palace is this world, of which he is called the prince, because he reigns and triumphs over those who are wholly given over to the things of this world and neglect heavenly and eternal goods. His vessels are the men who in the first parent, Adam, became his slaves, and whom he uses for superstitions, idolatry, crimes of every kind, and finally even for dreadful frenzies. This possession was safe and quiet for him for many centuries. For although promises of a future redemption stood among the patriarchs, and the true knowledge of God was handed down among the Jews along with those promises, he nevertheless held the other nations under the power of darkness, not to mention the Israelites and a great part of the Jews, who also served him in their own religion, and in the worship of God. Nor was there any need for him to be disturbed in defending his kingdom, since only a few attacked it, and he himself was equipped with strong and fitting arms. Among the nations a false wisdom reigned, which the philosophers professed, and who by their disputations daily obscured the knowledge of the true God. Likewise, the authority of oracles was very great, and in matters of difficulty they were consulted in place of God's word, and through their replies, some obscure and some ambiguous, Satan wonderfully deceived unhappy men. Added to this was the power of kings and princes, who with the greatest zeal defended superstitions and false worship, so that to deny those fictitious gods was a capital offence, as can be seen from the examples of Socrates and many others. Among all these things, moreover, unrestrained licence in morals prevailed, and most people were carried away by crimes committed with impunity, so that they were unwilling to admit any change. Nor was the condition of things much better among the Jews, as can be seen in the sermons of the prophets, except that God, out of singular grace, from time to time preserved a certain seed of his elect, from which the Church was to be restored in its own time. Since Satan had therefore brought matters by these arts to the point where all men obeyed him willingly, and even delighted in his most shameful and unhappy service, all his affairs were in peace, and he enjoyed the quiet possession of his ill-gotten kingdom. Nor was there any hope of liberation or of a better lot among men, since the condition of all was the same, so that no one could bring help to himself, let alone save others. For, on account of the innate corruption of nature in all and the vices that spring from it, the devil also had some right over those who were not polluted by atrocious crimes. Therefore a stronger and mightier deliverer was needed, one who, fortified with such great resources and so well armed, might conquer. This is indeed Jesus Christ, the eternal Son of God, who at the appointed time was made man, that he might rescue us from the unhappy tyranny. He is said to be stronger and mightier than the devil, not only with respect to his divine nature, and because the Father has delivered all power to him, but also with respect to the flesh he assumed. For since he was conceived by the Holy Spirit without any sin, and born of a chaste and undefiled Virgin, he was also free from every stain of original vice; and therefore that wicked tyrant, who had obtained dominion over the rest of mankind through sin, had no right over him. Christ therefore came into the world, that is, into the house and palace of the devil, and soon began to fight with him. For the beginning of the conflict was made at once, from his baptism, in the desert, where he repelled him with glorious victory, and also showed us the way of overcoming him. Afterwards he engaged him more openly, when he filled all Judea and Galilee with the preaching of the kingdom of God, and almost roused everyone to abandon the unhappy service of Satan and embrace that kingdom. To his teaching were added miracles, among which the most memorable were that he cast out demons from the possessed, to show that the longed-for time had now come, when Satan had to be thrown down from his possession and the kingdom of God set up. Even then, therefore, the devil's kingdom was shaken in the minds of many. At last Christ struck at his throat, when on the altar of the cross he expiated the sins of the world, and by his resurrection he conquered death, so that for believers it has ceased to be the punishment of sin. Thus he took from Satan all the armour in which he chiefly trusted, namely sin and death; and, what is especially memorable, he also imposed silence on the oracles by which, as we have said, the nations were deceived and driven out of their minds, as foreign writers also testify. Now that wicked one was bound, and Christ plundered his vessels and distributed the spoils. For the men whom he had so shamefully abused until then he rescued from his power, brought them to God the Father, and assigned them to various offices, in which, serving him, they might spread his kingdom. The victory was followed by a glorious triumph, namely Christ's ascension, in which (as Paul says) being carried above all the heavens, he led captivity captive, and from heaven distributed the gifts of his Spirit to the apostles and apostolic men, who, as if equipped with the most powerful arms, went out into the whole world, and by the saving preaching of the gospel brought to Christ the world, over which its prince now lay conquered and bound. And this is what he himself is speaking of in the present passage.

units.la: Num vero ista absq; labore & periculo facta sunt? Nequaquam. Imò cum improbus ille & versipellis hostis tempus illud fatale appropinquare videret, etiam antequam in mundum veniret Dei Filius, tumultuari cœpit, vt eius aduentum omnibus inuisum atq; suspectum faceret. Ciuilibus enim Romanorum bellis per Iulium & Pompeium excitatis, totum orbem turbauit, & paulò ante Pompeium in Iudæam adduxit, qui vrbe capta sanctum quoq; sanctorum ingressus prophano intui tu illud polluit, & Iudæorum gentem libertate spoliatam Romanorum tyrannidi subiecit. Secuta sunt mox graviora, quando Augustus & Antonius infelici genti Herodem Regem dederunt, qui & omnem regiam atq; sacerdotalem prosapiam trucidauit, Seniorum Senatum (quem illi corrupto Græco vocabulo Sanhedrim dicebant) aboleuit, sacerdotium vero ad homines obscuros & impro bos transtulit. Idè iam nato Christo crudeles insidias struxit, qua occasione infantes Bethlehemitici nouo & inaudito crudelitatis exemplo cæsi sunt. Quod non alia ratione fieri voluit Satan, quàm vt toti isti vicinia, in qua Filij Dei natiuitas primum per Angelos pastoribus innotuerat, ipsam quoq; Christi mentionem inuisam faceret, & publico tot parentum luctu Angelos mendacij suspectos red deret, qui gaudium ingens toti populo denuntiarant. Postea autem Christo docenti & per miraculaे sua virtute simul atq; aduentus sui causam manifestati, sese per Sacerdotes, Scribas, Seniores, Pharisæos, Herodem & innumeros alios magno conatu opposuit, qui non ante ab instituto desiterunt, quàm ille in crucem suffixus fuit. Et quàmuis per mortem Christi letale vulnus sibi inflictum esse Sentiret Satan, tamen huius quoq; meritum vnà cum illius resurrectione partim apertis mendacijs atq; calumnijs, partim falsa doctrina apud omnes in dubium vocare conatus est. Sed & in priuatis hominibus abunde ostendit, quanta sit sua pertinacia, tunc maximè insaniendo & tumultuando, quando ipsum Christum ex aliquo obsessorum eijcere voluit. At vbi posse huius ascensionem Apostoli Euangelium inter Iudæos & gentes prædicauerunt, tunc demum, victus licet & exarmatus, non vas turbas dedit, excitatis passim per Iudæos non solum persecutionibus, verumetiam seditionibus publicis, vt Christi prædicationem Romanus, qui tunc rerum domini erant, exosam redderet. Neq; ipsum spes sua omnino fefellit. Mox enim Nero contra Christianos edicta promulgauit, & plures illorum sub falso Romæ ab eis incendiæ crimine crudeliter occidit, vt Cornelius Tacitus, scriptor alioqui nobis non amicus, perhibet. Secuti sunt plures alij ex Imperatoribus, quorum crudelitas per annos trecentos fere longius & latius grassata est.
units.tr: But did these things happen without toil and danger? By no means. When that wicked and crafty enemy saw that the fated time was drawing near, he began to stir up tumult even before the Son of God came into the world, so as to make his coming hateful and suspect to everyone. Through Julius and Pompey he stirred up the civil wars of the Romans and threw the whole world into turmoil. Shortly afterwards he brought Pompey into Judea, who, after taking the city, entered the holy of holies and defiled it with profane gaze, and who stripped the Jewish nation of its liberty and subjected it to Roman tyranny. Worse things followed soon after, when Augustus and Antony gave King Herod to the unhappy nation. He slaughtered the whole royal and priestly line, abolished the council of elders (which they called the Sanhedrin, using a corrupted Greek word), and transferred the priesthood to obscure and wicked men. Then, once Christ was born, he laid cruel snares, and on that occasion the infants of Bethlehem were slain, a new and unheard-of example of cruelty. Satan wanted this done for no other reason than that the whole neighbourhood, where the birth of the Son of God had first been made known to the shepherds by angels, would come to hate even the mention of Christ, and that by the public grief of so many parents the angels who had announced great joy to the whole people would be made to seem liars. Afterwards, when Christ was teaching and had been made known by the power of his miracles and the cause of his coming, Satan set himself against him with great effort through the priests, scribes, elders, Pharisees, Herod, and countless others, and they did not desist from their purpose until he was fixed to the cross. And although Satan felt that a deadly wound had been inflicted on himself by the death of Christ, he nevertheless tried to call into doubt the merit of that death, together with his resurrection, partly by open lies and slanders, partly by false teaching among all people. But he also showed abundantly, even in private individuals, how stubborn he was, raging and stirring up tumult then most of all, when he tried to cast Christ out of one of the possessed. But when the apostles began to preach the gospel among Jews and Gentiles after Christ's ascension, then at last, though defeated and disarmed, he did not give up his disturbances, stirring up persecutions and also public seditions among the Jews everywhere, so that the Romans, who then were masters of affairs, might make the preaching of Christ hateful. Nor did his hope fail him altogether. For soon Nero issued edicts against the Christians, and cruelly put many of them to death at Rome on the false charge of arson, as Cornelius Tacitus, a writer otherwise not friendly to us, reports. Several other emperors followed, whose cruelty raged far and wide for nearly three hundred years.

units.la: Et hæc quidem fusiori & prolixiori narratione voluimus exponere, vt omnibus pateat, diabolu nô spote regno suo cessisse, sed in eo eijciedo diuina virtute simul & multo sanguine opus fuisse, adeoq; culi turbis ob- totum orbem terrarum illius furoribus fuisse turbatum, priusquā Christo locum daret. Sunt autem fendatur. hac probè obseruanda aduersus eos, qui nostri seculi turbis, seditionibus & bellis intestinis offendun-tur, & nobis pacem & otium illud magnificè iactant, quo totus orbis olim recepta & seruata pas-sim Papistica religione sit vsus. Multi etiam dum motus hosce Euangelio acceptos ferunt, non sine summa impietate Christum seditionum, bellorum & homicidiorum authorem faciunt. Atqui isto-rum malorum patrem & authorem esse constat diabolum. Christus autem pacis princeps est, & Euangelium pacis præconium est, quo vt ad vnum Deum omnes vocamur, ita vt per fidem in vnum corpus coalescamus & mutuam inter nos charitatem foueamus, docet. Itaq; ne fallamur, dia-boli ingenium nos diligentius obseruare oportet. In pace sunt & tranquilla eius omnia, dum armis & præsidijs munitus, regnum obtinet, & à nemine infestatur. Studet enim otij & pacis voluptati-bus suos continere, ne ad libertatem filiorum Dei aspirent. Et hic astutia admirabili vtitur, vt qui sententijs dissident, se tamen mutuò ferant, & speciem concordiæ foueant. Sic olim gentes, etiamsi diuersos Deos ritibus quoq; inter se diuersissimus colerent, consensum tamē habuerunt in oppugnan-do vero Deo, neque aliqui alijs propter religionis diuersitatem molestiam fecerunt. Et hodie in Pa-patu non eosdem Diuos inuocant omnes, neq; eadem omnino sacrorum forma aut ritu vtuntur, at-tamen inter sese consentiunt. Idem inter homines sceleratos est videre, qui etsi affectibus diuersis ducantur, concordiam tamen & amicitiam inter se mirificè conseruare norunt. At quia eiusmodi concordia per se minimè bona est, & in erroribus atq; vitijs homines confirmat, minimè probari meretur, & diaboli opus est, qui ideo quiescit, quòd omnia sua in tuto esse videt. Idem verò quàm primùm oppugnatur, & sibi loco cedendum esse sentit, mox in furorem conuersus cælum terræ misce-re conatur, vt regnum male occupatum peioribus artibus retineat. Hinc ergo parentū & filiorum dissidia, fratrum contentiones, rerumpub. motus, seditiones, bella cùm extera tum ciuilia, cædes & omnis generis mala nascuntur, quibus Euangelij doctrinam & reformationem orbis improbus ille conatur impedire. Et iuuat eum non mediocriter mundus infelix, qui lucem veritatis per se odit, ne eius opera mala arguantur. Nimium ergo iniqui iudices sunt, qui hæc nobis & Euangelio expro-brant, vt hoc falsi conuincant. Etenim hoc potius argumento constat, virtutem diuinam adesse, & diaboli regnum oppugnari, quod is seruatum vult. Nam cur prius ille tumultuaretur, cùm illi tu-ta esset rerum possessio, neq; aliquis ei occasionem tumultuandi præberet? At nunc per Euangelium superstitiones oppugnantur, & morum licentia coercetur, deniq; regnum eius inuaditur & indies coarctatur. Insanit ergo, & vt olim, ita hodie quoq; orbem terrarū turbat. At non ideo cessare de-bent fideles Christi serui: sed vt hic eò fortius in hostem illum impressionem fecit, quò ferocius illum resistere vidit: ita nobis quoq; eò constantius pugnandum est, quò crudelius ille furit. Et errant vehementer, qui se Regni Dei studiosos esse profitentur, & hoc vnum se optare aiunt, vt diaboli re-gnum totum destruatur: interim verò indignius ferunt, si Christi ministri spiritualia arma aduer-sus hunc exerant, & Euangelium liberius prædicent. Faciunt hi perinde, ac si quis hostem è finibus suis eiectum velit, prohibeat autem, ne quis eum oppugnet, aut aliquam illi molestiā exhibeat. Fal-lit autem illos humana prudentia. Quia enim inter homines facilitate & tolerantia multos vinci vident, vt tandem officium faciant, idem hic quoq; fieri posse sibi persuadent. At ingens inter homi-nes cordatos atq; modestos & diabolum discrimen est: multum etiam res huius seculi & religio di-ferunt. Admittunt rationes bonas modesti homines, nec facile propter res temporarias cum quoquā acrius contendunt: at diabolus nihil audit, & quamuis interdum aliquid concedere videatur, nil nī si inducias quærit, vt regnum suum interea magis stabiliat: qua intentione olim etiam Christo blan-ditus est, & huic honorificum testimonium perhibuit, qui tamen illum semper iussit tacere, & ab il-lo prædicari noluit. Deinde res huius seculi ferè in nostra potestate sunt, & tunc propter eas conten-dere nolle, pium & Christianum est. Cæterum religio ad Deum spectat, qui certam eius doctrinam atq; formam tradidit, in qua aliquid in alicuius gratiam mutare nefas est. Et tanta illius apud nos debet esse authoritas, vt cum parentibus quoq; & fratribus potius dissidere, quàm ab illius puritā-te discedere debeamus. Quantò minus igitur diabolo & membris eius tribui debet, cum quibus Chri-stiano homini nunquam conuenire poterit? Nec est quod de illis aliquid nobis polliceamur, quan-do constat omnium seculorum exemplis, acerrimas & implacabiles esse inimicitias, qua propter re-ligionis diuersitatem suscipiuntur.
units.tr: We have wished to set out these things in a fuller and more extended account, so that it may be plain to all that the devil did not give up his kingdom of his own accord, but that driving him out required divine power and much blood, and that the whole world was thrown into turmoil by his rage before he gave place to Christ. These things must be carefully observed against those who take offence at the disturbances, seditions and civil wars of our age, and who boast loudly of that peace and quiet in which the whole world once enjoyed the Papist religion, which was everywhere received and preserved. Many also, while they bear these movements as following from the gospel, make Christ, without the greatest impiety, the author of sedition, war and murder. Yet it is clear that the devil is the father and author of these evils. Christ, however, is the Prince of Peace, and the gospel is a herald of peace, teaching that we are called to the one God, so that through faith we grow together into one body and cherish mutual love among ourselves. Therefore, lest we be deceived, we must observe the nature of the devil more carefully. All his affairs are peaceful and quiet while he holds his kingdom, fortified with arms and garrisons, and is attacked by no one. For he takes care to keep his people in the pleasures of leisure and peace, lest they aspire to the liberty of the sons of God. And here he uses a remarkable cunning: men who disagree in opinion nevertheless bear with one another and foster an appearance of harmony. So in former times the nations, although they worshipped different gods and with very different rites, nonetheless agreed in attacking the true God, and none of them harassed the others on account of differences of religion. And today in Papacy not all invoke the same saints, nor do they use exactly the same form or rite of worship, yet they agree among themselves. The same may be seen among wicked men, who, although driven by different passions, nevertheless know how to keep up a wonderful concord and friendship among themselves. But because such concord is in itself by no means good, and confirms men in errors and vices, it does not deserve to be approved, and it is the work of the devil, who keeps quiet because he sees that all his possessions are safe. But as soon as he is attacked, and feels that he must give ground, he at once turns to rage and tries to mix heaven and earth, so that he may keep by worse arts a kingdom wrongly seized. Hence come the quarrels of parents and children, the contentions of brothers, the upheavals and seditions of commonwealths, wars both foreign and civil, slaughters, and every kind of evil, by which that wicked one tries to hinder the teaching of the gospel and the reformation of the world. And the unhappy world, which hates by itself the light of truth lest its evil works be exposed, helps him not a little. Therefore those are far too unfair judges who throw these things in our faces and in the face of the gospel, in order to prove that it is false. For it is rather by this argument that it is established that divine power is present and the kingdom of the devil is being attacked, because he wants it preserved. For why would he have been stirred to tumult before, when his possession of things was secure and no one gave him occasion to make a disturbance? But now superstitions are being attacked through the gospel, and licence in morals is being restrained, and finally his kingdom is being invaded and daily reduced. Therefore he rages, and, as in former times, so today too he troubles the world. But the faithful servants of Christ ought not on that account to cease: just as Christ pressed the attack on that enemy the more strongly the more fiercely he saw him resist, so we too must fight the more steadfastly the more cruelly he rages. And those greatly err who profess themselves zealous for the kingdom of God and say that this alone they desire, that the kingdom of the devil be utterly destroyed, while at the same time they take it ill if the ministers of Christ wield spiritual weapons against him and preach the gospel more freely. They act just as if someone wished an enemy driven out of his borders, yet forbade anyone to attack him or to cause him any trouble. But human prudence deceives them. For because they see many overcome among men by mildness and tolerance, so that in the end they do their duty, they persuade themselves that the same can happen here too. But there is a vast difference between the devil and men who are sensible and modest; there is also much difference between the affairs of this age and religion. Modest men admit good reasons, and they do not readily contend sharply with anyone over temporary things. But the devil hears nothing, and although at times he seems to concede something, he seeks only a truce, so that in the meantime he may make his kingdom more secure; with this intention he once flattered Christ too, and gave him an honourable testimony, yet Christ always ordered him to be silent and did not wish to be proclaimed by him. Moreover, the affairs of this age are for the most part in our power, and it is godly and Christian not to wish to contend over them. But religion concerns God, who has handed down a certain doctrine and form of it, in which it is wrong to change anything to please anyone. And its authority ought to be so great among us that we should rather fall out with parents and brothers than depart from its purity. How much less, then, ought anything to be granted to the devil and his members, with whom a Christian man can never agree? Nor is there any reason for us to promise ourselves anything from them, since the examples of all ages show that enmities are most bitter and implacable when they are undertaken on account of difference of religion.

units.la: Porrò
units.tr: Porro

units.la: Porro ad demonstrationem, vel potius suæ innocentiæ defensionem redit Christus, & alio argumento probat, sibi nihil cum diabolo commercij esse. Qui non est mecum (inquit) contra me est, & qui non colligit mecum spargit. Quibus minor propositio subijci debebat: Atqui diabolus mecum non est, neq; etiam mecum colligit. Unde sequitur, illum mihi contrarium, & nihil nobis esse commune. Sed quia cuius facile erat hoc colligere, unica illa sententia Christus contentus esse voluit. Et sane inter Christum & diabolum tam magnum tamen multiplex discrimen est, ut illis aliqua societas aut communio intercedere nequaquam possit. Diabolus tenebrarum princeps est, & hominum mentes excæcat: Christus autem lux mundi omnes illuminat, qui ipsum sequuntur. Ille peccati author est: Christus sempiternam iustitiam reduxit, imo nobis iustitia à Patre est factus. Ille homicida est: hic vita & salus. Ille dissidia seminat & coniunctos inter se scindit: hic colligit, & ideo in mundum venit, ut filios Dei qui dispersi erant, in unum cogeret, & sub uno pastore unum gregem faceret. Ille suum regnum stabilire nititur: hic regnum Dei instaurat & promovet. Ille mendax & mendacij pater: hic veritas est. Ille odio & invidia homines exagitat: hic charitatis igne credentes accendit. Et huius generis multa alia poterant adduci, quæ satis demonstrant, impudentissimam calumniam fuisse, qua hic Pharisæi & Scribæ Christum voluerunt infamem facere.
units.tr: Further, Christ returns to the demonstration, or rather to the defence of his innocence, and proves by another argument that he has nothing in common with the devil. "He who is not with me," he says, "is against me, and he who does not gather with me scatters." To these a minor premise ought to be added: "But the devil is not with me, nor does he gather with me." From this it follows that he is contrary to me and that we have nothing in common. But since this was easy to infer, Christ was content with that single saying. Indeed, between Christ and the devil there is such a great and manifold difference that no fellowship or communion can possibly exist between them. The devil is the prince of darkness and blinds men's minds; Christ is the light of the world and enlightens all who follow him. The devil is the author of sin; Christ has brought back everlasting righteousness, and has indeed been made righteousness for us by the Father. The devil is a murderer; Christ is life and salvation. The devil sows discord and tears apart those who are joined together; Christ gathers, and therefore came into the world to gather into one the children of God who were scattered, and to make one flock under one shepherd. The devil strives to establish his own kingdom; Christ establishes and advances the kingdom of God. The devil is a liar and the father of lies; Christ is the truth. The devil harasses men with hatred and envy; Christ kindles believers with the fire of love. Many other things of this kind could be adduced, which sufficiently show that the slander by which the Pharisees and scribes sought to make Christ infamous was most shameless.

units.la: Hinc autem nos colligere oportet, Christum nunquam in nobis regnum Dei instauraturum esse, nisi nos Satanam profligemus, cum quo ei tam male convenit. Quomodo enim apud eos locum obtineret Dei iustitia, qui iniustitiæ authori locum dant? Serio igitur Christum amplecti oportet, ut Deo toti consecremur: neq; putemus nobis licere, ut in tanto dissidio neutrales simus aut utrique simul seruiamus. Nam nisi cum Christo simus, illius aduersarij sumus, dum (quantum in nobis est) regnum eius concidere, aue saltem labefactari patimur. Dominus autem duobus tam aperte dissidentibus simul seruire, impossibile est. Confutantur ergo hoc dicto validissime, qui ut otio suo consulant, miris compositionibus religionem veram cum falsa, adeoq; Christum cum Belial conciliare student. Quibus relictis, nos duo hæc à nobis requiri cogitemus. Primum, ut palam nos Christo adiungamus neque nos eius pudeat coram mundo hoc prauo & degenere. Quem enim (inquit ille) mei & Euangelij puduerit coram hominibus, eius & me pudebit, cum venero in gloria Patris mei cum sanctis Angelis. Alterum, ut cum illo colligamus, nimirum ad regnum Dei & Ecclesiæ suæ consortium. Est hoc illi officium longè gratissimum: & ideo nomine Christiano prorsus indigni sunt, qui ad hoc non dirigunt studia sua omnia. Habent autem hic omnis loci & ordinis homines quod agant. Ministri cum Christo colligant, non dissipent, neque nouis doctrinis Ecclesiam distrahant. Peccant hic multi, qui colligunt quidem, sed non cum Christo, cum in hominum verba iurarint, quibus auditores suos adducere student. Paulum ergo imitentur illi, qui omnibus omnia fiebat, ut non sibi, sed Christo omnes lucrifaceret. Qui in magistratu sunt, se Ecclesiæ nutritios esse meminerint, & in huius gremio suæ fidei comissum populum contineant. Prouehant ergo verbi doctrinam, scholas aperiri curent, fidos ministros populo præficiant: & in primis curent, ne sua auaritia & rapacitate authores sint, ut Ecclesiæ fidus ministris destituantur. Parentes item tam liberos suos quam domesticos reliquos similiter Christo adducant, & priuatim domestica institutione hoc agant, ut Dei amorem, verbi eius studium & veræ pietatis principia animis illorum instillent. Qui verò neminem suæ fidei credi tum habent, curent ut & seipsos & eos quibus cum versantur, si qua se occasio offert, ad Regnum Dei colligant. Qui hoc sedulò faciunt, ii cum Filio Dei Iesu Christo colligunt, & olim ab ipso cum electis omnibus ad regnum cœleste colligentur, ut cum eo viuant & regnent. Ipsi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum, Amen.
units.tr: From this we ought to gather that Christ will never establish the kingdom of God in us unless we drive out Satan, with whom he has so ill a fellowship. For how could the justice of God hold a place among those who give a place to the author of injustice? We must therefore earnestly embrace Christ, so that we may be wholly consecrated to God; nor should we think it lawful for us to be neutral in so great a division, or to serve both sides at once. For unless we are with Christ, we are his adversaries, since (as far as in us lies) we allow his kingdom to be overthrown or at least weakened. But it is impossible for the Lord to be served at the same time by two so openly opposed. Those who, to secure their own ease, seek with strange compromises to join true religion with false, and so to reconcile Christ with Belial, are therefore most powerfully refuted by this saying. Leaving them aside, let us consider that two things are required of us. First, that we openly join ourselves to Christ and are not ashamed of him before this depraved and degenerate world. "For whoever is ashamed of me and of my gospel before men," he says, "of him also will I be ashamed, when I come in the glory of my Father with the holy angels." Second, that we gather with him, namely into the kingdom of God and the fellowship of his Church. This is by far the most pleasing service to him; and therefore those are altogether unworthy of the Christian name who do not direct all their efforts to this end. Yet men of every place and rank have something to do here. Ministers gather with Christ; they do not scatter, nor do they divide the Church with new doctrines. Many sin here who gather indeed, but not with Christ, since they have sworn allegiance to the words of men, to which they strive to draw their hearers. Let those therefore imitate Paul, who became all things to all men, so that he might gain all for Christ and not for himself. Those who are in the magistracy should remember that they are nursing fathers of the Church, and should keep the people committed to their trust within its bosom. Let them therefore advance the teaching of the Word, take care that schools are opened, and set faithful ministers over the people; and above all let them take care that they are not, through their own greed and rapacity, the cause of the Church being deprived of faithful ministers. Likewise parents should bring their children and the rest of their household to Christ in the same way, and should do this in private domestic instruction, so that they instil into their minds the love of God, zeal for his Word, and the principles of true piety. Those who have no one trustworthy in their faith should take care to gather both themselves and those with whom they live, whenever an opportunity offers, into the kingdom of God. Those who do this diligently gather with the Son of God, Jesus Christ, and at length they will be gathered by him together with all the elect into the heavenly kingdom, that they may live and reign with him. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever, Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CXVI.
units.tr: HOMILY CXVI.

units.la: Cùm impurus spiritus exierit ab homine, transit per arida loca, quæ-rens requiem: & non inueniens dicit: Reuertar domum meam, vnde exi-ui. Veniens igitur inuenit eam tersam & ornatam. Tunc proficiscitur, & accepit septem alios spiritus peiores quàm sit ipse: & ingressi habitant illic, & fiunt postrema hominis illius deteriora primis.
units.tr: When the unclean spirit has gone out of a man, it passes through dry places, seeking rest, and finding none it says: I will return to my house, from which I came out. So, coming back, it finds the house swept and adorned. Then it goes away and takes seven other spirits, worse than itself, and they enter and dwell there, and the last state of that man becomes worse than the first.

units.la: Cap. XI.
units.tr: Chapter XI.

units.la: DOminus noster Iesus Christus hucusq; Pharisæorum atq; Scribarum calumniam confutauit, qui ipsum dæmonia per Beelzebul eijcere dixerant. Docuit autem sibi adeo nihil commercij esse cum diabolo, vt potius hostiliter inter se dissideant, cum ipse promissus ille humani generis seruator sit, qui illius caput conculcare & ipsum e regno male occupato deturbare debeat. Finis omnium isto rum est, vt Christum agnoscamus qualis est, & ei per fidem insiti ipsi quoque aduersus diabolum & regnum eius pugnemus pro virili; ad Christum vero colligamus omnes, quibus cum nobis consue tudo aliqua intercedit. Caeterum quia sciebat tam ipsos quam plerosq; Iudaeorum prorsus incurabi les esse, hunc locum subijcit, quo & ingratitudinem eorum illius grauiter exprobrat, & huius poenas horribiles denuntiat. Quia autem in illis exemplum publicum toti mundo Deus propositurum, generalis etiam doctrina hic continetur, qua offenditur, quid omnes gratia Dei contemptores manent.
units.tr: Our Lord Jesus Christ has so far refuted the slander of the Pharisees and Scribes, who had said that he cast out demons by Beelzebul. He taught that he has no fellowship at all with the devil, so that they are rather at open enmity with one another, since he is that promised Saviour of mankind who must crush the devil's head and drive him out of the kingdom he has wrongly seized. The aim of all these things is that we should acknowledge Christ as he is, and, being grafted into him through faith, that we ourselves should also fight, as far as we are able, against the devil and his kingdom; and that we should gather to Christ all those with whom we have some acquaintance. But because he knew that both these men and most of the Jews were utterly incurable, he adds this passage, in which he sharply rebukes their ingratitude and announces the terrible punishment for it. Yet because God was going to set before the whole world a public example in them, a general teaching is also contained here, by which it is shown what awaits all despisers of the grace of God.

units.la: Primo autem videamus, vt ista Iudaeis conueniant. Nam ipsis potissimum Christum locutum esse, ex Matthaeo constat, vbi sub finem adijcitur: Ica enim erit nationi huic mala. Et quia miracu lum in daemoniaco caeco & muto editum, toti huic disputationi occasionem dederat, hic quoque pa rabola daemoniaci vtitur, & in huius hominis persona docet, quid toti genti sit euenturum. Verba per se clara sunt & perspicua, quare summam eorum, & finem, in quem dicuntur, tenuisse sufficit. Quemadmodum (inquit) daemoniacus, ex quo Satan expulsus est, si ingratus atque securus ei rur sus locum det, postea grauius laborat, adeo vt eius posterior conditio priori longe deterior fiat: Ita vobis quoque accidet, erga quos non semel Deus gratiam suam declarauit, vt ex diaboli tyrannide ereptos ad se reciperet, vos autem libertatis pertæsi subinde ad priores sordes relabimini, & diabo lo rursus hospitium prabetis. Paucis autem verbis tria agit, quæ ipsis considerat in primis necessaria erant. Primo enim beneficia Dei omnia, quæ iam inde ab initio genti illi contulerat, ipsis in memo riam reducit. Deinde ipsorum ingratitudinem & impiam securitatem accusat. Postremo poenas gra uissimas minatur.
units.tr: First, let us see how these things apply to the Jews. For it is clear from Matthew that Christ spoke chiefly to them, where at the end it is added: For so it will be for this evil nation. And since the miracle performed on the blind and mute demoniac had given occasion for this whole discussion, here too he uses the parable of the demoniac, and in the person of this man he teaches what will befall the whole nation. The words are clear and plain in themselves, so it is enough to grasp their sum and the end for which they are spoken. As (he says) the demoniac, from whom Satan has been cast out, if he is ungrateful and careless and gives him place again, afterwards suffers more grievously, so that his later condition becomes far worse than the former, so it will also happen to you, to whom God has more than once declared his grace, so that he might take you back, snatched from the tyranny of the devil; but you, weary of liberty, will from time to time slip back into your former filth and again offer lodging to the devil. In a few words he deals with three things, which he judged especially necessary for them. First, he calls to their memory all the benefits of God that he had bestowed on that nation from the very beginning. Next, he accuses them of their ingratitude and impious complacency. Lastly, he threatens the most severe punishments.

units.la: Quoad primum, satis constat, ipsos non semel gratiam Dei sensisse, qui illos ex diaboli tyrannide liberare studuit. Nam vt ad patrem illorum Abrahamum ascendamus, hunc cum inter idololatras ageret, & (vt Iosua testatur) Diis alienis seruiret, euocauit ex mera gratia, & in terram Canaan eduxit, vt cum ipso promissiones de semine benedictio & foedus illud instauraret, quod in dilumio abo litum esse videbatur. Deinde cum in Ægypto dira Pharaonis tyrannide oppressi non solum liber tatem corporum amisissent, verumetiam Ægyptiorum exemplo seducti, simulachra colerent, & va rijs superstitionibus essent immersi, rursus per Mosem eos liberauit, & (vt in Psalmo scribitur) misso verbo suo sanauit eos. Nam ex Ægypto eductus legem dedit, qua seipsum & voluntate suam ipsis abunde manifestauit, simulq; ceremonijs splendidissimis & mysteriorum plenis instruxit, ne quam haberent ad gentium superstitiones declinandi occasionem. Et quo din primis necessarium erat, sacerdotes instituit, qui Legis doctrinam subinde proponerent, ne huius ignorantia diabolo aditum prabe ret ipsos seducendi. Postea cessantibus in officio suo sacerdotibus, & idololatria cum omni scelerum genere sensim irrepente, extraordinarios doctores excitauit, Prophetas, qui populum ad veri Dei cultum revocarent, scelera accusarent, & diaboli conatibus se opponerent. Similis Dei gratia in exilio Babylonico eluxit. Nam ne illic diabolus eos Babyloniorum exemplo & authoritate ad ido lolatriam pertraheret, Danielem & eius socios spiritu suo instruxit, qui ipsum quoq; Nabuchodo nosorem in veri Dei cognitione adduxerunt, vt sub eius imperio fidei & religionis puritatem retine re possent. Et cum impius Balthazar relictus patrum suorum vestigijs veri cultus hostis esset, & prout dubio Iudaeos quoq; ad nefarios cultus & superstitiones cogere instituisset, illo extincto & Babylonis co regno ouerso, rerum summa ad Cyrum translata, qui illos libertate donatos honorifice dimisit, vt vr bem & templum aedificarent, & a Deo accepta sacra iterum obirent. Adde his, qua Machabæorum tempore sunt gesta: quando Antiochus templum prophanauit, legis libros exussit, multos ad fidei ve ra abnegationem horrendis supplicijs coegit. Tunc enim rursus heroes fortissimos, Iudam & fra tres eius excitauit, qui non solum Antiochi & sociorum eius tyrannidem repressi sunt, sed populum iam quasi redactum sub diaboli potestatem ad veri Dei cultum reduxerunt. Hos omnes secu tus est æternus Dei Filius Iesus Christus, qui plenam salutem & vniuersos gratia Dei thesauros illis obtulit sponte, & vt his fruantur hortatus est. Et ne quid possent tergiuersari, infinitis miraculis declarauit, se promissum illm seruatorem esse, qui ipsos ex diaboli tyrannide afferere velit. Vides ergo non semel liberatos fuisse, & Deum plus quam paternam bonitatem erga ipsos declarasse, quando toties suam gratiam illis obtulit.
units.tr: As to the first point, it is quite clear that they have more than once experienced the grace of God, who has sought to free them from the tyranny of the devil. For to go back to their forefather Abraham: when he was living among idolaters and (as Joshua testifies) served other gods, God called him out of pure grace and led him into the land of Canaan, so that with him he might renew the promises concerning the blessing of his seed and that covenant which seemed to have been wiped out by the Flood. Then, when they were oppressed in Egypt by the dire tyranny of Pharaoh, they lost not only the liberty of their bodies but also, led astray by the example of the Egyptians, they worshipped images and were immersed in various superstitions; again God freed them through Moses, and (as is written in the Psalm) sent forth his word and healed them. For, having led them out of Egypt, he gave them the law, by which he abundantly made himself and his will known to them, and at the same time instructed them with most splendid ceremonies full of mysteries, so that they would have no occasion to turn aside to the superstitions of the nations. And since it was necessary for the time being, he appointed priests, who would from time to time set forth the teaching of the Law, lest ignorance of it should give the devil an opening to lead them astray. Afterwards, when the priests ceased to perform their duty, and idolatry crept in little by little together with every kind of wickedness, he raised up extraordinary teachers, the Prophets, to call the people back to the worship of the true God, to accuse their crimes, and to oppose the attempts of the devil. A similar grace of God shone forth during the Babylonian exile. For lest the devil should draw them into idolatry there by the example and authority of the Babylonians, he endowed Daniel and his companions with his Spirit, and they brought even Nebuchadnezzar himself to the knowledge of the true God, so that under his rule they could keep the purity of faith and religion. And when the impious Belshazzar, having abandoned the footsteps of his fathers, was an enemy of the true worship, and was apparently resolved to compel the Jews also to wicked cults and superstitions, he was killed, the kingdom of Babylon was overthrown, and the supreme power passed to Cyrus, who, granting them liberty, sent them home with honour, so that they might rebuild the city and the temple and once more perform the sacred rites received from God. Add to these what was done in the time of the Maccabees: when Antiochus profaned the temple, burned the books of the Law, and forced many by horrible tortures to deny the true faith. Then God again raised up most valiant heroes, Judas and his brothers, who not only checked the tyranny of Antiochus and his allies, but led back to the worship of the true God a people who had already been, as it were, brought under the power of the devil. The eternal Son of God, Jesus Christ, followed all these, and offered them of his own accord full salvation and all the treasures of God's grace, and exhorted them to enjoy them. And so that they could make no excuse, he showed by countless miracles that he is the promised Saviour, who wishes to rescue them from the tyranny of the devil. You see, therefore, that they were set free not just once, and that God showed toward them more than a fatherly goodness, since he offered his grace to them so many times.

units.la: Quid vero illi? Ingratissimi omnium mortalium, quasi cum Deo certamen suscepissent, subinde ad pristinos errores relapsi sunt. Nam in deserto non multis ab accepta Lege diebus, vitulum aureum fecerunt, & gloriam immortalis Dei commutarunt cum imagine bovis comedentis fænum. Terra aut promissa iam potiti, multoties derelicto vero Deo, vicinarum gentium superstitionibus se polluerunt, & quamvis hoc illis nunquam impune cesserit, tamen quoties pax & otium illis data fuit, ad vomitum redierunt: adeo ut Samuel tempore inuenti fuerint adhuc, qui Astaroth & Deos alienos colerent. Sub regibus idem factum fuisse, Prophetarum sermones testantur. Et quamvis interdum pios reges Deus daret, qui abolitis cultibus peregrinis veram religionem magno studio instaurarent, plerosque tamen sibi aduersarios senserunt, qui publice & priuatim superstitiones retinere conabantur: quod sub Ezechia & Iosia in primis factum fuisse constat. Similiter post Machabaeorum obitum setis locum dederunt, quæ ex gentium schola prodierant, ut iam in Pharisæos, Sadducæos & Essenos scissi esset, qui unus populus & sub uno Deo una Ecclesia esse debebant. Denique ita iam locum inter illos inuenerat Satan, ut palam Sadducæis liceret resurrectionem mortuorum, & cum animarum immortalitate spiritus cum bonos tum malos negare. Erat præterea passim, quorum sensus quoque & corpora dæmones occuparant, qui furoribus actis omnia infesta reddebant. Quod ideo permisisse videtur Deus, ut in illis viderent infelicē totius generis conditionem. Idem tamen rursus illorum misertus Filium misit, qui rebus afflictis opem ferret. Is (ut alias monuimus) veritatis doctrina diaboli tenebras discussit, & dæmonia passim ex obsessis eiicendo ostendit iam adesse Regnum Dei, in quod ex diaboli tyrannide ipsos transferre velit, modo gratiam sibi oblatam non aspernentur. Et cogebatur iam Satan ex multis discedere, quorum exemplo Christi doctrina & promissiones confirmabantur. Caeterum adeo non mouit ingratos illos tanta Dei ipsos inuisentis bonitas, ut potius quasi res ipsorum per omnia incolumes essent, & ipsi sibi sufficerent, Christum non modo neglexerint, verumetiam odio letali persecuti sint: cuius odii exempla cum in tota Euangelii historia passim occurrant, non opus est plura de illo dicere. Hoc modo obseruemus, causam tantæ ingratitudinis & impietatis præcipuam fuisse, quod rebus suis optime consultum esse, neque sibi aliquo redemptore aut vindice opus esse putarent.
units.tr: But what of them? Most ungrateful of all mortals, as though they had entered into a contest with God, they kept falling back into their former errors. For in the desert, not many days after receiving the Law, they made a golden calf and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for the image of an ox eating hay. Once they had taken possession of the promised land, they often, having abandoned the true God, defiled themselves with the superstitions of the neighbouring nations; and although this never went unpunished for them, nevertheless whenever peace and leisure were given them they returned to their vomit, so that in Samuel's time there were still found people who worshipped Ashtaroth and foreign gods. That the same happened under the kings, the words of the Prophets bear witness. And although at times God gave pious kings, who with great zeal restored the true religion by abolishing foreign cults, nevertheless they found many opponents who tried to keep up superstitions both in public and in private; this is known to have happened especially under Hezekiah and Josiah. In the same way, after the death of the Maccabees, they gave place to sects that had come forth from the school of the nations, so that the people were already split into Pharisees, Sadducees and Essenes, though they ought to be one people under one God and one Church. Finally, Satan had found so much room among them that the Sadducees were openly permitted to deny the resurrection of the dead, and to deny, together with the immortality of souls, that there are spirits, both good and bad. Moreover, there were everywhere people whose senses and bodies demons had seized, and who, in their mad fits, made everything hostile. God seems to have allowed this so that they might see in these the wretched condition of the whole human race. Yet he, taking pity on them again, sent his Son, who would bring help to those in distress. He (as we have said elsewhere) dispelled the darkness of the devil by the teaching of truth, and by casting out demons from the possessed in various places he showed that the Kingdom of God is now at hand, into which he wishes to transfer them from the tyranny of the devil, provided they do not spurn the grace offered to them. And Satan was already being forced to withdraw from many, and by their example the teaching and promises of Christ were confirmed. But so far was that great goodness of God, which visited them, from moving those ungrateful men, that, as if their affairs were in every way secure and they were self-sufficient, they not only neglected Christ but pursued him with deadly hatred; examples of this hatred occur throughout the whole history of the Gospel, so there is no need to say more about it. In this way we may observe that the chief cause of so great ingratitude and impiety was that they thought their affairs were in the best order, and that they had no need of any redeemer or deliverer.

units.la: At ne se hoc impune facturos arbitrarentur, pœnas graues & horrendas Christus illis denuntiat Quod nimirum postrema eorum deteriora sint futura primis. Quasi diceret: Quoniam non agnoscitis toties vobis se offerentem Dei gratiam, & aduersus eam cum incurabili pertinacia atque ingratitudine luctamini, iusto iudicio permittet ille, ut diabolus maiori tyrannide vos opprimat, & totos redigat in sua potestate. Tunc vero in eas calamitates præcipitabimini, ut quæ hucusque passim est ipsius locum videri possint præ ijs, quæ vos porro manent. Nec inanes fuisse minas iństas, res ipsa demonstrat. Nam sive corpora sive animas spectemus, nulla unquam gens infelicior, miserior & calamitosior fuit, quam Iudæorum ab eo tempore fuerit. Nam qui Dei Filium, unicum & liberalissimum salutis omnisque boni authorem recipere noluerunt, ij postea (quod ille fore prædixerat) diaboli suggestionibus decepti, impostoribus impiis & seditiosis locum dedere, per quos factum est, ut Romani assidui turbis & tumultibus provocati, urbem cum templo excinderent, populum vero infelicem, qui superstes erat, hinc inde dispergerent. Itaque cum externo cultu, quem inuito Christo retinere volebant, libertatem quoque & omnem reipublicae formam amiserunt. Et cum patrum exilia & captiuitates certum finem habuerint, postrema hæc illorum dissipatio annis mille quingentis durauit, neque ulla adhuc liberationis spes ipsis affulget. Leuiculum tamen hoc videri poterat præ illis, quæ ad animam & salutis æternæ iacturam pertinent. Nam in reprobum sensum traditi, Scripturas ignorant, ab omni liberalium disciplinarum cognitione alieni sunt, toti autem a Rabbinis pendent, qui portentosis fabulis Dei Verbum corrumpunt, & vniuersum religionis atque salutis negotium non obscurant modo, verumetiam ludibrio omnium exponunt. Itaque (quod fore olim Amos prædixerat) famem quidem verbi Dei patiuntur, atque à mari ad mare, vel potius ab vna Rabbinorum palude ad aliam discurrunt, ut consolationem inueniunt, sed id absq; fructu faciunt. Nam quod omnem ad gratiam Dei aditum illis praeludit, Christum Iesum adhuc odio capitali persequuntur, & maiori quam patres ipsorum impietate conuitia omnis generis in illum congerunt, deniq; in Synagogis suis palàm eum diris deuouent. Quis ergo non videt diabolum assumptis infinitis alijs dæmonijs gentem illam inuasisse, & eius ditionem longè deteriorem esse nunc, quam olim fuerit? Unde vero hoc? Quia domum vacuam apud illos Satan inuenit, id est, tales reperit, qui repulso Christo (qui solus Legis & typorum legalium complementum est) sua somnia secuti sunt, & rerum securi admonitiones & correptiones omnes contempserunt. Quia autem Dominus hæc primum in genere proponit, deinde Iudæis applicat, quos omnium qui Dei populus & ecclesiæ eius membra censentur, typù vel exemplar fuisse constat, nobis quoque hinc generalis doctrina petenda est, quæ multa continet, & cuius singulæ partes nobis accommodari possunt.
units.tr: But lest they should think they could do this with impunity, Christ threatens them with grave and dreadful punishments, namely that their last state will be worse than their first. It is as if he said: since you do not recognise God's grace, which has so often offered itself to you, and you struggle against it with incurable obstinacy and ingratitude, he will, by just judgement, allow the devil to oppress you with greater tyranny and bring you wholly under his power. Then indeed you will be plunged into calamities such that those you have suffered until now may seem slight by comparison with what still awaits you. That these threats were not empty, the event itself shows. For whether we look at their bodies or their souls, no nation has ever been more unhappy, wretched and afflicted than the Jews have been since that time. For those who refused to receive the Son of God, the only and most generous author of salvation and of every good, were afterwards (as he had foretold) deceived by the suggestions of the devil and gave place to impious and seditious impostors, through whom it came about that the Romans, repeatedly provoked by their uproars and tumults, destroyed the city together with the temple, and scattered the unhappy people who survived in every direction. Thus, while they wanted to keep the external worship, which they retained against Christ's will, they lost both their liberty and every form of commonwealth. And although their fathers' exiles and captivities had a definite end, this final dispersion has lasted for fifteen hundred years, and still no hope of deliverance shines on them. Yet this might seem a trifling matter compared with those things which concern the soul and the loss of eternal salvation. For, delivered over to a reprobate mind, they are ignorant of the Scriptures, are strangers to all knowledge of the liberal disciplines, and are wholly dependent on the rabbis, who corrupt God's Word with monstrous fables, and not only obscure the whole business of religion and salvation but also expose it to the mockery of all. And so (as Amos had foretold would happen) they suffer a famine of the word of God, and run from sea to sea, or rather from one rabbinical marsh to another, seeking comfort, but they do this without profit. For they persecute Christ Jesus, who alone opens every approach to the grace of God, with deadly hatred, and with greater impiety than their fathers, they heap upon him insults of every kind, and at last openly curse him in their synagogues. Who then does not see that the devil, having taken in countless other demons, has invaded that nation, and that his dominion over it is now far worse than it once was? But whence does this come? Because Satan found the house empty among them, that is, he found people who, having rejected Christ (who alone is the fulfilment of the Law and of the legal types), followed their own dreams, and, secure in their possessions, despised all warnings and rebukes. Now because the Lord first sets this forth in general terms and then applies it to the Jews, who are known to have been a type or example of all who are counted God's people and members of his Church, we too must draw from here a general teaching, which contains much, and each part of which can be applied to us.

units.la: Primo adumbratur hic misera & infelix hominum conditio. Dum enim hominis mentione Christus facit, è quo diabolus exeat, non obscurè docet, omnes homines huius tyrannidi obnoxios esse, quo ad peculiari gratia liberentur. Quod verissimum esse, multis argumentis demonstrari poterat. Nam primus parens noster dum diabolo potius quam Deo fidem habuit, & illius consilium secutus diuinum mandatum transgressus est, seipsum sponte diaboli seruum fecit, neq; dignus fuit, quem pro suo Deus porro agnosceret. Quare paradiso eiectus à dignitate sua priori excidit, & simul eximias illas animi atq; corporis facultates amisit, quibus antea ornatus fuerat, & in quibus Dei imago eluceba t. Idè ergo (ut Moses scribit) in sua imagine peccatrice & corrupta liberos genuit, qui & ipsi ex matrum vtero misera hanc & seruilem conditione bauserunt, ut in illos Satanas & imperium haberet. Et quantum hic in nos possit, nemo est qui non in semetipso sentiat. Unde enim hoc esse dicemus, quod à pueris statim pessimis cogitationibus distrahimur? quod prauus cupiditatibus ardemus? quod à Dei voluntate bona & sanctâ abhorremus, admodum autè sumus proclives? Nũ ex Deo? Nequaquam, cum sit sanctus sit, & iniquitatem oderit. Num ex prima hominis creatione? Ne hoc quidem, quia ad suam imaginem Deus hominem creauit, bonum selicem, innocentem, omnium & rerum omnium principem. Restat ergo quod diabolus huius mali sit author, qui cum in peccato concipiamur & nascamur, sese mox infantum quoq; animis insinuat, vt cum ætate peccati quoq; vis augeatur, quæ illicitarum cogitationum atq; cupiditatum, & tandem apertorum quoq; scelerum causa est. Ita ergo nobis dominatur Satan, vt membra & facultates nostræ omnes ipsi seruiant ad omne iniustitiam, cuius stipendium est mors & totius hominis interitus. Est seruitus hæc eo grauior & pernitiosior, quod neq; dominum nobis mutare licet, neq; fuga nobis consulere possumus. Nam quocunq; te conferas, intra animum & viscera tua peccatum circumseris, & proinde sub diaboli ditione et potestate es. Accedit hoc quoque, quod ne volumus quidem liberari, eò quod ex peccato voluptatem capimus, & illo plus quàm vllis alijs rebus delectamur. Et hæc quidem omnium nostrum, quoad pro priam naturam conditio est: perdita nimirum & deplorata, nisi nobis aliunde auxilium veniat.
units.tr: First, the wretched and unhappy condition of mankind is here sketched out. For when Christ speaks of the man from whom the devil goes out, he teaches plainly that all men are liable to his tyranny, and that they are freed from it only by a special grace. This could be shown to be most true by many arguments. For our first parent, when he trusted the devil rather than God, and following the devil's counsel transgressed the divine command, of his own accord made himself the devil's slave, and was no longer worthy to be acknowledged by God as his own. Therefore, cast out of paradise, he fell from his former dignity, and at the same time lost those outstanding gifts of mind and body with which he had been adorned, and in which the image of God shone forth. Hence (as Moses writes) he begot children in his own sinful and corrupted image, who themselves from their mothers' wombs drew in this wretched and servile condition, so that Satan might have power over them. And how much he can do in us, there is no one who does not feel in himself. For whence shall we say it comes that from our earliest childhood we are drawn away by the worst thoughts, that we burn with wicked desires, that we shrink from the good and holy will of God and are very prone to what is evil? Does it come from God? By no means, since he is holy and hates iniquity. Does it come from the original creation of man? Not even this, since God created man in his own image, good, happy, innocent, and lord of all things. It remains, then, that the devil is the author of this evil, who, since we are conceived and born in sin, straightway insinuates himself into the minds even of infants, so that with age the power of sin also grows, which is the cause of unlawful thoughts and desires, and at last of open crimes as well. So Satan rules over us in such a way that all our members and faculties serve him for every unrighteousness, whose wages is death and the total ruin of the man. This slavery is the more grievous and destructive because we are not allowed to change our master, nor can we secure ourselves by flight. For wherever you turn, you carry sin about within your own mind and bowels, and so you are under the devil's dominion and power. To this is added the fact that we do not even wish to be freed, because we take pleasure in sin, and delight in it more than in any other thing. And this is the condition of all of us, as far as our own nature is concerned: namely lost and past hope, unless help comes to us from elsewhere.

units.la: Itaque hoc quoque Christus hac parabola indicat. Dum enim Iudæus minatur, diabolum assumptis alijs spiritibus peioribus denuo ipsos inuasurum esse, eò quod gratiam Dei in seipsis affulgentem impiè contemnant, satis docet, se eum esse, qui miseros nos ex diaboli tyrannide eripiat. Et sanè ater no Dei consilio ipsum ad hoc prædestinatum fuisse Apostoli testantur, & ex prima promissione, quâ Adamo fecit Deus, satis constat. In ea enim pugnam illam sanciuit, quæ semini mulieris cum serpente veteri perpetua futura fit, & in qua huius caput conteri oporteat. Venit ergo ille in mundum præsinito tempore, & (vt alias monuimus) pugnam hanc mox à baptismo aggressus, ab eo tempore tam docendo quam miraculis regnum diaboli oppugnauit, & multis opem tulit, quorum corpora & sensus ille obsidebat, multos item liberauit, in quorum animis pessimi affectus & cupiditates prauæ ab illo incensæ, astuabant. Et quam istis attulit salutem, omnibus communem esse vult, dum ad se vocat omnes qui laborant & onerati sunt, & omnibus qui ad se veniunt refocillationem & quietem certam pollicetur. Denique iam mortem adituris diserte docet, iam adesse tempus illud fatale, quo principem mundi foras eijci oporteat. Et mox expiatis per mortem sua meritum peccatis mundi, illum iis armis exuit, quibus initio regnum mundi occupauerat, & quibus maximè in hominibus capiendis atque retinendis vtitur. Et vt constaret redemptionem perfectam & plenam in ipso haberi, mortem quoq; resurrectione sua deuicit, ne hac quoq; credentibus posthac formidabilis esset. Redemptione vero hanc & salute tunc partam, postea per Euangelij praedicationem toti terrarum orbi denunciari & offerri voluit, & hodie adhuc nobis quoque offert, imo per eandem ipse suo spiritu & virtute diabolum quotidie oppugnat, ne electus suus iterum dominetur. Euangelij enim luce falsa doctrina arguitur, superstitiones profligantur, illicit cultus abolentur, detegitur scelerum & vitiorum turpitudo, emendantur corrupti mores, intellectus hominis illustratur, denique totus homo per fidei obedientiam Deo subijcitur, quo fit ut hic in illis regnare possit, qui prius diaboli mancipia erant. Perpetua enim & semper rata est promissio illa: Praedicate Euangelium omni creaturae: Qui crediderit & baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit. Nam quia ipse Christus per illud ad nos accedit, Satan ad eius praedicationem consistere non potest. Ideo angelus Cornelio Centurioni mandans, ut Petrum ad se accerseret, addit: Ille tibi loquetur verba, per quae salvaberis tu & domus tua. Et Macedonicus ille Angelus Paulum vocans dicebat: Veni, & iterum nos. Commendatur ergo hic nobis Euangelicae doctrinae dignitas atque excellentia, quae ipsum verbum salutis & vitae aeternae dicitur, sola denique medium illud est, per quod ex diaboli servitute infelici ad libertatem filiorum Dei transferimur. Et ut per illud vincitur & profligatur diabolus: ita illi victoria adversus Antichristum tribuitur, quoad hoc seculum. Euangelium enim Spiritus oris Christi & virga labiorum eius est, quo impium illum & magnum fidei adversarium Isaias & Paulus percuti & jugulari praedixerunt. Quod nostro seculo passim fieri videmus. Nam etsi adhuc magnifico splendore & regum sederibus ille sese venditet, in hominum tamen animis iam pridem jugulatus est, qui agnita Euangelij veritate illius minas atque fulmina contemnunt. Debent ista in eum finem considerari, ut Euangelij studium in nobis accendatur, & ut qui rebus praesunt, illud pure praedicari & latissime extendi curent. Ita enim tam propria quam multorum salute consulent, & destructa diaboli tyrannide Regnum Dei salutiferum propagabunt.
units.tr: Therefore Christ also indicates this by this parable. For when he threatens the Jew that the devil, taking in other, worse spirits, will again invade them because they impiously despise the grace of God shining upon them, he sufficiently teaches that he is the one who snatches us, wretched as we are, from the tyranny of the devil. And that he was predestined to this by the counsel of God the Apostles testify, and it is sufficiently clear from the first promise which God made to Adam. For in it he ordained that battle which was to be perpetual between the seed of the woman and the old serpent, and in which it was necessary that his head be crushed. He therefore came into the world at the appointed time, and (as we have elsewhere noted) began this battle immediately from his baptism, and from that time onward assailed the kingdom of the devil both by teaching and by miracles, bringing help to many whose bodies and senses that spirit beset, and likewise freeing many in whose minds wicked passions and depraved desires, kindled by him, were boiling. And the salvation which he brought to these he wishes to be common to all, since he calls to himself all who labour and are burdened, and promises rest and certain refreshment to all who come to him. Finally, when he was about to undergo death, he plainly taught that the fatal time had now come when the prince of this world must be cast out. And soon afterwards, having expiated by his death the sins of the world, he stripped him of those weapons by which at the beginning he had seized the kingdom of the world, and with which he chiefly takes and holds men. And so that it might be established that complete and full redemption is to be found in him, he also overcame death by his resurrection, lest it should henceforth be a fearful thing even to believers. This redemption and salvation, once obtained, he wished to be afterwards proclaimed and offered to the whole world through the preaching of the Gospel, and he still offers it to us today; indeed, through the same Gospel, he himself by his Spirit and power daily assails the devil, lest his elect be ruled by him again. For by the light of the Gospel false doctrine is refuted, superstitions are put to flight, unlawful worship is abolished, the baseness of crimes and vices is revealed, corrupt morals are amended, the understanding of man is enlightened, and finally the whole man is made subject to God through the obedience of faith, with the result that he may reign in those who were formerly the slaves of the devil. For that promise is lasting and always valid: "Preach the Gospel to every creature; he who believes and is baptised will be saved." For since Christ himself comes to us through it, Satan cannot stand before its preaching. Hence the angel, instructing Cornelius the centurion to send for Peter, adds: "He will speak words to you by which you and your household will be saved." And that Macedonian angel calling Paul said: "Come over and help us." Here, then, the dignity and excellence of the evangelical doctrine is commended to us; it is called the very word of salvation and eternal life; in short, it is the only means by which we are transferred from the unhappy servitude of the devil to the liberty of the sons of God. And just as through it the devil is conquered and put to flight, so victory over Antichrist is granted to it for this age. For the Gospel is the breath of Christ's mouth and the rod of his lips, by which Isaiah and Paul foretold that that impious and great adversary of the faith would be struck down and slain. We see this happening everywhere in our own age. For although he still puffs himself up with magnificent splendour and sits in the seats of kings, he has long since been slain in the minds of men who, having recognised the truth of the Gospel, despise his threats and thunderbolts. These things ought to be considered to this end: that zeal for the Gospel may be kindled in us, and that those who hold office see to it that it is preached purely and spread as widely as possible. For in this way they will consult both their own salvation and that of many others, and by destroying the tyranny of the devil they will extend the saving kingdom of God.

units.la: Et hic quidem magno studio & diligentia singulari opus esse Christus docet, quando inquietum & nocendi cupidum diaboli ingenium describit, qui ne vitus quidem & expulsus quiescat. Cum impurus spiritus (inquit) exierit ab homine, transit per arida loca quaerens requiem, & non inveniens dicit: Revertar domum meam, unde exivi: Veniens igitur invenit eam terjam & ornatam (Matthaeus vacantem quoque addit) itaque abit & accipit septem alios spiritus pejores quam ipse sit, & ingressi habitant illic, &c. Expulsum per deserta loca eum vagari, & requiem, id est, domicilium novum quaerere dicit. Quod bifariam potest intelligi, vel quod expulsio illa ipsi infaustum horridi deserti sit, in quo exulare cogitur (& sane nihil ei tristius accidere posse daemoniorum clamores testantur, quibus saepius de Christo conquesti sunt) vel quod ad homines impios transfeat, quos iam ante sub ditione tenet, & qui vere loca deserta sunt, cum neque Dei verbo se coli patiantur, neque aliquos fructus ferant Regno Dei dignos. Sed apud hos quoque requiem non invenit. Nam etsi pessimus illorum studijs & interitu delectetur, non tamen hoc ei satis est, quem perpetua nocendi & quam plurimos perdendi libido extimulat. Et ut praedo avarus praeda quidem iam parta gaudet, in ea autem acquiescere non potest, sed ad novas praedationes aspirat: ita quies diabolo nulla est, nisi novain horas occasio sese offerat, qua homines perdat. Quid ergo facit? Cum hominum mores & ingenium norit, qui rebus integris & salvis fere securi fiunt, de reditu in pristinum hospitium cogitat, ut amissam possessionem recuperet. Neque semper illum spes sua fallit. Plerunque enim accidit, ut otiosos & securos, adhaec mundi huius ornatui & splendori deditos inveniat. Quia enim natura ad otium proclives sumus, facile nobis perpetuam pacem & felicitatem pollicemur, si nobis Deus se propitium ostendat. Quae persuasio etsi per se non mala fit (est enim electorum & vere credentium salus firma & perpetua) nisi tamen serio pietatis studio temperetur, & fine nostrae redemptionis dili genter observemus, confidentes & securos reddit, & ita aditum patefacit veteri & malitioso hospiti, qui omnem nocendi occasionem indesinenter captat. Itaque, si tales inveniat, prioris electionis dolore adhuc exacerbatus, & ut rebus suis melius consulat, maiori conatu rem aggreditur. Na assumptis aliis quoque spiritibus pessimis, redit eo, unde egressus fuerat: quae causa est, ut eiusmodi hominum conditio posterior priori deterior sit, & infelicior. Exempla, quibus hoc probari poterat, multa passim occurrunt. Quotidie enim videmus homines qui a pueris bene institui magnos in regno Dei progressus fecerunt, postea securiores fieri & confidentia nimia inflari, qua alios quoq; prae se totum nunt. At ijdem plerunq; novis Satanae insidijs circumuenti ita ab eo possidentur, ut impietate, verbi Dei contemptu, morum licentia & libidine eos etiam superent, qui eximiu illud Euangelicae gratiae donum nunquam degustauerunt. Et quod priuatis hominibus accidit, hoc ipsum in totis populis atque Ecclesijs accidere solet. Docent hoc Ecclesiae Orientales, quae cum olim prae alijs floruerint, securitas & confidentia contentiones ambitiosas in illis excitauit, qua eo vsque progressae sunt, vt relicta Euangelij simplicitate disputationibus vanis atque inutilibus vacarent, & singulae humanae prasidijs sibi consulere conarentur. Ea igitur occasione obseruata diabolus hospitium, quod olim illic habuerat, repetijt, & Mahumetem miserum obtrusit, cuius partim doctrina impijssima, partim armis subiugati longe deteriori loco sunt quam olim, quando gentium superstitionibus erant immersi. Simile quid Occidens quoque sub Romanus pontificibus passus est. Et hodie vrbium aliquot exempla vidimus, quae postquam profligata & reiecta Euangelij luce tenebrarum principi denuo locum dederunt, non modo ad pristinas superstitiones relapsae sunt, sed simul omni timori Dei excusso & bonis legibus sublatis, omni scelerum generi fenestras aperuerunt. Vere ergo Christus ait, eiusmodi hominum postremam conditionem priori deteriorem fieri. Et de ijsdem Petrus scribit: Si postquam inquinamenta mundi per agnitionem Domini & Seruatoris Iesu Christi effugerint, bis rursus implicati superentur, fiunt postrema eorum peiora primis. Satius enim fuisset eis non cognouisse viam iustitiae, quam hac cognita regredi a sancta doctrina ipsis tradita. Sed accidit eis quod vero proverbio dici solet: Canis reuersus est ad suum ipsius vomitum, & Sus lota ad volutabrum luti. Ita vero verbi & gratiae suae contemptum iusto iudicio Deus vlcisci tur, vt qui tales sunt, impleta tandem iniquitatis mensura iustas ipsi poenas exoluant. Et videmus fere in hoc etiam saeculo tales infelicissimos esse. Nam amissa plerunque corporum quoque libertate, iugum alienum ferre coguntur, eoque miseriores sunt, quod in tanea carnis & scelerum licentia miseriam suam non agnoscunt. Sed sunt haec praeludia tantum eorum, quae olim patientur, quando cum principe suo diabolo ad aeternos infelicium cruciatus relegabuntur.
units.tr: And here Christ teaches that great zeal and singular diligence are needed, when he describes the restless nature of the devil, who, though cast out and driven away, does not rest. "When the unclean spirit," he says, "has gone out of a man, it passes through dry places seeking rest, and not finding it, it says: I will return to my house from which I came out. And coming, it finds it empty, swept and adorned" (Matthew adds "empty" as well); "so it goes and takes seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they enter and dwell there," etc. He says that when expelled it wanders through deserted places, seeking rest, that is, a new dwelling. This can be understood in two ways: either that expulsion itself is a dreadful misfortune for it, a banishment into the frightful desert in which it is forced to wander (and indeed the cries of the demons testify that nothing sadder could befall them, and they often complained of Christ on this account); or that it passes over to impious men, whom it already holds under its power, and who are truly "deserted places," since they neither suffer God's Word to be honoured in them nor bear any fruit worthy of the kingdom of God. But it does not find rest even among these.
