units.la: Propterea etiam Sapientia Dei dixit: Mittam ad eos Prophetas & Apostolos, & ex ipsis quosdam trucidabunt, & quosdam expellent: vt à natione ista requiratur sanguis omnium Prophetarum, effusus à iactis fundamentis mundi, à sanguine Abel ad sanguinem Zachariae, qui periit inter altare & aedem: Etiam dico vobis requiretur ab hac natione.
units.tr: For this reason also the Wisdom of God said: "I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will kill, and some they will drive out; so that the blood of all the prophets, shed since the foundation of the world, may be required of this nation, from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the temple. Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this nation."

units.la: QVemadmodum Deus per salutarem verbi sui doctrinam in filio suo Iesu Christo omnes Regni sui et gratiae thesauros nobis offert: ita non aliud sciens indignius ferre solet, quam si illa vel impie contemnatur, vel traditionibus humanis corrumpatur aut obscuretur. Quia qui hoc faciunt, ii ingratitudine adversus Deum multiplici peccant. Nam primum ab illo recedunt, qui fons est aquae viventis, & contempta eius liberalitate cisternas pertusas atque pestilentes sibi ipsis effodiunt. Deinde cultum Dei euacuant, & paulatim exeusso omni timore cum illo ludere assuefecunt. Unde tandem effrenis atque indomita peccandi licentia nascitur. Et haec causa est, quod Christus, qui erga peccatores publicos quoque flagitiis infames se passim facilem & mansuetissimum praebet, tanta verborum vehementia & multorum criminum quasi congerie quadam adversus Pharisaeos & Legisperitos Iudaeorum inuebitur, qui & doctrinam legis foedissime adulterabant, & patrum vestigia secuti vera docentes hostiliter persequebantur, cum interim patres accusarent, & hos vellent sanctiores haberi. Quia autem dixerat, illos patrum mensuram implere, adeoque hos esse deteriores, id nunc probat, & apertius quid facturi sint docet.
units.tr: Just as God offers us all the treasures of his kingdom and grace through the saving teaching of his Word in his Son Jesus Christ, so nothing is usually borne with less patience than when this teaching is either impiously despised or corrupted and obscured by human traditions. For those who do this sin in several ways of ingratitude against God. First, they turn away from him who is the fountain of living water, and, having scorned his generosity, dig for themselves broken and pestilent cisterns. Second, they empty out the worship of God and, once all fear has been shaken off little by little, they grow accustomed to trifling with him. From this at last is born an unbridled and untamed licence to sin. And this is the reason why Christ, who shows himself everywhere easy-going and most gentle towards sinners, even those notorious for public crimes, rails against the Pharisees and the lawyers of the Jews with such vehemence of words and such a heap, as it were, of many accusations. They were shamefully corrupting the teaching of the law, and, following the footsteps of their fathers, they hostilely persecuted those who taught the truth, while at the same time they accused the fathers and wished these men to be held holier than others. But since he had said that they fill up the measure of their fathers, and so are worse than them, he now proves this and shows more openly what they are going to do.

units.la: Propterea etiam Sapientia Dei dixit: Mittam ad eos Prophetas & Apostoles, & ex ipsis quosdam trucidabunt, & quosdam expellent, &c. Sapientiam Dei loquentem inducit per prosopopoeiam vt & gravior fit oratio, & ista non temere fieri ostendat, sed iam olim Dei consilio sic decretum esse, qui certa cum ratione omnia agat. Pulchre autem confert bonitatem Dei cum illorum contumacia quae adversus illam magno suo malo luctentur. Singularis enim bonitatis fuit, quod Prophetas & Apostolos misit. Apud Matthaeum Sapientes quoque & Scribas nominat, vt gratia Dei liberalitas melius exprimatur: E contra autem magnum summae ingratitudinis & contumaciae argumentum est, quod non modo non obtemperaturos dicit, verumetiam trucidaturos & expulsuros esse eos, qui salutis ipsorum causa ad ipsos mittantur, quibus deinde grauem poenae comminationem infert, qua peccatum ipsorum magis quoque amplificatur. Sed praestat singula ex ordine videre.
units.tr: For this reason also the Wisdom of God said: "I will send to them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will slay, and some they will drive out," etc. He introduces the Wisdom of God speaking by prosopopoeia, both so that the discourse may be weightier and to show that these things do not happen by chance, but were decreed long ago by the counsel of God, who acts everything with certain reason. Moreover, he beautifully sets the goodness of God over against their obstinacy, by which they struggle against it to their great harm. For it was a singular goodness that he sent prophets and apostles. In Matthew he also names wise men and scribes, so that the generosity of God's grace may be expressed more fully. On the other hand, it is a strong proof of the greatest ingratitude and stubbornness that he says they will not only refuse to obey, but will even slay and drive out those who are sent to them for their salvation; then he adds a grave threat of punishment, by which their sin is made even greater. But it is better to see each point in order.

units.la: Primo, vt diximus insigne & praeclarum diuina bonitatis exemplum hic proponitur, qua ille erga mundum quantumus ingratum & contumacem solet vti. Eam autem euidentius agnoscemus si tempus consideretur, quo haec à Domino dicta sunt: Tunc nimirum, quando postquam regni diuisione à Solomonis morte factam, annis amplius mille cum ista gente Deus nequicquam egerat: quando ad ipsos missi Prophetae indigne modis reiecti & occisi erant: quando ex Babylone reuersi ad verbi Dei contemptum & Prophetarum caedes redierant: quando relicta vnitate ecclesiae in sectas erant diuisi: quando legem Dei suis traditionibus corruperant, cultum & religionem omnem partim ad hypocrisim instituerant, partim sibi ipsis quasdam fecerant: quando denique iam ipsum quoque Dei Filium in gentium manus tradituri & crudelissime occisuri erant. Tunc (inquam) Deus ex aeterno suo decreto plures adhuc misit, qui infelicem populum à sceleribus & ab interitu reuocarent. Et sicut per Joelem promiserat, effudit magna cum liberalitate Spiritum suum, & ex ipsorum filiis atque senibus Prophetas excitauit, qui de futuris poenis illos admonerent, & ad poenitentiam hortarentur. Dedit item viros sapientes & scripturarum peritos, qui consilia sana & utilia suggererent. Adhaec ex ipsis delegit Apostolos, qui Spiritus virtute pleni aeternae salutis verbum primo in sanguinaria Hierosolymorum vrbe, deinde in Iudaea, & tandem per totum orbem terrarum diuulgarent. Quibus ad de, quod (sicut olim minatus erat) gentium exemplo illos ad aemulationem prouocare conatus est, vt suam dignitatem tueri studerent.
units.tr: First, as we have said, a remarkable and outstanding example of divine goodness is set forth here, which he is wont to show towards the world, however ungrateful and stubborn it may be. We shall recognise this more clearly if we consider the time at which these things were spoken by the Lord: namely, when, more than a thousand years after the division of the kingdom made at Solomon's death, God had laboured in vain with this nation; when the prophets sent to them had been shamefully rejected and killed; when, returned from Babylon, they had gone back to despising God's Word and slaying the prophets; when, having abandoned the unity of the Church, they had been divided into sects; when they had corrupted the law of God by their own traditions, and had established worship and religion, partly as hypocrisy, partly devised by themselves; when, finally, they were about to hand over the very Son of God himself into the hands of the Gentiles and have him most cruelly put to death. Then (I say) God, by his eternal decree, sent still more, who might call back the unhappy people from their wickedness and from ruin. And as he had promised through Joel, he poured out his Spirit with great generosity, and raised up prophets from among their sons and old men, who would warn them of the punishments to come and exhort them to repentance. He likewise gave wise men, skilled in the Scriptures, who might offer sound and useful counsel. Besides these, from among them he chose apostles, who, full of the power of the Spirit, were to spread the word of eternal salvation first in the bloodthirsty city of Jerusalem, then in Judaea, and at last throughout the whole world. To these he added, so that they might be stirred to emulation (as he had once threatened), the example of the Gentiles, so that they might strive to defend their own dignity.

units.la: Sapientia Dei loquitur.
units.tr: The Wisdom of God speaks.

units.la: Bonitas Dei magna in Iudaeos.
units.tr: The great goodness of God towards the Jews.

units.la: Sunt hæc incomparabilis bonitatis & gratiæ Dei argumenta: nobis ante universalem Dei bonitatem commendandam, qua erga omnes homines vtitur. Nam vt Paulus ait, hoc eius ingenium est, quod omnes vult saluos fieri, & ad veritatis cognitionem peruenire. Et huius tam benignæ voluntatis exempla infinita extant ab ipso mundi exordio. Huc enim pertinet, quod hominem, quo minimè opus habebat, ex terra creauit, vt nimirum cum mundi primas iam conditi principem constitueret, & bonorum suorum omnium faceret consortem. Fuit hæc insignis bonitas, sed maior in eo elucet, quod eundem hominem turpi defectione lapsum, & iam morte æterna dignum denuo erexit, promissionibus de venturo vindice & Seruatore consolatus est, denique quod in Filio suo nos regenuit, & quasi nouos creauit, vt in filiorum locum adoptaret & regni sui cœlestis hæredes scriberet posset. Quis vero in his non agnoscat atq; admiretur illius plus quam paternam misericordiam? Est autem argumentum eius aliud quoque non minus euidens: quod nimirum sceleratissimos & ingratissimos quosque non punit, nisi sapius & fideliter antea pramonitos & edoctos, qua ratione pœnas ipsis imminentes possint effugere. Quam bonitatem Amos Propheta commendans ait: Non facit Dominus Deus quicquam, nisi reuelet arcanum suum seruis suis Prophetis. Quod ipsum quoque omnium gentium exemplis probari potest. Nam vt à Caino exordiamur, nonne hunc cum iniquum contra fratrem odium animo concepisset, & eius nefariam cædem meditaretur, fidelissimè & in tempore quidem admonuit, & quid de ipso futurum esset docuit, nisi ab instituto desisteret? Deinde cum filij Dei cæca libidine abrepti cum Cainitarum filiabus sese miscuissent, & inde impia Nephilim, id est, defectorum & ab omni religione alienorum progenies propagata totum mundum suo exemplo inficeret, & iam omnis caro corrupisset viam suam, non ante diluuij aquas immisit, quam prius pœnitentiæ agendæ tempus daret annorum centum viginti, & prædiconem iustitiæ suæ excitaret Noam, qui non verbis modo illos hortaretur, vt relictis sceleribus ad Deum rediret, verumetiam arcæ ædificatione pœnas adumbraret, quas de ipsis ille esset sumpturus, nisi eius admonitionibus obtemperarent. Post diluuium vero, cum maior hominum pars ad peccandi licentiam, illicitos cultus & idololatriam redijsset, Patriarchas excitauit, qui Prophetas agerent. Et hi quidem hinc inde incertis sedibus peregrinantes salutis promissiones omnibus inculcarunt, & suo exemplo vnius & veri Dei cultum tradiderunt. Et cum inter alias gentes luxu & dominandi libidine Ægyptij maximè peccarent, hos quoque non punivit, quin prius ad illos Iosephum destinaret, qui suo consilio ipsis adesset: pœnas leniores & famem immissam tolerabiliorem faceret, bonas leges constitueret, quibus intemperantia & peccandi licentia coercerentur. Postquam autem hoc mortuo Reges novi & rerum ignari successerunt, qui filios Israelis immani tyrannide affligebant, & cum tota gente in illius populi exitium conspirauerant, non tamen mox in illos fulminauit, sed per Mosem & Aaronem tam verbis quam gravibus & horrendis plagis eos admonuit, vt iram ipsius & pœnam graviorem matura pœnitentia declinarent. Cananæos quoque primùm per Patriarchas nequicquam admonitos, postea Ægyptiorum & Bajanitarum exemplis terruit (sicuti Rahab testatur) vt intra conscientias suas facile intelligerent, quid de ipsis esset futurum. De Iudæis vero quid attinet dicere, inter quos perpetuam verbi sui prædicationem esse voluit, qua admonerentur, & eius tausa Leuitas & Sacerdotes instituit, adhæc his in suo officio cessantibus, extraordinariè Prophetas ex omni hominum genere excitauit, qui scelera principum & populi corriperent, pœnas venturas denuntiarent, & ad pœnitentiam hortarentur. Quod si ad gentes exteras siue prophanas, quæ tunc fuerunt, oculos conuerteremus, his quoque admonitiones omnis generis adhibuit. Nam etsi verbo eius destituerentur, natura tamen legem cordibus inscriptam habuerunt, quæ quid rectum, quid prauum sit doceret. Dedit etiam illis Deus viros Sapientiæ studiosos, qui virtutis studium tam doctrina quam proprio exemplo illis commendabant. Habuerunt item Romani libros Sibyllinos, qui de multis eos admonebant. Quod si autem propter enormia & assidua peccata illos Deus vel pestè, vel famè, vel bellis affligere voluit, portenta & prodigia præmisit, quibus iram suam aperte reflatus est, vt huius metu territi de vitæ emendatione cogitarent. Taceo nunc, quod Ionam ad Niniuitas misit, quod reliqui Prophetæ vicinis etiam gentibus sua fata prædixerunt, quod Babylonijs Danielem dedit fidelissimum consultorem, quod per totum Romanum imperium Apostolos emisit, & in ipsa vrbe Roma verbum suum prædicari voluit; priusquam imperij dissipatio fieret. Quod autem olim fecit Deus, hoc ipsum hodie fieri videmus. Regnat ubique illius contemptus, & aut prophana audacia numen omne hominess ridper dent, aut ineptis atque impijs superstitionibus deditì verum illius cultum conculcant. Merebatur ergo mundus subitum & extremum exitium. Veruntamen non stricto iure agit Deus, sed verbi sui lucernam nouissimis hisce temporibus accendit, huius doctrinam inuitis etiam tyrannis per totum orbem diuulgat, per hanc scelera corripit, poenas minatur, ad poenitentiam excitat, prodigiis & signis in caelo & reliquis mundi partibus propositis, adhaec quotidianis iudiciorum suorum exemplis doctrinam atque minas Verbi sui confirmat, & (quod in primis memorabile est) eum omnium fere hominum animis sensum inserit, ut unanimiter & quasi uno ore testentur, hanc mundi faciem consistere non posse, & mutationem orbis totius omnino fieri oportere, alioqui uniuersale exitium breui sequuturum esse. Audiuntur haec passim ex vulgi ore, & cum infinitis dissensionibus inter se homines scindantur, in hoc tamen uno consentiunt. Sunt autem haec diuinae bonitatis argumenta, qua externis simul & internis praemonitionibus nos ab imminenti interitu reuocare satagit. Illam ergo nos agnoscere, in nosipsos descendere, ad Deum hunc tam benevolum converti, & procul relicta sceleribus sub misericordia eius alas confugere decet, ne nobis quoque dicatur aliquando, quod Christus apud Matthaeum incurabili Hierosolymitanorum civitati dicit: Ierusalem, Ierusalem, quae trucidas Prophetas, & lapidas eos qui ad te mittuntur, quoties volui congregare liberos tuos, quemadmodum gallina congregat pullos suos sub alas, & noluistis?
units.tr: These are arguments of incomparable goodness and grace of God, which must be commended to us before the universal goodness of God, by which he deals with all men. For, as Paul says, it is his nature that he wills all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. And countless examples of this most kindly will stand from the very beginning of the world. For to this belongs the fact that he created man out of the earth, though he had no need of him at all, so that, having made him prince of the world already formed, he might make him a sharer in all his goods. This was a remarkable kindness, but it shines out more greatly in this, that when the same man had fallen through shameful defection, and was already worthy of eternal death, he raised him up again, comforted him with promises of a coming avenger and Saviour, and finally that in his Son he gave us new birth and, as it were, created us anew, so that he might adopt us into the place of sons and enrol us as heirs of his heavenly kingdom. Who, indeed, does not recognise and marvel at his mercy, more than paternal, in these things? Yet there is another proof of it, no less evident: namely, that he does not punish even the most wicked and ungrateful, unless they have first been warned and taught often and faithfully about how they might escape the punishments hanging over them. The prophet Amos, commending this goodness, says: "The Lord God does nothing unless he reveals his secret to his servants the prophets." This can also be proved from the examples of all nations. To begin with Cain: when he had conceived in his mind an unjust hatred against his brother and was planning his wicked murder, did not God warn him most faithfully and in good time, and teach him what would become of him unless he gave up his purpose? Then, when the sons of God, carried away by blind lust, had mingled themselves with the daughters of the Cainites, and from them the impious Nephilim, that is, the offspring of apostates and men alien to all religion, had been propagated and had infected the whole world with their example, and all flesh had already corrupted its way, he did not send the waters of the flood until first he had given a time for repentance of one hundred and twenty years, and had raised up Noah as a preacher of his righteousness, who was not only to urge them with words to turn back to God and abandon their wickedness, but also by the building of the ark was to foreshadow the punishments he would inflict on them unless they obeyed his warnings. After the flood, however, when the greater part of mankind had returned to licence in sinning, to unlawful worship and idolatry, he raised up the patriarchs, who acted as prophets. And these, wandering here and there in uncertain dwellings, impressed the promises of salvation upon everyone, and by their own example handed down the worship of the one true God. And when among the other nations the Egyptians sinned most of all through luxury and the lust to rule, he did not punish them either without first sending them Joseph, who by his counsel would stand by them: he would make the penalties milder and the famine sent upon them more bearable, and would establish good laws by which intemperance and licence to sin would be restrained. But after this man died, new kings arose who knew nothing of these matters, and who oppressed the sons of Israel with monstrous tyranny, and conspired with the whole nation for that people's destruction. Yet he did not strike them down at once, but through Moses and Aaron admonished them, both by words and by terrible and grievous plagues, so that by timely repentance they might turn aside his anger and a heavier punishment. The Canaanites too, first warned in vain through the patriarchs, he afterwards terrified by the examples of the Egyptians and the Bashanites (as Rahab bears witness), so that in their own consciences they might easily understand what would become of them. As for the Jews, what need is there to speak? Among them he willed a continual proclamation of his Word, by which they might be admonished, and for its sake he instituted Levites and priests; and when these were negligent in their office, he raised up prophets, outside the ordinary way, from every rank of men, who would rebuke the crimes of princes and people, announce the punishments to come, and exhort them to repentance. But if we turn our eyes to the foreign or profane nations, which then existed, he likewise brought to them admonitions of every kind. For although they were without his Word, they nevertheless had the law written in their hearts by nature, which taught them what is right and what is wrong. God also gave them men devoted to wisdom, who recommended the pursuit of virtue to them both by teaching and by their own example. The Romans also had the Sibylline books, which warned them about many things. But if God wished to afflict them with plague, famine or wars because of their monstrous and constant sins, he sent beforehand portents and prodigies, by which he openly showed his anger, so that, frightened by fear of it, they might think about amending their lives. I say nothing now of how he sent Jonah to the Ninevites, how the other prophets foretold their fate even to the neighbouring nations, how he gave Daniel as a most faithful counsellor to the Babylonians, how he sent out the apostles through the whole Roman empire, and wished his word to be preached in the city of Rome itself before the dissolution of the empire. But what God did of old, we see him doing today as well. Everywhere his contempt reigns; some, with profane audacity, deride every divinity of man, while others, given over to foolish and impious superstitions, trample underfoot his true worship. The world therefore deserved sudden and final destruction. Yet God does not act with strict right, but in these latest times he has kindled the lamp of his Word; he spreads its teaching throughout the whole world, even against the will of tyrants; through it he rebukes sins, threatens punishments, and stirs men to repentance, setting forth prodigies and signs in the heavens and in the other parts of the world. Besides, by the daily examples of his judgements he confirms the teaching and threats of his Word, and (what is especially worth remarking) he has implanted in almost all men's minds such a sense that they testify with one accord, as if with one mouth, that this face of the world cannot stand, and that a change of the whole world must of necessity come about, or else universal destruction will soon follow. These things are heard everywhere from the mouths of the common people, and although men are divided among themselves by countless disagreements, in this one point they agree. These, then, are the proofs of divine goodness, by which he strives to call us back from impending ruin with warnings both outward and inward. It is fitting, therefore, that we acknowledge that goodness, come down into ourselves, turn to this so kind God, cast our sins far away and flee under his wings of mercy; lest it be said to us also at some time what Christ says to the hopeless city of Jerusalem in Matthew: "Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to you! How often would I have gathered your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not!"

units.la: Debet nos ad diligentiorem huius studij considerationem excitare, quod ipsum Dei sapientiam loquentem Christus inducit: Mittam ad vos Prophetas & Apostolos. Eo enim docet, verbi sui praecones non temere prodire aut surgere ad docendum, sed ab illo mitti & destinari. Quod Paulus uno verbo explicans ait: Quomodo praedicabunt nisi missi fuerint? Nam cum ex seipsis homines ne ad cogitandum quidem idonei sint (ut idem Apostolus testatur) nemo tantam functionem recte obire poterit, nisi donis ad eam necessarijs fuerit a Deo instructus. Id vero de illis nequaquam sperari potest, qui non ab eo missi fuerint. E contra autem ubi dotes ternuntur, quae ministrum ecclesiae decent, solida nimirum Scripturarum cognitio, docendi facultas, fides & zelus gloriae Dei, fortitudo & constantia in veritate asserenda, & quae alia sunt huius generis, illic dubitare non possumus, quin tales a Deo missi sint. Qui ergo horum admonitiones atque minas contemnunt, si in Deum peccant, et huius bonitatem atque gratiam aspernantur. Est hoc saepe meditandum, ut patientius feramus correptiones administrorum verbi, imo oremus Deum, ut tales mittat, qui non quae carni nostrae arridیent, sed quae ad salutem nostram faciunt, nobis praedicent.
units.tr: This should move us to consider this matter more carefully, since Christ introduces the very wisdom of God speaking: "I will send to you prophets and apostles." By this he teaches that the heralds of his Word do not come forward or rise up to teach on their own initiative, but are sent and appointed by him. Paul explains this in a single sentence: "How shall they preach unless they are sent?" For men are not fit even to think by themselves (as the same Apostle bears witness), and no one can rightly discharge so great a task unless he has been equipped by God with the gifts needed for it. Such gifts cannot be hoped for from those whom God has not sent. On the other hand, where we find the qualities that befit a minister of the Church, namely solid knowledge of the Scriptures, the ability to teach, faith and zeal for the glory of God, fortitude and steadfastness in defending the truth, and others of this kind, there we cannot doubt that such men have been sent by God. Those, then, who despise their admonitions and threats sin against God and scorn his goodness and grace. This is something we should often reflect on, so that we may bear the corrections of the ministers of the Word more patiently; indeed, let us pray God to send such men as will preach to us not what pleases our flesh, but what serves our salvation.

units.la: Caeterum ad alterum quoq; huius loci caput accedamus, quo Iudaeorum ingratitudinem & contumaciam cum summa crudelitate coniunctam describit, dicens: Ex ipsis quosdam trucidabunt, & quosdam expellent. In Matthaeo plures species enumerans ait: Ex illis nonnullos trucidabitis & crucifigetis, & nonnullos ex ipsis flagellabitis in Synagogis vestris, & persequemini ex urbe in urbem. Et haec quidem omnia illos fecisse constat. Nam ab ipso Domino, principe Prophetarum initio facto, eum in crucem egerunt. Ab eius autem ascensione Stephanum lapidarunt, Apostolos non semel in carcerem coniectos in Synagogis vel Concilijs virgis ceciderunt, & uniuersali persecutione per Saulum excitata multos utriusque sexus inhumanissime tractarunt, quorum alij crudeliter occisi, alij infirmiores fidem abnegare coacti, multi vero amissis fortunis omnibus per Iudaeam & Samariam dispersi sunt. Tandem Iacobum Apostolum Herodes capite multauit, & quia hoc faciens Iudaeis gratissimum esse videbat, Petrum quoq; comprehendit, hunc etiam occisurus, nisi cum Angelus Domini mirabiliter liberauisset. Quam iniuste autem & inique cum Paulo egerint, Lucas in Actorum libro prolixe exponit. Sua certe iniquitate eum ad Caesarem Neronem, monstrum libidinis & crudelitatis, prouocare coegerunt, & Romae ius quaerere, quod illi in urbe Sanctae negabatur. Tanta denique fuit istorum hominum aduersus Christum & eius seruos rabies, ut qui inter gentes hinc inde dispersi habitabant, non veriti fuerint Apostolis sese opponere, & seditiones excitare publicas, ut Euangelij praedicationem impedirent: quod in Antiochia Pisidiae, Iconij, Derbae, Lystris, Corinthi & multis alijs locis factum fuisse legimus: adeo ut verissime de illis Paulus scripserit: Qui etiam Dominum Iesum occiderunt & proprios Prophetas, nosq; expulerūt: neq; Deo placent, & omnibus hominibus aduersantur, probibentes nos gentibus praedicare vt seruē tur, vt semper compleant peccata sua: Occupauit enim eos ira ad extremum vsq;. Poterant haec mi-ra & incredibilia videri, eum videlicet populum eò impietatis olim esse progressum, quem Deus ex omnibus gentibus sibi peculium delegerat, quem gentem sanctam & solam dicit, inter quos cultum suum constituerat, quibus solis fere verbu suum reuelarat, & ex quibus Filium suum secundum carnem nasci oportuit: nisi adhuc hodie in infelicibus reliquijs hinc inde dispersis vetus illud ingenium & odij veterū argumenta clarissima elucerent. Etsi enim extrema olim passi sint, & adhuc Repub. simul & ordinarij cultus exercitijs destituantur, omnium item ludibrio & iniurijs expositi sint, & mortuum potius populi cadauer quam populus censeri mereantur, non desinunt tamen Christo Iesu maledicere, & quibuscunq; possunt modis illius cultoribus nocere. Adhuc ergo implent mensuram patrum suorum, sicut nuper Dominus dixit, ideoq; domus eorum deserta manet.
units.tr: But let us now come to the second part of this passage, in which he describes the ingratitude and obstinacy of the Jews, joined with the greatest cruelty, saying: "Some of them they will kill, and some they will drive out." In Matthew, listing several kinds of cruelty, he says: "Some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues, and you will persecute them from city to city." And it is clear that they did all these things. For, beginning with the Lord himself, the prince of the Prophets, they drove him to the cross. After his ascension they stoned Stephen; they cast the Apostles into prison more than once and beat them with rods in the synagogues and councils; and, when a general persecution was stirred up by Saul, they treated many men and women most inhumanly, some of whom were cruelly put to death, others, being weaker, were forced to deny the faith, and many, having lost all their possessions, were scattered throughout Judea and Samaria. At last Herod had the Apostle James beheaded, and, because he saw that this pleased the Jews, he also seized Peter, intending to kill him as well, had not the Angel of the Lord wonderfully delivered him. How unjustly and iniquitously they dealt with Paul, Luke sets out at length in the book of Acts. Indeed, by their own wickedness they compelled him to appeal to Caesar Nero, a monster of lust and cruelty, and to seek justice at Rome, since it was denied him in the holy city. In short, such was the fury of these men against Christ and his servants that, though they lived scattered among the nations here and there, they did not hesitate to oppose the Apostles and to stir up public disturbances in order to hinder the preaching of the gospel. We read that this happened at Antioch in Pisidia, at Iconium, Derbe, Lystra, Corinth and many other places. So Paul wrote very truly of them: "They who killed the Lord Jesus and their own prophets, and have driven us out; they do not please God and are opposed to all men, forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles that they may be saved, so that they always fill up their sins. For wrath has come upon them to the uttermost." These things might seem wonderful and incredible: that the people whom God chose from all the nations as his own possession, whom he called a holy nation and the only one, among whom he established his worship, to whom almost alone he revealed his Word, and from whom his Son was to be born according to the flesh, should have advanced so far into impiety. Yet this is clearly seen even today in the wretched remnants scattered here and there: that old disposition and the clearest signs of ancient hatred still shine forth. For although they have suffered the worst, and still lack both a commonwealth and the regular exercise of worship, and although they are exposed to the mockery and injuries of all, and deserve to be regarded as the corpse of a people rather than a people, they do not cease to curse Christ Jesus and to harm his worshippers by every means they can. Therefore they still fill up the measure of their fathers, as the Lord recently said, and so their house remains desolate.

units.la: Interea simul docet hic locus, quae administrorum verbi Dei fors sit in hoc mundo. Constat hic fere ex Pharisaeis propria iustitia fiducia turgentibus, & Epicuraeis, qui cum Deo sacra omnia contemnunt, & cum risu excipiunt quaecunque de caelo & inferis, deque futura vita praemijs & poenis dicuntur. At neutri horum verbi diuini lucem & Christi praedicationem ferre possunt. Illi enim in sua iustitiam suam damnari nolunt, & gratia doctrinam oderunt, quae nostrorum operum merita confutat: Hi vero disciplinam nullam admittere, neque suam licentiam villis admonitionibus aut correptionibus volunt coerceri. Est enim hoc natura insitu omnibus hominibus, vt virtuti quidem studendum esse intelligant, simul autem carnis affectibus abrepti ad vitia inclinent, & hus potissimum delectentur. Hinc fit quod borum quidem illos pudeat, virtutis autem vmbram modo & fucum sequantur, quo vitia sua pallient. Nihil ergo illis tam aduersum & molestum est, quam si per Verbum Dei vitia arguantur, & fucus ille virtutis abstergatur. At quia lucem ipsam extinguere non possunt, aduersus huius administros insurgunt, quasi hic è medio sublatus illa non amplius lucere queat. Et mirum est, haec duo hominum genera, cum inter se quam maxime pugnent, posse tamen conuenire, quoties de Euangelij luce obruenda agitur. Sic olim Pharisaeos cum Sadducaeis & Herodianis, quorum impietas omnibus nota erat, in Christi perniciem coniurauisse legimus. Et hodie Monachos, qui mundo & carni omnino mortui videri volunt, non solum inter aulicos luxu & libidine diffluentes, verum etiam in medijs castris, inter militum acies & utrinque tonantium bombardarum fulmina vt litare, & militiae contra Christi vnius cultores duces esse videmus. Taceo quod ijdem saepe piorum quaestionibus intersunt, & carnifices in adhibendis & excogitandis tormentis adiuuant. Tanta odij aduersus veritatem concepti vis est atq; rabies. Nemo autem quando haec fieri videt, vt nouus & insolitus offendatur, sed in mentem reuocet quae olim facta sunt, & quae tam hic quam alibi a Christo praedicuntur. Vniuersalis enim quam omnibus suis cultoribus praescribit regula est: Si quis vult post me venire, abneget semetipsum, & tollat crucem suam quotidie & sequatur me. Et Paulus ait: Omnes qui volunt pie viuere in Christo Iesu persecutionem patientur. Item: Per multas tribulationes oportet nos ingredi in regnum Dei. Quod propter eos annotamus, qui solos verbi praecones ad crucem vocari putant, sibijpsis vero otium, opes, honores, pacem huius seculi & omnia laeta pollicentur.
units.tr: Meanwhile this passage also teaches what lot awaits the ministers of God's Word in this world. It is made up almost entirely of Pharisees, puffed up with confidence in their own righteousness, and of Epicureans, who despise all sacred things with God and greet with laughter whatever is said of heaven and hell and of rewards and punishments in the life to come. Yet neither of these groups can bear the light of the divine Word and the preaching of Christ. The former are unwilling to be condemned for their own righteousness, and they hate the doctrine of grace, which refutes the merit of our works; the latter will admit no discipline and do not want their licence to be restrained by any admonitions or corrections. For this is implanted by nature in all men: they understand that they ought to pursue virtue, yet, carried away by the desires of the flesh, they incline to vices and take their greatest pleasure in them. Hence it comes about that they are ashamed of the one thing, while they follow only the shadow and mask of virtue, by which they cloak their vices. Nothing is therefore so hostile and troublesome to them as when their vices are exposed by the Word of God and that mask of virtue is wiped away. But since they cannot extinguish the light itself, they rise up against its ministers, as though, once this man is removed from the midst, the light could no longer shine. And it is remarkable that these two kinds of men, though they fight with each other most bitterly, can nevertheless come together whenever there is a question of crushing the light of the gospel. Thus we read that the Pharisees conspired with the Sadducees and the Herodians, whose impiety was known to all, for the destruction of Christ. And today we see monks, who wish to appear wholly dead to the world and to the flesh, not only wallowing in luxury and lust among courtiers, but also, in the midst of camps, among the battle lines and the thunder of cannon on both sides, offering sacrifices and acting as captains of the army against the sole worshippers of Christ. I say nothing of the fact that the same men often attend the examinations of the godly, and help the executioners both in applying and in devising torments. So great is the force and fury of hatred conceived against the truth. Yet when we see these things happening, no one should be offended as though they were something new and unusual; rather, let him recall what was done in former times, and what Christ foretold both here and elsewhere. For he prescribes one general rule to all his worshippers: "If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross daily, and follow me." And Paul says: "All who wish to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution." Likewise: "We must enter the kingdom of God through many tribulations." We note this on account of those who think that only the heralds of the Word are called to the cross, while they promise themselves leisure, wealth, honours, the peace of this age, and every pleasant thing.

units.la: At quia carnis ratio curiosa nimis miratur, cur ista Deus fieri sinat, & cur Euangelij sui nuncios mittat, quos à mundo infelici tam duriter & tam iniquè tractandos esse nouit: nonnulla de hoc adijcienda erunt. Etenim inter homines parum prudens, & vix vir bonus haberetur, qui seruulos vilissimos, ne dum filios suos, sciens volensque in manifestum vitae discrimen absque fructu conijceret. Sed longè alia est ratio apud Deum, cuius aeterna sapientia, bonitas, veritas & iustitia in hoc maximè elucent. Primò enim omnium suarum rationem habet; quae inter huius seculi filios hinc inde dispersa, pastoribus indiget, qui ipsas colligant, pascant, confirment & ducant, ne eodem cum impijs lupis & vulpibus exitio inuoluantur. Nec enim aequum foret impiorum malitiam & contumaciam electis Dei fraudi esse, quos ab eius dilectione (vt Paulus ait) nemo separare potest. Deinde neque ministri aut pastores habent, de quo iure conquerantur. Quia enim aeternus Dei Filius ideo in mundum venit, & post infinitos labores atq; pericula mortem crudelem in cruce
units.tr: But since the curious reasoning of the flesh wonders too much why God allows these things to happen, and why he sends the messengers of his gospel whom he knows will be treated so harshly and so unjustly by an unhappy world, some points must be added on this matter. For among men, someone who knowingly and willingly exposed his most worthless servants, let alone his own sons, to a manifest peril of life without any profit would scarcely be thought prudent, and hardly a good man. But the reasoning with God is quite different, whose eternal wisdom, goodness, truth and justice shine most brightly in this matter. For first of all he takes account of all his own: those who are scattered here and there among the children of this age and need shepherds to gather them, feed them, strengthen them and lead them, so that they are not involved in the same destruction with the wicked wolves and foxes. For it would not be fair that the malice and obstinacy of the wicked should be a cheat to the elect of God, whom (as Paul says) no one can separate from his love.

units.la: Sors praeconum verbi in munedo.
units.tr: The lot of the heralds of the Word in the world.

units.la: Cur Deus suos indignius tractari sinat.
units.tr: Why God allows his own to be treated more unworthily.

units.la: Ioan. 13. subijte, vt filios Dei dispersos ad sui gregis vnitatem reduceret, quae obsecro iniuria fit hominibus, si eorum opera in eo ipso vtatur, quod ipse prior praestitit? Quin potius suam gloriam & dignitatem cales agnoscere debent, quod nimirum Christus illos pro suis adiutoribus & cooperatoribus (vt Paulus loquitur) habere dignatur, & eosdem sibi in cruce & affl. Ationibus conformes facit, vt olim eiusdem gloriae & regni socii atque coheredes fiant. Et huc promissio eius referri debet: Volo vt vbi ego sum, illic sit etiam minister meus. Quorum Apostoli olim memores gaudebant, quod dignos iudicauisset Deus, qui pro nomine Filij sui virgis caederentur. Postremo impios Dei & veritatis contemptores omni excusationis praetextu spoliari necesse est. Nam nota satis est humani ingenij improbitas, qua fit, vt pessimi quique effugia captent, & suae perditionis causam in ipsum Deum, vitae auctorem, reijcere audeant, quod nos ex primis parentibus quasi iure haereditario contraxisse alibi demonstrauimus. Si ergo quos incurabiles esse nouit Deus, omni doctrina & verbi sui praedicatione in vniuersum destitueret, iam haberent illi quod ipsi obijcerent, quasi ab eo per inuidiam effent neglecti. Qua propter illis etiam verbi sui medicinam adhibet, vt quādo eos ex illa deteriores fieri videmus, quae aliis ad vitae adiumento est, omnibus constet, ipsos sibi proprij exitij authores esse. Exigit ire Dei iustitia vt eos non ante puniat quam mensura suam impleuerint. Id vero ea occasione fit, dum oblata sibi in verbo Dei gratia impie reijciunt, atque conculcant. Nihil ergo in tota hac causa Deus vel imprudenter vel iniuste facit: & intra hos fines pij suas cogitationes continere debent, ne dum in consiliorum illius arcana profundius inquirunt, temerarij nimis fiant, & tandem cum impijs illusoribus puniantur.
units.tr: John 13. He submitted himself so that he might bring the scattered children of God back to the unity of his flock. What wrong, I ask you, is done to men if God makes use of their labour in that very work which he himself first accomplished? Rather, they ought to recognise their glory and dignity, since Christ deigns to have them as his helpers and co-workers (as Paul puts it), and makes them conformable to himself in the cross and in afflictions, so that one day they may become partners in his glory and kingdom and joint heirs. His promise should also be referred to this: "I will that where I am, there my minister also may be." The Apostles, mindful of this, once rejoiced that God had counted them worthy to be beaten with rods for the name of his Son. Finally, the impious despisers of God and of the truth must necessarily be stripped of every pretext for excuse. For the wickedness of the human mind is well known: the worst men seek escape routes and dare to lay the cause of their own perdition at God's own door, the author of life, although we have shown elsewhere that we have drawn this from our first parents as if by hereditary right. If God were therefore to abandon altogether, with all teaching and the preaching of his Word, those whom he knows to be incurable, they would have something to throw back at him, as if they had been neglected by him out of spite. For this reason he applies the medicine of his Word even to them, so that when we see them grow worse through that which is a help to life for others, it may be plain to all that they themselves are the authors of their own ruin. The justice of God requires that he not punish them before they have filled up their measure. This happens on the occasion when they impiously reject and trample underfoot the grace offered to them in the Word of God. Therefore in this whole matter God does nothing either rashly or unjustly, and within these limits the godly ought to keep their thoughts, lest, while they inquire too deeply into the secrets of his counsels, they become too bold and at last be punished along with the impious mockers.

units.la: Restat tertium & postremum huius loci caput, quo poenam Iudaeis persecutoribus seruorum Dei denuntiat his verbis: Vt a natione ista requiratur sanguis omnium Prophetarum effusus a iactu fundamentis mundi. Et mox per amplificationem addit: A sanguine Abeli vsque ad sanguinem Zachariae, qui perijt inter altare & aedem. Nec eo contentus, affirmationis vehementioris loco subijcit: Etiam dico vobis, requiretur ab ista natione. Est autem haec grauissima comminatio, quod facile intelligemus, si quantum fit apud Deum homicidij & effusi sanguinis scelus consideretur. Hoc certe sub initio mundi in Caino seuerissime puniuit. A diluuio autem hanc legem fere solam Noe & filijs suis dedit, ne hominis sanguinem fundant, & poenam capitalem homicidae iam tunc constituit: neque minus excideret Legis tam necessaria memoria, sanguinis efusi interdixit. In lege vero non contentus caedes simpliciter & diserte prohibuisse, inter alia sic dicit: Ne recipiatis pretium redemptionis pro vita homicidae, qui ad mortem damnatus est, sed omnino interfici debet. Ne faciatis vt terra, in qua habitatis, fallat. Sanguis enim facit, vt terra fallat, neque potest terra a sanguine qui in ea effusus est, expiari, nisi per sanguinem illius, qui sanguinem effudit. Quod si vnius caedes scelus tantae abominationi est Deo, quid ergo de illis fiet, qui multorum simul reatu tenentur? Ideo Ezechielis dirum quoddam supplicium minatur, quo ipsum puniri oporteat, si in suo officio sit negligentior, ait: Sanguinem eorum, qui pereunt, de manu tua requiram. Et apud Matthaeum Iudaeorum genti spem simul omnem restitutionis negat, dicens: Idcirco relinquetur vobis domus vestra deserta: Dico enim vobis, nequaquam videbitis me ab hoc tempore, vsque dum dicatis, Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini. Et quod minatur, vere illis accidisse ex historiis patet. Cum enim mensuram impietatis impleuissent, Romanorum legiones illis induxit Deus, qui terra omni capta & vastata, tandem Hierosolymae murus exercitum admouerunt, quam post diuturnam & diram famem atque caedes innumeras coeperunt, captam vna cum templo solo aequarunt, reliquias autem populi infelicis in diuersa loca distribuerunt. Manifestum abeo tempore locus, vbi vrbs fuit desertus, ne que Templum vnquam reaedificari potuit: Iudaei autem hodie adhuc miserrimi hominum patrijs sedibus eiecti exulant, omniumque iniurias & ludibria sustinent. Et ita suorum seruorum sanguinem vltus est Dominus.
units.tr: There remains the third and last head of this passage, in which he threatens the Jews, the persecutors of the servants of God, with punishment in these words: "That the blood of all the Prophets, shed since the foundation of the world, may be required of this nation." And soon, by way of amplification, he adds: "From the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the temple." Not content with this, he adds, by way of a more vehement affirmation: "Yes, I say to you, it shall be required of this nation." This is a most grievous threat, as we shall readily understand if we consider how great a crime murder and the shedding of blood is before God. At the beginning of the world he punished this most severely in Cain. After the Flood, he gave almost only this law to Noah and his sons, that they should not shed man's blood, and from that time he established the capital punishment of the murderer. Nor, lest this so necessary law should fall out of memory, did he forbid the shedding of blood only in general terms. In the Law, not content to prohibit murder simply and plainly, he says among other things: "You shall not take a ransom for the life of a murderer who is condemned to death, but he shall surely be put to death. You shall not defile the land in which you dwell, for blood defiles the land, and the land cannot be cleansed of the blood that is shed in it, except by the blood of him who shed it." If the murder of one man is so great an abomination to God, what then will become of those who are bound by the guilt of many at once? Hence he threatens a certain dreadful punishment to Ezekiel, by which he must be punished if he is negligent in his office: "I will require the blood of those who perish at your hand." And in Matthew he denies to the Jewish nation all hope of restoration, saying: "Therefore your house is left to you desolate; for I say to you, you shall not see me from now on, until you say, Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord." And that what he threatens truly befell them is plain from the histories. For when they had filled up the measure of their impiety, God brought upon them the legions of the Romans, who, having taken and laid waste all the land, at last brought their army against the wall of Jerusalem. After a long and dreadful famine and countless slaughters they took it, and together with the temple razed it to the ground, and scattered the remnant of the unhappy people into various places. From that time the place where the city was is plain to see as a desert, nor could the temple ever be rebuilt. The Jews, most wretched of men, even today are driven from their ancestral homes and live in exile, and endure the wrongs and mockery of all. And so the Lord has avenged the blood of his servants.

units.la: Docet autem locus hic, quam graue quamque noxium peccatum sit impiorum, & quidem patrum quoque improbis consilijs atque sceleribus communicare. Nam qui id faciunt, ij non solum flagitij quod ipsi committunt, verumetiam omnium iam ante a similibus commissorum sese reos faciunt. Vt enim qui latronum societati se coniungit, cum illis comprehensus eadem cum illis omnium furtorum, rapinarum atque caedium, quas prius illi commiserunt, poenas luit: ita qui impiorum mores & facta imitatur, eodem cum illis reatu & ijsdem poenis inuoluitur. Nam in ipsis mundi primordijs, in duas quasi ciuitates totum genus humanum diuisum esset, Ciuitatem nimirum Cainitarum & Ciuitatem filiorum Dei. Vt ergo quicunque filij Dei per fidem in Christum fiunt, eandem cum veteribus Patriarchis, Prophetis, Apostolis, electis deniq; omnibus, regni coelorum hereditatem adeunt: ita qui Cainitarum generi per libidinem, rapinas, caedes & alia flagitia adfrutescunt, ij quoq; ijdem cum primis illis Dei & aequi omnes contemptoribus poenas affligentur. Recte ergo Dominus a Iudaeis requiren dum fore dicit sanguinem omnium Prophetarum, qui ab ipsius Abel ... caede per Cainum fasta effusa sit, usq; ad Zachariam filium Barachiae, quem ipsorum patres inter templum & altare occiderunt. Fuit autem Zacharias ex duodecim Prophetarum, quos Minores dicunt, numero, & ex Babylone reuersis concionatus esset, sicuti in illius expositione demonstrauimus. Et loci meminit Christus, vt patrum impiam crudelitatem arguat, quos nec templi nec sacrorum religio continere potuerit, vt ab innoxij sanguinis effusione sibi temperarent. Ita vero cristas detrahit ijs, qui patrum virtute gloriabantur. Nos autem hinc discamus, non temere a Dauide eum beatum pronuntiari, qui non ambulat in consilio impiorum, nec in via peccatorum pedem figit, neq; in consessum illusorum sese ingerit. Cauteamus ergo talium hominum consuetudinem, & si id non omnino poterit fieri, saltem nihil cum illorum moribus, studijs atq; consilijs commune habeamus. Nec enim inultum finit suorum sanguinem Dominus, etiamsi ad tempus vim atq; iniuriam illis factam dissimulet. Et pretiosa est in oculis eius mors sanctorum ipsius, quorum animae sub magno illo altari delitescentes vindictam postulant. Exempla quae huc faciunt, infinita cum priuata tum publica adduci poterant, sed cum multorum loco esse possit, quod hic in Iudaorum gente proponitur, alijs non est opus.
units.tr: This passage teaches how grave and how harmful a sin it is to share in the wicked counsels and crimes of the impious, and indeed of the fathers as well. For those who do so make themselves guilty not only of the wickedness they commit themselves, but also of all the crimes committed before by similar men. For just as one who joins a band of robbers, when caught with them, pays the same penalties for all the thefts, robberies and murders which they committed earlier, so one who imitates the manners and deeds of the impious is caught up in the same guilt and the same punishments. For at the very beginning of the world the whole human race was divided, as it were, into two cities, namely the city of the Cainites and the city of the sons of God. Therefore, just as whoever become sons of God through faith in Christ enter into the inheritance of the kingdom of heaven together with the ancient Patriarchs, Prophets, Apostles, and in short all the elect, so those who grow strong in the stock of the Cainites through lust, robbery, murder and other shameful deeds are likewise punished together with those first despisers of God and of all justice. Rightly, therefore, the Lord says that the blood of all the Prophets, which has been shed from the murder of Abel by Cain onwards, will be required of the Jews, down to Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom their fathers slew between the temple and the altar. Zechariah was one of the twelve Prophets whom they call the Minor, and after the return from Babylon he preached, as we have shown in his exposition. And Christ mentions the passage to convict the impious cruelty of the fathers, whom not even the sanctity of the temple and of the sacred rites could restrain from shedding innocent blood. In this way he strips of their pride those who boasted in the virtue of their fathers. But let us learn from this not to call lightly blessed the man whom David pronounced blessed, who does not walk in the counsel of the impious, nor stand in the way of sinners, nor sit in the seat of the scornful. Let us then beware of the company of such men, and if this cannot wholly be done, at least let us have nothing in common with their manners, pursuits and counsels. For the Lord does not allow the blood of his own to go unavenged, even if for a time he overlooks the violence and wrong done to them. Precious in his sight is the death of his saints, whose souls, hiding under that great altar, demand vengeance. Examples bearing on this could be brought forward in infinite number, both private and public, but since what is set forth here in the nation of the Jews can stand for many, there is no need of others.

units.la: Obseruari autem hic debet, vnde vrbium & gentium excidia fere proueniant? Nimirum ex verbi Dei contemptu & innocentis sanguinis effusione. Fieri enim non potest, vt suam gratiam, quam per verbum nobis offert Deus, reiici & conculcari patiatur. Ferunt quidem interdum principes subditorum suorum rebellionem, & culpam suam agnoscentes in gratiam recipiunt: At si ijdem non modo seditiose tumultuentur, sed gratiam quoq; sibi oblatam aspernentur, & aduersus eius nuntios hostili ter insurgant, id nemo bonus princeps patienter ferre potest. Atqui eadem est ratio inter nos & Deum. Natura enim omnes rebellionis reatu tenemur, & quotidie in illius leges peccamus. Condonat ille nobis clementer hanc culpam, & per Euangelium nobis pacem in Filio suo Iesu Christo offert. Quem si recipiamus, concordia facta & rata est. At si Euangelium pacis contemnamus, huius Mediatorem Christum audire detrectemus, & eius seruos sine praeconis persequamur, proscindamus, occidamus de nique, id demum nulla venia dignum scelus est, & aduersus tales mox sui iudicij rigore Deus stringit, vt digno exitio illos male perdat. Est hoc probatum omnium seculorum exemplis, quae cum historias legentibus subinde occurrant, nolumus illos recensendis immorari: Nostrorum potius temporum mores & statum considerremus, & quae hic dicuntur, illis omnino couenire patebit. Regnat vbiq; peccandi licentia, vt verissime hodie dici possit, quod de suo seculo olim Dauid cecinit: Omnes defecerunt, omnes pariter corrupti sunt, nullus est qui quod bonum est faciat, ne vnus quidem: Devorant populum meum perinde ac si panem vorarent, neq; Dominum inuocant, &c. Nihilominus tamen verbi sui doctrina nos Deus dignatur, qua ad poenitentiam inuitat, & ad se conuersis gratiae suae thesauros pollicetur. Quid vero fit? Verbum hoc alij secure contemnunt, alij gratiae praedicationem erroris & haereseos accusant, multi in huius praeconès vim faciunt, ferro & igne tam hos quam horum sectatores crudelissime persequuntur. Quid ergo aliud faciat Deus, quam vt suam quoq; manu ad verbera exerat, & infelicem mundum turbis, seditionibus, bellis externis atq; ciuilibus inter se committat, vt qui aduersus ipsum tumultuatur, dignas suae impietatis poenas luant? Fiunt ista hodie, & grauiora sequentur, nisi ad Deum serio conuertamur. Agnoscamus ergo gratiam Dei, quam indignus offert, audiamus Euangelii pacis, & huius principi nos humiliter subiiciamus, Iesu Christo nimirum, qui solus rebus afflictis opem ferre poterit. Huic debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: It should be noted here from what cause the destruction of cities and nations mostly arises. Surely from contempt of the Word of God and the shedding of innocent blood. For God cannot suffer his grace, which he offers to us through the Word, to be rejected and trodden underfoot. Indeed, princes sometimes bear the rebellion of their subjects, and when the subjects acknowledge their fault they receive them again into favour. But if the same subjects not only riot seditiously, but also scorn the grace offered to them, and rise up in hostility against its messengers, no good prince can bear this patiently. Yet the same reasoning holds between us and God. For by nature we are all bound by the guilt of rebellion, and we sin daily against his laws. He mercifully pardons us this fault, and through the Gospel offers us peace in his Son Jesus Christ. If we receive him, the reconciliation is made and confirmed. But if we despise the Gospel of peace, refuse to hear Christ the Mediator, and persecute, tear apart and finally kill his servants, the heralds of the Gospel, this crime is at last one deserving no pardon, and God straightway bends the rigour of his judgement against such men, so that he may destroy them with a fitting ruin. This has been proved by the examples of all ages, which, since they constantly meet readers of histories, we do not wish to dwell on by recounting them. Let us rather consider the manners and condition of our own times, and it will plainly appear that what is said here fits them entirely. Everywhere licence to sin reigns, so that it can be said most truly today what David once sang of his own age: "They have all gone aside, they are all alike corrupt; there is none who does good, no, not one. They eat up my people as though they ate bread, and they do not call upon the Lord," and so on. Nevertheless God deigns to address us with the teaching of his Word, by which he invites us to repentance and promises the treasures of his grace to those who turn to him. But what happens? Some carelessly despise this Word, others accuse the preaching of grace of error and heresy, and many do violence to its heralds, and persecute both these and their followers most cruelly with sword and fire. What else then should God do than stretch out his hand to strike, and leave the unhappy world to clash with itself in tumults, seditions, and foreign and civil wars, so that those who rise up against him may pay the fitting penalties of their impiety? These things happen today, and worse will follow unless we seriously turn to God. Let us therefore acknowledge the grace of God, which he offers though we are unworthy, let us hear the Gospel of peace, and humbly submit ourselves to its Prince, that is, to Jesus Christ, who alone can bring help to afflicted things. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CXXIIII.
units.tr: HOMILY CXXIV.

units.la: Vae vobis Legis interpretibus, quoniam sustulistis clauem cognitionis: ipsi non introiuistis, & eos qui introibant prohibuistis. Cum autem hæc eis diceret, coeperunt Scribæ & Pharisæi vehementer ipsi imminere, & eum allicere ad loquendum de multis, insidiantes ei, & quærentes vænari aliquid ex ipsius ore, vt eum accusarent.
units.tr: "Woe to you lawyers, for you have taken away the key of knowledge; you did not enter in yourselves, and you hindered those who were entering." As he said these things to them, the Scribes and Pharisees began to press upon him fiercely and to draw him out to speak about many things, lying in wait for him and seeking to catch something from his mouth, so that they might accuse him.

units.la: Voniam Dei Filius, Iesus Christus, vt nos saluos faceret in mundum venit, officij sui fuit omnia ea oppugnare & e medio tollere, quæ nos impediunt, quo minus salute consequamur. Inter illa primum locum tenent falsi doctores, qui verbi Dei doctrinam suis traditionibus & figmentis vel corrumpunt, vel omnino abolent & sepeliunt. Faciebant utrumque inter Iudæos Scribæ & Sacerdotes. Ideo grauissime in illos inuehitur, non quidem quod illos curari posse speraret, sed vt simplicem populum ab illis abstraheret. Quia enim Sacerdotum ordo Dei institutione nitebatur, qui legem ab illis requirere, & eosdem in omnibus, quæ agenda sunt, consulere iusserat, populus eos, qui tum hoc nomine gloriabatur, pro legitimis & ordinarijs doctoribus habebat, quibus necessario esset obtemperandum. Quæ persuasio multis exitij & perditionis causa erat, eo quod hos secuti ipsum negligebant, qui nobis a Patre veritatis doctor datus est, & in quo vno omnis salus habetur. Itaque illis alteris larvam detrahi necesse erat, vt eos non legitimos aut veros doctores, sed seductores, non pastores, sed lupos esse, omnes viderent, & proinde se ab illis seduci non paterentur. Quod autem Christus fecit, hoc etiam hodie fieri debet, quando multi in Ecclesia sibi omne ius vendicant, quos similiter rudes & rerum imperiti suspiciunt & venerantur, cum revera lupi sint, & Christi oule horribiliter dissipent. Contra illos ergo verbi ministri vocem suam attollere, errores & tyrannidem eorum arguere, & omnes admonere debent, vt ab illis sibi caveant. Neque audiendi sunt, qui hoc facto indignum & a ministrorum Ecclesiæ officio alienum putant, quos lenitas & manstuetudo in primis deceat. Nam vt hac erga peccatores vti conuenit, vt corrigantur & spem salutis certa concipiant: ita crudelitas fuerit maxima lupis permittere, vt incautas oues subinde lanient atque devorent. Et maior earum ratio habenda est, quando videmus multos, qui Christum iam amplexi sunt, inani antiquitatem eiusmodi splendore sic decipi, vt se sponte in illorum vngues & fauces ingerant. Nec est quod hominum huius seculi iudicia multum morentur fideles ministri, quando ad hos defendendos Christi exemplum sufficit, quo nemo unquam mitior & mansuetior in terris visus est. Sed vt ad præsentia locis tractationem accedamus, nuper tyrannidem legis interpretum & doctorum accusauit, quam partim docendo exercebant, cum miseros homines traditionibus portatu difficillimis grauarent: partim perse-cutionibus, quibus veritatis præcones expellere & in eos crudeliter græssari solebant, maiorum suorum vestigia nimirum secuti, qui olim idem fecerant. Nunc vero ad ipsum Colophonem impietatis & tyrannidis ipsorum accedit, & illos fures sacrilegos atque latrones esse ostendit, quales apud Ioannem cap.10. dixerat.
units.tr: Since the Son of God, Jesus Christ, came into the world to save us, it was his task to attack and remove all those things that hinder us from obtaining salvation. Among these, false teachers hold the first place: they either corrupt the doctrine of God's Word with their traditions and inventions, or altogether abolish and bury it. The Scribes and priests among the Jews did both. Therefore he inveighs most severely against them, not indeed because he hoped they could be cured, but so that he might draw the simple people away from them. For since the order of priests rested on God's institution, and he had commanded that the law be sought from them and that they be consulted in all matters to be done, the people regarded those who boasted of this name at that time as lawful and ordinary teachers, whom it was necessary to obey. This persuasion was the cause of much ruin and destruction, because by following these men they neglected him who has been given to us by the Father as the Teacher of truth, and in whom alone all salvation is found. Therefore it was necessary to strip the mask from the others, so that everyone might see that they were not lawful or true teachers but seducers, not shepherds but wolves, and so would not allow themselves to be led astray by them. What Christ did, this ought to be done today too, when many in the Church claim every right for themselves, whom simple and inexperienced people likewise admire and venerate, although they are really wolves and dreadfully scatter Christ's sheep. Therefore ministers of the Word ought to raise their voice against them, to expose their errors and tyranny, and to warn everyone to be on their guard against them. Nor should those be heard who think this unworthy and foreign to the office of Church ministers, for whom gentleness and meekness above all are fitting. For just as it is proper to use gentleness toward sinners, so that they may be corrected and conceive a sure hope of salvation, so it would be the greatest cruelty to allow wolves to mangle and devour the unwary sheep again and again. And greater regard must be had for them, since we see many who have already embraced Christ being so deceived by the empty splendour of such antiquity that they willingly thrust themselves into their claws and jaws. Nor should faithful ministers linger much over the judgments of the people of this age, since the example of Christ is enough to defend them, than whom no one was ever seen to be milder and gentler on earth. But to come to the matter now in hand: he recently accused the tyranny of the lawyers and teachers, which they exercised partly by teaching, when they burdened wretched men with traditions very hard to bear; and partly by persecutions, by which they were accustomed to drive out the heralds of truth and rage cruelly against them, following, of course, the footsteps of their forefathers who had done the same. But now he comes to the very summit of their impiety and tyranny, and shows that they are sacrilegious thieves and robbers, as he had said in John chapter 10.

units.la: Væ vobis (inquit) Legis interpretibus, quoniam sustulistis clauem cognitionis: ipsi non introistis, & eos qui introibant prohibuistis. Quæ verba apud Matthæum sic enuntiantur: Væ vobis Scribæ & Pharisæi hypocritæ, quoniam claudit regnum cælorum coram hominibus: vos enim non introitis, neque introeuntes finitis introire. Ergo de regno cælorum & æternæ salutis negotio hic agitur. Per clauem vero cognitionis aut scientiæ, doctrina & prædicatio verbi Dei intelligitur, per quam Regni Dei mysteria referantur, vt homines ea videre & huius consequendi rationem atque viam intelligere possint. Et admonet nos ista locutio, quam necessaria sit doctrina & diligens Verbi Dei atque Scripturarum enarratio. Nam vt non profuerit palatium magnificum coram videre, aut arcam habere rebus pretiosissimis refertam, nisi clauem quoque habeas, qua palatij fores aperias, vt in illud ingredi possis, & arcam reseres, & ita ijs fruaris, quæ in illa recondita sunt: ita simplici & rudi populo non satis est Scripturas habere, in quibus regnum Dei & omnes gratiæ thesauri proponuntur, nisi interpretatio earundem & ex hu desumpta doctrina accedat, quæ illum instituat & aditum patefaciat ad Regni huius & salutis æternæ possessionem. Elucet autem in hoc singularis Dei Bonitas, qui miseris hominibus & a Regno suo exulantibus claues eiusmodi dedit, & ianitores (vt ita dicam) constituit, qui in illud admittant & deducant eos, quibus alioqui pereundum erat. Et hæc causa est, quod Euangelij præcones dicuntur homines ferunare: non quidem quod ipsi salutis authores sint, sed quod ad hanc aditum faciunt, dum verbum Dei dextrè interpretantur, & illud singulorum institutioni, prout opus est, accommodant. Rursus autem hinc colligi potest, quanta sit eorum improbitas, qui verbi ministerium aspernantur atq; sublatum volunt. Peccant illi ingratitudine in Deum, & simul sibi ipsis ostium regni cœlorum præcludunt, ne unquam in illud ingrediantur.
units.tr: "Woe to you," he says, "lawyers, for you have taken away the key of knowledge; you did not enter in yourselves, and you hindered those who were entering." These words are rendered in Matthew thus: "Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for you shut the kingdom of heaven against men; for you do not enter in yourselves, nor do you allow those who are entering to go in." Therefore the matter under discussion here is the kingdom of heaven and the business of eternal salvation. By the key of knowledge or understanding is meant the teaching and preaching of God's Word, through which the mysteries of the kingdom of God are unlocked, so that men may see them and understand the way and manner of attaining them. And this expression reminds us how necessary is sound teaching and a careful explanation of the Word of God and the Scriptures. For just as it would profit nothing to see a magnificent palace from a distance, or to possess a chest filled with most precious goods, unless you also had the key by which you could open the palace doors to enter in, and unlock the chest, and so enjoy the things stored within: so for the simple and untaught people it is not enough to have the Scriptures, in which the kingdom of God and all the treasures of grace are set forth, unless their interpretation and doctrine drawn from it are added, which instructs them and opens the way to the possession of this kingdom and of eternal salvation. Moreover, in this is shown the singular goodness of God, who gave such keys to wretched men exiled from his kingdom, and appointed, so to speak, doorkeepers who admit and lead into it those who would otherwise have to perish. And this is the reason why the heralds of the Gospel are called stewards of the mysteries: not that they are the authors of salvation, but that they make the way to it, while they interpret the Word of God rightly, and adapt it to the instruction of each person as need requires. Again, from this it may be gathered how great is the wickedness of those who despise the ministry of the Word and wish it abolished. They sin by ingratitude toward God, and at the same time bar for themselves the door of the kingdom of heaven, so that they never enter into it.

units.la: Porrò quoad Iudæorum Scribas aut legis interpretes, tria in illis Christus accusat & reprehendit. Primum, quòd clauem cognitionis sustulerint. Erat quidem illis commissa legis doctrina, & ideo in cathedra Mosis sedere dicuntur. Atqui lex, si rectè intelligatur, pædagogus est nos ad Christum deducens, qui nobis Patrē placauit, & fores regni cælorū, quas Adam nobis præcluserat, rursus aperuit, ut in illud iam nobis accessus pateat. Illi verò doctrinam veram legis traditionibus suis obruerant, ut vix aliquis esset, qui verū eius usum intelligeret: imò populū à Christo reuocabant, ut eius ignorantia ad quæstū suum possent abuti. E medio igitur sustulerant clauem illam cognitionis, quæ sola hominibus regnum Dei patefacit, & proinde fures erant atq; sacrilegi. Alterum est, quòd ipsi quoq; non ingrediantur in regnū Dei. Quibus verbis prophanum religionis & salutis propriæ contemptū illis exprobrat, & quòd qui alijs suo exemplo præire debuerint, potius toti populo scandalū posuerint. Est hoc grauissimum scelus, ut alibi Christus admonet: & proinde in primis studere debent verbi præcones, ut ipsi primi salutis via ingrediantur, (& quod de bono pastore dicitur) oues suas præcedant atq; viæ duces sint. Nam si ita viuant, ut omnibus appareat, ne ipsos quidem credere ea, quæ alijs prædicant, quid inde aliud sequi poterit, quàm prophanus doctrinæ omnis contemptus, & effrænis in toto populo scelerum licentia? Ideo Paulus ad Tim. suum scribebat: Esto exemplar fidelium in sermone, in conuersatione, in charitate, in spiritu, in fide, in puritate. Quod sibi quoq; dictum putare debent, quotquot in Ecclesiæ ministerio versantur: omnes item qui vel in repub. vel re domestica alijs præsunt. Magna enim exemplorum vis est, & malorū quidem maxima propter naturæ nostræ vitiositatem. Quòd si verò ijsdē authoritas ex persona eminentia aut dignitate accedat, non possunt non plurimi illis seduci. At quàm diras & graues pœnas scandalorū authoribus Christus minetur, alibi diximus. Vtinā de ijs diligentius cogitarent omnes, quibus prædicandi Euangelij munus commissum est. Postremò hoc legu interpretibus exprobrat Dominus, quòd nō ipsi solum non ingressi sint in regnū Dei, verumetiam si qui pij & boni in illud ingredi velint, & de via salutis serió quærant, ij per ipsos prohibeantur, quò minus eò perueniant. Id autē non vno modo faciebant. Nam vt supra diximus, cùm illorū esset verum finem legis docere, & populum Christo adducere, qui solus via est, per quam ad Patrē venitur, ipsi ab hoc potius abducebant ad inanes sibi autem quæstuosas ceremonias, quas vt facilius retinerent, in locum legis diuinæ traditiones patrū inuexerant, quibus illius doctrina prorsus abolebatur. Deinde non contenti doctrinā falsa populum seduxisse, aperta quoq; vi agebant, & si qui illis relictis ad Iesum Christum concedebant, eos excommunicationibus & infinitis alijs modis territabant: quæ causa fuit (vt Ioannes scribit) quòd cum multi ex principibus in illum crederet, fidem tamen suā non auderent profiteri propter Pharisæos, qui iam constituerant, vt omnes Christi sectatores è Synagoga eijcerentur. Quòd si autem principibus formidabilis fuit illorum potentia atq; tyrannis, facile ex eo conijci potest, quàm misera & infelix sub illis fuerit populi conditio. Itaq; iam nō fures modo & sacrilegi erant, verumetiā latrones, cùm suæ curæ creditos impedirent, ne salutis viam ingrederentur, imò cogerent ad ea, quæ certum animabus exitiū afferunt. Et eò grauius erat ipsorū scelus, quòd ad hoc religionis prætextu abutebantur, & Dei templum spelunctam latronū fecerant. Digni ego fuerunt, quibus horrendū illud væ denuntiaret Dominus, & qui non multò post cum vrbe simul & templo excinderentur.
units.tr: Furthermore, as regards the Scribes or lawyers of the Jews, Christ accuses and rebukes three things in them. First, that they had taken away the key of knowledge. The teaching of the law had indeed been committed to them, and so they are said to sit in the chair of Moses. Yet the law, if rightly understood, is a schoolmaster leading us to Christ, who reconciled the Father to us and opened again the doors of the kingdom of heaven, which Adam had closed against us, so that access to it now lies open to us. But they had buried the true teaching of the law under their own traditions, so that scarcely anyone was left who understood its true use; indeed, they called the people away from Christ, so that they might exploit their ignorance for their own gain. They had therefore taken away from the midst that key of knowledge which alone opens the kingdom of God to men, and so they were thieves and sacrilegious. The second is that they themselves did not enter into the kingdom of God. By these words he reproaches them with profane contempt for religion and their own salvation, and with the fact that, although they ought to have gone before others by their example, they had rather placed a stumbling block before the whole people. This is a most grievous crime, as Christ warns elsewhere; and therefore the heralds of the Word ought above all to take care that they themselves first enter the way of salvation, and (as is said of the good shepherd) go before their sheep and be leaders on the way. For if they so live that it is plain to all that they do not even believe the things they preach to others, what else can follow but a profane contempt for all doctrine and an unbridled license for sins among the whole people? Therefore Paul wrote to his Timothy: "Be an example to the faithful in word, in conduct, in love, in spirit, in faith, in purity." This ought to be taken as said to themselves by all who are engaged in the ministry of the Church, and likewise all who preside over others in the commonwealth or in household affairs. For great is the power of example, and of bad example the greatest, on account of the sinfulness of our nature. But if authority is added to such men from their eminent person or dignity, many cannot help being seduced by them. And how dire and grievous punishments Christ threatens against the authors of scandals, we have said elsewhere. Would that all to whom the task of preaching the Gospel has been committed thought more carefully about these things. Lastly, the Lord reproaches the lawyers with this: that not only did they themselves not enter into the kingdom of God, but if any pious and good people wished to enter it and seriously sought the way of salvation, they were hindered by them, so that they could not reach it. And they did this not in only one way. For, as we said above, although it was their duty to teach the true end of the law and to bring the people to Christ, who alone is the way by which one comes to the Father, they rather drew them away from him to empty and, for themselves, profitable ceremonies, which, so that they might more easily keep them, they had introduced in place of the divine law as the traditions of the fathers, by which the teaching of the law was utterly abolished. Then, not content with having led the people astray by false doctrine, they also acted with open violence; and if any left them and went over to Jesus Christ, they terrified them with excommunications and countless other means. This was the reason (as John writes) that although many of the rulers believed in him, they did not dare to confess their faith because of the Pharisees, who had already decided that all followers of Christ should be cast out of the synagogue. But if the power and tyranny of those men was dreadful even to the rulers, it can easily be inferred from this how wretched and unhappy the condition of the people was under them. And so they were now not only thieves and sacrilegious, but also robbers, since they hindered those committed to their care from entering the way of salvation, and indeed compelled them toward those things which bring certain ruin to souls. And their wickedness was all the graver because they abused religion as a pretext for this, and had made the temple of God a den of robbers. They were worthy that the Lord should pronounce upon them that dreadful woe, and that not long afterwards they should be destroyed together with the city and the temple.

units.la: Admonet autem nos locus iste, non nouum hoc aut insolens esse, quòd qui Ecclesiæ & regni Dei ianitores esse debebant, primi fere sunt, qui populum ab eius ingressu arcent, neq; tamen inde sequi quòd nulla sit prorsus Dei ecclesia. Est hoc diligenter obseruandū propter aduersarios nostros, qui apud rudem & imperitum populum hoc potissimum argumento sese tuentur. Si (inquiunt) non vera est religio, quæ in Papatu exercetur, si item non legitimi sunt Episcopi, qui à Pontificibus ordinantur, si deniq; Dei verbo repugnat quæ hucusq; seruata est Ecclesiæ œconomia, Ecclesiam ipsam tot seculis errauisse, adeoq; Ecclesiam nullā fuisse oportet. Vbi ergo interea locū habuit promissio Christi: Ego vobiscum sum vsq; ad consummationem seculi? Falsi etiā arguitur Paulus Apostolus, qui
units.tr: This passage also reminds us that it is neither new nor unusual for those who ought to be the gatekeepers of the Church and of the kingdom of God to be among the first to keep the people from entering. Yet it does not follow from this that there is no Church of God at all. This must be carefully observed because of our adversaries, who chiefly defend themselves before the unlearned and inexperienced people with this argument. "If," they say, "the religion practised under the Papacy is not true, and if the bishops ordained by the Pontiffs are not lawful, and if, finally, the order of the Church that has been kept until now is opposed to the word of God, then the Church itself must have erred for so many centuries, and so the Church must have been nowhere. Where, then, meanwhile, has the promise of Christ held good: 'I am with you always, even to the end of the age'? The Apostle Paul is also convicted of falsehood, who

units.la: Ecclesiam columnam & stabilimentum veritatis esse dixit. Sed facilis est ad ista responsio.
