Quod autem de illis dicitur, hoc ipsum Reipub. etiā gubernatores & quotquot in magistratu sunt, ad se transferre debent. Nam hi quoq; non rerum Domini, sed Dei serui & ministri sunt, vt Paulus loquitur. Ergo neq; horum fuerit, in illius populū aliquid ex suo cerebro statuere, sed (vt scripturae docent) Dei iudicia exequi, & itaque omnes administrare debent, vt illi rationem redere possint.
units.tr: The first part is what he says: A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country for a long time. By the vineyard is understood the Jewish people, among whom it is quite clear that at that time the title of the Church resided. This parable is very frequent in the Scriptures, because it vividly portrays God's care for us and admonishes all those who wish to be counted members, or some part, of the Church. For just as the possession of vineyards is most precious and their cultivation very laborious, so they are tended for no other end and use than to bear fruit; and unless they bear it, the vines are soon cut out, lest they occupy the ground in vain. Here, however, the chief point is that Christ says the vineyard was let out to husbandmen. By these he means the priests, whom God had once made the husbandmen of his people, so that by careful teaching of the Law, by the lawful practice of the sacred rites, and also by their own example, they should cultivate it to piety, and gather from it fruits worthy of their profession and such as could delight him. These fruits are true faith, which depends on the knowledge of the true God and his Son, zeal for holiness and innocence, and brotherly or mutual love, which Paul calls the fulfilment of the whole Law. In this part Christ strips the arrogance from the priests, who, forgetting that they had been appointed husbandmen by God, claimed dominion for themselves over the vineyard of the Lord and ordered everything at their own pleasure. He therefore admonishes them that they have no cause for pride against anyone, nor are they under any obligation to render an account of their teaching or their actions to others, since the Church of God is his peculium and vineyard. Rather, it is their part, mindful of their condition, to be faithful husbandmen, and to think of spreading the glory of God and the salvation of the people rather than of their own advantage and private honour. And indeed this one point could have been enough to refute the rashness of those who had profaned the use of the temple, changed the whole form of divine worship, and likewise corrupted doctrine with human traditions. Let us observe here, then, that all are refuted who in the Church take to themselves this right and power, so as to devise everything from their own brain, to make new laws, to draw up new articles of faith, likewise to alter the form of worship, and to abuse their authority against those who strive to restore the old form of religion and of the Church handed down by God. Therefore the Pontiffs need not object to us today the Catholic succession from Peter and its perpetuity. For even if we grant them all this, and admit that they were instituted and ordained directly by the Son of God himself, we can still call them nothing but husbandmen, who ought not to give laws but to receive them from Christ; who ought not to lord it over the Church but rather to serve it; who ought not to seek their own profit from it, but to refer everything to the glory and honour of him who acquired it by the price of his blood. From this it also follows that they are worthy of rebuke if they do anything beyond their duty. For although the authority of the priests was once indeed great, and it was a capital offence to resist their judgment stubbornly, yet we know that they were sharply rebuked by the Prophets and even publicly reproved, whenever they were either too negligent or not faithful enough in their office. And what is said of them, the governors of the commonwealth and all who hold magistracy must apply to themselves. For these too are not lords of things, but, as Paul says, servants and ministers of God. Therefore it is not for them to set down anything from their own brain for that people, but (as the Scriptures teach) to carry out the judgments of God; and so all of them ought to govern in such a way that they can render an account to him.

units.la: Sed alteram quoque parabolae partem videamus, qua scelerata Sacerdotum ingratitudo atque impietas depingitur. Quae vt melius pateat, Deum nullam illis causam praebuisse, ostendit, cur ista facerent. Nam peregrè profectus multum temporis abfuit. Quod non ita accipi debet, quasi Deus vnquam à sua Ecclesia absit: sed ostendit, illum nequaquam molestum fuisse suis illis colonis, vt fere solent heri ad rem attentiores, qui etsi suas terras colonis elocent, ijsdem tamen multis alijs in rebus negotium faciunt, vt minus possint praestare ea, quae in primis fieri debebat. Praeterea in tempore demum misit seruos, qui fructum exigerent, quem illi reddere tenebantur, etiamsi nemo exegisset. Et suos seruos misit, qui istorum conserui erant, non alienos, de quorum rigore aut insolentia possent conqueri. Ergo nihil hic factum est, quod vel iniquum, vel inhonestum, vel graue aut molestum possit censeri, si quis rem maturo iudicio examinet. Per seruos autem intelliguntur Prophetae, quos extraordinariè à Deo vocatos & missos fuisse, alibi diximus: & quàmuis illi quoque cultores vineae Dominicae strenuissimi fuerint, hic tamen exactoribus conferuntur: eò quòd praecipuum illorum munus erat, cessantibus in suo officio Sacerdotibus, tam hos quam omnes alios hominum ordines ad fructus poenitentiae reddendos exhortari. Trium vero seruorum mentionem facit, qui ex ordine alius post alium missi sunt, vt continuam Dei curam exprimat, qua populi istius salutem quaesiuit, & ideo nullum tempus elabi passus est, quo non eos de officio suo admoneret. Patet hoc euidentissimè in sacra historia. Nam cùm primùm terram ingressi à Dei veri cultu ad idololatriam deficerent, mox Prophetas misit, qui eos monerent, & ad se conuersis vindices excitauit, quorum virtute ex hostium manibus eriperentur: & quàmuis interdum pretiosum ac rarum esset verbum Dei (sicuti in Samuelis historia legitur) nunquam tamen omnino extinctum fuit, & tandem Samuel datus est, qui & cultum Dei restituit, & Philistaeorum tyrannidem fregit, qua diu oppressi fuerant. Similiter cùm post Solomonis mortem decem tribus manifestam à Domo Dauidis simul & religione patria secessionem fecissent, & in Regno Iuda quoque multa subinde contra Legem fierent, nunquam defuerunt Prophetae, qui Reges, Sacerdotes, iudices, populum denique vniuersum ad poenitentiam excitarent. Imò cùm incurabiles in exitium ruerent, iamque fatale illud tempus Babylonici exilij instaret, magno studio apud eos causam hanc egerunt Sophonias, Ieremias, Baruch & multi alij, vt non temere Deus testetur, se manè surrexisse, & omnem lapidem mouisse, vt eos in viam reduceret. Quid quòd ne in Babylone quidem agentibus defuit, sed Ezechiele dedit & Danielem cum alijs quibusdam, quorum ministerio edocerentur? Ab exilio autem reuersi, Haggaeum, Zachariam & Malachiam habuerunt, quos suo tempore Ioannes Baptista secutus est, qui acerrimi exactoris officium faciens clamauit: Resipiscite, in propinquo enim est Regnum coelorum: Facite fructus dignos iis qui resipuerint: quia securis ad radicem arborum posita est, & omnis arbor non faciens fructum bonum, exciditur, &c. Et haec quidem omnia Christus paucis verbis comprehendit, quando seruos missos fuisse dicit, qui à colonis fructum exigerent.
units.tr: But let us also look at the other part of the parable, in which the wicked ingratitude and impiety of the priests is portrayed. So that this may appear more clearly, he shows that God gave them no cause for doing these things. For having gone abroad, he was absent for a long time. This should not be understood as if God were ever absent from his Church; rather, he shows that he was by no means troublesome to those husbandmen of his, as men of substance who are more careful about their affairs usually are. Although they let out their lands to tenants, they still meddle with them in many other matters, so that they are less able to do what ought chiefly to be done. Moreover, at the proper time he sent servants to demand the fruit, which the tenants were bound to render even if no one had demanded it. And he sent servants who were fellow servants of those men, not strangers, of whose severity or insolence they could complain. Therefore nothing has been done here that could be judged unjust, dishonourable, grievous, or troublesome, if anyone examines the matter with mature judgment. By the servants, moreover, the Prophets are understood, whom we have elsewhere said were called and sent by God in an extraordinary way. And although they too were most zealous cultivators of the Lord's vineyard, here they are compared to collectors, because their particular office was, when the priests were failing in their duty, to exhort these men and all other orders of people to bring forth the fruits of repentance. He mentions three servants, sent one after another, in order to express God's continual care, by which he sought the salvation of that people; and therefore he allowed no time to slip by in which he did not admonish them of their duty. This is very clearly seen in sacred history. For as soon as they entered the land and began to fall away from the true worship of God into idolatry, God immediately sent Prophets to warn them, and when they turned back to him, he raised up deliverers, by whose power they were rescued from the hands of their enemies. And although at times the word of God was precious and rare (as we read in the history of Samuel), it was never utterly extinguished; and at last Samuel was given, who both restored the worship of God and broke the tyranny of the Philistines, under which they had long been oppressed. Similarly, when after the death of Solomon the ten tribes openly seceded from the house of David and from their ancestral religion, and in the kingdom of Judah too many things were done from time to time contrary to the Law, there were never lacking Prophets who stirred up kings, priests, judges, and finally the whole people to repentance. Indeed, when they were rushing incurably to destruction, and that fatal time of the Babylonian exile was already at hand, Zephaniah, Jeremiah, Baruch and many others pleaded this cause with great zeal among them, so that God does not testify in vain that he rose early and moved every stone to bring them back to the way. And what of the fact that even while they were in Babylon he did not fail them, but gave Ezekiel and Daniel with certain others, by whose ministry they might be taught? After their return from exile they had Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi, whom in his time John the Baptist followed, who, performing the office of a most severe collector, cried out: Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand; bring forth fruits worthy of those who repent; for the axe is laid to the root of the trees, and every tree that does not bring forth good fruit is cut down, etc. Christ comprehends all these things in a few words, when he says that servants were sent to demand fruit from the husbandmen.

units.la: Non debet autem ofcitanter haec particula considerari, qua Prophetas suos exactoribus confert. Ea enim omnes Verbi administros sui officij admonet: ut nimirum cogitent, non sufficere, si obiter doceant, quid unumquenque facere conueniat, sed exactores esse debere, qui ius heri sui sedulo persequantur, & (ut Paulus ait) tempestiue & intempestiue instent apud eos, quos malae fidei debitores esse cernunt. Hoc olim Prophetae fecerunt, & eorum vestigijs incessisse Apostolos scimus, & hoc illud est, quod ministerium verbi mundo exosum facit. Nam gratia Dei praedicationem omnes facile ferunt, imo illam sibi annuntiari volunt. Vt primum verò peccata sua argui seque ad vitae emendationem excitari sentiunt, aut etiam fortius vrgeri, mox quasi furore perciti aduersus stimulum calcitrant, & in fidos monitores hostiliter insurgunt. At nihilominus officium facere oportet eos, qui ad illud se à Deo vocatos & missos esse vident. Obseruabis praeterea, quòd etsi vinea fructum ferre debeat, hic tamen à colonis exigitur, qui illum hero reddere debeant. Eo enim admonemur, quòd omnium quidem sit fidem suam vero Dei cultu, vitae innocentia, morum probitate, & fraternae dilectionis officijs declarare: in primis tamen in hoc incumbere debere eos, quos Ecclesiae & populi sui colonos Deus constituit, vt ista fiant, & ipse in omnium vita atque factis glorificetur. Istud ergo ad se pertinere meminerint omnes Verbi administri, omnes item qui in Republica praesunt, ne sibi ipsis pernitiose imponant, dum aliorum facta & mores nihil ad se pertinere arbitrantur. Est hoc fere causa multorum scelerum, & vix aliud est, quo poenitentia publica magis impeditur, quàm quòd ijs, qui rebus praesident, sibi impune fore arbitrantur, si ad aliorum vitia conmueant. Cur (inquiunt) ego meipsum discruciem propter huius aut istius petulantiam? cur labores & molestiam mihi accersam propter infelicis populi improbitatem, in quo quisq; prout libet, viuere iampridem coepit? Egone me omnium odijs exponam, vt eos in viam reducam, qui perire malunt? Sed audi tu quisquis es. Nonne vinea Domini est populus, cui tu siue docendo, siue ius dicendo praesides? Nonne tu idem Domini colonus es? Id certè si negaueris, iam non dignus es, qui vel in Ecclesiae ministerio, vel in Republica locum habeas. At si Domini colonus es, vtique ad te ista cura pertinet, vt vinea ista fructum dignum & multum ferat, & hunc de tuis manibus Deus requiret. Et haec causa est, ob quam olim Prophetae tanto studio cum Regibus & principibus, adhaec cum Sacerdotibus & omnibus illis egerunt, qui authoritate & potestate in populo eminebant. Excitet ergo hoc omnes principes & Ecclesiarum pastores, vt in sui gregis mores atque studia diligentius inquirant, & se rationem Deo reddituros esse meminerint, si disciplinam collabi patiantur, si vinea Domini fruticet aut lasciuiat, si vuarum loco labruscas ferat, si vitia impune regnent, si denique Dei cultus & morum honestas intermoriatur. Similiter qui in vinea ista vites referunt, singuli nimirum ex populo, patienter ferre discant fidos colonos, quando hi ex officio istud omne faciunt. Tu enim quis es qui vel verbi praeconem, vel magistratum opus sibi à Deo mandatum facere prohibeas? Id certè nullo iure poteris, nisi te non ad vineam Domini pertinere, sed ab eius populo alienum esse fateasimilaris: vel etiam ex professo colonos istos imitari velis, de quibus hic agitur.
units.tr: This particle, by which he sets his prophets over the tax-collectors, should not be read carelessly. For it reminds all ministers of the Word of their office: they should consider that it is not enough to teach in passing what each person ought to do, but that they must be exactors, who diligently press the claims of their master and (as Paul says) insist, in season and out of season, upon those whom they see to be debtors of bad faith. The prophets did this of old, and we know the apostles walked in their footsteps; and this is what makes the ministry of the Word hateful to the world. For people readily bear the preaching of grace; indeed they want it announced to them. But as soon as they feel their sins being rebuked and themselves roused to amend their lives, or pressed more sharply, they straightway kick against the goad, as if driven by fury, and rise up hostilely against faithful admonishers. Nevertheless, those who see that they have been called and sent by God to that office must perform it. You will observe, besides, that although the vineyard ought to bear fruit, here the fruit is demanded from the tenants, who ought to render it to the master. By this we are reminded that all people should indeed declare their faith by the true worship of God, innocence of life, uprightness of morals and the duties of brotherly love; yet above all those whom God has appointed as tenants of his Church and people ought to devote themselves to this, that these things be done and that he himself be glorified in the lives and deeds of all. Let all ministers of the Word, and likewise all who preside in the commonwealth, therefore remember that this pertains to them, lest they deceive themselves to their own ruin while they think the deeds and morals of others are no concern of theirs. This is nearly the cause of many crimes, and there is hardly anything else by which public repentance is more hindered than that those who preside over affairs think they will go unpunished if they wink at the vices of others. "Why," they say, "should I torment myself on account of this man's or that man's wantonness? Why should I bring labour and trouble upon myself because of the wickedness of an unhappy people, among whom each has long since begun to live as he pleases? Shall I expose myself to the hatred of all, in order to lead back those who prefer to perish?" But hear, whoever you are. Is not the people the vineyard of the Lord, over which you preside, whether by teaching or by administering justice? Are you not yourself the Lord's tenant? If you deny it, you are now unworthy to hold a place either in the ministry of the Church or in the commonwealth. But if you are the Lord's tenant, then surely this care pertains to you: that the vineyard bear worthy and abundant fruit, and God will require this from your hands. And this is the reason why the prophets of old dealt so earnestly with kings and princes, and besides with the priests and all those who stood out in authority and power among the people. Let this therefore stir all princes and ministers of the churches to inquire more diligently into the morals and pursuits of their flock, and to remember that they will have to render account to God if they allow discipline to decay, if the vineyard of the Lord runs to brambles or grows wanton, if it bears wild grapes instead of grapes, if vices reign with impunity, and finally if the worship of God and the honesty of morals die out. Likewise let those who bear the vines in this vineyard, that is, each of the people, learn to bear patiently with faithful tenants when they do all this out of duty. For who are you, that you should forbid a herald of the Word or a magistrate to do the work commanded him by God? You certainly cannot do so by any right, unless you confess that you do not belong to the Lord's vineyard but are alien to his people, or unless you wish to imitate, on purpose, those very tenants of whom this passage speaks.

units.la: Dicit de his Christus, quòd seruos istos omnes caesos ac vulneratos non sine contumelia inanes dimiserint, vel potius violentius eiecerint. Ad cuius loci expositionem faciunt, quae habentur in sine Paralip. vbi Babylonicae captiuitatis causas Spiritus sanctus exponens inter alia sic scribit: Misit Dominus Deus patrum eorum ad eos mane surgendo, & nuntios suos mittendo (quoniam parcere cupiebat populo suo atq; habitaculo suo) At illi subsannabat nuntios Dei, & contemnebat verba eius, illudetes Prophetis eius, donec ascenderet furor eius, &c. Et Elias de sui saeculi corruptissimo statu loquens de eo etiam queritur, quod Prophetas Dei gladio occiderint, Ereni Isaia sub Manasse serra disse secu, Ieremia et Zacharia lapidibus obrutos, Amos ab Amasia filio fuste occisum, Micheã ex rupe praecipitatum. præcipitatum, alios item supplicijs extinctos fuisse, Ecclesiastici scriptores prodiderūt. Fuit hæc extrema impietas, & quia præcipui semper cædiū eiusmodi authores fuerunt Sacerdotes, qui populum ad pietatem excollere debebant, merito hos præ alijs Christus reos agit.
units.tr: Christ says of these that they dismissed all those servants, beaten and wounded, empty-handed and not without insult, or rather drove them out more violently. What is found at the end of Paralipomenon helps to explain this place, where the Holy Spirit, setting out the causes of the Babylonian captivity, writes among other things as follows: "The Lord God of their fathers sent to them, rising early and sending his messengers (for he wished to spare his people and his dwelling place). But they mocked the messengers of God and despised his words, mocking his prophets, until his wrath arose..." And Elijah, speaking of the most corrupt state of his own age, also complains of it: that they put the prophets of God to death with the sword, that Isaiah was sawn asunder under Manasseh, that Jeremiah and Zechariah were stoned, and that Amos was killed with a club by Amaziah's son, and Micah was thrown down from a rock. Ecclesiastical writers have also recorded that others were put to death by torture. This was extreme impiety, and because the chief authors of such slaughters were always the priests, who ought to have trained the people to piety, Christ rightly charges these men above others with guilt.

units.la: Debet autem hīc obseruari vniuersalis mundi ingratitudo & scelerata contumacia, qua omnibus seculis in Dei seruos vsus est. Vt enim omnes homines Dei debitores sunt; ita non possunt non propter innatam sibi malitiam malæ fidei debitores esse, vt qui suis studijs, vel etiam diabolo ea im pendere malunt, quæ Deo reddere debebant. Fieri ergo non potest, quin eos oderint & extinctos velint, qui debita Dei nomine ab illis exigunt. Nec dubium est multa indigna tulisse sanctos illos patres, qui ante diluuium iustitiæ præcones fuerunt, & cum mundi iamiam perituri contumacia colluctati sunt. Quæ verò Abrahami, Isaaci & Iacobi conditio fuerit inter Chananæos, ex vnius Lothi exemplo conijci potest, quem intra animum suum graviter afflictum fuisse Petrus scribit, cum impuros Sodomæorum mores quotidie intueri cogeretur. Nec melior Moysis fors fuit, quem postin finita & incomparabilia beneficia, tot tamq; atrocibus iniurijs atque contumelijs affecerunt Israelitæ, vt nescigam illorum ne ingratitudinem magis, aut eius patientiam admirari debeamus. Et si tempora Apostolorum & quæ hos secuta sunt, consideres, tam illos quam omnes alios Dei seruos crudelissimis & indignissimis modis tractatos fuisse videbis, qui mundum verę pietatis doctrina excolere studuerunt. Pertinent huc Martyrum fere omnium historiæ, quorum maior pars non alio nomine trucidati sunt, quam quòd Deo suum ius inter homines vendicare conati sunt. Et si vnusquisque in seipsum descendat, mox diræ istius & sanguinariæ impietatis semina in seipso deprehendet. Natura enim admonitionum impatientes sumus, & quam primùm odio indulgere incipimus, mox indies longius progredimur, vt ab illo ad conuitia, ab his ad verbera & vulnera vsque peruenianus. Prodest ergo hanc nostri ingenij prauitatem obseruauisse, vt nobisipsis initio statim frænum iniciamus, quo illa cohiberi possit, ne prorsus immedicabilis fiat.
units.tr: Here we must observe the universal ingratitude of the world and the wicked obstinacy with which it has dealt with the servants of God in every age. For just as all men are debtors to God, so because of their innate malice they cannot but be debtors of bad faith, since they prefer to spend on their own pursuits, or even on the devil, what they ought to render to God. It is therefore inevitable that they hate and wish dead those who demand God's dues from them. Nor is there any doubt that those holy fathers who were heralds of righteousness before the flood, and who wrestled with the obstinacy of a world about to perish, suffered many unworthy things. What the condition of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob was among the Canaanites may be conjectured from the example of Lot alone, whom Peter writes was grievously afflicted in his soul when he was forced to look daily upon the impure ways of the Sodomites. Nor was Moses' lot better: after his countless and incomparable benefits, the Israelites treated him with such great and atrocious injuries and insults that I do not know whether we ought to marvel more at their ingratitude or at his patience. And if you consider the times of the apostles and those that followed, you will see that they, and all the other servants of God who strove to adorn the world with the teaching of true piety, were treated in the cruellest and most unworthy ways. To this belong almost all the histories of the martyrs, most of whom were butchered for no other reason than that they tried to vindicate God's right among men. And if each one descends into himself, he will straightway find within himself the seeds of this dire and bloody impiety. For by nature we are impatient of admonitions, and as soon as we begin to indulge hatred, we progress further day by day, so that we come from that to abuse, from abuse to blows and wounds. It is therefore useful to have observed this perversity of our nature, so that from the beginning we may immediately put a bridle on ourselves, by which it can be restrained, lest it become altogether incurable.

units.la: At non minori diligentia seruorum istorum fortitudo atque obedientia considerari debet, qui quàmuis primò rem male cessisse viderent, secundus tamen & tertius idem officium hero suo præstare non detrectant. Fit quidem interdum, vt sancti Dei serui initiò se difficiliores præbeant, quando cum mundi contumacia & periculis vndique imminentibus suam infirmitatem diligentius conferunt: at ijdem, quando Deum hoc ita velle vident, ad omne obsequiū sese promptos & paratos offerunt. Exempla eius rei in Mosè, Isaia, Ieremia & multis alijs videmus. Et hos quidē imitari prodest, ne vel nimium præcipites nos absq; certa Dei vocatione in periculū non necessarium conijciamus, vel Deo nos vocanti pertinacius reluctando eius iram prouocemus, quæ nobis periculi maioris causa fit: quod olim Ionæ accidit, quando legationem ad Niniuitas subire detrectabat. Nec est, quòd de mundi malitia aut pertinacia apud Deum multis conqueramur, aut eidem prolixius exponamus, quàm tenues & infirmæ nobis vires sint. Novit enim ille hæc omnia, & idem negotij totius exitum iam pridem prospexit. Et quàmuis quid de nobis decreuerit ignoremus, eius tamen vocatio ni & mandato nos parere necesse est: & vt id alacrius fiat, nunquā excidere nobis debet, illum viribus & facultatibus necessarijs eos instruere, quorum opera vti dignatur, & ijsdem mercedem in cælis vberrimam esse repositam, si in commisso sibi munere fideles fuerint.
units.tr: But the fortitude and obedience of these servants must be considered with no less diligence. Although at first they saw that the affair had gone badly, they nevertheless did not refuse to render the same service to their master a second and a third time. It does happen at times that the holy servants of God show themselves reluctant at first, when they weigh their own weakness more carefully against the world's obstinacy and the dangers threatening on every side; yet these same men, when they see that God wills it, offer themselves ready and prepared for every obedience. We see examples of this in Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah and many others. It is profitable to imitate these men, so that we neither rush headlong into unnecessary danger without a sure calling from God, nor provoke his anger by stubbornly resisting the God who calls us, which is a cause of greater danger to us, as once happened to Jonah when he refused to undertake the embassy to the Ninevites. Nor is there any reason that we should complain to God at length about the world's malice or obstinacy, or set out to him more fully how slender and weak our powers are. For he knows all these things, and has long since foreseen the outcome of the whole business. And although we do not know what he has decreed concerning us, it is nevertheless necessary for us to obey his calling and command. And so that we may do this more eagerly, we must never let slip the thought that he equips with the necessary strength and resources those whose work he deigns to use, and that a most abundant reward is laid up for them in heaven if they are faithful in the duty committed to them.

units.la: Cæterùm quia quæ hucusq; dicta sunt ad Sacerdotes qui olim fuerant, maximè pertinent, nunc adeos propius accedit Dominus, quibus cum ipsi res erat, & quid ab illis passurus sit docet. Vt vero eorum impiam atque detestabilem malitiam magis amplificet, aut illustriorem reddat, Deum de ipsis consultantem inducit. Dixit igitur dominus vineæ: Quid faciam? mittam filium meum dilectum, forsitan cùm hunc viderint, reuerebuntur. Vbi nemo putauerit, consultationes eiusmodi in Deum cadere: sed ἀνθρωποπάθως ista de illo dicit Dominus, vt æterni illius decreti causam exprimat apertius, quo ipse nobis in redemptorem & seruatorem prædestinatus est. Et hanc quidem illius gratuitam misericordiam fuisse ostendit. Cùm enim iam ab æterno sciret, quid eventurum esset Prophetis, adhæc incurabilem esse huius mundi malitiam, nihilominus tamen Filium mittere dignatus est, vt is non tam exactor quàm fideiussor veniret, & infelices homines ipsi reconciliaret. Est bonitas hæc Dei incomparabilis, & in consideratione eius nos perpetuò versari decet. Nam vt omnem meriti nostri fiduciam excludit: itain tentationibus consolationem nobis affert efficacissimam: & nos simul officij admonet, ne rigidiores simus in eos, qui nos iniurijs quidem nostro iudicio graviBus laeserunt, minimè tamen conferendis cum illis, quibus olim Iudaeorum antistites in illum peccauerunt, &c. In primis autem hanc Dei clementiam imitari debent ij, quos Ecclesiae suae colonos ille fecit, ne rigidiores sint in condemnandis aut abijciendis illis de quibus adhuc aliqua spes esse potes, quòd à peccatis ad illum reuersuri sint. Si enim colonos perfidissimos olim tam diu tulit Deus, & hodie Pontificum iniustam tyrannidem tam patienter fert, licet illi quotidie eius iram prouocent: quantò magis decet seruum Dei, quem is suae gratiae praeconem fecit, placidum esse erga omnes, qui malos quoque tolerare possit, & cum lenitate erudire, si forte conuersi Veritatem agnoscant? Et cùm illis omnis potestas data sit ad aedificationem, non autem ad destructionem, in nullius exitium temere debent consentire. Vide secundum Timoth.secundo, & secundum Corinthiorum decimo.
units.tr: But because what has been said so far applies chiefly to the priests who were then in office, the Lord now comes closer to them, to those with whom he had the matter at hand, and teaches what he is going to suffer at their hands. To magnify their impious and detestable malice, or to make it more conspicuous, he introduces God taking counsel about them. So the lord of the vineyard said: "What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps when they see him they will respect him." No one should suppose that such deliberations belong to God. The Lord speaks these things of him in a human manner [ἀνθρωποπαθῶς], to set forth more plainly the cause of that eternal decree by which he was predestined for us as redeemer and saviour. And here he shows that this was his free mercy. For although he knew from eternity what would befall the prophets, and that the wickedness of this world was incurable, he nonetheless deigned to send his Son, so that he would come not as an exactor but as a surety, and reconcile wretched men to himself. This goodness of God is incomparable, and it is fitting that we should always dwell upon its consideration. For while it excludes all confidence in our own merit, it also brings us the most effective consolation in temptations, and at the same time reminds us of our duty not to be too harsh toward those who have wronged us, by our judgment, quite grievously, yet who are in no way to be compared with those by whom the chief priests of the Jews once sinned against him, and so on. Above all, those whom he has made the husbandmen of his Church ought to imitate this clemency of God, and not be too harsh in condemning or casting off those about whom some hope may still remain that they will turn from their sins to him. For if God long endured the most faithless husbandmen of old, and today patiently bears the unjust tyranny of the Popes, although they provoke his wrath every day, how much more ought the servant of God, whom he has made a herald of his grace, to be gentle toward all, able to bear even the wicked, and to instruct them with gentleness, should they perhaps turn and acknowledge the truth? And since all power has been given to them for building up, not for destruction, they ought not rashly to consent to anyone's ruin. See 2 Timothy 2 and 1 Corinthians 10.

units.la: Porrò audiamus cum extrema impietate & crudelitate coniunctam colonorum istorum ingratitudinem. Nam viso herili filio, sermones inter se conferunt, dicentes: Ipse est haeres, venite, trucidemus eum, ut nostra fiat haereditas. Non temere autem consultantes inducit Dominus, ut ostendat Iudaeorum Sacerdotes non ex ignorantia aut praecipiti ira peccauisse, sed deuotis ad impietatem animis & probè deliberato consilio fecisse, quaecunque in ipsum designarunt. Itaque in eum finem ista dicuntur, ut inexcusabiles esse doceat: quo in primis facit, quod filium viderunt, & haeredem vineae legitimum esse confessi sunt. Quod de illis verissimè dicitur. Quis enim nescit, quàm saepe dictis & factis Christus demonstrarit, se aeternum Dei Filium & redemptorem illum esse, ad quem Ecclesiae haereditas pertineat? Quoties item eius demonstrationibus conuicti obmutuerunt? Quoties populi vocibus in illo diuinam virtutem glorificantis conuicti sunt? Veruntamen nihilominus aduersus eum conspirauerunt, & quotidie ferè Concilia coegerunt, in quibus de illo occidendo deliberarent. Haereditatis autem nomine ipsam vineam, id est, Ecclesiam aut populum Dei intelligi, notius est, quàm ut multis demonstrari oporteat. Ita enim passim Iudaica gens apud Prophetas dicitur, & in Psalmis Deus Pater Filio gentes omnes pollicetur, ut eius sint haereditas siue patrimonium. Atqui vnicum illud vocabulum Sacerdotes istos officij sui admonere debuerat, ne quid mala fide agerent. Quid enim iniustius est, quàm haereditatem alienam inuadere? Vulgo certè male audiunt haeredipetae, qui apud senes & viduas aut quoscunque alios muneribus & blanditijs sese insinuant, ut ab illis haeredes scribantur, praeteritis ijs, ad quos haereditas iure pertinet. Quam ergo sceleris sui excusationem afferent, qui filiorum vitae insidias struunt, ut haereditas ad ipsos perueniat?
units.tr: Let us further consider the ingratitude of those husbandmen, joined with extreme impiety and cruelty. For when they saw the master's son, they talked among themselves, saying: "This is the heir; come, let us kill him, so that the inheritance may become ours." The Lord introduces them as taking counsel, not without reason, in order to show that the priests of the Jews did not sin from ignorance or headlong anger, but with minds devoted to impiety and with a well-considered plan they did whatever they plotted against him. Therefore these things are said for this purpose: to teach that they are without excuse. He does this chiefly in that they saw the son and admitted that he was the lawful heir of the vineyard. This is said most truly of them. For who does not know how often Christ, by words and deeds, showed that he is the eternal Son of God and that redeemer to whom the inheritance of the Church belongs? How often were they also silenced, convicted by his demonstrations? How often were they convicted by the voices of the people glorifying the divine power in him? Yet nevertheless they conspired against him, and almost every day they convened councils in which they deliberated on killing him. Now that by the name of inheritance the vineyard itself, that is, the Church or the people of God, is meant, is too well known to need demonstrating to many. For so the Jewish nation is called everywhere among the Prophets, and in the Psalms God the Father promises all the nations to the Son, so that they may be his inheritance or patrimony. And yet that single word ought to have reminded those priests of their office, that they should do nothing in bad faith. For what is more unjust than to seize another's inheritance? Certainly those who insinuate themselves by gifts and flattery into the favour of old men and widows, or of any others, so that they may be written down as heirs, passing over those to whom the inheritance rightly belongs, are commonly ill spoken of as fortune hunters. What excuse, then, will they offer for their crime, who lay snares for the lives of their sons, so that the inheritance may come to themselves?

units.la: Voluit autem hoc loco docere Christus, quae illa causa sit, quae & Ecclesiae pastores & principatos quosque mouet, ut in ipsum ingrati, perfidi & iniqui fiant: Nimirum, quod ipsius haereditatem sibi vendicare, & pro sua libidine res omnes instituere cupiunt. Apparet hoc evidentissimè in Iudaeorum Sacerdotibus. Gentem enim illam suum peculium Deus fecerat: & in ea cultus sui sedem esse volebat, ut in illis glorificaretur. At constat Sacerdotes cultum omnem sibi ipsis quaestum, & ipsum templum emporium fecisse, adeoque sibi in populum iflumins omne vendicauisse, ut sibi quiduis in illum licere putarent. Hanc eorum improbitatem quia Christus arguebat, & sibi debitam haereditatem iure optimo vendicabat, illi ad consilia ista non iniqua solum, verumetiam sanguinaria descenderunt. Videbant enim populum à Christo pendere, discipulorum eius numerum indies augeri, suam autem potentiam atque authoritatem collabi atque euerti. Et quàmuis postea nefarijs suis consilijs salutem publicam praetexant, causam tamen veram, quae ipsos mouebat, dissimulare non possunt, sicuti in illorum verbis apparet, quibus in Concilio suo vsi sunt: Si ita sinamus eum, omnes credent ei, venientque Romani & auferent nobis terram & gentem. Haec ergo illa Helena est, pro qua isti pugnant: & hodie non alia causa Pontifices atque Episcopos, Monachos item & sacrificulos in Euangelij odium accendit, quàm quòd Ecclesiam in libertatem vindicari nolunt, & se ab eius possessione deturbari, quam priuata temeritate occupauerunt. Et hic quidem egregio stratagemate vsi sunt. Ne enim res suas agere putarentur, Petrum suis cōsilijs praetexuerunt, & patrimonium huius finxerunt esse Ecclesiam, eò quòd eum Apostolorum suorum principem Christus constituerit. Quo fundamento iacto, successionem quandam commenti sunt sunt, cuius iure hæreditas illa ad ipsos pertineat, qui in Petri cathedram euecti vniuersales totius orbis Christiani pastores sint. Quàm insatiabili verò auaritia in religione quæstum fecerint, quàm intolerabili tyrannide populum Christianum oppresserint, quot Dei seruos crudeliter iugularint, quanta item impudentia Reges ac principes conculcarint, omnium ferè gentium historiæ loquuntur. Et hi illi sunt, qui nostro seculo Christum per Euangelij sui doctrinam ipsis appropinquantem ferre non possunt, ne à malè vsurpata possessione deturbentur. Vt ergo olim Iudæorum Sacerdotes Christum non modò persecuti sunt, verumetiam vt Samaritanum, vt dæmoniacum, vt nefarium impostorem & communione Ecclesiæ indignum eiecerunt, & prophani iudicis libidini tradiderunt: Ita isti quoq; Christum in verbo suo loquentem omnibus hisce criminibus impudentissimè grauant, & dignum iudicant, aduersus quem Turcarum quoque arma concitent, vt ipsi tyrannidem suam retinere possint. Et hæc hodie præcipua & vera omnium persecutionum causa est, quibus vinea Christi vastatur, & ipse in membris suis crudelissimè discerpitur. Vtinam verò in eo soli Pontifices peccarent, & non ab aliis multis adiuuarentur, qui cum ipsi priuatim Christo consecrati sint, & eius peculium esse deberent, seipsos ab illo alienare solent, vt pro suorum affectuum libidine vitam instituant; quorum rabies eò magis quotidie accenditur, quòd Euangelio eiecto & extincto sibijpsis impunitatem pollicentur, & se non alia ratione beatos fore sibi persuaserunt, quàm si Christi iugum prorsus excutiant. At non debent istorum conatus atque successus aliquem offendere: quando enim olim impijs Sacerdotibus tantum permisit Deus, vt Filium suum extra vineam suam eiectum trucidarent, & ne in suo quidem patrimonio locum haberet, cui omnis potestas in cœlo & in terra debebatur: quid mirum fuerit, si hodie etiam Christiani homines excommunicationis fulmine feriantur, & Euangelij doctrina ab Ecclesia eijciatur? Meminerimus tunc, nos non debere nobisipsis meliorem sortem polliceri, quàm ipsius Christi in terris fuerit.
units.tr: Christ wished in this place to teach what is the cause that moves both the ministers of the Church and the rulers of every sort to become ungrateful, faithless and unjust toward him. Namely, that they desire to claim his inheritance for themselves and to order all things according to their own lust. This is most evident in the priests of the Jews. For God had made that nation his own special possession, and he wanted the seat of his worship to be among them, so that he would be glorified in them. But it is clear that the priests made all worship a source of gain for themselves, and the temple itself a marketplace, and so claimed for themselves all the wealth of that people, so that they thought they could do whatever they pleased with it. Because Christ rebuked this wickedness of theirs, and rightly claimed for himself the inheritance owed to him, they fell to plans that were not only unjust but also murderous. For they saw that the people depended upon Christ, that the number of his disciples increased daily, and that their own power and authority were crumbling and being overthrown. And although afterwards they pretended public safety as the reason for their wicked plans, they could not hide the true cause that moved them, as appears from their own words, which they used in their council: "If we let him alone like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away from us both our land and our nation." This, then, is that Helen for whose sake these men fight. And today it is no other cause that stirs up hatred of the gospel in the Popes and bishops, and likewise in the monks and little priests, than that they are unwilling for the Church to be set free, and do not want to be thrown out of possession of it, which they have seized by private presumption. And here they have used an excellent stratagem. For lest they should be thought to be pursuing their own affairs, they put Peter forward as the pretext for their schemes, and they feigned the Church to be his patrimony, because Christ appointed him the chief of his apostles. Once this foundation was laid, they invented a certain succession, by whose right that inheritance belongs to those who, raised to the chair of Peter, are the universal pastors of the whole Christian world. sunt, The histories of almost all nations tell of how insatiable their greed in religion has been, how intolerable the tyranny with which they have oppressed the Christian people, how many servants of God they have cruelly strangled, and likewise with what shamelessness they have trampled upon kings and princes. And these are the men who in our age cannot bear Christ approaching them through the doctrine of his gospel, lest they be thrown out of a possession wrongly seized. Therefore, just as the priests of the Jews once not only persecuted Christ but also cast him out as a Samaritan, as a demoniac, as a wicked impostor, unworthy of communion with the Church, and handed him over to the lust of a profane judge, so these men too most shamelessly load Christ, speaking in his word, with all these charges, and judge him worthy to have the arms of the Turks also roused against him, so that they may keep their tyranny. And this today is the chief and true cause of all the persecutions by which the vineyard of Christ is laid waste and he himself is most cruelly torn apart in his members. Would that only the Popes sinned in this, and were not aided by many others, who, though they have been consecrated to Christ in private, and ought to be his special possession, are accustomed to estrange themselves from him, so as to order their lives according to the lust of their own passions. Their rage is kindled ever more each day, because once the gospel has been cast out and extinguished, they promise themselves impunity, and they have persuaded themselves that they will be happy in no other way than if they shake off the yoke of Christ altogether. But the attempts and successes of these men ought not to disturb anyone. For since God once permitted the impious priests to kill his Son, thrown outside his vineyard, and he did not have a place even in his own patrimony, to whom all power in heaven and on earth was owed, what wonder is it if today even Christian men are struck by the thunderbolt of excommunication, and the doctrine of the gospel is cast out of the Church? Let us remember that then we ought not to promise ourselves a better lot than Christ himself had on earth.

units.la: Quàmuis autem videantur interdum suam tyrannidem probè stabiliuisse mali antistites, non tamen impunè ferunt suam malitiam: quod in præsenti Christus aperte docet. Nam ad Sacerdotes conuersus, vt ex ipsorum ore responsum eliciat, vel saltem conscientias eorum acutius feriat, quaerit: Quid ergo faciet colonis istis dominus vineæ? Et mox infert: Veniet, & perdet eos, & dabit vineam alijs. Venturum dicit Dominum vineæ. Ergo non in perpetuum abest aut dissimulat Deus, quæ improbi antistites aduersus eum designant: neque potest causa suæ deesse, qui iudex est vniuersæ terræ, & qui Deus vltionum in Scripturis dicitur. Duo autem illis minatur, quòd & illos perditurus sit, vt merentur: & vineam alijs elocaturus. Istis verò excidium gentis Iudaicæ, & eiusdem repudium comprehendit, quodque in Iudæorum locum successuræ sint gentes, ad quas Regnum Dei transferri oporteat, sicuti apud Matthæum ipse interpretatur. Vtrumque olim Prophetæ etiam sæpius minati fuerunt, & vtrumq; accidisse scimus. Nam vt Capite decimo nono dictum est, Romani postea diuturnum ac crudele bellum vrbem cum templo exciderunt, & tunc prorsus perditi sunt & extincti Sacerdotes impij, vnà cum suo sacerdotio quæstuoso, quod iam annis amplius mille quingentis prorsus abolitum iacet, nec vnquam instaurari poterit. Et quàmuis gens quoque excisa sit, & Reipub. forma omnis sublata, non tamen vinea Domini in vniuersum vastata est: sed (quod Prophetæ fore prædixerant) ex pauculis fidelium reliquijs illam instaurauit Deus, vt per totum orbem terrarum propagaretur, & inter gentes passim fructus colligerentur, qui Christianam professionem decent. Nunquam ergo Ecclesia extinguetur, etiamsi malè pereat, qui huius nomine & titulo aliquandiu superbiuerunt. Qui enim ex lapidibus potest Abrahami filios creare, idem vbiuis etiam locorum vineam plantare potest, & ex ijs qui steriles erant fœcundos reddere, qui ipsum digne colant. Obseruemus autem, Deum in Iudæorum populo & Sacerdotibus memorabile exemplum ædidisse, quo omnium locorum atque temporum homines admonere voluit, quid Euangelij sui contemptores maneat, qui eius doctrina vel ad quæstum vel ad licentiam abutuntur. Et debemus nos in illius consideratione eò diligentius versari, quòd multis populis atque vrbibus idem iam accidisse constat, quod Iudæi olim passi sunt: & non desunt nostri seculi exempla, quæ nos ad seriam salutis curam excitare poterant, nisi iampridem omnem mali sensum exuissemus: quod præsentis exitij est argumentum infallibile.
units.tr: Although wicked bishops sometimes seem to have firmly established their tyranny, they do not bear their wickedness with impunity, and Christ clearly teaches this in the present passage. Turning to the priests, in order to draw an answer from their own mouths, or at least to strike their consciences more sharply, he asks: "What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do to those tenants?" And presently he adds: "He will come and destroy those men, and will give the vineyard to others." He says that the lord of the vineyard will come. God, then, is not absent for ever, nor does he overlook what the wicked bishops plot against him. Nor can he lack a cause, he who is judge of the whole earth and who is called in Scripture the God of vengeances. He threatens them with two things: that he will destroy them, as they deserve, and that he will let out the vineyard to others. The second includes the ruin of the Jewish nation and its rejection, and the fact that the Gentiles, to whom the kingdom of God must be transferred, will succeed the Jews, as he himself explains in Matthew. The prophets also often threatened both of these, and we know that both came to pass. For, as was said in chapter nineteen, the Romans afterwards destroyed the city together with the temple in a long and cruel war, and then the wicked priests were utterly ruined and extinguished, together with their lucrative priesthood, which has lain completely abolished for more than fifteen hundred years and can never be restored. And although the nation too was cut off and every form of commonwealth taken away, the vineyard of the Lord was not laid waste altogether. Rather, as the prophets had foretold, God restored it from the few remnants of the faithful, so that it might spread through the whole world, and fruits befitting the Christian profession might be gathered everywhere among the nations. The Church therefore will never be extinguished, even if those who for a while took pride in its name and title perish wretchedly. For he who can raise up sons of Abraham from stones can equally plant a vineyard in any place, and make fruitful those who were barren, who will worship him worthily. Let us observe, moreover, that God set before us in the Jewish people and priests a memorable example, by which he wished to warn men of every place and time what awaits the contemners of his gospel, who abuse its doctrine for gain or for licence. We ought to dwell on the consideration of this all the more diligently, because it is well established that many peoples and cities have already suffered the same things the Jews once suffered, and there are not lacking examples from our own age which might have roused us to a serious care for salvation, unless we had long since cast off all sense of evil. This is an infallible sign of impending ruin.

units.la: LII.2
units.tr: LII.2

units.la: Sed ad Sacerdotes redeamus, quos similis stupiditas & caeca de perpetua impunitate persuasio decepit. Cum enim haec dicentem Christum audiuissent, non solum non excitantur ad salutis studium & diligentiorem eorum, quae dicebantur, considerationem: sed admonitionem tam grauem tamque seriam non sine detestatione reijciunt, quasi nihil ad se pertinentem. Absit, inquiunt: nimirum, ut tale quid in Filium Dei & promissum Seruatorem siue Messiam unquam facturi simus. Est hoc innata nobis prauitatis argumentum, quod in hypocritis omnibus elucet. Norunt hi peccata & scelera poenas mereri, & ijdem mox sentiunt de ipsis agi, quando illa arguuntur. Eadem tamen in seipsis minime agnoscunt, multo minus autem adduci possunt, ut se supplicio dignos esse fateantur. Itaq; sibijpsis quidem blandiuntur, & omnia anxie colligunt, quibus conscientiae suae stimulos retundant: in eos autem qui ipsorum impietatem arguunt, impudenter insurgere audent, & grauissimis quoque protestationibus crimen omne abs se reijcere. Exempla huius generis hodie multa videmus in ijs, qui cum Euangelicae doctrinae & meriti Christi Iesu, acerrimi hostes sint, nihil tamen minus videri volunt, & non modo detestationibus eiusmodi vtuntur, verumetiam cum conuitijs & minis horrendis eos reijciunt, a quibus accusantur. At non propterea illis cedere oportet, sed eo fortius instare conuenit, & ad Dei tribunal tales citandi sunt, ut tandem intra conscientias conuincantur.
units.tr: But let us return to the priests, whom a similar stupidity and a blind persuasion of perpetual impunity deceived. For when they had heard Christ speaking these things, they were not only not roused to a concern for salvation and a more careful consideration of what was being said; they also rejected such a grave and serious warning, not without loathing, as though it had nothing to do with them. "Far be it," they say, "that we should ever do such a thing to the Son of God and the promised Saviour or Messiah." This is an innate sign of our wickedness, which shines forth in all hypocrites. They know that sins and crimes deserve punishment, and they feel at once that these things are being said about them when such sins are charged against them. Yet they by no means acknowledge the same faults in themselves, and they are even less easily brought to confess that they deserve punishment. And so they flatter themselves, and anxiously gather everything by which they may blunt the goads of their conscience; but against those who expose their impiety they dare to rise up shamelessly, and by the most solemn protestations they cast off every charge from themselves. We see many examples of this kind today among those who, though they are the bitterest enemies of the evangelical doctrine and of the merit of Christ Jesus, nevertheless wish to appear in no way such, and they not only use protestations of this sort, but also reject with insults and dreadful threats those by whom they are accused. Yet we ought not on that account yield to them; rather we should press on all the more strongly, and such men must be summoned to the tribunal of God, so that at last they may be convicted within their own consciences.

units.la: Facit hoc in praesenti Christus, qui Sacerdotes istos intuitus (quod animi intrepidi & optime sibi conscij argumentum est) dixit eis: Quid illud est quod scriptum est: Quem lapidem reprobauerunt aedificantes, is factus est caput anguli? Quasi diceret: Audio quidem vobis indignissimum videri quod dico, & in vos tantum scelus cadere non posse arbitramini, ut Messiam occidatis. Num vero Dauidem quoque, imo per illius os loquentem Spiritum sanctum, mendacij arguere audebitis? Annon is fore praedixit, ut qui in Ecclesia aedificatores & primi architecti videri volunt, pretiosum illum lapidem reijciant, quem Deus in caput anguli destinauit, ut tota Ecclesiae salus ipsi innitatur, & ab eo vno pendeat? Cum ergo vos architecti haberi velitis, nihil me vobis alienum dicere putabitis, quin cauete potius, ne priuati quaestus & gloriae studio excaecati faciatis, quod nunc tam topere detestamini. Extat autem locus iste in Psalmo centesimo decimo octauo, quem de Messia exponi debere inter Iudaeos publice confessum erat, sicuti ex acclamationibus populi patet, quibus Christum aduentantem prosecuti sunt, & quas ex illo desumptas fuisse, tunc ostendimus. Continet autem hic locus omnia fere Christi & Ecclesiae eius mysteria, sed quia de his saepe dictum est, & de ijsdem amplius dicendi locus subinde occurrit, ea nunc copiosius tractare non est opus.
units.tr: Christ does this in the present case. Looking upon those priests (which is a mark of a fearless mind and one well aware of its own cause), he said to them: "What then is this that is written: The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner?" As if he were saying: "I hear that what I say seems to you most unworthy, and you think that so great a crime cannot fall upon you, that you would kill the Messiah. But will you dare to convict of falsehood David also, or rather the Holy Spirit speaking through his mouth? Did he not foretell that those who wish to be seen as builders and first architects in the Church would reject that precious stone, which God has appointed as the head of the corner, so that the whole salvation of the Church might rest upon him and depend on him alone? Since, then, you wish to be regarded as the architects, you will think that I am saying nothing alien to you. Take heed rather lest, blinded by the pursuit of private gain and glory, you do the very thing you now so vehemently detest." Now this passage is in Psalm one hundred and eighteen, which was publicly acknowledged among the Jews as referring to the Messiah, as is clear from the acclamations of the people with which they accompanied Christ when he came, and which, as we showed at that time, were taken from it. This passage contains almost all the mysteries of Christ and of his Church. But since these have often been spoken of, and an occasion for speaking of them more fully constantly recurs, it is not necessary to treat them more copiously now.

units.la: Nunc id obseruemus, cuius causa parabolam istam Dominus adduxit, & eandem huius testimonij authoritate confirmauit. Nam ut initio monuimus, personatis illis praesulibus larvam detrahi oportebat, ut scandalum illud e medio tolleretur, quo multi in fide impediebantur, quando Christum videbant ab ijs reijci & damnari, penes quos Ecclesiae potestas erat, & praecipua pietatis atq; doctrinae existimatio. Docet ergo hoc non nouum esse, quando id fore Spiritus sanctus olim praedixerit. At non minus ista ad eos pertinent, ut hanc Christi perpetuam in terris sortem esse cogitemus, ut ab ijs potissimum reijciatur, quorum erat omnes super illum aedificare. Neque hic aliquem moueat functionis & dignitatis ecclesiasticae titulus, quem tales nefarijs suis conatibus praetexunt, ut se errare posse negent. Habebant enim & isti quaecunque ad authoritatem conciliandam faciunt, & in eo sacerdotio ministrabant, quod a Deo ipso olim per Mosem institutum erat: attamen immani hoc parricidio Filij Dei se polluerunt, & indigni fuerunt, quorum exemplo aliquis moueretur. Cur ergo nostrorum authoritate quis ducatur hodie, quos Iudaeorum Sacerdotibus similLimos esse, res ipsa abunde docet? Quin potius consolationis argumentum ex eo petamus, quod ut Christum improbi antistites reijciant, idem tamen aeterno Patris decreto extollitur, ut Ecclesiae suae caput sit, et supremus ille lapis angularis, in quo totum aedificium congruenter coagmentatum crescit in templum sanctum Domino.
units.tr: Now let us observe the purpose for which the Lord brought forward this parable, and confirmed it by the authority of this testimony. For, as we noted at the beginning, the mask had to be torn from those counterfeit prelates, so that that stumbling-block might be removed from the midst, by which many were hindered in the faith when they saw Christ rejected and condemned by those in whose hands the power of the Church lay, and who were held in special esteem for piety and doctrine. This teaches us, therefore, that this is not new, since the Holy Spirit foretold long ago that it would happen. But these things pertain no less to them, so that we may consider this to be the perpetual lot of Christ on earth: that he is rejected chiefly by those whose task it was to build everything upon him. Nor should the title of ecclesiastical office and dignity, which such men put forward as a pretext for their wicked endeavours and by which they deny that they can err, move anyone here. For these men also had all the things that serve to win authority, and they ministered in that priesthood which God himself had once instituted through Moses. Yet they polluted themselves with this monstrous parricide of the Son of God, and they were unworthy to be imitated by anyone. Why, then, should anyone today be led by the authority of our people, whom the very facts abundantly show to be most like the priests of the Jews? Rather, let us seek from this a ground of consolation: that although the wicked bishops reject Christ, he is nonetheless exalted by the eternal decree of the Father, to be the head of his Church, and that supreme cornerstone, in which the whole building, fitly joined together, grows into a holy temple to the Lord.

units.la: At ne quis hostibus eius hoc impune fore putaret, quod tanta temeritate in ipsum insurgunt, ijsdem poenas graues denuntiat, dicens: Quisquis ceciderit super illum lapidem, conquassabitur: super quem autem ceciderit, dissipabit eum. Duo facit hominum genera, primum eorum, qui ad
units.tr: But lest anyone should suppose that it will go unpunished for his enemies that they rise up against him with such recklessness, he threatens them with grievous penalties, saying: "Whoever falls upon that stone will be broken to pieces; but upon whomever it falls, it will crush him." He makes two kinds of men: first, those who stumble against or strike upon that stone; second, those upon whom it falls. He teaches that what they do will be deadly for both groups. The first are those who in the matter of salvation follow the reasoning of their own flesh. These stumble at the cross of Christ and at his despised appearance, which in...

units.la: qui ad lapidem illum impingunt vel offendunt: alterum eorum, super quos ille cadit: vtrisque autem quod faciunt exitiale fore docet. Primi sunt, qui in salutis negotio carnis suae rationem sequuntur. Hi offendunt ad Christi crucem & contemptam speciem, quam in hoc mundo sustinet. Exemplum horum in Nazarethanis & Capernaitis Euangelistae proponunt, qui cum aliud illi obijcere non possent, parentes & cognatos obscuros exprobrant. Et habent isti hodie multos imitatores, qui cum religionem quaestu & huius seculi commodis aut splendore metiantur, non possunt non offendi, quando in Christo omnia ipsorum expectationi aduersa siue contraria vident. Fit his fere idem, quod ijs qui in angularem lapidem impingunt. Vt enim hunc impetu tali non mouent, ipsi vero conquassantur & caput laedunt: ita isti Christo quidem nihil detrahere possunt, neque eum ex gradu suo deturbare, seipsos autem graviter vulnerant quoad conscientiam, & nisi resipiscat, sibijsis interitum accersunt. Alteri sunt, qui Christum incurabili contumacia contra se provocant, adeoque illum quasi ex alto in proprium caput detrahunt, vt in ipsos ruat, dum suae irae ac iusti iudicij rigorem in illos exerit. Vt ergo lapis ex alto decidens maiori impetu fertur, & omnia dissipat: ita isti a Christo dissipantur & toti comminuuntur quoad fortunas suas, corpus item & animam. Quod Iudaeis primum, deinde Romanis Imperatoribus ac multis aliis accidit, qui aduersus Christum & Ecclesiam eius insurgere ausi fuerunt. Et huc pertinet, quod apud Danielem legitur de lapide, qui absque hominum manibus reuulsus statuam contriuit, quae Monarchias mundi huius adumbrabat. Nam vt alias ostendimus, omnibus illis haec vna exitij causa fuit, quod Dei Ecclesiam, quae Christi haereditas esset, extinguere aut vastare conati sunt. Potest etiam huc referri, quod de lapide oneris Zacharias praedixit, quando Hierosolymam saxo immani & graui similem fore dicit, in quo tollendo robustissimi quique virium suarum periculum facturi sint, at non sine damno aut membrorum suorum laceratione. Exempla huius generis multa nostro seculo vidimus, quae recensere longum foret. Nunc singuli meminerint, parabola ista communem doctrinam de Ecclesia contineri. Est haec vinea Domini, iam inde a prima rerum origine plantata. Vites in ea sunt singuli fideles: coloni autem & vinitores dicuntur Verbi Dei ministri. Possessio eius ad Filium Dei pertinet. Hunc ergo omnes obseruent, vt fructus ei reddant dignos. Ita incredulis atque perfidis coloni atque vitibus sterilibus paratum exitium effugient, cum suo autem Domino & Seruatore Iesu Christo ad coelestis regni haereditatem colligentur. Illi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: who stumble over or strike against that stone: the other kind is those on whom it falls. He teaches that both will find their undoing in what they do. The first are those who, in the business of salvation, follow the judgement of their own flesh. These stumble at the cross of Christ and at the despised appearance he bears in this world. The evangelists set the Nazarenes and Capernaites before us as examples of this: since they could find nothing else to object to him, they reproach him with his obscure parents and relatives. Today too this kind has many imitators, who measure religion by profit, by the advantages of this age, or by its splendour. They cannot help but stumble when they see that everything in Christ runs contrary to their expectations. For them it is much the same as with those who strike against the cornerstone. The stone is not moved by such a blow, but they are shaken and injure their heads. So these people can take nothing away from Christ or thrust him from his place, but they severely wound themselves as to their conscience, and unless they repent they bring destruction upon themselves. The others are those who provoke Christ against themselves by an incurable obstinacy, and so drag him, as it were from on high, down upon their own heads, so that he falls upon them when he exercises the severity of his wrath and of his just judgement against them. Just as a stone falling from on high is carried with greater force and scatters everything, so these people are scattered by Christ and utterly crushed as to their fortunes, and likewise in body and soul. This happened first to the Jews, then to the Roman emperors and to many others who dared to rise up against Christ and his Church. To this also belongs what is read in Daniel about the stone which, cut out without human hands, shattered the statue that foreshadowed the monarchies of this world. For, as we have shown elsewhere, the one cause of ruin for all those monarchies was that they tried to extinguish or lay waste the Church of God, which was Christ's inheritance. This may also be referred to what Zechariah foretold about the burdensome stone, when he says that Jerusalem will be like a huge and heavy stone, in lifting which the strongest men will try their strength, yet not without loss or the tearing of their limbs. We have seen many examples of this kind in our own age, too many to recount. Now let each one remember that this parable contains the common teaching about the Church. This is the vineyard of the Lord, planted from the very beginning of things. The vines in it are the individual faithful; the husbandmen and vinedressers are called the ministers of the Word of God. Its possession belongs to the Son of God. Let all therefore observe him, so that they may render him fruit worthy of him. In this way they will escape the destruction prepared for the unbelieving and faithless husbandmen and barren vines, and will be gathered with their Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ into the inheritance of the heavenly kingdom. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA CLXXX.
units.tr: HOMILY CLXXX.

units.la: Tunc studuerunt principes Sacerdotum & Scribae inijcere manus in eum eo ipso momento, sed timuerunt plebem. Cognouerunt enim eum aduersus ipsos dixisse similitudinem istam. Itaque obseruantes eum miserunt insidiatores, qui se iustos esse simularent, vt carperent eius sermonem ad tradendum eum imperio & potestati Praesidis. Et interrogauerunt eum dicentes: Magister, scimus te recte dicere & docere, nec accipere personam: sed viam Dei in veritate docere. Licet nobis censum dare Caesari, an non? Animaduersa autem eorum calliditate, dixit eis: Quid me tentatis? Ostendite mihi denarium: cuius habet imaginem & inscriptionem? Responderunt autem dixerunt, Caesaris. Tunc dixit eis: Reddite igitur quae sunt Caesaris, Caesari: & quae sunt Dei, Deo. Itaque non potuerunt verba eius carpere coram populo: & mirati super eius responso, siluerunt.
units.tr: Then the chief priests and scribes sought to lay hands on him at that very moment, but they feared the people. For they perceived that he had spoken this parable against them. So, watching him closely, they sent spies who pretended to be righteous, to catch him in his words, so that they might hand him over to the authority and power of the governor. They asked him, "Teacher, we know that you speak and teach rightly, and that you show no partiality, but teach the way of God in truth. Is it lawful for us to give tribute to Caesar, or not?" But he perceived their craftiness and said to them, "Why do you test me? Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it bear?" They answered and said, "Caesar's." Then he said to them, "Render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's." And so they could not catch his words before the people, and marvelling at his answer, they were silent.

units.la: Quemadmodum Dominus & Seruator noster Iesus Christus, cum iam mortis hora instaret, totus in hoc fuit, vt hostium quoq; saluti consuleret: ita isti eo ipso tempore indies deteriores facti, omnes ingenij sui vires ad ipsum perdendum intenderunt. Voluit autem horum exemplo nos docere Spiritus sanctus, quid nobis de omnibus illis debeamus polliceri, qui semel excussό Dei timore, suis affectibus & prauis desiderijs indulgere coeperunt. Vt enim pij inter contentionum atq; persecutionum certamina maiores quotidie in pietate progressus faciunt: ita improbi homines & impostores in peius proficiunt, dum & alios seducunt, & ipsi à suis cupiditatibus seducuntur. Nec enim illis satis videtur, si verbis Veritatem oppugnent, sed tandem rabie maiori accensi, sanguinaria consilia ineunt de illis opprimendis, quos Christo suum ius vendicare & eius gloriam constantius tueri vident. Docuit hoc ipse nuper in parabola de vinea & infidis colonis: at quod verbis docuit, id nunc Sacerdotes & Scribæ proprio exemplo confirmant. Describit enim Lucas, quid aduersus illum tentauerint, & mox nouum congressum narrat, in quo cum crudelitate mirificam aßutiam conjunxerunt. Continet autem historia hæc multa, quæ ad vitæ Christianæ institutionem & fidei nostræ confirmationem faciunt, ideoq; dignissima est, quam diligentius consideremus.
units.tr: Just as our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, when the hour of his death was at hand, was wholly intent on caring for the salvation even of his enemies, so these men, at that very time, became worse by the day, and bent all the powers of their wit to destroy him. The Holy Spirit, however, wished by the example of these men to teach us what we ought to expect for all those who, once the fear of God has been cast off, begin to indulge their passions and wicked desires. For just as the godly make greater progress in piety every day amid the struggles of contention and persecution, so wicked men and impostors go from bad to worse, while they both mislead others and are themselves led astray by their own lusts. For it does not seem enough to them to assail the truth with words; at last, inflamed with greater fury, they form murderous plans for crushing those whom they see defending Christ's right and maintaining his glory more steadfastly. He taught this himself recently in the parable of the vineyard and the faithless tenants; but what he taught in words, the chief priests and scribes now confirm by their own example. Luke describes what they attempted against him, and soon narrates a new encounter in which they joined remarkable cunning to cruelty. This history contains many things that serve the training of the Christian life and the confirmation of our faith, and is therefore well worth considering the more carefully.

units.la: Et de aduersarijs quidem Christi hæc dicuntur: Tum studuerunt principes Sacerdotū & Scribæ inijcere manus in eum eo ipso momento, sed timuerunt plebem. Cognouerunt enim eum aduersus ipsos dixisse similitudinem istam. Quibus verbis malitia eorum Euangelista sic describit, ut simul deuotum & incurabile Veritatis odium arguat, quo in proprium exitium abrepti sunt. Si enim intellexerunt parabolam istam de ipsis dictam esse, vtiq; se quoq; colonos illos perfidos & crudeles esse, propriæ conscientiæ testimonio conuicti sunt. Num vero propterea emendantur? num cum Deo in gratiam redire cupiunt? Nihil minus. Imò è vestigio cupiunt illi manus inijcere, & perdere eum, qui ipsos tam amicè & grauiter monebat. Et hoc illud est, quod initio diximus, homines improbos & impostores in peius proficere. Vt enim electorum corda peccatorum redargutione salubriter tanguntur, ut de pœnitentia serio cogitent: ita impiorum conscientiæ Verbo Dei vulnerantur quidem, sed quia ijdem suum honorem & quiduis audendi licentiam gloriæ Dei præferunt, ex eo dolorem concipiunt, qui eos in rabiem accendit, vt lucem illam Verbi cum eius administris extinctam velint. Peccant ergo tales in propriam conscientiam: & quia huius stimulis non mouentur, nihil adhiberi potest, quod eos possit in viam reducere. Exempla huius contumaciæ in Caino, Pharaone, Saule & multis aliis historia sacra proponit: & huius generis multa hodie etiam cernimus.
units.tr: These things are said of the adversaries of Christ: "Then the chief priests and scribes sought to lay hands on him at that very moment, but they feared the people. For they perceived that he had spoken this parable against them." By these words the Evangelist describes their malice in such a way as to show at once their devoted and incurable hatred of the truth, by which they were carried headlong to their own destruction. For if they understood that the parable had been spoken about them, then, convicted by the testimony of their own conscience, they knew that they too were those wicked and cruel tenants. Do they therefore amend their ways? Do they desire to be reconciled to God? Nothing could be further from it. Rather, they at once wish to lay hands on him and destroy him, who was warning them so kindly and so seriously. And this is what we said at the beginning: wicked men and impostors go from bad to worse. For just as the hearts of the elect are salutarily touched by the rebuke of sin, so that they seriously consider repentance, so the consciences of the ungodly are indeed wounded by the Word of God; but because they prefer their own honour and the licence to dare anything to the glory of God, they conceive from this a pain that inflames them to rage, so that they wish that light of the Word, together with its ministers, to be extinguished. Such men therefore sin against their own conscience; and since they are not moved by its goads, nothing can be applied that could bring them back to the way. Sacred history sets before us examples of this obstinacy in Cain, Pharaoh, Saul and many others, and we see many of this kind even today.

units.la: At hic consolationi nostræ seruiat, quòd cùm penes Sacerdotes summa rerum in religione potestas esset, non audent tamen effectum dare, quod maximè volunt. Et quid illis obstat? Timent populum, quem Christo applaudere & de eo honorificè sentire atque loqui videbant. Hoc ipsum aliàs quoque ipsis accidisse scimus: & solet Deus hoc præposfero metu hostes suos punire, ut qui eius metu sive reuerentia non tanguntur, eos timeant, à quibus ipsi debebant timeri. Est quidem communis hæc tyrannorum vox, Oderint dum metuant: sed si animos eorum penitius intueri liceret, facilè videremus, non tam securos esse quàm videri volunt. Quomodo enim ab aliorum metu possent liberi esse, qui efficere non possunt, quò minus seipsos metuant? Enimuero constat eiusmodi homines frequenter furijs ac conscientiæ stimulis agitatos, sibijpsis terrores fingere, qui somni beneficio eos fraudant, & ipsam vitam iniucundam reddit. Hoc ut omnes excitare debet ad custodiendam vitæ innocentiam: ita eos in primis, qui Rempub. administrant, ne turpi metu succumbant ijs, qui ipsis timorem atque obedientiam legitimam debent.
units.tr: But here let this serve our consolation: although supreme power in religious matters rested with the priests, they do not dare to carry out what they most want. And what stands in their way? They fear the people, whom they saw applauding Christ and speaking and thinking honourably of him. We know that this has happened to them at other times as well; and God is accustomed to punish his enemies with this reversed fear, so that those who are not moved by fear or reverence of him should fear those by whom they ought themselves to be feared. This saying of tyrants is indeed common: "Let them hate, provided they fear." But if it were allowed to look more deeply into their minds, we would easily see that they are not as secure as they wish to appear. For how could those be free from the fear of others who cannot prevent themselves from fearing themselves? Indeed it is well established that men of this kind, often driven by the furies and goads of conscience, invent terrors for themselves, which rob them of sleep and make life joyless. This ought to rouse all men to guard the innocence of their life; but especially those who administer the commonwealth, lest they succumb to shameful fear of those to whom they owe fear and lawful obedience.

units.la: Cæterum etiamsi nunc metu territi manum abstineant Sacerdotum principes, non tamen quiescunt, quin noua consilia ineant, quibus ipsum irretire, & ut seditiosum præsidis Romani authoritate opprimere possint. Quem conatum Lucas ita describit: Itaq; obseruantes eum miserunt insidiatores, qui se iustos esse simularent, ut carperent eius sermonem, ad tradendum eum imperio & potestati Præsidis. Insidiatores iflos ex Herodianis & Pharisæis, vel potius Pharisæorum discipulos fuisse, Matthæus & Marcus annotarunt. Erant vtriq; ad insidias aptissimi. Pharisæi enim reliquis fan&tiores habebantur, Herodiani verò à religione Iudaica non prorsus alieni erant; sed quàmuis cum Herode Romani Imperij maiestatem reuererentur, populi tamen commodis & libertati fauere videbantur: & quod aulicis fere proprium est, religionis professionem cum ambitione & voluptatum studijs miscebant. Interim non dubium est Pharisæos illis infensissimos fuisse, qui & mores aulicos oderant, & libertatis recuperandæ studio præ alijs ardebant. Quàmuis ergo non parua esset inter duos istos hominum ordines diuersitas, vterque tamen principibus Sacerdotum dignus visus est, cuius opera aduersus Christum vterentur, & ipsis eriam in eo oppugnando facile poterat conuenire. Est hoc impijs proprium, quòd cùm in ijs, quæ ad huius vitæ vsum spectant, ipsis nunquam inserfe inter se conueniat, sed vel ambitione vel auaritia vel alijs cupiditatibus superati rixas quotidie excitent, aduersus Christum tamen vnanimi consensu conspirant: eò quòd huius doctrina omnibus ex æquo inuisa & exosa est. Sic inter Sadducæos & Pharisæos, diuersissimarum sectarum homines, non semel pacem, aut saltem inducias, fuisse legimus, vt Christum coniunctis viribus aggrederentur? Quid nonne milites sanguinarios sua amicitia dignos iudicarunt, quando his in illo capiendo opus erat, qui prius eum calumniari solebant, quòd cum publicanis familiarius versaretur? Et quis hodie nescit Monachos, qui mundo mortui videri volunt, non raro cum impijssimis militibus conspirare, vt horum opera aduersus germanos Christi cultores abutantur? Et poterant ista ferri, nisi his turpiora nostro tempore fierent: quando Christianos principes non pudet cum Turcis inducias facere, vt in veritatis Euangelicæ sectatores arma sua conuertant: & vtinam non inuenirentur, qui inimicorum crucis auxilia aduersus eos petunt, qui in huius solius merito omnem salutis fiduciam collocatam habent. Non debent autem ista aliquem terrere. Omnibus enim istis per Isaiam loquitur Ecclesia: Societatem inite o populi, at inferiores eritis: auscultate qui in remotis estis regionibus, accingamini, at inferiores eritis: inite consilium, at fiet irritum: loquimini sermonem, sed non stabit: quoniam nobiscum est Deus. Interim excitent nos impiorum conspirationes, vt ipsi quoque animis consentiamus, & in Christo Iesu vnum atque idem loquamur. Hinc denique petamus argumentum, quo nos in eius fide confirmemus. Quia enim hæc omnibus impijs ex æquo inuisa est, ipsam veram & solam sanctam esse oportet.
units.tr: Moreover, even though the chief priests, now terrified by fear, keep their hands off him, they do not rest, but form new plans by which they might ensnare him and crush him by the authority of the Roman governor as a seditious man. Luke describes this attempt thus: "So, watching him closely, they sent spies who pretended to be righteous, to catch him in his words, so as to hand him over to the authority and power of the governor."
