Hence arises that joy which cheers the minds of the godly even in the midst of afflictions, and which Paul wills to be perpetual among Christians. For as it springs from pious causes, so it also has a most blessed end, and it does not turn into mourning, as usually happens to the wicked, who rejoice in the fleeting and dishonourable things of this world.

units.la: Quartò frequentes in templo fuerunt Apostoli toto illo tempore, quod ab Ascensionis die ad Pentecosten vsque effluxit: in templo autem laudarunt & benedixerunt Deum. Non ergo propter Sacerdotum aut Scribarum doctrinam, aut quòd in sacris venalibus spem salutis repositam haberent, coetus publicos adierunt: sed vt fidem suam publicè profiterentur, Deo Patri pro exhibito Messia gratias agerent, beneficia eius praedicarent, & Spiritum sibi promissum precibus assiduis expeterent. Neque a templo abhorruerunt, etsi huius vsum & totam religionem externam impij Sacerdotes corrupissent, & in populo, qui illuc confluebat, cum impietate scelera grauissima regnaret. Quia enim templi vsus per se sanctus erat, & aliquas sciebant esse in corruptissima gente reliquias, ex quibus Ecclesiam ministrari oporteret: noluerunt illis deesse, neq; aliquam occasionem negligere. qua suum Christo obsequium praestare possent. Longè ergo alia illorum mens fuit, quàm Anabaptistarum, qui dum Ecclesiam puram & omnibus numeris absolutam quaerunt, à coetibus sacris in vniuersum abstinent, imò eos etiam Satanae tradunt, qui fidem in Christum ingenuè profitentur, peccata sua agnoscunt, & ad poenitentiam sese praeparant. Referūt illi Donatistas, & vt hi olim turbas graues dederunt, ita isti quoq; passim scismatum & periculosissimorum motuum authores sunt, quibus Euangelij doctrinam multis suspectam, multis inuisam quoque & exosam reddunt.
units.tr: Fourthly, the Apostles were frequently in the temple during the whole period that passed from the day of the Ascension to Pentecost, and in the temple they praised and blessed God. They did not therefore frequent the public assemblies because of the teaching of the priests or scribes, or because they placed their hope of salvation in the sacred things that were bought and sold, but so that they might profess their faith publicly, give thanks to God the Father for the Messiah now revealed, proclaim his benefits, and with constant prayers seek the Spirit promised to them. Nor did they shun the temple, although the wicked priests had corrupted its use and all its outward worship, and although among the crowd that flocked there the most grievous wickedness reigned together with impiety. For since the use of the temple was holy in itself, and they knew that some remnants were left among that most corrupt people from which a Church ought to be formed, they were unwilling to fail them, nor to neglect any opportunity by which they could render their obedience to Christ. Their mind was therefore far different from that of the Anabaptists, who, while seeking a pure Church altogether perfect in every respect, abstain entirely from the sacred assemblies, and even hand over to Satan those who openly profess faith in Christ, acknowledge their sins, and prepare themselves for repentance. They imitate the Donatists, and just as the latter once caused serious disturbances, so these too are everywhere the authors of schisms and most dangerous commotions, by which they make the doctrine of the Gospel suspect to many, and odious and hateful to many more.

units.la: At quia de his saepe dictum est, nos discipulorum exemplum imitemur, vt quod hi tunc fecerunt, nos nunquam non faciamus in beneficiorum nobis in Christo factorum grata memoriam. Sunt ea omni aestimatione maiora, nec in nobis aliquid est, quod cum tanta tamen multiplici Dei bonitate conferri mereatur. Omnibus autem sacrificijs atq; oblationibus ille obedientiam praefert. Huius primum & praecipuum caput est, vt in eum credamus, quem ille misit, Iesum Christum videlicet. Hunc ergo agnoscamus Seruatorem, redemptorem & aduocatum nostrum, hunc adoremus & colamus in Spiritu & veritate, atq; fidem in hunc vitae totius actionibus profiteamur. Seruiunt professioni huic coetus sacri, quos apud omnes veri Dei cultores in summo pretio semper fuisse constat, quia in illis et Deus coniunctis quasi viribus colitur, et animorum in fide consensio confirmatur, quae fraternae charitatis, ex qua germani discipuli dignoscuntur, mater est. In illis ergo frequentes simus, vt Dei verbu audiamus, beneficia Dei praedicemus, & indesinenter oremus, vt quàhoc nouissimo tempore nobis manifestare dignatus est, Euangelij lucem in dies magis atq; magis in omniu animis accendat, vt Filium suum vnigenitum, Iesum Christum, fide firma apprehendant, & salutē in illo aeternam consequantur. Ipsi debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: But since this has often been said, let us imitate the example of the disciples, so that what they then did, we may always do in grateful remembrance of the benefits bestowed on us in Christ. These benefits surpass every estimate, and there is nothing in us that deserves to be set against such great and manifold goodness of God. Above all sacrifices and offerings, however, he prefers obedience. Its first and chief head is that we believe in him whom he sent, namely Jesus Christ. Let us therefore acknowledge him as our Saviour, Redeemer and Advocate, let us adore and worship him in spirit and truth, and profess faith in him in all the actions of our whole life. Holy assemblies serve this profession; among all true worshippers of God they have always been held in the highest esteem, as is well established, because in them God is worshipped with united strength, and the agreement of minds in faith is confirmed, which is the mother of brotherly love, by which true disciples are recognized. Let us therefore be frequent in them, so that we may hear the Word of God, proclaim the benefits of God, and pray without ceasing that he, who in this last age has deigned to make himself manifest to us, would kindle the light of the Gospel more and more in the hearts of all, so that they may firmly grasp his only-begotten Son, Jesus Christ, by faith, and obtain eternal salvation in him. To him be blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: CHRISTO AETERNO DEO OPT. MAX. S.
units.tr: TO CHRIST, THE ETERNAL GOD, BEST AND GREATEST. S.

units.la: Hos aeterne tibi consigno CHRISTE labores:
units.tr: To you, eternal Christ, I dedicate these labours of mine:

units.la: O vtinam dignos, quos tua Sponsa legat.
units.tr: Oh, that they may be worthy of being read by your Bride!

units.la: Iactatur grauibus dum circumuenta procellis,
units.tr: While she is tossed about, surrounded by heavy storms,

units.la: Vt ratis in medio sola relicta mari.
units.tr: Like a ship left alone in the middle of the sea.

units.la: Tu regito fessam, tu clauum CHRISTE teneto,
units.tr: You, Christ, steer her when she is weary; you hold the helm.

units.la: Su precor o seruis tu Cynosura tuis.
units.tr: Be, I pray, the guiding star (Cynosure) for your servants.

units.la: Da pacem optatam, motos componito fluctus,
units.tr: Grant the peace we long for, and calm the rising waves.

units.la: Fac summi iurent in tua verba Duces.
units.tr: Make the mighty leaders swear to your words.

units.la: Sparge salutiferi per terras semina Verbi:
units.tr: Scatter the seeds of the saving Word over the earth,

units.la: Vt toto nomen crescat in orbe tuum.
units.tr: So that your name may grow throughout the whole world.
